# Triangular powering of the finite P3 core: exact cycles and charged phases

Date: 2026-09-13. **Finite H orbits have an exact constructive transient/cycle
normal form. Their periods are powers of two, with an all-length spacing
restriction on period doublings.** This supports exact large-time queries
after a width-dependent construction. It does not give a sublinear singleton
center algorithm. Two actual seed-core examples show that discarding the
transient, or extrapolating the eventual cycle backward, gives a wrong
center bit.

The [verifier](../../experiments/rule30/p3_triangular_core_power.py) and
[artifact](../../experiments/rule30/p3-triangular-core-power.json) contain
complete per-column certificates, including every transient and periodic
seam. No long center prefix, paid compute, or finite-state census is used.

definitions_and_conventions.heading: ## 1. The triangular system and a constructive normal form
definitions_and_conventions.text:
## 1. The triangular system and a constructive normal form

Use the [bulk-core map](RESULTS-p3-bulk-core-formula.md)

```
H(x)=(x>>2) XOR ((x>>1) OR x).
```

For a nonnegative finite integer with bits x_j(t),

```
x_j(t+1)=x_(j+2)(t) XOR (x_(j+1)(t) OR x_j(t)).    (1)
```

The highest one stays fixed, so H preserves the width w of every positive
input. The two coordinates above the width are identically zero. At a
lower coordinate, write u=x_(j+2), v=x_(j+1), z=x_j. Its update is

```
z' = u XOR z       when v=0;
z' = 1 XOR u      when v=1.                        (2)
```

This is the existing reset/toggle mechanism; the four-map monoid itself
is already recorded in [aggregate affine blocks](RESULTS-p3-aggregate-affine-blocks.md).
The new conclusions below use the relations between consecutive Rule 30
coordinates, rather than treating their drivers as arbitrary.

Suppose the entire upper prefix has an eventual primitive period P from
a certified time T. Compose (2) over its next P updates. Exactly one of
the following occurs:

| Return map on z | Condition | Extended prefix period | Safe new start |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Constant | v has a1 in the cycle | P | T+P |
| Identity | v is zero and the P values of u have even parity | P | T |
| Toggle | v is zero and the P values of u have odd parity | 2P | T |

The prefix period cannot fall, since that prefix remains part of the
extended state. In the toggle case z(t+P)=1-z(t), so the new period is
exactly2P. An identity return can yield distinct lifted cycles depending
on the entering bit; no unique-attractor assumption is made.

This gives an exact algorithm. Start at the highest bit and retain each
coordinate's complete transient followed by one periodic block. Obtain
the next return map from the already constructed upper sequences; advance
the new bit from its given initial value to the safe new start, and save
one full block. Evaluation at time k reads the transient if k<T, and
otherwise reads index T+((k-T) mod P). The table contains the phase; it
is not supplied externally.

Correctness is inductive in the coordinates. Once the full upper prefix
is periodic, the displayed unary return map proves the new seam closes.
The saved recurrence through the seam then proves every later update by
induction in time. The checker validates precisely these finite edges.
It accepts no promise that a large enough-looking table is periodic.

Starting with P=1, every final primitive period is P=2^q. Each reset adds
at most the current P to the certified transient. As periods only grow,

```
actual transient mu <= certified T <= (w-1)*P.     (3)
```

The top bit adds no transient. These are all-length bounds; neither P nor
mu is asserted to be polynomial in w.

The input0 is fixed and has width0, transient0, and period1. The verifier
handles it with an empty coordinate list rather than applying a positive
width formula to a nonexistent highest bit.

coordinate_hypothesis_formula_source.heading: ## 3. No fixed temporal period covers arbitrarily large widths
coordinate_hypothesis_formula_source.text:
## 3. No fixed temporal period covers arbitrarily large widths

There is also a lower restriction that holds for every positive periodic
state, not merely a selected attractor:

```
w <= 4^P-1.                                         (6)
```

Here w is the actual highest-one position plus1, not an arbitrarily
padded buffer width. The uniform upper bound (4a) can use a larger
ambient width; this lower bound cannot.

Proof. Encode a temporal column over P times by a P-bit word. For three
consecutive spatial columns u,v,z, (1) gives

```
u(t)=z(t+1) XOR (v(t) OR z(t)),  with time modulo P. (7)
```

Hence every ordered target pair (v,z) has exactly one predecessor (u,v).
Begin with the two zero columns above the highest bit. The first nonzero
column is the constant1 column. Along the subsequent spatial path, no
ordered pair can repeat: applying the unique predecessor repeatedly
would propagate any repetition back to the initial zero pair. That pair
has itself as its only predecessor, which is incompatible with the path
having left it through a nonzero column. Likewise the path cannot return
to the zero pair.

The w pairs ending at the w coordinates of the positive state are
therefore distinct nonzero elements of a set with4^P elements. This proves
(6). In particular periods are unbounded as the width grows. This does
not refute a polynomial upper bound for period or transient, and it does
not address a center query whose input width also grows with its time.

The same pair representation gives an exact directed spatial test at
fixed P: a nonzero immediate driver yields one continuation; a zero
driver with odd parity prevents a P-periodic continuation; an even one
gives two. No repeated-pair shortcut occurs on a path descending from
the finite zero boundary, by the preceding argument. Thus waiting for a
spatial cycle is not a valid compression strategy for these paths.

coordinate_hypothesis_formula_source.heading: ## 4. Actual singleton cores invalidate premature cycle reduction
coordinate_hypothesis_formula_source.text:
## 4. Actual singleton cores invalidate premature cycle reduction

The bulk theorem represents the singleton query using an initial core
U=C^L. Its integer x=U(0) has width exactly2L. The relevant H iteration
count is L-1 for the odd query and L-2 for the even query. These counts
need not reach the eventual cycle of x.

For L=6, x=3204 has the exact orbit

```
3204,3559,3214,3564,3205,3558,3214,...
```

Its transient is2 and period4. The actual query c_11 is bit0 of H^5(x),
which is0. Replacing5 by5 mod4=1 gives bit0 of3559, which is1. The
period is correct, but dropping the transient loses the phase.

For L=10, x=820716 has transient10 and period4. The actual even query
c_18 is bit1 of H^8(x). It equals bit1 of820681, which is0. Extending
the eventual cycle backward with

```
10+((8-10) mod4)=12
```

instead selects H^12(x)=820683, whose bit1 is1. This is a failure even
when the eventual cycle's phase is retained: the queried time precedes
the transient. The complete fourteen-state orbit is saved and every edge
and the final return are checked. The corresponding odd query at time19
happens to agree with this backward extrapolation at bit0; no contrary
claim is made for that bit.

Both wrong answers are checked against independent singleton row
evolution at the two specified query times. They refute these particular
cycle shortcuts, rather than faster ways of constructing the correct
transient or requested observable.

coordinate_hypothesis_formula_source.text:
## 1. Direct bitplanes: compute the high field, then the low field

All additions and multiplications in the formulas below are over F2.
Write an input digit of Y as D_i+2H_i and its output under B as P_i+2Q_i.
The original output-driven equations are

```
P_i = D_i + (P_(i-1) OR Q_(i-1)),
Q_i = H_i + (Q_(i-1) OR D_i),
(P_-1,Q_-1)=(1,0).                              (1)
```

The second equation does not use P. Thus first compute the entire high
field using

```
Q_i = H_i + D_i + (1+D_i) Q_(i-1), Q_-1=0.       (2)
```

With Q fixed, compute the low field using

```
P_i = D_i + Q_(i-1) + (1+Q_(i-1)) P_(i-1),
P_-1=1.                                         (3)
```

Equations (2) and (3) are simply the expansion x OR y=x+y+xy in (1).
They preserve the fixed B boundary. The second scan uses exactly the high
field produced by the first scan.

For fixed D, the map H->Q in (2) is affine on every finite prefix and on
the whole one-sided field. For fixed Q, the map D->P in (3) is likewise
affine. Each is bijective on prefixes: its current input enters with
coefficient1, and all other dependence is on previous outputs. Their local
inverse equations are

```
H_i = Q_i + D_i + (1+D_i) Q_(i-1),
D_i = P_i + Q_(i-1) + (1+Q_(i-1)) P_(i-1).       (4)
```

To invert the complete update, recover D from the supplied P,Q by the
second equation, then recover H by the first. Only adjacent supplied
output digits are used. These are all-input identities; no seed ancestry
or assumption about reset locations is required.

Each forward scan has a Boolean carry acted on by one of four affine maps:
identity, flip, reset to0, or reset to1. This allows exact aggregation of
**supplied** control blocks. It does not construct those blocks across
successive B times.

# Two conditional affine scans and a local Gray basis

Date: 2026-09-14. **The itinerary map B can be evaluated by two consecutive
prefix scans, each affine in the field it updates when the other field is
fixed. A pointwise Gray-code basis gives an equivalent two-field update and
a local readout of every requested bit.**

This is a direct consequence of the already saved
[bitplane equations](RESULTS-p3-bitplane-temporal-squaring.md), made explicit
here. It corrects an overly strong interpretation of the nonaffine half in
the [staggered factorization](RESULTS-p3-staggered-affine-field.md): that
nonaffinity concerns its particular choice of the fixed old field. It does
not require one intrinsically nonaffine half in every coordinate system.
The two halves below remain jointly nonlinear, and their control fields
change along the actual orbit. No faster temporal powering or P3 algorithm
is proved.

The [verifier](../../experiments/rule30/p3_two_affine_scans.py) and
[artifact](../../experiments/rule30/p3-two-affine-scans.json) check the local
identities, both boundaries, inverse formulas, and bounded exact comparisons
with the original itinerary transducer. No orbit or capacity census is
needed for the all-length statements.

coordinate_hypothesis_formula_source.heading: ## 2. A local Gray-code representation
coordinate_hypothesis_formula_source.text:
## 2. A local Gray-code representation

Define two binary fields

```
U_i=D_i, Z_i=H_i+D_i.                            (5)
```

This is a pointwise linear bijection, with D=U and H=Z+U. It neither
requires an inverse prefix scan nor adds an auxiliary history. Write the
output fields as U'=P and Z'=Q+P.

There is an exact factorization in the opposite order. First update U,
holding the old Z fixed:

```
U'_i = U_i + Z_(i-1) + (1+Z_(i-1)) U'_(i-1),
Z_-1=0, U'_-1=1.                                (6)
```

Then update Z, holding the newly produced U' fixed:

```
Z'_i = Z_i + U'_i(1+U'_(i-1)) + U'_i Z'_(i-1).
                                                     (7)
```

At the origin equation (7) uses the auxiliary values
U'_-1=Z'_-1=0, giving Z'_0=Z_0+U'_0. Equivalently one may use both
auxiliary values1, since they enter only through their sum. This is a
separate boundary convention for the second scan; it does not alter any
produced U'_i at i>=0. In particular it must not be mixed with
U'_-1=1,Z'_-1=0 in (7).

Here is a direct proof, retaining the output boundary of (1). Rewriting its
high equation gives

```
Q_i = Z_i + U'_i Q_(i-1).                        (8)
```

Indeed if Q_(i-1)=0, both sides reduce to H_i+D_i. If Q_(i-1)=1,
(1) forces U'_i=1+D_i, and substitution again gives equality. Hence

```
U'_i OR Q_i = U'_i OR Z_i,
```

because the additional term in (8) is masked whenever U'_i=1. Substituting
this identity at the preceding digit in the low equation proves (6).
Finally Z'_i=Q_i+U'_i and Q_(i-1)=Z'_(i-1)+U'_(i-1) prove (7) for
i>=1. At i=0, Q_-1=0 gives its stated origin equation directly.

Both halves are again affine in the field being updated. Their inverses
are local once the controlling field and output are supplied:

```
U_i = U'_i + Z_(i-1) + (1+Z_(i-1)) U'_(i-1),
Z_i = Z'_i + U'_i(1+U'_(i-1)) + U'_i Z'_(i-1).   (9)
```

To invert the full update, use the second formula to recover Z, then the
first to recover U. Use the same separate origin conventions as in the
forward scans.

coordinate_hypothesis_formula_source.heading: ## 4. What has and has not been simplified
coordinate_hypothesis_formula_source.text:
## 4. What has and has not been simplified

For a supplied prefix of m digits, either representation evaluates one B
step using two O(m) Boolean-operation scans and constant carry memory in
addition to its O(m) input/output storage. The Gray transformation and
readout cost constant work per digit. Materializing the actual fields
through N times still costs O(Nm) Boolean work; for (11), m=h and N is of
order h, so this gives the usual quadratic work in the center time.
Index handling and representation costs are additional implementation
costs, not free operations on arbitrarily large indices.

Conditional affinity does not make the entire map affine. The coefficients
of the second scan use the field constructed by the first, and the next
time step uses both newly constructed fields. For example the root Gray
rule is U'_0=U_0+1, Z'_0=Z_0+U_0+1, but higher digits already use products
between fields in (6)-(7). More decisively, the two-fine-digit inputs
0,1,2,3 have B outputs5,14,15,0, whose XOR is4; this violates an affine
rectangle identity and remains a violation under the linear Gray change.

Products of the affine scan operators can be written with their complete
ordered control history. A binary product tree reduces their dependency
depth. It does not by itself reduce the work required to produce the
control fields, align their spatial blocks, or evaluate both child
products. No factor-refactorization identity eliminating this actual
history dependence is proved here. Freezing a control field and powering
its operator would address a different supplied-context problem.

The result supplies an exact simpler representation and local observable,
and corrects a coordinate-specific obstruction. It provides neither an
all-scale dyadic closure nor an improved P3 complexity bound.

coordinate_hypothesis_formula_source.heading: ## 2. Hard-core control gives a first-order reset scan
coordinate_hypothesis_formula_source.text:
## 2. Hard-core control gives a first-order reset scan

Consecutive entries of rho cannot both be1. At a site i with rho_i=1,
equation (3) at i-1 therefore says
Z_(i-1)=q_(i-1)+q_(i-2). Substitution at i eliminates the older carry.
With q_-1=Z_-1=0, the resulting uniform rule is

```
q_i=Z_i+(1+rho_i)q_(i-1)+rho_i(1+Z_(i-1)).       (4)
```

Thus rho_i=0 propagates the preceding carry by XOR with Z_i, while
rho_i=1 resets it to Z_i+Z_(i-1)+1. At i=0 the same formula gives
q_0=Z_0+rho_0 directly; no negative-time or negative-site value is inferred.

For a requested position i, if rho has no1 at positions0 through i, then

```
q_i = XOR_(j=0..i) Z_j.
```

Otherwise, if k is the last position at most i with rho_k=1, then

```
q_i = 1 + XOR_(j=max(0,k-1)..i) Z_j.             (5)
```

Only the last rise and the displayed input parity are needed once the
control and input fields are supplied. This does not make their
construction free.

# Two-time high-field transport controlled by rising edges

Date: 2026-09-14. **The high field of B squared depends on the intermediate
low field only through its rising edges. Each rising edge resets the
remaining high-field carry, giving an exact last-rise/range-parity query.**
A corrected C-boundary version gives such a high-field query for **both
parities of the actual center column**. The final low field, when needed
for continued full evolution, still requires the intermediate low field.

This isolates a reduced control field in an exact temporal composition.
The saved [B-squared kernel](RESULTS-p3-bitplane-temporal-squaring.md) already
evaluates B squared in one spatial scan. The result here therefore does
not establish a faster B-squared implementation, an all-scale closure, or
an improved P3 complexity bound.

definitions_and_conventions.heading: ## 1. The complementary-factor cancellation
definitions_and_conventions.text:
## 1. The complementary-factor cancellation

Work over F2. Write the input digits of Y as D_i+2H_i, and put

```
Z=D+H,  A=low(BY), C=high(BY),
p=low(B²Y), q=high(B²Y).
```

Let S be the spatial right shift with zero padding, and let
L_a=I+diag(a)S. The exact Gray identity in the
[two-affine-scans report](RESULTS-p3-two-affine-scans.md) and the high-field
inverse of the second B step give

```
Z=L_A C,
C=L_(1+A) q+A.                                  (1)
```

These involve the actual intermediate field A; no independent replacement
or completed history is inserted. Define

```
rho=A(1+SA),
rho_0=A_0, rho_i=A_i(1+A_(i-1)) for i>=1.         (2)
```

Direct operator multiplication gives

```
L_A L_(1+A)=I+S+diag(rho)S²,
L_A A=rho.
```

Consequently the complete high-field relation is

```
Z=q+Sq+rho(1+S²q).                               (3)
```

This is an identity of one-sided fields and of every finite prefix. The
coefficient of S has become constant. All remaining dependence on A in
this relation is through rho.

coordinate_hypothesis_formula_source.text:
## 5. The C boundary and actual center queries of both parities

The same bitplane equations define C with the distinct virtual output
boundary (low,high)=(0,1). For this paragraph set

```
A=low(CY), Cmid=high(CY), q=high(C²Y), Z=D+H,
rho=A(1+SA),
```

again using zero padding only for S and rho. Let e_i denote the field
with its only1 at position i. Retaining the actual high boundary1 gives

```
Z=L_A Cmid+A_0 e_0,
Cmid=L_(1+A)q+A+(1+A_0)e_0.
```

Since L_A e_0=e_0+A_1e_1, the corrected identity is

```
Z=q+Sq+rho(1+S²q)+e_0+rho_1 e_1.               (10)
```

In particular its first two sites and subsequent scan are

```
q_0=H_0,
q_1=Z_1+q_0,
q_i=Z_i+(1+rho_i)q_(i-1)+rho_i(1+Z_(i-1))
     for i>=2.                                  (11)
```

The first equality also uses A_0=1+D_0, the actual low origin update of
C. The rises at positions0 and1 do not reset this scan. If the last rise
k at or before i with k>=2 exists, the answer is still
1+XOR Z_[k-1..i]. If none exists, it is
H_0+XOR Z_[1..i], with an empty XOR when i=0. The coefficient at site2
is valid because (10) makes Z_1=q_1+q_0 regardless of rho_1; subsequent
resets use the same hard-core argument as before.

The proved [actual center identities](RESULTS-p3-actual-b-query.md) give,
for h>=1,

```
c_(2h)   = high(digit_(h-1)(C^(h+1)(0))),
c_(2h+1) = high(digit_(h-1)(B^(h+2)(0))).         (12)
```

Thus both cases use the high-only control reduction:

| Center query | Old input Y | Intermediate low A | Last-rise rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| c_(2h) | C^(h-1)(0) | low(C^h(0)) | (11), rises k>=2 |
| c_(2h+1) | B^h(0) | low(B^(h+1)(0)) | (5), rises k>=0 |

Both are queried at i=h-1. On the actual C orbit, the baseline H_0 in
(11) equals (h-1) mod2, since C complements its root digit. The cases
c_0=c_1=1 remain separate. These formulas require no final low-field
readout for either center parity. They still require the actual old Gray
parity range and the rises of the actual intermediate low field; those
are not supplied for free by (12).

# Two-time high-field transport controlled by rising edges

Date: 2026-09-14. **The high field of B squared depends on the intermediate
low field only through its rising edges. Each rising edge resets the
remaining high-field carry, giving an exact last-rise/range-parity query.**
A corrected C-boundary version gives such a high-field query for **both
parities of the actual center column**. The final low field, when needed
for continued full evolution, still requires the intermediate low field.

This isolates a reduced control field in an exact temporal composition.
The saved [B-squared kernel](RESULTS-p3-bitplane-temporal-squaring.md) already
evaluates B squared in one spatial scan. The result here therefore does
not establish a faster B-squared implementation, an all-scale closure, or
an improved P3 complexity bound.

definitions_and_conventions.heading: ## 1. The complementary-factor cancellation
definitions_and_conventions.text:
## 1. The complementary-factor cancellation

Work over F2. Write the input digits of Y as D_i+2H_i, and put

```
Z=D+H,  A=low(BY), C=high(BY),
p=low(B²Y), q=high(B²Y).
```

Let S be the spatial right shift with zero padding, and let
L_a=I+diag(a)S. The exact Gray identity in the
[two-affine-scans report](RESULTS-p3-two-affine-scans.md) and the high-field
inverse of the second B step give

```
Z=L_A C,
C=L_(1+A) q+A.                                  (1)
```

These involve the actual intermediate field A; no independent replacement
or completed history is inserted. Define

```
rho=A(1+SA),
rho_0=A_0, rho_i=A_i(1+A_(i-1)) for i>=1.         (2)
```

Direct operator multiplication gives

```
L_A L_(1+A)=I+S+diag(rho)S²,
L_A A=rho.
```

Consequently the complete high-field relation is

```
Z=q+Sq+rho(1+S²q).                               (3)
```

This is an identity of one-sided fields and of every finite prefix. The
coefficient of S has become constant. All remaining dependence on A in
this relation is through rho.

coordinate_hypothesis_formula_source.heading: ## 3. An all-length zero-staircase jump
coordinate_hypothesis_formula_source.text:
## 3. An all-length zero-staircase jump

There is a sufficient condition that really closes repeated jumps. Fix
`M>=1`. Assume the following complete triangular collection of zero facts:

\[
x_{j+1+4a}(t+2b+e)=0,
\quad a,b\ge0,\quad a+b\le M-1,\quad e\in\{0,1\}.\tag{3}
\]

Then

\[
x_j(t+2M)=\bigoplus_{a=0}^{M}
 \left(\binom Ma\bmod2\right)x_{j+4a}(t).\tag{4}
\]

Proof: put `y_b(a)=x_(j+4a)(t+2b)`. Every applicable cell of the triangular
region satisfies `y_(b+1)(a)=y_b(a)+y_b(a+1)` by (1). Its M-step update
is therefore `(I+E)^M`, where E shifts a by one. Expanding this commuting
operator proves (4) over the exact finite dependency triangle.

In particular, if `M=2^(s-1)` for `s>=1`, Frobenius gives the two-term jump

\[
\boxed{x_j(t+2^s)=x_j(t)+x_{j+2^{s+1}}(t).}\tag{5}
\]

The Frobenius operation here acts on an already proved linear recurrence
inside the guarded region. It is not being substituted for decimation
of the original nonlinear sequence.

# Exact H jumps across a chronological zero corridor

Date: 2026-09-13. **A guarded bulk identity is proved, with an explicit
four-step residual and actual-core counterexamples. No faster general
singleton query is obtained.** This continues beyond the already proved
[four-element affine block monoid](RESULTS-p3-aggregate-affine-blocks.md):
the issue here is when its driving histories permit a spatial jump.

Write `x_j(t)=bit_j(H^t(x))`, where

\[
H(x)=(x\gg2)\mathbin{\mathrm{XOR}}((x\gg1)\mathbin{\mathrm{OR}}x),
\quad x_j(t+1)=x_{j+2}(t)+(x_{j+1}(t)\lor x_j(t)).
\]

Additions below are in `F_2`. A zero corridor at column `j+1` means that
this bit is zero at **every specified chronological time**, not merely
at its endpoints or in the initial row.

definitions_and_conventions.heading: ## 1. Two exact local jump laws
definitions_and_conventions.text:
## 1. Two exact local jump laws

If `x_(j+1)(t)=x_(j+1)(t+1)=0`, then

\[
x_j(t+2)=x_j(t)+x_{j+4}(t).\tag{1}
\]

Proof: the zero column's update forces
`x_(j+2)(t)=x_(j+3)(t)`. Consequently the difference of the two successive
drivers of `x_j` is exactly `x_(j+4)(t)`. This uses both driving columns
and their consistency under H.

Four zero-driver times do not justify blindly doubling (1). The exact
formula, assuming `x_(j+1)(t+i)=0` for `i=0,1,2,3`, is

\[
\boxed{x_j(t+4)=x_j(t)+x_{j+8}(t)
             +x_{j+4}(t)(1+x_{j+6}(t)).}\tag{2}
\]

Here is an algebraic derivation of the residual. Suppress the initial time
and name the successive columns
`z,p,q,r,s,u,v,w,y` at positions `j` through `j+8`. The zero conditions
give `q=r` at the first three times and `u=qs` at the first two. Hence
`q'=q+s` and `s'=s+v` at the needed times. Comparing the update of u with
`u'=q's'` gives

\[
w=s+v(1+q)(1+s),\qquad w(1+v)=s(1+v).
\]

Applying (1) at times t and t+2 gives
`z(t+4)+z(t)=s(t+2)+s(t)=v(t+1)+v(t)`.
The update of v makes the last expression `y+w(1+v)`, proving (2).
The complete five- and nine-bit local truth domains independently verify
(1) and (2); no higher initial input bit can enter these target cones.

coordinate_hypothesis_formula_source.heading: ## 2. Failure occurs on an actual singleton core
coordinate_hypothesis_formula_source.text:
## 2. Failure occurs on an actual singleton core

The core family used by the [exact center representation](RESULTS-p3-query-cone-rewrite.md)
includes

```text
C^5(0)=891,
891 --H--> 801 --H--> 889 --H--> 803 --H--> 891.
```

Every state in this cycle has bit two equal to zero. Take `j=1` in (2).
After four steps its bit one is 1, whereas the prediction without the
residual is

```text
bit1(891) XOR bit9(891) = 1 XOR 1 = 0.
```

The missing term is `bit5(891) AND NOT bit7(891)=1`.
This rejects the proposed doubling rule even when its single zero-driver
corridor persists forever. The witness is a value of an actual initial
C-headed query core; the claim being refuted is a row identity at the
specified column.

There can be no finite upper bound on a corridor's length based only on
the finite width above it. Already the smaller actual core has

```text
C^2(0)=12,       12 --H--> 13 --H--> 12.
```

Its width is four and bit one stays zero forever. These are exact closed
cycles, not finite observations extrapolated to arbitrary time.

Even the two-step law needs its chronological guard. Input9 starts with
bit one zero, but H(9)=15 has that bit one. The unguarded two-step formula
predicts1 while H^2(9)=12 has bit zero equal to0.

## 2. Operational convention for this repository

Until the organizers clarify the predicate, this repository uses the
narrative falsification target:

```text
exhibit one uniform correct machine with T(n)=o(n).
```

That is the conservative meaning used by the binary-kernel, observational
quotient, support-set, and Hashlife probes.  A measured exponent below two but
above one is only a speedup over naive spacetime simulation; it is not a P3
answer.  A `Theta(n)` construction would be important and would contradict
the displayed formal predicate, but it would not be reported as a prize
solution without a ruling from the organizers.

For a positive lower-bound result, the manuscript must choose one of `(A)` or
`(B)` and prove it in the stated Turing-machine model.  Neither arbitrary-row
decision-tree depth nor the size of one derivation system establishes either
predicate for the fixed sequence `n -> c_n`.

coordinate_hypothesis_formula_source.heading: ## 6. Erratum: Lemma 5's general-`k` formula is off by a `k`-dependent constant
coordinate_hypothesis_formula_source.text:
## 6. Erratum: Lemma 5's general-`k` formula is off by a `k`-dependent constant

Lemma 5 states, for `F` a `k`-fold composition of `H` with `X_1^F = X_1^H`:
`X_{kn-1}^H = X_n^F`. Take `k=1`: `F=H` trivially, so the claim reduces to
`X_{n-1}^H = X_n^H`, which is false for evolving `H`. The correct relation,
matching the paper's own generation convention ("`X_n` denotes the
configuration after `n-1` applications... beyond the initial configuration,"
§2) and its own worked `k=2` proof (Eq. 9: `X_3^H = X_2^G`), is

```
X_{k(n-1)+1}^H = X_n^F
```

This coincides with the printed `kn-1` exactly at `k=2` (`k(n-1)+1 = 2n-1 =
kn-1` only when `k=2`), which is the case Lemma 3 derives it from; the
general-`k` statement in Lemma 5 appears to carry that special case forward
without adjusting the additive constant. The §3 numerical check (45 trials,
`k=1..5`) confirms the corrected formula and refutes the printed one for
`k≠2`.

This is cosmetic. Theorem 8 and Corollary 9 do not depend on the exact
alignment constant — they only need *some* fixed offset, bounded by `k`, to
translate `H`'s target generation into a count of `F`-steps, and reaching a
generation not exactly on that offset costs at most `k-1` extra naive `O(n)`
steps, i.e. `O(n log n)`, absorbed into the `O(n²/log n)` bound. The
complexity results are unaffected.

# Characterization: Natal & Al-saadi, "Fast Simulation of Cellular Automata by Self-Composition"

Date: 2026-09-13

Primary source: Joseph Natal, Oleksiy Al-saadi, arXiv:2409.07065v2 (submitted
2024-09-11, revised 2025-06-22), cs.CC, CC BY 4.0. Full text and HTML retrieved
directly; not a self-published or unreviewed target — normal arXiv revision
history, standard theorem/lemma structure.

This is a characterization, not a refutation. The construction and its proofs
are checked and found correct (with one minor, non-load-bearing indexing slip
in Lemma 5, isolated in §6). The question this audit answers is what the
result actually establishes and how it relates to P3, not whether it is wrong.

**Correction from the subsequent P3 investigation, 2026-09-13.** The earlier
version called this bound a generic simulation "ceiling." That was not
justified. [Two-dimensional macroblock tabulation](RESULTS-p3-macroblocks.md)
gives `O(n²/log² n)` word-RAM time, including table construction; the
tabulation principle already appears in Grandjean and Jachiet,
[arXiv:2206.13851v2, §8.2 and Appendix 11](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2206.13851v2).
The claims of a generic ceiling are corrected below. This does not refute
Natal and Al-saadi's upper bound or supply a sublinear P3 algorithm.

definitions_and_conventions.heading: ## Verdict
definitions_and_conventions.text:
## Verdict

The paper proves a genuine, correct **logarithmic-factor time
speedup** for computing an entire generation-`n` configuration of *any*
one-dimensional 2-color CA, at the cost of asymptotically **more** space than
naive simulation, not less. It does not claim to touch any Rule 30 prize
problem, and does not: the P3 connection is entirely external framing, absent
from the paper's own introduction, contributions, and discussion. Under the
paper's own declared model of computation, the same O(n²/log n) time bound is
already implied by standard bit-parallel word-RAM simulation — the technique
already implemented in this repository's own `center_column.py` — at
asymptotically less space. Its self-composition construction is a valid
alternative way to obtain that upper bound. The theorem does not prove
optimality, and a generic block-table construction improves the bound as
explained in the correction above. Neither construction supplies a Rule 30

records.t: Conditional logarithmic lower bound on lone-seed zero-set mismatches
records.st: If the lone-seed centre column c has period P after time T_0, then every interval [T,2T+P-1] with T>=T_0 contains a time t at which c_t=0 and r_(t+P)!=r_t, so along the disjoint intervals given by T_(k+1)=2T_k+P, that is T_k=2^k(T_0+P)-P, the number of such zero-set mismatches up to time N is at least log_2 N - O(1), with the constant depending on T_0 and P. records.sc: The implication is proved; the premise is exactly the negation of P1 and is not. It combines the finite-interval mismatch bound with the period-shifted centre equation l_(t+P) XOR l_t = (1-c_t)(r_(t+P) XOR r_t) for t>=T_0. The consequence is stronger than saying the neighbour cannot become P-periodic, since it forces mismatches inside prescribed intervals. An upper bound o(log N) at some period multiple would contradict it, and such a bound would still permit infinitely many mismatches; none is known, and this restatement is not asserted to be logically easier than P1. records.t: Exact error budget for independently driven halves: M_P(N) + 2G(N+P) is at least logarithmic

records.t: At a rational frequency an eventually periodic trace has bounded or linear sums
records.st: Let s_t be bounded and eventually periodic and let alpha = p/q be rational. records.st: Put omega = exp(-2*pi*i/3), s_t = (-1)^c_t on the Rule 30 singleton centre and F_k = sum_(0<=t<4^k) s_t*omega^t. If 3^(-k)*F_k -> L != 0, then along N = 4^k the sums have size N^(log_4(3)), which is unbounded, while F_k/4^k -> 0. The rational-frequency dichotomy excludes both behaviours together for every eventually periodic centre, so the limit would prove P1.

It gives neither P2 nor a P3 algorithm: the normalized coefficient at frequency one third tends to zero along these scales rather than to a coherent line. The hypothesis is unproved; the Thue-Morse unnormalized amplitude 3^(m/2) at length 2^m is established context (Baake, Grimm and Nilsson), not a property shown to survive the residual. source_context.heading: 1. Eventually periodic sequences have bounded-or-linear rational sums

records.t: Exact four-adic recurrence F_(k+1) = 3*F_k + D_k for the residual variation
records.st: With tau_t = (-1)^theta(t), b_t = (-1)^R_t for t>=1 and b_0 = -1, so that s_t = tau_t*b_t for every t>=0, define delta_n = b_(4n) - omega*b_(4n+1) - omega^2*b_(4n+2) + b_(4n+3) - 3*b_n and D_k = sum_(n<4^k) tau_n*omega^n*delta_n. Then tau at the four children equals tau_n*(1,-1,-1,1), omega^(4n) = omega^n and 1-omega-omega^2+1 = 3, so F_(k+1) = 3*F_k + D_k and 3^(-k)*F_k = b_0 + sum_(j<k) D_j/3^(j+1).
records.sc: An exact identity with no approximation, independence assumption, limiting measure or P1/P2 hypothesis. records.t: Nonvanishing at four-adic endpoints is automatic and carries no lower bound
records.st: For any binary sign sequence and N = 4^k, write the three residue sums as A_0, A_1, A_2, so that F_k = (A_0-A_2) + (A_1-A_2)*omega. For k >= 1 the numbers of terms in these sums have parities even, odd, odd, and every sign is odd, so the first Eisenstein coefficient is odd and the second even; the same parities hold at k = 0. Therefore F_k is never zero and |F_k| >= 1, for every binary input sequence whatsoever.

records.t: Classification of the bounded one-sided linear spatial weights
records.st: Let (Lx)_j = x_(j-1)+x_j+x_(j+1) and seek complex w with w_j = 0 for j <= 0 solving (L - lambda*I)w = delta_0, the condition that the linear contribution to P_w(Fx) - lambda*P_w(x) isolate x_0 for P_w(x) = sum_(j>=1) w_j*x_j. This forces w_0 = 0, w_1 = 1 and w_(j+1) = (lambda-1)*w_j - w_(j-1). The solution is bounded iff lambda is real with -1 < lambda < 3, where writing lambda = 1+2*cos(theta) with 0 < theta < pi gives the unique w_j = sin(j*theta)/sin(theta). At the endpoints lambda = 3 and lambda = -1 the solutions are j and (-1)^(j-1)*j respectively; outside, the two characteristic roots have product one and neither is unimodular, since a unit-modulus root would force lambda-1 = r+r^(-1) real in [-2,2], so (r_+^j - r_-^j)/(r_+ - r_-) has a growing term.
records.sc: A classification of the one-sided weights of this one algebraic equation, stated without complex conjugation. Boundedness matters only for applying the extraction to an infinite row or obtaining a bounded functional; the finite-row identity holds at every lambda. The document calls this an elementary extension of the archive's quarter-wave identity and claims no literature novelty. records.t: Thue-Morse at frequency one third is an exact enhanced peak with vanishing normalized amplitude
records.st: For the standard Thue-Morse signs a_t = (-1)^popcount(t), the doubling recurrence gives the exact finite Fourier polynomial sum_(t<2^m) a_t*z^t = product_(j<m) (1 - z^(2^j)). At z = exp(-2*pi*i/3) every factor has modulus sqrt(3), so the unnormalized sum has modulus 3^(m/2) and the normalized coefficient satisfies |C_(2^m)(1/3)| = (sqrt(3)/2)^m -> 0.
records.sc: A statement about the Thue-Morse sign sequence, not about the Rule 30 centre. It is a useful intermediate control between square-root cancellation and a persistent line. The Rule 30 residual can change the contribution and the identity does not transfer this scaling to the centre: at N = 2^20 the measured centre amplitude at 1/3 is 0.00160046 against the Thue-Morse control's 0.05631351. The source is dated 2026-09-15, was read 2026-09-16, and is untracked in the working tree, as are its probe and artifacts.
records.nt: The probe's Thue-Morse third control, 0.056313514710373484, agrees with the exact product value 0.056313514709472594 = (3/4)^10 at m = 20; both were read from fundamental-frequency-audit.json. The same object appears in r30-tfs-scaled-limit-target-proves-p1 under the unnormalized amplitude 3^(m/2), which is this one multiplied by 2^m; the exact seed decomposition 0081391386ad06b3 is the reason the sequence is relevant at all.

source_context.heading: 3. A real peak need not be a fundamental line

records.t: Elementary frequency-perturbation bound on the normalized coefficient
records.st: For a bounded sign sequence and a frequency perturbation delta, |C_N(alpha+delta) - C_N(alpha)| <= pi*(N-1)*|delta|. At the largest sample N = 1,048,576, one standard uncertainty of the 2022 CODATA dimensionless fine-structure value 0.0072973525643, namely 1.1e-12, therefore changes the coefficient by at most 3.623615e-06.
records.sc: Elementary continuity of a finite sum in its frequency. It certifies only that the tabulated fine-structure entry is insensitive to the constant's stated uncertainty; it does not make the candidate meaningful. Constants are read as cycles per update with no rescaling, reciprocal or phase fitted, and dimensionful constants such as the speed of light fix no frequency at all, since bare Rule 30 supplies no seconds per update or metres per cell. The source is dated 2026-09-15, was read 2026-09-16, and is untracked in the working tree, as are its probe and artifacts.
records.nt: The numerical bound is the artifact's fine_structure_amplitude_error_bound_one_standard_uncertainty, 3.623615068411709e-06. The CODATA source cited is https://physics.nist.gov/cuu/pdf/all.pdf.

source_context.heading: 4. Fixed candidates and held-out blocks

records.t: Summable bilateral Green function at every lambda off the real interval [-1,3]
records.st: Let (Lx)_j = x_(j-1)+x_j+x_(j+1) on the full integer line. For lambda outside the real interval [-1,3], r + r^(-1) = lambda-1 has exactly one root r with rho = |r| < 1: the two roots have product one, and a unimodular root would force lambda real in [-1,3]. With C = 1/(r - r^(-1)) and w_j = C*r^|j|, (L - lambda*I)w = delta_0 and W := ||w||_1 = |C|*(1+rho)/(1-rho) is finite. This w is the unique bounded bilateral solution, since the difference of two such solutions is homogeneous and boundedness toward each end kills one of the two characteristic roots. For nonreal lambda there is also W <= 2/|Im(lambda)|, from the imaginary parts of r+r^(-1) and r-r^(-1) with (1+rho)^2/(1+rho^2) <= 2. In particular this covers every lambda = exp(2*pi*i*alpha) with alpha neither an integer nor a half-integer.
records.sc: Algebra of one linear equation, stated with no complex conjugation in the pairing. It is the bilateral counterpart of the one-sided classification, which has no summable solution at a nonreal lambda, and its point is a bounded functional on arbitrary binary rows; it supplies no estimate of the nonlinear current and no statement about Rule 30. Both real unit frequencies are excluded. The source is dated 2026-09-16, was read 2026-09-16, and is untracked in the working tree, as are its audit, probe and both JSON artifacts.
records.nt: The source equation and the W formula were re-checked in this review in exact Gaussian-rational arithmetic at ten decaying rational roots over |j| <= 12 (250 checks), the l1 norm against the summed weights at 41 sampled unit frequencies, and W*|Im(lambda)| <= 2 over a 3,999-point unit-circle sweep with worst observed value 1.99999969. Those are checks of the printed formulas at sampled lambda rather than of the uniqueness argument, which was read and is correct as printed, so no independent reproduction is claimed. The document's own audit uses eight rational roots whose lambdas need not be unimodular, which is deliberate: they test the general identities, not the unit-frequency endpoint bound.

source_context.heading: 1. The exponentially decaying Green function

records.t: Exact bilateral current identity with uniform potential and current bounds
records.st: For a binary row x take the local nonlinear defect D_j(x) = x_j*x_(j+1) + 2*x_(j-1)*x_j + 2*x_(j-1)*(1-x_j)*x_(j+1), so that (Fx)_j = (Lx)_j - D_j(x) and 0 <= D_j <= 3, and put P_lambda(x) = sum_j w_j*x_j and K_lambda(x) = sum_j w_j*D_j(x) for the summable bilateral weights. Both sums converge absolutely for every binary row, including rows of infinite support, with |P_lambda(x)| <= W and |K_lambda(x)| <= 3W, and x_0 = P_lambda(Fx) - lambda*P_lambda(x) + K_lambda(x) holds exactly, absolute convergence being what justifies shifting indices in the linear term.
records.sc: What is new against the one-sided and quarter-wave identities is only the absolute convergence for every binary row, infinite support included, and the uniform bounds W and 3W; the one-sided record cannot state either, its weights being unbounded off [-1,3]. The defect is the same object as the quarter-wave current's q, under D_j = q_(j-1) and K_lambda = sum_i w_(i+1)*q_i. The identity supplies no estimate of the nonlinear term, which is the unresolved object. The source is dated 2026-09-16, was read 2026-09-16, and is untracked in the working tree, as are its audit, probe and both JSON artifacts.
records.nt: Re-derived in this review from the integer expansion and re-checked in exact Gaussian-rational arithmetic on all 8,190 binary rows of length 1 through 12 -- that is the recorded sample size -- at every origin and at six decaying rational roots, 737,244 checks with zero mismatches. The document's own 1,024 seven-bit cases were not rerun. The infinite-support half of the statement is not a finite check; it follows from 0 <= D_j <= 3 and the summability of w.

source_context.heading: 2. Exact current and finite-radius approximation

records.t: Uniform exponential truncation bound for the bilateral potential and current
records.st: For an integer R >= 0 truncate the P and K sums to |j| <= R and put E_R = 2*|C|*rho^(R+1)/(1-rho). Uniformly over all binary rows, |P_lambda - P_(lambda,R)| <= E_R and |K_lambda - K_(lambda,R)| <= 3*E_R. The truncated current reads only the sites -R-1,...,R+1.
records.sc: Exponential in R and uniform in the row. The full current is an exponentially weighted sum of local three-cell charges, not a fixed finite-window observable, and the truncation supplies no closed dynamics for the cells it reads. The source is dated 2026-09-16, was read 2026-09-16, and is untracked in the working tree, as are its audit, probe and both JSON artifacts.
records.nt: The tail was re-summed in this review at six decaying roots and R in {0, 1, 5, 12} and never exceeds E_R.

source_context.heading: 2. Exact current and finite-radius approximation

records.t: Telescoped transfer of the centre Fourier average to the nonlinear current
records.st: Fix a nonreal unit lambda, let x^t be any actual Rule 30 orbit, and write c_t = x^t_0, P_t = P_lambda(x^t), K_t = K_lambda(x^t). For every N >= 1 the identity telescopes exactly to sum_(0<=t<N) lambda^(-t)*(c_t - K_t) = lambda^(1-N)*P_N - lambda*P_0. After division by N the error is at most 2W/N, and at most (W+|C|)/N for the singleton initial row, where P_0 = C. Hence the centre and current Fourier averages have the same limit whenever either limit exists, and their finite averages differ by O_lambda(1/N).
records.sc: An exact reformulation transferring the centre question to the nonlinear current at a fixed frequency. No existence and no vanishing of either limit is proved, and the current stays nonlinear and dependent on the actual orbit. It applies only off the two real unit frequencies, where the uniform potential bound fails. The source is dated 2026-09-16, was read 2026-09-16, and is untracked in the working tree, as are its audit, probe and both JSON artifacts.
records.nt: The telescope was re-checked in this review on the true singleton orbit at alpha = 1/3 through N = 256, residual 4.4e-14 against endpoint terms of order one, with P_0 = C exactly. That is a floating-point spot check of the finite identity, not of the limiting statement, so no independent reproduction is claimed.

source_context.heading: 3. Fourier coefficients reduce to the current with a bounded endpoint

records.t: Explicit unnormalized estimate for the signed centre sum against a truncated current
records.st: With signs chi_t = 2*c_t-1, signed current J_t = 2*K_t-1 and its truncation J_(R,t) = 2*K_(lambda,R)(x^t)-1, the endpoint of the telescope doubles and combining it with the truncation bound gives |sum_(t<N) lambda^(-t)*(chi_t - J_(R,t))| <= 4W + 6*N*E_R = 4W + 12*N*|C|*rho^(R+1)/(1-rho).
records.sc: This removes a growing endpoint at fixed frequency. It does not make the nonlinear current independent of the centre or of the seed history and supplies no cancellation estimate for that current; at fixed R the second term grows linearly in N, so the radius must grow with N for the estimate to say anything. The source is dated 2026-09-16, was read 2026-09-16, and is untracked in the working tree, as are its audit, probe and both JSON artifacts.
records.nt: The sign convention is chi_t = 2*c_t-1, matching r30-ffs-normalized-coefficient-periodic-vanishing and the negative of the third-frequency cluster's (-1)^c_t.

source_context.heading: 3. Fourier coefficients reduce to the current with a bounded endpoint

records.t: No summable bilateral Green function at either real unit frequency
records.st: At lambda = 1 the characteristic roots are i and -i. Bounded Green functions exist, for instance w_j = (1/2)*sin(pi*|j|/2), every solution differing from it by a combination of the global sine and cosine modes, but none decays to zero at both ends and none is summable, so the uniform all-row potential bound is unavailable there. At lambda = -1 the repeated characteristic root is -1, a particular Green function is w_j = -(1/2)*|j|*(-1)^j, every other solution adds (-1)^j*(A+B*j), and no choice removes linear growth at both ends, so there is no bounded bilateral Green function at all. Neither endpoint is covered by the summable construction.
records.sc: About these two frequencies and this weight family only. It says nothing about the centre's spectrum at alpha = 0 or alpha = 1/2; what it establishes is that the telescoped transfer does not reach those two frequencies, which is why the zero-frequency approach has to be attempted through a limit. The source is dated 2026-09-16, was read 2026-09-16, and is untracked in the working tree, as are its audit, probe and both JSON artifacts.
records.nt: Both printed endpoint Green functions were re-checked in this review over |j| <= 12 and satisfy their source equations. The archive's one-sided quarter-wave weight is the other bounded nonsummable solution at lambda = 1, as the document notes.

source_context.heading: 4. The two real unit-frequency endpoints

records.t: The two uniform zero-frequency estimates vanish in opposite regimes
records.st: As real alpha -> 0 through nonzero values the decaying root satisfies rho = 1 - pi*|alpha| + O(alpha^2) and |C| -> 1/2, so W ~ 1/(pi*|alpha|), the root approaching -i for positive alpha and i for negative alpha. The universal normalized endpoint estimate therefore has order 1/(N*|alpha|) and vanishes when N*|alpha| -> infinity, while the signed centre average obeys |S_N(alpha) - S_N(0)| <= pi*(N-1)*|alpha|, which vanishes in the opposite regime N*|alpha| -> 0. These two sufficient uniform estimates cannot simultaneously vanish.
records.sc: A limitation of combining these two particular estimates, not a no-go theorem: not for the singleton, not for improved endpoint estimates, not for cancellations, and not for a different approach to zero frequency. The zero-frequency current estimate of the quarter-wave route remains unresolved, so this yields no progress on P2. The source is dated 2026-09-16, was read 2026-09-16, and is untracked in the working tree, as are its audit, probe and both JSON artifacts.
records.nt: The continuity estimate is r30-ffs-frequency-perturbation-continuity-bound at alpha = 0 and is cited rather than re-extracted. The asymptotics were recomputed in this review at the artifact's five alphas and reproduce its columns to 1e-12: (1-rho)/(pi*|alpha|) rises from 0.7516256179197767 at alpha = 0.125 to 0.9999760300183805 at alpha = 1.52587890625e-05, |C| to 0.49999999942551343, and pi*|alpha|*W to 1.0000000009574095.

source_context.heading: 5. Approaching zero frequency does not recover P2 from these bounds alone

records.t: A logarithmic spatial radius preserves a chosen sublinear Fourier scale
records.st: At a fixed nonreal unit frequency set kappa = -log(rho) > 0. For 0 < beta < 1 the unnormalized signed estimate is o(N^beta) provided R_N >= ((1-beta)/kappa)*log(N) + omega(1), so any fixed positive extra multiple of log(N) suffices and a logarithmically growing spatial window approximates the signed Fourier sum to that accuracy.
records.sc: An approximation statement about the window, not a spectral-growth or cancellation theorem. The window still contains an increasing number of cells and supplies no closed dynamics for their current, and neither it nor the third-frequency scale identity supplies the growth bound that the conditional P1 criterion is missing. The source is dated 2026-09-16, was read 2026-09-16, and is untracked in the working tree, as are its audit, probe and both JSON artifacts.
records.nt: The alpha = 1/3 calibration was read from bilateral-frequency-current-audit.json and recomputed here from the characteristic equation, matching to 1e-15: rho = 0.5806918319929524, |C| = 0.5266403878479265, W = 1.985308713220264, a signed-current tail at radius 30 of 7.252359461155095e-07, which is below 1e-6 and reads radius 31, and log(4/3)/kappa = 0.5292796859082326 as the coefficient of k for N = 4^k at beta = log(3)/log(4), so a coefficient such as 0.530 suffices. The scale identity referred to is r30-tfs-scaled-limit-target-proves-p1.

source_context.heading: 6. Logarithmic radius preserves a chosen sublinear Fourier scale

records.t: Exact optimal spatial decay rate within the unit-frequency Green family
records.st: Write r = a+i*b and t = |r|^2 < 1. The unit-modulus constraint |1+r+r^(-1)| = 1 simplifies to 4*a^2 + 2*(t+1)*a + (t-1)^2 = 0, whose discriminant requires -3*t^2+10*t-3 >= 0 and hence t >= 1/3. Equality occurs precisely at the conjugate pair r_* = (-1-i*sqrt(2))/3, lambda_* = (-1+2*i*sqrt(2))/3, C_* = (1+2*i*sqrt(2))/6, rho_* = 1/sqrt(3), alpha_* = acos(-1/3)/(2*pi) = 0.3040867..., and their conjugates. This frequency therefore optimizes the spatial decay rate of the extraction kernel.
records.sc: Optimality of the kernel, not of Rule 30: alpha_* is the cheapest frequency to read with this family of Green functions, and no optimization of a measured centre amplitude or of all finite-radius prefactors is asserted. Nothing predicts that the centre column carries energy there. The source is dated 2026-09-16, was read 2026-09-16, and is untracked in the working tree, as are its audit, probe and both JSON artifacts.
records.nt: Re-derived and re-checked in this review in exact Q(i*sqrt(2)) arithmetic, independently of the document's audit: r_* gives lambda_* and C_* exactly as printed, |r_*|^2 = 1/3, |lambda_*| = 1, and lambda_* + lambda_*^(-1) = -2/3, and (a,t) = (-1/3,1/3) is an exact root of the quadratic. The reduction to that quadratic was separately confirmed on a 20,000-point sweep of the unit-lambda curve, where it holds to 1e-9 and the minimum of |r|^2 is 0.3333333341 at alpha = 0.6959, the conjugate frequency, against 1 - acos(-1/3)/(2*pi) = 0.6959132760153037.

source_context.heading: 7. An optimal localization frequency, not an identified centre tone

records.t: A nonzero limiting centre coefficient at the optimal frequency would rule out eventual periodicity
records.st: alpha_* is irrational: otherwise lambda_* would be a root of unity, making lambda_* + lambda_*^(-1) = -2/3 a rational algebraic integer. A nonzero limiting centre Fourier coefficient at alpha_* would therefore rule out eventual periodicity of the centre, since every eventually periodic sequence has zero Fourier average at an irrational frequency by a finite geometric-series calculation, and the telescoped identity transfers that conditional target to the nonlinear current.
records.sc: Conditional and one-directional. No nonzero coefficient and no limiting centre tone is established here, and a null or small coefficient at any finite horizon excludes nothing about the infinite orbit. It is the optimal-frequency instance of the general irrational-line criterion, not a new criterion. The source is dated 2026-09-16, was read 2026-09-16, and is untracked in the working tree, as are its audit, probe and both JSON artifacts.
records.nt: The arithmetic the irrationality rests on, lambda_* + lambda_*^(-1) = -2/3, was confirmed exactly in the same Q(i*sqrt(2)) check as r30-bfc-optimal-localization-frequency; the conditional itself is a reading of the argument and is not reproduced.

source_context.heading: 7. An optimal localization frequency, not an identified centre tone

records.t: The preregistered kill condition fires at the optimal frequency on 2^29 cached centre bits
records.st: With the statistic S_N = mean_(t<N) (2*c_t-1)*exp(-2*pi*i*alpha_*t) and the kill and positive conditions fixed before the run, the ladder of 18 dyadic prefixes 2^12 through 2^29 of the cached centre column keeps sqrt(N)*|S_N| in [0.2798, 0.9560], mean 0.6545 and median 0.6616, against the Rayleigh reference for an incoherent sign sequence, mean sqrt(pi)/2 = 0.8862 and median sqrt(log 2) = 0.8326; the log-log slope of |S_N| is -0.5233, where -0.5 is exact cancellation and 0 a coherent line. At the horizon sqrt(N)*|S_N| is 0.9380 for the centre against 2.1534 for the seeded random +-1 control, and the binary oscillator at the same frequency gives 0.6366197730, matching 2/pi. The preregistered kill condition fired.
records.sc: A finite diagnostic at one derived, unfitted frequency, measuring this horizon only. The nested prefixes are not independent of one another, the control is a calibration and not a statistical rejection rule, and nothing here is an absence theorem for a line at alpha_* or a statement about the infinite orbit. The source is dated 2026-09-16 and was read 2026-09-16. It was untracked when the claims were extracted; it, its probe and its JSON artifact are tracked in the repository as of this review.
records.nt: Every figure was recomputed in this review from the artifact's stored per-rung coefficients: the range, the mean 0.6545388528229192, the slope -0.5232608436553312, and both horizon controls. The median recorded here, 0.6615574797900741, is the conventional median of the 18 values. The document originally printed 0.693, their upper median and tenth order statistic, beside a conventional mean; that inconsistency was corrected in the source on 2026-09-16 and the document now prints 0.662. The coefficients themselves were not recomputed. Two cross-checks the document reports: the nine rungs shared with the 2^20 probe reproduce exactly under this script's different implementation, chunked accumulation with exact dyadic starting phases rather than one whole-array pass. The cache is the Wolfram Data Repository billion-bit centre column, payload offset 239, 536,870,912 bits with used-payload sha256 c46e9665...; 1,048,576 of them are re-derived from the singleton seed by packed 64-bit row evolution cell by cell against the cache, alongside the helper's 8,192-bit big-integer check and its 257-bit scalar check. The remaining 511/512 of the horizon is not independently recomputed and the document names that provenance gap, not the arithmetic, as the dominant risk: regenerating 2^29 centre bits is an O(T^2) evolution.

records.t: A single thresholded oscillator cannot generate the Rule 30 centre column at any frequency
records.st: The model c_t = 1{cos(2*pi*alpha*t + beta) >= q}, with alpha, beta and q arbitrary real constants, cannot generate the Rule 30 singleton centre column, for any choice of those constants and with no frequency fitting or numerical approximation to alpha. More generally let c_t = g(theta + t*alpha mod 1), where g is binary and constant on the arcs left by removing at most two boundary points from the circle, with arbitrary values permitted at those points. For a length-m block the m translates of the boundary set have at most 2m distinct points; between them every coordinate of the block is constant, so k > 0 distinct points give k open arcs and k singleton boundary cells and at most 2k <= 4m distinct blocks, while no boundary points give a single block. Rational rotation rates, coincident boundaries and threshold equality do not increase the bound. The first 29 Rule 30 centre bits, 11011100110001011001001110101, contain 21 distinct length-five blocks, and 21 > 4*5 = 20, so this finite prefix contradicts the model at every alpha, beta and q. Under the consistent half-open [a,b) convention every boundary takes the block value of the arc immediately to its right even when boundaries coincide, sharpening the bound to p(m) <= 2m, and the first 15 centre bits already contain all eight triples against 2*3 = 6. The 29-bit certificate has margin 1 and needs no endpoint convention; the 15-bit one has margin 2 but does. All 32 length-five blocks occur by prefix length 120.
records.sc: An exact exclusion of one specified model class, not a prize result. It does not exclude a representation beginning after an unknown transient, a more complicated observation of a rotation, an arbitrary formula involving mathematical constants, a general finite union of arcs, or a nonlinear digit formula; and it is not a finite-prefix proof of centre nonperiodicity, of density one half, or of any computational lower bound. The counting bound and both witnesses concern formulas valid from time zero. The source is dated 2026-09-15, was read 2026-09-16, and is untracked in the working tree, as are its verifier and JSON artifact.
records.nt: Every witness figure was recomputed in this review from a third generator independent of both in the shipped script, a numpy boolean row evolved as roll(x,1) XOR (x OR roll(x,-1)) rather than the scalar truth table or the packed integer: the 29-bit prefix matches character for character, and the counts 21 length-five blocks in 29 bits, 8 triples in 15 bits, 32 length-five blocks in 120 bits, 248 length-eight blocks in 1024 bits, and the first-occurrence horizons 15, 29 and 120 all reproduce exactly. The bound p(m) <= 4m was checked by hand, not machine-verified; a 4,978-model sweep of the thresholded oscillator itself, including small-denominator rational alpha and q at exactly +-1 and just outside [-1,1], reached at most p(5) = 10 and p(3) = 6, consistent with the 4m bound and saturating the sharper 2m bound at m = 3. Related but not prerequisites: ceb0bf38188a55ec is the formal-power-series analogue over F_2, and 31efc53c3c3878d9 and 1c4c4611d8c4a0ca carry the Morse-Hedlund criterion and the measured factor complexity; 1c4c4611d8c4a0ca reports p(8) = 256 on a 200,000-bit prefix against this artifact's 248 on 1,024 bits, which is consistent rather than conflicting, since complexity is nondecreasing in prefix length and 2^8 = 256 is the ceiling. The artifact also records a finite-union extension, at least 8 arcs with arbitrary endpoints and at least 16 consistently half-open, from the 248 length-eight blocks; the arithmetic is correct but the document asserts it nowhere, so it is not extracted.

source_context.heading: 1. A precise version of the frequency proposal

records.t: Encoding the centre column as a real constant supplies neither P1 nor P2
records.st: Every binary sequence can be encoded as a real constant, and for the Rule 30 singleton centre column this is R_30 = sum_(t >= 0) c_t * 2^(-(t+1)). P1 is then exactly equivalent to irrationality of that particular number, and P2 is a statement about the limiting proportion of its binary digits equal to one. Defining the constant establishes neither property. Likewise, identifying the digits of some independently defined constant with c_t would still require a proof of the identification, together with a separate account of the relevant digit properties and of the computation costs.
records.sc: A restatement of the two prize problems in terms of one encoding, not progress on either. The same section separately observes that Rule 30 assigns no physical duration or distance to its cells and updates, so a frequency in hertz requires an additional choice of seconds per update and dimensionful physical constants do not determine a frequency for the bare automaton; a dimensionless constant could occur in a proposed identity, but the identity would still require a derivation. That observation is recorded here rather than extracted separately, since nothing cites it alone. The source is dated 2026-09-15, was read 2026-09-16, and is untracked in the working tree, as are its verifier and JSON artifact.
records.nt: The equivalence is the standard base-2 fact that a real number is rational exactly when its binary expansion is eventually periodic, applied to the centre column. Related but not a prerequisite: ceb0bf38188a55ec states the formal-power-series analogue over F_2, rationality of A(z) with Q(0) != 0 being equivalent to eventual periodicity of the coefficients; that is a different statement from irrationality of the real number R_30, and neither implies the other as recorded.

source_context.heading: 2. Physical units and constants that encode a sequence

records.t: Actual-seed window collisions exclude every time-independent local boundary correction at radius at most five
records.st: Let W_r(t) = x^t[-r,...,r] on the lone-seed orbit and consider the time-independent boundary correction K_t - rho = h(W_r(t+1)) - lambda*h(W_r(t)), with h an arbitrary complex-valued function on the finite window state space and lambda, rho arbitrary complex constants; h is necessarily bounded, but the argument uses no bound on its magnitude and no polynomial ansatz. No h, lambda and rho satisfy that identity at all seed times for any radius r <= 5. At radius 5, times 20 and 31 share the window 11000001111 before and 00100011000 after, while K_20 = -1 and K_31 = 1; at radius 2, times 29 and 41 share 00101 before and 11101 after, while K_29 = -1 and K_41 = -4. Identical windows force identical right sides, and the left sides differ, so the identity fails; restricting both identical windows to a smaller radius preserves the contradiction. The exclusion covers every lambda, including every proposed unit-modulus temporal multiplier, and in particular the case lambda = 1, rho = 1/2 that would absorb the centred current into a temporal difference.
records.sc: Exact finite counterexamples on the actual lone-seed orbit, excluding precisely the displayed window classes and the time ranges containing the witness pairs. They leave open a larger or growing window, additional history or ancestry, a later-onset identity, a sum of local correction terms over the growing half-row, a nonlocal or growing potential, and a nonzero residual that cancels on average; none of those is supplied with a successful correction here. Nothing about P1, P2 or P3 follows. The source is dated 2026-09-16, was read 2026-09-16, and is untracked in the working tree, as are its verifier and JSON artifact.
records.nt: Recomputed in this review from a third generator independent of both in the shipped verifier, a set of occupied sites stepped by the literal neighbourhood test rather than a truth-table lookup or a packed-integer shift. Reproduced exactly: the 43-bit centre prefix 1101110011000101100100111010111001110101011, both window pairs before and after, all four currents, the four potentials -1/0, 0/-1, -1/1 and -4/1, and the clock phases. The potential/current identity c_t = P_(t+1)-P_t+K_t was re-checked on all 44 transitions through time 44 with no failure, and the q_i form of K agreed with the weighted multilinear defect form sum_(j>=1) sin(pi*j/2)*D_j on all 45 rows. The shipped verifier checks only these two specified witnesses, with no extended search, so neither the radius bound 5 nor the times are claimed minimal.

records.t: On a spatial ring the quarter-wave current is already a temporal coboundary
records.st: On a spatial ring of length L divisible by four, with P_L and K_L defined by the same phase weights on cyclic cells, the cutoff identity becomes 0 = P_L(Fx) - P_L(x) + K_L(x), because x_L = x_0. The bulk ring current is therefore already the temporal coboundary K_L = P_L - P_L o F, and its sum on every temporal cycle is zero. Removing that current with the correction -P_L simply erases the observable and yields no centre-column estimate, so a meaningful correction must retain the centre or boundary contribution and control the corrected potential.
records.sc: An observation about the ring, explaining why an unqualified torus test of the correction is vacuous; it substitutes a different periodic origin for the actual seed and so says nothing about the lone-seed orbit, where the collisions are established instead. The source is dated 2026-09-16, was read 2026-09-16, and is untracked in the working tree, as are its verifier and JSON artifact.
records.nt: The ring identity was re-derived and checked here on 6,368 rows with zero failures: exhaustively on all 2^L rows for L = 4, 8 and 12, and on 2,000 random rows at L in {16, 20, 24, 40}. The vanishing of the left side, rather than a centre bit, is exactly the cancellation the document describes.

source_context.heading: 3. Why an unqualified torus test misses the issue

records.t: Exact binary-kernel cardinality of a monomial power sequence
records.st: Under the convention that the state count of a sequence is the cardinality of its full binary kernel, for every r>=0 the exact kernel of the monomial x^(2^r) is the set {x^(2^r), x^(2^(r-1)), ..., x, 1, 0}, where 1 is the sequence supported only at index zero and 0 is the all-zero sequence, so its cardinality is exactly r+3. Equivalently |K_2(x^N)| = bit_length(N)+2 for every N>=1. The two Cartier operators send x^j to x^floor(j/2) in the matching parity and to zero in the other parity, which gives closure, reachability and distinctness of every listed state. This corrects the a20 report's claim that x^(2^(k-1)) has exactly k states.
records.sc: A statement about auxiliary automatic sequences over F_2 (monomials and their kernels) in the a20 report's stated convention, not about the Rule 30 centre sequence. It corrects an exact count only; it does not change Bridy's Proposition 2.13, the data-cost table, or the fidelity of a20's quotation of Example 2.14. It supplies no automaticity or nonautomaticity conclusion for Rule 30.
records.nt: The document reports an independent standard-library Cartier-closure check over all monomial exponents 1..4096 and the powers 2^r for 0<=r<=16, giving |K_2(x^N)|=bit_length(N)+2 (x^8 has six states). The proof is all-length; those finite checks are stated to be controls. No catalog record covers monomial kernel state counts (grep: no Bridy, no Ore-height monomial record).

records.t: Corrected exponential-height witness against a polynomial Ore-height bound
records.st: In the original report's inhomogeneous Ore convention the minimal Ore height of x^N is exactly N for every N>=1: if all coefficient degrees are less than N then the supports of the constant polynomial term and of the terms P_i(x) x^(N*2^i) lie in disjoint intervals, so no nonzero relation can cancel, and the relation x^N + F = 0 attains height N. Combined with the exact kernel cardinality, a correct exact witness against a bound polynomial in the state count is height 2^(k-3) with k states, for every k>=3. Exponential height is therefore necessary and the generic rejection of a polynomial Ore-height bound stands.
records.sc: Applies to the auxiliary monomial family x^N over F_2 in the stated inhomogeneous Ore convention, not to the Rule 30 centre sequence. It fixes the exact parameters of a witness whose qualitative conclusion (refutation of the generic 'Lemma L' height and order bounds) was already established elsewhere. It supplies no Rule-30-specific Ore order or height bound.

records.t: Nonautomaticity as a strictly stronger sufficient condition for P1
records.st: P1 asserts non-eventual-periodicity of the centre column. Its negation is eventual periodicity, which implies automaticity; the converse fails, since Thue-Morse is automatic and not eventually periodic. Hence nonautomaticity of the centre column is sufficient for P1 and is a strictly stronger target, and automaticity is not the negation of P1. Consequently assuming automaticity inside a contradiction argument is legitimate and not circular: either of the implications 'Automatic(c) => some Ore relation of order <= r0' together with the all-height statement S(r0), or 'Automatic(c) => some Ore relation of order <= r0 and height <= d0' together with the finite certificate S(r0,d0), would suffice for nonautomaticity.
records.sc: A logical scope correction to the a22 follow-up's claim that such conditional bounds are definitionally unavailable. The constants r0, d0 must still come from an independently proved Rule-30-specific argument; a finite certificate S(r0,d0) alone does not prove S(r0), and a bound growing without limit with unknown state count does not convert one finite certificate into an exclusion of all automatic models. This supports 'no such conditional bound obtained', not a logical impossibility theorem for conditional bounds, and it supplies no nonautomaticity proof.
records.nt: The same correction is restated in docs/rule30/AUDIT-entrypoint-overlooked-2026-09-15.md section 3, which defers to this document for detail. The document also states that the established Rule 30 finite rank certificates and the equivalences S(0) <=> P1 and all S(r) <=> nonautomaticity are unaffected.

records.t: The triangular-core-to-Collatz conjugacy carries only topological orbit data
records.st: Let H be the triangular core map with Phi(Hx) = Phi(x) >> 2 for a bijective 2-adic isometry Phi of Z_2, and let Q(x) = sum_i (T^i(x) mod 2) 2^i be the Lagarias-Bernstein parity-vector map, a measure-preserving homeomorphism of Z_2 with Q T Q^(-1) = S. Then J := Q^(-1) Phi satisfies J H J^(-1) = T^2 by transitivity of conjugacy alone, and J is determined only up to the centralizer of S^2. What J transfers is exactly Q(J(x)) = Phi(x): the base-4 itinerary of x under H is, symbol for symbol, the pairwise grouped Collatz parity vector of J(x), so period, preperiod and orbit closure transfer and nothing arithmetic about J(x) does. The reported value J(3) = -1 is the expected artifact and not a defect: H(3) = 3, Phi(3) = 3 * sum_t 4^t = -1, and T(-1) = -1, so a fixed point went to a fixed point; likewise the singleton seed in bit coordinates is x = 1 with H(1) = 1, Phi(1) = -1/3 whose bits 1,0,1,0,... are the parity vector of the trivial cycle {1,2}, giving J(1) = 1.
records.sc: Establishes existence and exact content of the conjugacy, not a transfer of any prize target. Nothing is preserved about the positive integers. J maps rationals to rationals, and is a bijection of the rationals exactly when Lagarias's Periodicity Conjecture holds, which is open. The route is recorded CLOSED as a transfer route; the audit does not itself work any residual obligation.

AMS 121 (1994) / Bernstein and Lagarias, Canad. J. Math. 48 (1996) eq. (1.3), (1.5). No catalog record mentions Collatz or parity vectors (grep count 0 for both).

records.t: Refutation of the proposed centre-column-to-Collatz-divergence conditional
records.st: The externally proposed conditional 'if the single-seed centre column is eventually periodic, then some positive integer has a Collatz orbit never reaching 1' cannot be derived from the conjugacy and fails for three independent reasons: (i) the only 2-adic point whose Collatz parity vector is the column is xi_30, which carries no seed information, since the seed's own image is J(1) = 1 and no relation between the column's preimage x_c and the seed data C^(h+1)(0) is known; (ii) eventual periodicity of the column would yield a rational 2-adic point, not a positive integer, and the 3x+1 conjecture says nothing about rationals with odd denominator, equivalently about the 3x+k maps where nontrivial cycles are known, for example 3x+5; (iii) the direction it needs, Q^(-1)(Q cap Z_2) = Q cap Z_2, is Lagarias's Periodicity Conjecture and is open, while the proved direction is that an eventually periodic parity vector implies a rational point.
records.sc: Refutes one specific proposed implication and closes the Collatz conjugacy as a transfer route. It does not refute any relation between Rule 30 and Collatz-type maps in general, and it is not a statement about the 3x+1 conjecture itself.
records.nt: The elementary proof of Bernstein 1994 Corollary 1 (periodic parity vector implies rational) is reproduced in section 4 of the document. The research decision recorded there is not to rerun conjugacies between H, or any auxiliary map already conjugate to a full shift, and Collatz-type maps.

records.t: Irrationality of the column's Collatz preimage as a sufficient arithmetic target for P1
records.st: Let c_0 c_1 c_2 ... be the actual centre column, s = sum_t c_t 2^t in Z_2, and d_0 < d_1 < ... the positions of its ones. Bernstein's non-iterative form of Q^(-1) gives the unique 2-adic point whose Collatz parity vector is the column, xi_30 = Q^(-1)(s) = - sum_(j>=0) 2^(d_j) / 3^(j+1). Since s rational implies xi_30 rational by Bernstein 1994 Corollary 1, the contrapositive gives: xi_30 irrational in Z_2 implies P1, that is, the centre column is not eventually periodic. This uses no Collatz conjecture and no assumption about the triangular core map H.
records.sc: A sufficient target only. Necessity is not proved: it would follow from Lagarias's Periodicity Conjecture, which is open. Irrationality of s alone is already equivalent to P1 by the ordinary rationality criterion for 2-adic digit expansions, so this is a restatement rather than progress: the definition of xi_30 consumes the centre sequence itself. xi_30 is not established to equal J of any seed-derived point. The open obligation is to derive arithmetic structure of xi_30 directly from the local rule and the singleton origin without passing through the column.
records.nt: The document flags the 3^(-j) weighting as suggesting Mahler-type methods but records that no evidence either way was gathered. Related record: r30-c2b-proposed-conditional-refuted.

records.t: Logarithmic lower bound on period-P mismatches in column minus one
records.st: A quantitative corollary of the existing driven-left-half-plane proof: if the boundary starts at c_0 = 1 and is eventually periodic with period dividing P, then for every sufficiently late T, column -1 has a period-P mismatch in the window [T, 2T+P-1]. In a glued Rule 30 diagram such a mismatch must occur at a zero phase and must also be a right-neighbour mismatch, because the proof propagates a hypothetical long agreement backward until it contradicts the exact leftmost seed edge. Consequently any compatible right history must have at least logarithmically many such mismatches, and an origin-specific upper bound o(log N) at one fixed period multiple would already contradict it, even if there were infinitely many mismatches.
records.sc: A quantitative replacement obligation on the R1 route, not a claim that P1 has become logically easier. No such o(log N) upper bound is proved. The corollary assumes the stated eventually-periodic boundary hypothesis with c_0 = 1; it does not identify the seed's right history and does not by itself exclude a compatible right history.

records.t: Shift-rule control showing column insensitivity is not a no-go theorem
records.st: An O(1/W) response of a bulk statistic to overwriting the centre column disqualifies the statistic only on arbitrary arrays, not on valid seed orbits, because an overwritten diagram generally violates Rule 30 and so does not supply two counterexamples inside the domain of a theorem about valid orbits. The explicit control is the fixed shift rule s(t+1,x) = s(t,x+1) on the two initial rows 0^Z and (01)^Z: bulk density distinguishes their centre densities, respectively zero and one half, while a nontrivial overwrite of just their centre changes bulk averages by O(1/W) and breaks the shift rule. Hence column insensitivity alone is not a no-go theorem for deductions that use the evolution law, and a discrepancy of order 1/W can retain information erased by taking an unscaled limit.

records.t: Cost-model granularity as the controlling variable in a fitted-exponent fitness
records.st: When fitness is a fitted asymptotic exponent, the charging granularity of a variable-width primitive operation controls the fitted exponent in both directions. Charging by bits rather than by machine words injects a spurious log n term that inflates a known Theta(n^2) ground truth to 2.12-2.15, where the word model recovers 1.99946 at r^2 = 0.9999999. Charging too coarsely loses a full exponent unit: a flat opcode counter charging O(1) per operation regardless of width reads the bit-packed Theta(n^2) candidate at 0.99938 and the cubic Theta(n^3) candidate at 1.99690, while the word model reads the same two at 1.99410 and 2.97449, recovering two different known exponents to within 0.03. This is a three-point claim on the granularity axis at two distinct exponents, and the flat-counter direction was obtained as a pre-registered strong outcome.
records.sc: Measured on five pre-registered candidate programs with known true exponents 2 and 3, under one instrument in CPython with WORD_BITS = 30, fitted over its ladder; it is finite measurement in that regime, not a theorem, which is why the status is conjectured rather than proved. records.t: Exact four-to-one preimage count for unrestricted one-step Rule 30 output words
records.st: On the ordinary Rule 30 De Bruijn graph with vertices ab, edges ab -> bc and output label a XOR (b OR c), every prescribed length-m output word has precisely four length-(m+2) input words: choose the two rightmost input bits freely, then reconstruct the remaining bits right to left by a = output XOR (b OR c). Hence the unrestricted one-step output language is the full binary language, with spatial word entropy log(2).
records.sc: Concerns the unrestricted one-step output language only. It does not compute or identify any other notion of dynamical or trace entropy, and the all-zero and spatially alternating fixed configurations remain present, so maximal growth of allowed row words cannot exclude their constant columns, let alone identify the lone-seed centre's asymptotics. A graph route must retain chronological guards and original ancestry, or prove a separate theorem transferring its graph property to those objects.
