records.t: Exact Walsh product expansion of the guarded original-fiber probability
records.st: Fix r and alpha and totalize the prescribed trajectory by appending 3 - alpha_t after each scan, even when that scan fails its guard, and set e_(t,u)(w) = terminal_u(w,t) XOR alpha_t and e_(t,v)(w) = terminal_v(w,t) XOR alpha_t. Then the unconditional probability under uniform legal original words is exactly p_alpha = |C_r(alpha)| / 2^(2r-1) = E_w PRODUCT_(t=1..N, xi in {u,v}) (1 + (-1)^(e_(t,xi)(w)))/2. Proof: each factor is the indicator of one required terminal bit; if the first invalid guard occurs the product is zero regardless of the artificial continuation, and if all factors are one this is the actual successful trajectory with exactly the required births and tape, so no artificial post-crash state is counted as a successful ancestor. Expanding the product gives a sum of joint Walsh correlations over all subsets of the residual constraints, and the exact chain rule p_alpha = PRODUCT_t |C_r(alpha[:t])| / |C_r(alpha[:t-1])| holds for a surviving tape.
records.sc: An exact reformulation suitable for a correlation attack, not a bound. Individual biases or pairwise correlations do not bound the subset sum without an additional theorem, and the chain-rule factors equal one at the known repeats in the 36-ancestor plateau, so a valid information bound must account for the whole history. No uniform bound for the auxiliary histories follows, and no cumulative counting inequality, positive repeat information rate, auxiliary mortality or period-two exclusion is established.
records.nt: Meier and Staffelbach's Rule 30 generator attack is cited as context, not as the source of this identity. records.t: Counting corollary of the seam intertwining for the three reduced endpoint families
records.st: Fix k = a+b within one of the three reduced capacity-18 rows. The k+1 splits of k into (a,b) yield distinct full second endpoints, because the moving seam changes the first 0 position in rows 5 and 12 and the second 0 position in row 27, and their original fibers are disjoint, each of size 18. records.t: Exact nonnegative disjoint-support factorization of a guarded-history MPS tensor
records.st: At one temporal site, flatten a nonnegative integer tensor row over the coordinates (physical symbol, child state), divide each nonzero row by the gcd of its coefficients, and merge identical normalized rows. Processing the distinct normalized rows in increasing support size, a row v whose support admits a partition into two nonempty disjoint sets L, R with both normalized restrictions already occurring among the original normalized rows is rewritten exactly as v = c(v_L) nu(v_L) + c(v_R) nu(v_R) and the smaller rows' expressions are substituted recursively; otherwise v is kept as a basis row. Restoring the gcd scales gives E_j(x) = C B_j(x) for every physical symbol x with C >= 0 and B_j(x) >= 0 integer, and replacing the tensor by B_j while multiplying the preceding tensor by C on the right leaves the entire MPS function unchanged, since E_(j-1)(x) E_j(y) = (E_(j-1)(x) C) B_j(y). The recursion terminates because support size strictly decreases, and the identity is exact on disjoint coordinates so it cannot remove a positive coefficient or introduce a new nonzero coordinate. These identities hold at arbitrary finite temporal depth and preserve both A0 boundary values, every guard encoded by the terminal signature, and the original count. The resulting object can have multiple next states for the same physical symbol, so it is no longer restricted to a weighted deterministic automaton.
records.sc: A representation change, not a counting result. Searching only some support partitions affects the amount of compression, not correctness: an unrecognized row is retained exactly. The construction does not assert that the retained rows form a minimal nonnegative cone or that all possible positive decompositions have been found, and it proves no cumulative counting inequality, finite-frontier mortality, or period-two exclusion.
records.nt: For a right-to-left sweep the final nonnegative boundary column is first absorbed into the last tensor, permitting one terminal state. Related record: r30-dcm-bounded-conic-sweep-result.

records.t: Quadratic memory-traffic wall on centre-column generation independent of core count
records.st: Each step of a row-based centre-column generator reads and writes the full active row, so reaching depth T moves about T^2 / 2 bytes regardless of core count, and this traffic dominates every other consideration. At Apple M4 bandwidth of about 120 GB/s, depth 10^9, which equals the published record, moves 5 * 10^17 bytes and takes about 48 days; on an 8x H100 pod at about 24 TB/s aggregate the same depth takes about 6 hours, depth 5 * 10^10 moves 1.25 * 10^21 bytes and takes about 1.6 years at about $500k, and depth 2 * 10^13, what rung 1 of the patch scan needs, moves 2 * 10^26 bytes and takes about 500,000 years. The VRAM ceiling of two rows of 2T bits, about 250 MB at 10^9, 25 GB at 10^11 and 250 GB at 10^12, is real but never the operative limit, since the time wall bites two to three orders of magnitude earlier.
records.sc: An analytical traffic count for this class of full-row generator, with the wall-clock figures following from assumed aggregate bandwidths rather than from measurement at those depths. It does not bound a generator using a different memory layout or algorithm, and it bears on no prize problem; its use is to correct circulating estimates of a few hours for 10^9 on a desktop GPU and a month and $25k for 5 * 10^10 on an 8x H100 pod, which the document calls optimistic by roughly two orders and twentyfold respectively.
records.nt: Active-cone dispatch is reported to save asymptotically 2x, since sum_t 2t = T^2 against 2T^2 for full width; the T^2/2 figure is the active-cone one. No artifact; prose-only figures.

records.t: Light-cone width condition for finite-array centre-column simulation
records.st: The centre cell at time t depends on cells [-t, t], so a fixed W-cell array with zero boundary reproduces the true infinite-lattice evolution only while t <= W/2 - 1. Past that point the zero boundary is not the true evolution and every later centre bit is wrong with nothing raised: a 10^7-cell array silently corrupts everything beyond t about 5 * 10^6. A correct implementation therefore sizes the lattice from the requested depth and asserts the margin.
records.sc: A correctness condition for finite-array simulation, not a mathematical result about Rule 30. It bears on no prize problem. The document records it as one of four implementation defects, three of which produce wrong numbers rather than errors, the others being swapped neighbour shifts, a history index that must be batch-local, and a missing COPY_DST usage flag.
records.nt: Recorded because a silently-wrong finite-width simulation is the failure mode most likely to be repeated by any future generator in this repository.

source_context.heading: Four defects fixed, one silent

records.t: Affine triangular form of the depth extension of a fixed-word column map
records.st: If F_n is the depth-n column map for a fixed spatial word, its depth-(n+1) extension has the triangular form (q,x) -> (F_n(q), g_q(x)) with x = (a,b) in F_2^2 and g_q(a,b) = (a + t*b + e, b + c) for t, e, c in F_2. Proof: for one scanned symbol all lower-layer information is fixed, so with incoming constants p, A, B and c = p OR B the new pair satisfies v = b + c and u = a + (v OR A) = a + (1+A)*b + A + (1+A)*c, which is the displayed affine form. The eight such forms are closed under composition with t_total = t + t', c_total = c + c' and e_total = e + e' + t'*c, and they form the eight-element dihedral permutation group on the four pairs with element orders 1, 2 and 4. Consequently a pure depth-n block orbit lifts to a pure depth-(n+1) orbit with period ratio 1, 2 or 4, and inductively the order of a block on its fixed-A_0 slice divides 4^n.
records.sc: An exact structural lemma for the capacity-18 family 213(13)^a 1213(13)^b 03 with initial scalar tape 00 and, by the same argument, for any fixed spatial word in this auxiliary bulk dynamics. The ordered cross-term sum_(i<j) t_j*c_i means arbitrary reordering of the local maps is invalid, and the three coefficients describe only ONE extra pair: they do not specify the return's action on another temporal layer, so the actual ordered block word must still be retained for subsequent lifts. No mortality or period-two conclusion follows.
records.nt: Artifact experiments/rule30/capacity18-guarded-15.statistics.json lists exactly eight affine_group_packed_permutations (27, 57, 78, 108, 147, 177, 198, 228), consistent with the eight-element group. Capacity 18 for this family is relayed from RESULTS-capacity18-joint-mortality.md.

source_context.heading: 1. Exact columns and the four-sheet extension

records.t: Exact cover construction for depth-lifted guard-surviving columns
records.st: Retain at depth n the complete first-star orbit with its exact parameter phases, every reachable joint column G_n whose endpoint passes all n guards, the first-return permutation on G_n with each edge labeled by the positive integer L meaning the actual spatial word (13)^L, and for every first-star phase the first visit of its seam column to G_n with its exact b-offset or a certified cycle having no such visit. Then all reachable depth-(n+1) columns whose lower projection lies in G_n are obtained exactly by: closing the complete lifted first-star orbit, whose old phase is the new phase modulo the old period; transporting every lifted seam column along its old first-entry word; closing the union of these entries under the lifted old first-return edges to a cover H_(n+1) with at most 4|G_n| states; and reading the fixed suffix and testing the complete chronological guard history to keep exactly G_(n+1), then contracting its weighted return cycles again. The construction is exact because both block maps are bijections on the fixed-A_0 slices, so a finite closed reachable graph is a union of cycles and deleting unmarked vertices gives an exact weighted first-return permutation, and because a failed lower guard cannot be repaired by adding a higher pair. The argument applies at every n.
records.sc: An exact construction, not a mortality certificate. A deleted vertex is not assumed to die for every larger b: its next surviving vertex and exact distance are retained, and only entire cycles with no marked vertex are discarded. An empty G_n would prove a uniform temporal cutoff for this family, but a cap, a nonempty set, or a projected closure without the actual return words does not have that implication. Extending this family alone would leave the other unresolved capacity-18 families and arbitrary capacity untreated.
records.nt: The certified layers themselves (depths 13, 14, 15 with covers 425, 703, 1088 and survivors 216, 351, 545, and the depth-16 route-cache cap) are already covered by existing record r30-cap18-index15-guarded-lift-depth15 and are not re-extracted; all of those figures were re-verified against experiments/rule30/capacity18-guarded-15.json and match.

records.t: Balanced guard lemma and the doubling bound on guard-surviving columns
records.st: For any q in G_n, exactly two of the four ambient depth-(n+1) lifts pass the new guard, and in pair labels 0,1,2,3 the accepted set A_n(q) is one of {0,1}, {0,3}, {1,2}, {2,3}. Proof: the fixed suffix acts on the new pair by the same eight-element affine group and all earlier guards and birth symbols depend only on q, so scanning the now-fixed birth suffix composes invertible maps v <- v XOR constant and u <- u XOR (v OR constant), and the final condition u = v pulls back to either a = constant or a + b = constant, each selecting exactly two pairs, one for either value of b. Writing R_n(q) for the new pairs actually reachable by the joint two-star action, the exact count recurrence is |G_(n+1)| = sum_(q in G_n) |R_n(q) intersect A_n(q)|, and in particular |G_(n+1)| <= 2|G_n|.
records.sc: A conditional statement about ambient column extensions in this capacity-18 family. These columns are NOT original ancestors and their number is not |C_r(alpha)|; the lemma does not charge an independent bit to a chronological repeat, and it is compatible with the previously recorded unchanged original-fiber plateau. It gives an upper bound on growth, not mortality.
records.nt: The four accepted guard masks are confirmed present at every saved layer in experiments/rule30/capacity18-guarded-15.statistics.json (accepted_guard_mask_histogram keys 3, 6, 9, 12 at depths 13, 14, 15).

source_context.heading: 3. The next guard and the spatial return action

records.t: Order-four cycle monodromy as a local survivor-reproduction mechanism
records.st: Along an old first-return cycle the reachable sets R_n(q) are carried bijectively by its edge permutations, so after a full cycle the resulting cycle monodromy preserves the reachable set. If that monodromy has order 4 it is a four-cycle, hence every nonempty invariant reachable set is all four pairs, and such a cycle gives exactly two new survivors per old survivor. In the saved layers this occurs at depths 13, 14 and 15 on 4, 8 and 13 cycles respectively, accounting for 13, 11 and 20 old survivors and exactly 26, 22 and 40 new survivors, while all eight possible first-return pair permutations and all four possible guard acceptance sets occur at each layer.
records.sc: Proves a local reproduction mechanism, not its persistence at the next depth: the new return cycles have new ordered transports and new guards, and controlling this mixture across temporal depths is the missing step. The finite counts cover every first-return cycle of the three completed layers (depths 13, 14, 15) of one capacity-18 family only. Neither universal loss of descendants nor a single fixed guard line describes these layers. Finite growth of the surviving set is not an all-depth branching theorem, an infinite finite-parameter trajectory, or an unbounded repeat count at fixed capacity.

The witness a=1248, b=260 with total tape 00110011111111111, length 17 and repeat count 13 matches the artifact's max_repeat_witness.

source_context.heading: 3. The next guard and the spatial return action

records.t: Existence and uniqueness of the constant-cut forced continuation for every four-state source
records.st: Let A={0,1,2,3} be the four-state endpoint alphabet, I the inverse-terminal map, sigma the left shift, P the local Peel map P(x)_i = phi(x_i, x_(i+1)), and G_n = P^n o I. For every nonempty source W in A^n and every c in {2,3} there is exactly one infinite four-state word Q_c(W) with G_n(W Q_c(W)) = c^infinity. The proof is the all-length triangular argument: when a new endpoint symbol is appended, the newest cell of G_n is a permutation of that symbol (a composition of the boundary permutation with fixed-left rows of phi), so exactly one of the four endpoint symbols attains the specified output c, and inductively choosing it gives compatible prefixes of every length. The padded implementation computes this exactly via the iterated rotated identity G_n(f) = sigma^(2n) I(0^n f).
records.sc: Holds for every nonempty four-state source, with no binary or hard-core assumption. Q_c forces BOTH bits of every output cell and permits appended symbols 0 and 3, so it is NOT the binary high-bit-only continuation Q_n(W) used to define Psi; no equality of the two continuation maps is asserted once their constraints diverge. Supplies no mortality bound, no rotated-wedge separator, no period-two exclusion and no solution of P1.
records.nt: The bounded controls in experiments/rule30/p1-continuation-scale-shift-audit.json validate the implementation only (16 local phi pairs, 4 boundary symbols, 5,460 independent four-state edge reconstructions over lengths 1-6); the universal quantifier comes from the symbolic argument. Cites experiments/rule30/p1-period2-invariant/RESULTS-BINARY-WEDGE-HIGH-ELIMINATION.md for the same triangular argument.

source_context.heading: 1. Force the complete cut symbol

records.t: All-length continuation identity linking a source to its next-scale shift
records.st: Write Q = Q_c(W) for a nonempty W in A^n and define the length-(n+1) word S_c(W) = W[1:] Q[:2] (delete the first source symbol, append the first two forced symbols). Then Q_c(S_c(W)) = Q_c(W)[2:] for every nonempty four-state source W and c in {2,3}. The proof applies the rotated inverse-cone identity P I(sigma f) = sigma^2 I(f) together with P sigma = sigma P to f = W Q, giving G_(n+1)(sigma f) = sigma^2 G_n(f) = c^infinity; the first n+1 symbols of sigma f are exactly S_c(W) and uniqueness of the forced continuation finishes. Iterating, the compatible source at scale n+k is the block f[k:n+2k] and its forced continuation is Q[2k:], so neighbouring scales cannot be chosen independently along one forced trajectory.
records.sc: An exact identity between forced continuations at neighbouring scales, for every nonempty four-state source. This transformation DELETES a symbol before appending two, so it does not assert that a scale-(n+1) source extends the scale-n source, and therefore does not contradict the append-only obstruction of RESULTS-GAMMA-PROOF-ATTEMPT.md section 2. It supplies no mortality bound and no separator.
records.nt: Bounded controls in experiments/rule30/p1-continuation-scale-shift-audit.json: 1,020 binary source/tail cases through length eight (12 forced symbols before the shift, 10 after) and 168 arbitrary four-state source/tail cases through length three; artifact figures agree with the prose. Premise identity from experiments/rule30/p1-period2-invariant/RESULTS-ROTATED-PEEL-IDENTITY.md.

source_context.heading: 2. Delete one source symbol and append two forced symbols

records.t: Two-row live-state equality under source-symbol deletion
records.st: Let E(A) be the newest dependency edge after reading a finite endpoint word A, indexed by depth from zero, with new[0]=B(q), new[1]=phi(previous_endpoint, new[0]) and new[d]=phi(old[d-2], new[d-1]) for d>=2; the live state is E(A)[:-1]. Then for every W in A^n with n>=1 and every pair q_0, q_1 in A, E(0^n W q_0 q_1)[:-1] = E(0^(n+1) W[1:] q_0 q_1)[:-1], with no forcing assumption on the appended pair. The proof is a dependency bound: the edge entry at endpoint position i and depth d depends only on input positions [i - ceil(d/2), i]; the two words have length 2n+2 and differ only at absolute input coordinate n, which lies outside every live dependency interval since all live inputs have index at least n+1. Dropping the final cell is essential: E(0100)=(3,2,1,1) and E(0000)=(3,2,1,2) have equal live states but unequal complete edges.
records.sc: Combined with the forced continuation, this establishes AT ALL LENGTHS the realizability of the two-row live-state embedding that was previously only finite evidence in fembed_RESULTS.md section A. The stored representative word there need not equal S_c(W), since distinct source words can represent one live state; no injectivity and no preservation of survivor counts is asserted.
records.nt: Bounded control: all 21,824 four-state source/appended-pair cases through source length five, plus the retained negative control E(0100) vs E(0000), both recorded in experiments/rule30/p1-continuation-scale-shift-audit.json and matching the prose exactly. The finite-evidence predecessor is experiments/rule30/p2-needle-attack/fembed_RESULTS.md section A.

source_context.heading: 3. Equality of the complete live states

records.t: Binary continuation horizon drops by exactly two per scale shift, yielding no mortality bound
records.st: For a binary source W let h_c(W) be the length of the initial binary continuation of Q_c(W), with value infinity if it never fails. Whenever h_c(W) >= 2, h_c(S_c(W)) = h_c(W) - 2, and equivalently h_c(S_c(W)) + 2(n+1) = h_c(W) + 2n, so the absolute first-failure position in moving scale coordinates is invariant. The same formula holds for the hard-core continuation horizon that also forbids 11, junction included. This quantity is NOT a computable finite ranking function: using its finiteness would already assume mortality, and the identity is equally consistent with infinite survival at every scale. It gives the known lower bound on maximal survival, not the upper bound a wedge horizon theorem needs.
records.sc: Binary and hard-core sources only. S_c(W) is binary exactly when the first two symbols of Q_c(W) lie in {1,2}; for the stronger actual-endpoint language avoiding both 11 and 22222, the new source stays in that language whenever W Q[:2] does, because S_c takes a suffix. No assertion of actual-right realizability or actual-orbit ancestry for arbitrary words passing those forbidden-factor tests. Unfailed finite prefixes are not treated as infinite survivors.
records.nt: The audit records finite_horizon_recurrence counts of 255 binary and 166 hard-core-with-junction cases where a first failure was observed inside the bounded continuation window (experiments/rule30/p1-continuation-scale-shift-audit.json).

source_context.heading: 4. Binary and hard-core scope; no mortality deduction

records.t: Proposed filter-ratio separation between tame and resonant separated-gap words
records.st: Instrumenting every micro call and every filter step of zero_phase_schedule at width 16 on four words gives first-period filter ratios (reachable-set size after the parity filter rows[(rows&1)==0], divided by the size just before it): tame adjacent (g1,g2)=(0,4) at p=6 gives [0.522, 0.287, 0.638, 0.392]; resonant (2,3) at p=7 gives [0.834, 0.593, 0.708, 0.647, 0.392]; tame (0,8) at p=10 gives [0.522, 0.287, 0.638, 0.392, 0.0]; resonant (1,7) at p=10 gives [0.834, 0.696, 0.61, 0.652, 0.478, 0.684, 0.602, 0.528]. The document proposes from these four cases that both tame words have at least one aggressively low ratio (0.287, or 0.0 emptying the set outright) in their first period while resonant words never drop below about 0.39-0.48, so that a word resonates when none of its individual kicks is strong and decay must accumulate over 2-3 periods, and that this tame/resonant qualitative split is expected to hold generally.
records.sc: Four hand-picked examples at width 16, first period only; the document itself states no closed form or bound for the filter ratio of a kick of length L was derived, that ratios were not tracked to convergence, and that the exact numbers are a width-16 artifact. The generalization expectation stated here is refuted by the widened sample; the four raw ratio lists themselves reproduce exactly.

They match experiments/rule30/r1-general-period/kick-ratio-sample-widen.json cases p6_g0_4, p7_g2_3, p10_g0_8 and p10_g1_7 (all_filter_ratios) digit for digit. The generalization and the mechanistic attribution are refuted by r30-kfw-no-separating-threshold and r30-kfw-minimum-ratio-is-always-bare. The document labels these as KICK ratios but the lists are every schedule segment's ratio, kick or bare; see discrepancies.

source_context.heading: What was measured

records.t: Failure of any first-period filter-ratio threshold to separate tame from resonant words
records.st: Refuted proposal: a first-period filter-ratio threshold separates tame from resonant separated-gap words. Widening the sample to all 33 cases (28 tame, 5 resonant) consisting of every (g1,g2) case in separated-gap-resonance-sweep.json with a confirmed DIES verdict (labelled resonant when peak/p >= 1.4) plus the k=1 isolated-one and k=2 adjacent-ones families for p=5..12, at width 16, first period, gives overlapping ranges under both readings. Kick-only ratios: tame 0.5217-0.8345, resonant 0.6958-0.7079, so resonant's floor sits inside tame's range and tame's ceiling exceeds resonant's. All-filter-event ratios: tame 0.0-0.5209, resonant 0.3923-0.6099. The k=1 isolated-one family 0^(p-1)1, with exact closed-form peak p+2, has min_all = 0.5209 at every tested p = 5..12, exceeding p7_g2_3 (word 1001000, peak 21 = 3p, the strongest confirmed resonance) at min_all = 0.3923. It refutes the proposed threshold and the prior document's generalization expectation, not the four-example observation itself, which reproduces exactly. It does not rule out a separating statistic built from multi-period accumulation, which the document names as the likelier location of the real signal.

source_context.heading: 3. Result: overlap under both readings

records.t: Bare zero-segments, not kicks, attain the first-period minimum filter ratio
records.st: Refuted proposal: only schedule segments crossing a 1 (kicks) can shrink the reachable set, a run of pure 0-bit micro calls merely advancing the strip without comparing against a 1. In every one of the 33 widened cases (28 tame, 5 resonant) the segment attaining the first period's MINIMUM filter ratio is a bare-0 segment, never a kick: the artifact's min_ratio_attribution records n_min_is_kick = 0 and n_min_is_bare = 33, and the same holds at every tested width (16, 20, 24). A bare-0 segment ends in the same parity filter rows[(rows&1)==0] that a kick does, nothing in zero_phase_schedule or micro weakens that step when no 1 was crossed, and the data show it is usually the stronger one.
records.sc: 33 labelled cases, first period, widths 16/20/24. It refutes the mechanistic attribution of the tame/resonant split to kick strength; it does not establish any positive closed form for the filter ratio of a bare segment either, and section 5.1 argues no such form can come from segment shape alone once the surviving set is small.

source_context.heading: 4. The stronger falsification: kicks are never the mechanism

records.t: Multi-period filter ratios as small-integer fluctuation rather than a per-segment decay rate
records.st: Extending the per-segment trace across periods on the resonant cases p7_g2_3 and p9_g1_6 shows that once the reachable set first drops to a small count, most subsequent schedule indices report ratio 1.0 (the filter removes nothing) for one or more periods, then a single bare index abruptly drops it, often to exactly 0. For p7_g2_3, index 3's ratio sequence across periods is [0.6469, 0.2716, 0.2655, 0.0] while every other index sits at 1.0 for periods 1-2 before the population dies at index 3 in period 3. The document reads this as plain small-integer fluctuation (a few dozen surviving rows, so a filter's ratio is a small numerator over a small denominator) rather than an intrinsic per-segment decay rate, and concludes that a closed form would have to track the surviving set's actual structure at small size, since which specific rows survived is history-dependent and decides the next ratio rather than the segment's bit pattern.
records.sc: Two resonant words traced across a handful of periods at width 16, console output only. This is an interpretation of a small observation, not a theorem: it neither proves that no per-segment decay rate exists nor bounds the number of periods to extinction.
records.nt: Not persisted to JSON; the document states it is console-only, following the same pattern as the original mechanism document. The single-period value 0.6469 for p7_g2_3 index 3 does appear in that case's all_filter_ratios in kick-ratio-sample-widen.json.

source_context.heading: 5.1. Multi-period trace: small-N discreteness, not a decay rate

records.t: Exact Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for dyadic-difference correlations of a sign word
records.st: For any signs z_0,...,z_(N-1) with N>=1, put S_N = sum_(t<N) z_t and C_N(h) = sum_(t<=N-1-h) z_t z_(t+h) for h>=1 (zero when h>=N). For m>=1 set a_j = 2^j - 1 for 0<=j<m and H_m = 2^(m-1) - 1. Then m^2 S_N^2 <= (N + H_m) [ m N + 2 sum_(0<=i<j<m) C_N(2^j - 2^i) ]. Proof: extend z by zero to all integers, set Y_t = sum_(j<m) z_(t+a_j), whose support lies in the N + H_m positions [-H_m, N-1] and whose total is m S_N; expanding squares gives sum_t Y_t^2 = m N + 2 sum_(i<j) C_N(a_j - a_i), and Cauchy-Schwarz finishes. The bracket is nonnegative even when individual correlations are negative, there is no independence assumption, and the inequality also holds when N <= H_m.
records.sc: An exact finite inequality for arbitrary sign words, with no Rule 30 content. It is a specialization of the elementary Cauchy-Schwarz / van der Corput argument to dyadic translations, not a new general analytic method, and it proves no cancellation estimate for Rule 30.
records.nt: Checked in integer arithmetic on every nonempty sign word through length ten for m = 1..5: experiments/rule30/p2-sparse-difference-correlations-audit.json records 2,046 nonempty sign words, maximum_length 10, translation_counts [1,2,3,4,5] and 10,230 finite inequality and energy-identity checks.

source_context.heading: 1. Exact finite inequality

records.t: Dyadic-lag correlation hypothesis sufficient for P2 and for P1
records.st: Let c_t be the singleton Rule 30 centre trace, z_t = 1 - 2 c_t, and D = {2^a - 2^b : a > b >= 0}. If limsup_(N->infinity) C_N(h)/N <= 0 for every h in D, then centre density is 1/2 and P2 follows: dividing the exact inequality by m^2 N^2 with m held fixed, the finitely many cross terms have nonpositive limsup and H_m/N -> 0, giving limsup (S_N/N)^2 <= 1/m, and only afterwards is m let tend to infinity. Equivalently, with D_N(h) = #{0<=t<N-h : c_t != c_(t+h)} and C_N(h) = (N-h) - 2 D_N(h) for N > h, the hypothesis is liminf D_N(h)/(N-h) >= 1/2 for each h in D. The same hypothesis also excludes every eventual period, hence would prove P1: for any period p two powers of two share a residue mod p, their positive difference h lies in D and is divisible by p, and an eventually p-periodic trace has C_N(h)/N -> 1. A weaker aggregate alternative suffices too: it is enough that for an unbounded set of m, limsup_(N) (1/N) sum_(0<=i<j<m) C_N(2^j - 2^i) <= 0.
records.sc: Conditional only. Neither the per-lag hypothesis nor the aggregate alternative is established for Rule 30, and neither is claimed necessary for P2. No uniform rate in h or m is required, but letting m grow with N without further bounds would not be justified. These are ordinary time shifts, not XOR shifts of binary time indices. The missing step remains an origin-specific cancellation argument.
records.nt: A Rule 90 control confirms the hypotheses are not vacuously universal: for the Rule 90 singleton c_0=1 and c_t=0 for t>=1, so C_N(h) = N - h - 2 and C_N(h)/N -> 1 for each fixed h>=1, and the hypotheses fail as required (178 finite Rule 90 formula checks in experiments/rule30/p2-sparse-difference-correlations-audit.json). Depends on the exact inequality r30-sdc-dyadic-translation-inequality.

source_context.heading: 2. Sufficient seed theorem and order of limits

records.t: Polylogarithmic sparsity of the dyadic difference lag set
records.st: Every integer in D = {2^a - 2^b : a > b >= 0} has one contiguous run of ones in binary, h = 2^b (2^(a-b) - 1). If 1 <= h <= X then 2^(a-1) <= X, so with L = floor(log_2 X) + 1 one gets |D intersect [1,X]| <= sum_(a=1)^(L) a = L(L+1)/2, i.e. only O((log X)^2) lags up to X are requested, compared with every positive lag in the earlier consecutive-translation sufficient theorem.
records.sc: A counting bound on the lag set only. It weakens the hypothesis a sufficient theorem must assume; it does not prove the remaining estimates on those lags are easier for the Rule 30 seed.
records.nt: experiments/rule30/p2-sparse-difference-correlations-audit.json holds 11 lag_count_checks, each pairing the exact count with the stated upper bound.

source_context.heading: 3. How sparse the lag set is, and an additional implication

records.t: Counterexample to a generic powers-of-two-only balance implication
records.st: Refuted proposal: vanishing correlations at powers-of-two lags alone force density 1/2. The artificial periodic bit word (110100010000)^infinity has density 1/3, with one positions A = {0,1,3,7} modulo 12. For h = 1, 2, 4, 8 exactly one t in A has t+h in A, so the signed cyclic correlation numerator is 12 - 4|A| + 4|{t in A : t+h in A}| = 0; all higher powers of two alternate between 4 and 8 modulo 12 because 2*4 = 8 and 2*8 = 4 mod 12, so C_N(2^j)/N -> 0 for every j >= 0 despite the biased density. The correlations at the omitted dyadic DIFFERENCES do not all vanish: h = 6 = 8-2 gives numerator 4 and h = 12 = 16-4 gives 12.
records.sc: An exact counterexample to a universally quantified powers-of-two-only implication. The word is artificial and is explicitly not asserted to be a Rule 30 centre trace. Because XOR correlations of the time-index Walsh route and the ordinary correlations used here are different statistics, this does not refute the Walsh theorem of RESULTS-p2-time-index-walsh.md.
records.nt: The audit's periodic_control block confirms word 110100010000, period 12, 4 ones, one_density 1/3, cyclic correlation numerators 0 at h = 1,2,3,4,5,7,8,9,10,11 and 4 at h = 6, with powers_of_two_residue_prefix [1,2] and residue cycle [4,8]; the positive dyadic-difference entries are recorded as normalized densities 1/3 at h=6 and 1 at h=12, consistent with the prose numerators 4 and 12 over period 12.

source_context.heading: 4. Powers-of-two lags alone are insufficient

records.t: Logarithmic growth in depth of the tallest column-0 p-consistent patch
records.st: Define a patch, for period p and half-width w, as a maximal run of consecutive times t on which s(t,x) == s(t+p,x) for every x in [-w,w], and let H(p,w) be the tallest such patch with t + p + H <= T. For the Rule 30 lone seed the exact bit-parallel scan gives H(p,0) = 12, 15, 20, 20, 21 for p=1; 11, 14, 19, 19, 20 for p=2; 13, 15, 18, 18, 19 for p=3; and 12, 12, 17, 17, 20 for p=4, at T = 10^4, 3*10^4, 10^5, 3*10^5, 10^6, giving fitted slopes against log2 T of 1.38, 1.38, 0.90 and 1.27 respectively. At T = 10^6 the full profile in w for p=2 is 20, 15, 14, 11, 9, 8, 6, 4, 2, 1 at w = 0..9 and zero at w >= 10. The document reads these as logarithmic growth with no saturation.
records.sc: Finite evidence at T <= 10^6, wmax 14, four periods, five depths; explicitly MEASURED, no theorem. A finite scan cannot distinguish no patch exists from none exists below depth T, and logarithmic growth is unbounded, so this excludes nothing about the half-plane branch: reading the tables as period 2 is excluded is a misreading the document warns against. It also excludes nothing the published 10^9-bit centre column does not already exclude.
records.nt: Every H value verified against experiments/rule30/ladder/scan30-{10000,30000,100000,300000,1000000}.json, all with gate_ok true; the tables agree exactly. Endpoint slopes recompute as 1.364, 1.364, 0.909 and 1.21 against the document's fitted 1.38, 1.38, 0.90, 1.27, consistent with a least-squares rather than endpoint fit. Soundness: the bit-parallel scan agrees exactly with an independent dense-grid implementation at T=120 for both rules at every p in {1,2,3} and every half-width, and every run re-derives the first 30 centre-column terms against experiments/rule30/center_column.py.

source_context.heading: MEASURED: Rule 30, lone seed

records.t: Growth rate of the period-two patch width reach and the depth it implies
records.st: Let the width reach be the largest w with H(2,w) > 0. It measures 6, 7, 7, 8, 9 at T = 10^4, 3*10^4, 10^5, 3*10^5, 10^6, where log2 T = 13.3, 14.9, 16.6, 18.2, 19.9, so the reach advances at roughly 0.45 half-widths per unit increase of log2 T, i.e. per doubling of T. Extrapolating that rate, a period-two consistent patch spanning half-width 20 requires log2 T about 44, i.e. T about 2*10^13 - four orders of magnitude past the published 10^9-bit dataset, itself the largest ever computed. The document concludes that brute depth demonstrably will not reach the regime that would decide rung 1, arguing for the diagonal-coordinate automaton and against any further scan-deeper strategy.
records.sc: An extrapolation from five depths, not a theorem, and the underlying growth is unbounded so it rules nothing out. It quantifies the cost of the empirical route only; it is not a lower bound on any algorithm and does not settle the half-plane branch.
records.nt: Reach values recomputed from the H['2'] arrays of experiments/rule30/ladder/scan30-*.json and match the prose (6,7,7,8,9). The rate is stated in the source as 0.45 half-widths per DOUBLING of log2 T; the arithmetic ((9-6)/(19.9-13.3) = 0.4545) and the document's own extrapolation to log2 T ~ 44 both use 0.45 per UNIT of log2 T, so the per-doubling wording is a slip. See discrepancies.

records.t: Rule 90 lone-seed control separates from Rule 30 by five orders of magnitude on patch height

source_context.heading: Control: Rule 90

records.t: Exact sharp first-failure deadline for finite-left rows over the two proved periodic cylinders
records.st: Let u_N be one of the two exact right prefixes (N = 124 or 104) proved to force periodic neighbours under the alternating centre drive. Let x be any initial Rule 30 row with x_0 = 0, x_i = 0 for i < -d with d >= 0, and (x_1,...,x_N) = u_N, the bits at -d,...,-1 and every cell beyond N arbitrary and the right tail not required to be finite. Let v be the corresponding source torus's phase-zero spatial row, S its spatial period, a_j = v_((-j) mod S) for j>=1 the forced left bits, and j_d = min{j > d : a_j = 1}. Then the exact maximum first-failure time of the centre trace against 0,1,0,1,... is exactly j_d, for every fixed right continuation of u_N, and its gap above d has period S in d. Since the largest cyclic gap between ones of v is 7 for u_124 (S = 155, neighbour time period 10) and 10 for u_104 (S = 728, neighbour time period 14), the centre trace must differ from the alternating trace at some time t <= d + 7 for u_124 and t <= d + 10 for u_104, and both additive constants are sharp uniformly over d. No bounded-depth extrapolation is used. The proof needs the forced left tail to be independent of the right continuation: the inverse local equation s(t,i-1) = s(t+1,i) XOR (s(t,i) OR s(t,i+1)) uniquely determines every left column from the centre drive c and the fixed periodic neighbour column r, which is the same pair the known source torus has; sharpness follows because Rule 30 is permutive in its left argument, so the leftmost differing ancestor has coefficient one at time j_d and more distant differences cannot yet arrive.
records.sc: Uniform exclusion for two right-prefix families only. The support hypothesis is a bound and not a requirement that the leftmost one sit exactly at -d, so the forced bit a_d may be zero. The unrestricted period-two problem and P1 remain open; this is a corollary of the two existing cylinder certificates and left-permutive trace reconstruction, not a new cylinder construction or a literature priority claim. The uniqueness argument concerns two full adjacent time columns and is not an assertion that arbitrary one-cell traces are injective.
records.nt: Every figure checked against experiments/rule30/r1-cylinder-deadline-audit.json (status PASS): witness u_124 has reference_spatial_period 155, neighbour_period 10, uniform_deadline_extra 7; u_104 has 728, 14 and 10. The audit's counts sum exactly to the prose totals: 1,550 + 10,192 = 11,742 torus cells, 1,024 + 16,384 = 17,408 return cones, 159 + 732 = 891 sharp truncated-left examples, 511 + 511 = 1,022 arbitrary-left examples with d <= 8, and 4 + 4 = 8 independent scalar first-failure checks. Premise: the periodic-cylinder theorem, catalog id ba37969e4c8f2d55.

source_context.heading: 2. The exact deadline

records.t: Necessary cylinder-avoidance condition for an eventually alternating singleton orbit
records.st: At actual singleton time T the leftmost one is at -T. Consequently, if the centre is zero and the right row begins with u_124, an alternating continuation must fail by absolute time 2T + 7; with u_104 it must fail by 2T + 10. Therefore an actually eventually alternating singleton orbit would have to avoid these two right-prefix cylinders at every sufficiently late centre-zero phase. This is a proved necessary avoidance condition.
records.sc: No theorem that the singleton must enter either cylinder is supplied, and eventual entry is not proved for every finite driven right row; the earlier generic locking failures cannot be bypassed by assuming such entry. The result excludes two infinite families of possible onset rows, not all rows and not every period-two tail.
records.nt: Direct corollary of r30-cyd-exact-sharp-deadline with d = T.

source_context.heading: 5. Meaning for the singleton orbit

records.t: Exact aperiodicity observation condition for a fixed automatic-diagram transition core
records.st: For a fixed transition core of an N-state MSB automaton, take its time-axis binary transitions and compute every endpoint pair (q(n), q(n+P)) for n >= H with H = 2^N and P = 2^N * lcm(1,...,N); an exact finite MSB addition product computes this entire relation with an actual integer witness for each pair, and it depends only on transitions, not on output labels. Folding each endpoint through the fixed low-coordinate suffix specifying a centre-clock phase and spatial coordinate 1, the neighbour on that phase is aperiodic exactly when some folded endpoint pair has unequal output labels; this is the proved eventual-period bound, not an inference from observing a long nonperiodic prefix. For a centre clock with finitely many zero phases, the masked vector is aperiodic if and only if at least one of those scalar phase signals is aperiodic, since otherwise the maximum of their onsets and the lcm of their periods would make the vector eventually periodic. Hence, conditioned on the proposed core transitions, the exact observation requirement is an OR over eligible phase/output-state pairs: the phase clock is zero and the two labels differ. The time-axis reachable state set is closed under symbols with spatial bit zero, so guarding all four outgoing transitions of its reachable states fixes the endpoint relation and every folded output pair; if all original endpoint pairs are diagonal, every folded pair is diagonal regardless of the final suffix, so fixing just the two time-axis transitions per reachable state already excludes that core from the aperiodic class.
records.sc: An exact criterion permitting removal of the 111-bit existential witness circuit from automatic-diagram synthesis; it changes the encoding, not the intended construction class. The finite all-coordinate Rule 30 and centre checkers remain unchanged and output aperiodicity alone is never accepted as a diagram. The observation logic is intentionally rule-generic and passes a Rule 90 construction control, so it does not purport to prove a rule-generic R1. No Rule 30 counterdiagram and no R1 proof is claimed.
records.nt: Controls: the endpoint-relation implementation was checked on all 252 labelled time-axis transition tables with one through three states and a root leading-zero self-loop, and all 1,978 binary output labelings agree with an independently implemented exact MSB classifier; an independent verifier compares complete endpoint-pair sets using a different construction on every one of those 252 tables. Premise: the MSB automatic sequence period theorem, catalog id 6cdca41320d7d11d, from RESULTS-r1-msb-automatic-period-bound.md.

source_context.heading: 1. An exact observation condition for each proposed core

records.t: Exact state-space bound proving the gate checker's cap cannot truncate this class
records.st: For the fixed class of five MSB states, temporal output clock 4 and spatial output-label clock 14, the gate checker's full product has at most 5^4 * 2^3 * 4 * 14 = 280,000 states: four automaton states, three two-valued coordinate differences, and the two output-label residues. Consequently the configured 500,000-state cap cannot truncate any candidate gate check in this class.
records.sc: An exact state-space bound for this one parameter class, not a claim about the largest coordinate tested by direct simulation and not a bound for any other N, temporal or spatial clock length.

source_context.heading: 2. Why the conditional cuts preserve the construction class

records.t: Existential equivalence of shared and per-cut observation selectors
records.st: Every pair selector has the core-independent meaning selector(phase,a,b) => clock(phase) = 0 and output(phase,1,a) != output(phase,1,b), so selectors may be shared across observation cuts; at five states and four phases there are at most 4 * binomial(5,2) = 40 of them. Sharing is existentially equivalent to separate copies: OR all eligible copies to obtain a shared assignment, and conversely copy the shared assignment into every occurrence, with all implications and guarded disjunctions still satisfied and no exclusivity between selectors required. The shared base additionally requires at least one of the 40 selectors, which is a necessary condition because an aperiodic zero-phase observable must distinguish at least two raw output states on that phase.
records.sc: The raw-output necessity condition does not assert that the distinguished states are reachable; the exact observation test is still required. With it, the rebuilt base has 2,028 variables and 80,353 clauses while retaining all 47,060 path and 12,205 observation refinements from the prior run.

source_context.heading: 4. Shared selectors and semantic continuation

records.t: Capped searches of the five-state N=5 T=4 q=14 diagram class all end UNKNOWN
records.st: Three capped Glucose searches of the complete class (five MSB states, temporal output clock 4, spatial output-label clock 14) under the lean observation encoding all ended UNKNOWN at their time caps and established neither unrealizability nor a counterdiagram. The first lean run went from 1,988 seed variables and 20,982 clauses to 122,042 variables and 440,394 clauses after 14,095 candidate models, 47,060 necessary path clauses and 12,205 exact observation refinements in 180.31 seconds. A 180-second shared-selector continuation added 25,571 candidates, reaching 39,666 candidates, 173,742 path cuts and 32,996 observation cuts with 2,028 variables and 227,762 clauses. A subsequent single 900-second Glucose process ran 900.8199 seconds and examined 148,808 further candidates, for cumulative totals of 188,474 candidates, 730,820 path cuts and 162,590 observation cuts, with 2,028 variables and 914,165 final clauses. These counts are measurements, not a class exclusion; no conclusion follows from a resource cap.
records.sc: Applies to this one parameter class under this encoding. An UNKNOWN result establishes neither unrealizability nor a counterdiagram, and R1 and P1 remain open. Any future UNSAT claim requires a checked DRUP proof against the reconstructed final CNF as well as semantic replay of all cuts.
records.nt: An independent verifier using a different endpoint-relation construction replays every path without the producer's helpers and reconstructs the entire final CNF: 1,163 axis tables, 241,032 endpoint pairs, 187,040 coordinate paths and 877,020 transition steps for the first run; 3,935 tables, 682,399 endpoint pairs, 691,641 paths and 3,280,916 steps for the shared continuation; 13,093 tables, 3,474,756 endpoint pairs, 2,916,143 paths and 14,095,903 steps for the 900-second run, with maximum path-clause width 21 and at most 17 distinct transition guards. Unchanged controls.rule90_control(6) passes in every case. Checkpoint artifacts are retained compressed with raw and compressed SHA-256 recorded in .provenance.json sidecars.

source_context.heading: 4. Shared selectors and semantic continuation

records.t: Soundness and literal width of the deterministic path clause refinement
records.st: For a failed local gate, evaluate a candidate's four MSB coordinate paths at (t,x-1), (t,x), (t,x+1) and (t+1,x), each starting at root state zero, and record every selected transition variable together with the signed output-assignment literal at its final state. Under the one-hot transition constraints the conjunction of those literals forces the same four coordinate outputs in any later candidate, so if those outputs violate the frozen Rule 30 truth table, negating the conjunction gives a single clause satisfied by every actual diagram in the class; deterministic path induction proves the implication and the final four-bit contradiction is checked against the unchanged ladder FWD. A centre failure is handled the same way with its required clock-assignment literal included. A candidate core has at most 4N distinct selected transition variables regardless of coordinate magnitude, so a full four-site gate cut has at most 4N + 4 literals and no ground-state or ground-output variables are introduced. The cut is safely strengthened by deleting unnecessary output-site assignments, tested against all eight ordinary valid truth-table rows without assuming any alias relation between candidate output variables, so changing an unguarded discarded path cannot invalidate the implication.
records.sc: A refinement-encoding improvement only. Every proposed model still goes through unchanged check_centre and check_gates on their exact finite all-coordinate product closures, so changing the refinement encoding does not replace the final test with a sample of coordinates. The method is generic and can refine either rule; the different ordinary truth tables supply the required nonlinear content. R1 and P1 remain open and no Rule 30 counterdiagram was found.
records.nt: An independent verifier that does not call the producer's path extractor, cube minimizer or clause constructor rebuilt the base formula and checked 13 exact candidate aperiodicity inequalities, 1,108 imported actual-coordinate constraints, 196 path clauses, 781 coordinate paths, 5,468 individual transition steps and 1,560 ordinary truth-table row checks; all pass. Among the eight invalid Rule 30 output quadruples the ordinary cube minimizer retains three sites in six cases and all four in two; for Rule 90 it retains three sites in all eight and always discards the irrelevant centre input. Unchanged controls.rule90_control(6) passes at periods 2, 4 and 6.

source_context.heading: 2. A single clause replaces a ground unrolling

records.t: Single capped comparison of path-clause against ground-constraint refinement
records.st: One 180-second comparison on the same five-state MSB class, both backends starting from 19,396 variables and 233,140 clauses, gave: ground constraints 2 candidate models, 33 new failed-coordinate refinements, 19,902 final variables, 239,404 final clauses in 180.31 seconds, outcome UNKNOWN; path clauses 13 candidate models, 196 refinements, 19,396 final variables (unchanged), 233,336 final clauses in 180.17 seconds, outcome UNKNOWN. The first path-backend candidate appeared at 123.26 seconds and ten candidates had been processed by 164.80 seconds, so the initial solve consumed most of the budget and subsequent path refinements were substantially cheaper in this run. The largest saved clause has 18 literals including at most 14 distinct transition literals.
records.sc: One performance comparison, not a parameter census or a controlled statistical benchmark. The cut strengths differ - one full coordinate equation excludes every invalid assignment at that coordinate, whereas one path clause excludes its certified implication cube - so raw cut counts are not equal measures of eliminated models. Neither capped UNKNOWN answer is evidence that the class is empty, and no UNSAT result or proof artifact is claimed.

source_context.heading: 3. The 180-second comparison

records.t: Failure of the wall-clock tail-exponent scorer to separate constant-factor from algorithmic speedups
records.st: Refuted proposal: at the smoke profile's n <= 16000 the wall-clock tail-exponent evaluator resolves the difference between a constant-factor speedup and an algorithmic one. Measured on this machine, the naive O(n^2) control - algorithmically identical to the program baseline_exponent.json was measured from, stored tail 2.2147 - produced tails 1.9289, 2.1635 and 1.8069 (spread 0.357) and combined_scores 0.2957, 0.2667 and 0.7896 against its own stored baseline, i.e. the evaluator credited the baseline with beating itself by 0.41 exponent-units. The provably O(n^2/64) bit-packed control produced tails 1.6923, 1.8333, 1.5861, 1.8029, 1.5731 and 1.7727 over six runs (mean 1.712, stdev 0.111). The two ranges overlap outright, 1.807-2.164 against 1.573-1.833. Under interleaved A/B/A/B measurement the paired gap read 0.590 exponent-units in the first pair and 0.034 in the second nine minutes later, both full-window with r2 > 0.997. The pre-registered noise band of +/-0.2-0.3, whose upper end is the full-credit bar, is smaller than the instrument's own scatter, so the required sanity gate failed and the search was not launched; no LLM call was made.
records.sc: A claim about this instrument at this scaling range on this machine under this load, not a claim that bit-packing is sub-quadratic (it demonstrably is not) and not a finding about Rule 30 - the question the arm exists to answer was never put to a search. A quiet machine is necessary but not shown sufficient: candidate (c) can only return to its documented 0.210 if its tail measures about 2.21, which n <= 16000 did not produce in six attempts.
records.nt: Raw logs cited as experiments/openevolve-p3/sanity_rerun_20260831.log and interleaved_ab_20260831.log; no JSON artifact carries these numbers, so the figures are taken from the prose, which repeats them consistently in section 3b and in register row 91. The pre-registration's >=3 independent runs rule re-measures the candidate, not the baseline comparison, so it would not have caught this. evaluator.py, its scoring, baseline_exponent.json, ground_truth.json, the profiles and PREREGISTRATION.md were deliberately left unchanged.

source_context.heading: 3b. Load-independent: the exponent estimate is too unstable to discriminate

records.t: Fit-quality metrics do not reveal that two candidates were scored over different depth windows
records.st: Refuted proposal: the evaluator's reported metrics reveal when two candidates were scored over incomparable scaling windows. Under a load average of 77-105 on 10 cores, the naive O(n^2) candidate exceeded the smoke profile's 180-second per_call_timeout at n = 16000 and that point was silently dropped, so its tail was computed on the 4000 -> 8000 segment while the roughly 50x faster bit-packed candidate still completed n = 16000 and kept the 8000 -> 16000 segment. Nothing in the metrics reveals this: r2 and tail_consistency measure whether the fit is clean, not whether the window is right, and every truncated run still reported r2 > 0.999. The mechanism was checked rather than assumed - scaling_dropped recorded 'timing call failed: ' with an empty message, which is exactly how concurrent.futures.TimeoutError stringifies.
records.sc: A defect of this wall-clock evaluator configuration, diagnosed on one machine under one load episode. It is the proximate cause only; the document states the load-independent instability of section 3b is the serious problem and is not fixed by a quiet machine.
records.nt: usable_ns was recorded as [2000, 4000, 8000] for the naive control and [2000, 4000, 8000, 16000] for the bit-packed one in the sanity re-run. For the interleaved A/B passes usable_ns was only captured for B2; for A1, B1 and A2 the full window is an inference from their tails sitting near the stored full-window baseline, which the document states explicitly.

source_context.heading: 3a. Proximate: load truncates the naive control's measurement window

records.t: Bit-identical fuel counts across processes and exact recovery of the stored baseline
records.st: The AST-rewriting word-RAM fuel counter produces bit-identical counts across separate processes. Each of candidate_a_correct.py, candidate_c_bitpacked.py and the seed initial_program.py was measured in three separate processes with PYTHONHASHSEED left randomised, nine workers in total under load average 20.3 to 34.8 on 10 cores, and every n produced exactly one distinct value: candidate (a) and the seed both gave 1,760,513 / 7,021,013 / 28,042,013 / 112,084,013 / 448,168,013 at n = 250 / 500 / 1000 / 2000 / 4000, and candidate (c) gave 21,874 / 85,745 / 337,474 / 1,342,945 / 5,349,874. Nothing here is a claim about Rule 30, no search was launched and no LLM call was made; evaluator.py, PREREGISTRATION.md and baseline_exponent.json are untouched and the fuel evaluator is a parallel one that imports the pre-registered scoring, gates and thresholds rather than restating them. source_context.heading: 6. Determinism check

records.t: Failure of both flat-opcode and bit-granularity cost models to recover known exponents
records.st: Refuted proposals: (i) a flat opcode counter charging 1 per operation regardless of operand width measures asymptotic cost correctly, and (ii) charging by raw bit length rather than 30-bit words does. Against candidates with known true exponents, the flat counter is wrong by a full exponent-unit whenever a wide operand is present: candidate (c) candidate_c_bitpacked (true exponent 2) reads 0.99938 and candidate (e) candidate_e_cubic (true exponent 3, correct and identical to (a) and (c) for all n < 120) reads 1.99690, against word-model readings of 1.99410 and 2.97449. Candidate (a) agrees to five decimals (1.99946 word, 1.99947 flat) and is non-discriminating by construction, since it iterates per cell so every operand already fits one word. In the other direction, charging by raw bit length puts a spurious log n factor on every loop-index operation and the naive O(n^2) simulation then fits 2.151 / 2.140 / 2.129 / 2.119 across its windows, against 1.9957 -> 1.9995 under the word model. Granularity is therefore the controlling variable: too coarse loses a full exponent-unit, too fine adds a spurious 0.12-0.15, and the word model recovers two distinct known exponents to within 0.03.
records.sc: An instrument ablation on a fixed candidate set, pre-registered for the flat-opcode arm in PREREG-flat-opcode-ablation.md. Not a claim about Rule 30. The word model's adjacent slopes for candidate (e) rise 2.90164 -> 2.96786 -> 2.97449, converging toward 3 from below as the exact cost's lower-order quadratic term predicts, so 2.97449 is not itself the asymptote.
records.nt: Candidate (e) exists because every prior test of this instrument, the bit ablation included, checked it only against a true exponent of 2, so an instrument biased toward 2 would have passed all of them. Figures are from the document's tables; no JSON artifact for the ablations is cited.

source_context.heading: 2.1 The unit: a word-RAM model, `WORD_BITS = 30`

records.t: An 84x constant-factor speedup left uncredited by the fuel-instrumented score
records.st: At n = 4000 the bit-packed control costs 5,349,874 fuel against the naive control's 448,168,013, a factor of 83.8x, which is exactly what big-integer bit-packing buys. Its tail exponent is 1.994104692887 against the baseline's 1.999459168018799, giving improvement 0.005354, bonus 0.01785, confidence 0.99689 and combined_score = 0.2 + 0.8 * 0.01785 * 0.99689 = 0.21423, against the 0.210 the pre-registration documents for this candidate. The 84x speedup is therefore invisible to combined_score, which is the design intent, and 0.0054 sits 56x below the pre-registered 0.3 exponent-unit full-credit bar. Under WORD_BITS = 64 the same candidate's gap below the naive control is 0.02252 in the 1000 -> 2000 window and 0.00686 in 2000 -> 4000, against 0.00637 and 0.00535 at WORD_BITS = 30; the widest of these, 0.02252, scores 0.26 against the 0.3 bar, so the verdict that (c) is a constant-factor win and not an exponent win holds at both word sizes. All four pre-registered sanity candidates pass under the fuel instrument - (a) 0.200000, (b) 0.0, (c) 0.214234, (d) 0.0 - against two failures under the wall clock, (a) 0.2957 and (c) 0.9335.
records.sc: Instrument validation on the four pre-registered sanity candidates and one word-size sweep; not a claim about Rule 30 and not a search result. The word size changes the constant, not the conclusion. The wide diagnostic sweep runs n = 125..4000 while the scoring ladder is n = 250..4000, and the extra 125 -> 250 row takes no part in any combined_score.

Setup fuel is reported separately and never folded in: at n = 137 the seed has setup 8, candidates (a) and (c) have 0, and the lookup-table cheat (d) has call fuel 2 against setup fuel 31,999, flat at every n in 250..4000.

source_context.heading: 4. The sanity gate under the fuel instrument

records.t: Shortened reach of the anti-lookup-table gate under the 4000-point fuel ladder
records.st: The fuel ladder tops out at n = 4000 while the wall-clock profile reached n = 16000. The scaling-range correctness check is the harness's principal defence against a precomputed lookup table - PREREGISTRATION.md gate 4 states it is the only check that reaches beyond n = 3000 - so a 4000-point ladder shortens its reach by a factor of four. A table covering n <= 4000 would pass the evolve, holdout and trap gates, all of which use n <= 3000, and every scaling point as well, and would read a slope near 0; the _scan_literals backstop does not catch a dict comprehension, as the pre-registration itself notes. Until a scaling point far above any plausible embedded table is added, or a near-zero slope or large setup fuel is itself treated as suspicious, the instrument measures scaling correctly but the anti-table gate is weaker than the pre-registered one.
records.sc: An open gap in the harness, deliberately not closed because either candidate fix is a pre-registration question rather than an instrument question. No search should be run until one is in place. This is not a claim about Rule 30, and no lookup-table candidate was actually constructed to demonstrate the bypass.
records.nt: max_setup_fuel is already surfaced in the evaluator's metrics for exactly this purpose: candidate (d) reads 31,999 against 0 for every honest candidate, flat at n = 250, 500, 1000, 2000 and 4000 because the table is built once at module level.

source_context.heading: 8. Verdict, including what is NOT closed

records.t: Canonical balanced grammar fails to recover the half-width core's node-count regression
records.st: At the directed control n = 32 the original section evaluator constructs 205 grammar nodes with 246 distinct section and pair-transduction subqueries; a pair pass after every original section gives 401 nodes and 646 subqueries; the half-width core gives 437 nodes and 317 subqueries; and the half-width core plus a pair pass gives 385 nodes and 431 subqueries. To test whether the core's regression is merely parenthesization overhead, a canonical balanced grammar was implemented without flattening: it reduces the n = 32 core from 437 to 244 nodes, still above the original 205. The pair rules therefore perform real cancellations but their naive schedules cost more than the work they avoid, and smaller expanded words need not have smaller shared graphs.
records.sc: Three directed controls at n = 8, 17 and 32 that discriminate the implementations; not a scaling fit and not an asymptotic lower bound. All recursive reshaping costs are recorded and the artifacts separately record cuts, concatenations and the normalizer's own work, so no cost is hidden. It does not exclude a different schedule or a composition theorem that would reduce total cost to o(n); no successful bulk rewrite is claimed and Problem 3 remains open.
records.nt: The balanced-grammar control (experiments/rule30/p3_query_balanced_slp.py) is specific to this document and is not covered by the existing r30-p3-observable-rewrite-pairs-implementation record, whose source document reports only that the tested rewrite schedule costs more than the unrevised evaluator. No JSON artifact for the node-count table is cited in the document; figures are from its section 4 tables. The four rewrites themselves are already catalogued under r30-p3-query-pruning-zero-prefix-deletion, r30-p3-query-cone-rewrite-suffix, r30-p3-observable-rewrite-pairs-identities and r30-p3-precision-filtration-original.

source_context.heading: 4. Cost was measured including the rewrites

records.t: Withdrawal of the self-composition bound as a ceiling on generic simulation methods
records.st: The earlier self-composition audit's O(n^2/log n) figure was incorrectly described as a ceiling on generic methods; that description is withdrawn. It is an upper bound achieved by one indexed-RAM construction, and the same time is available by bit packing, while paid two-dimensional macroblocks improve the generic word-RAM upper bound further to O(n^2/log^2(n+2)). None of these establishes o(n) singleton work, and none is a lower bound on what a generic simulation method can achieve. Two-dimensional table simulation is prior art in Grandjean and Jachiet section 8.2 and Appendix 11; the contribution recorded here is only the explicit singleton-query implementation and geometry plus the precisely restricted model analysis, not a new generic simulation method.
records.sc: A retraction of a mis-description in AUDIT-natal-alsaadi-self-composition.md, not a retraction of that construction's own upper bound, which stands. The replacement macroblock bound is charged under the stated RAM model with constant indexed access, and no improved Turing-machine bound follows from it.
records.nt: The corrected positive statement is already catalogued as 4f6bbdaa2d0f0f37 (AUDIT-natal-alsaadi-self-composition.md, 'Self-composition gives a RAM upper bound, not a generic simulation ceiling'); no catalog record carried the retraction notice itself, checked by grep for 'ceiling on generic' and 'incorrectly described' across rule30_research_db.jsonl.

records.t: Largest achievable minimal period of the left neighbour column at each even time period through T=20
records.st: For alternating-centre Rule 30 tori of even time period T, the largest achievable minimal period of col_-1 is 4 at T=4, 6 at T=6, 4 at T=8, 10 at T=10, 6 at T=12, 14 at T=14, 4 at T=16, 6 at T=18 and 10 at T=20. It is a finite census of achievable periods, not a theorem about which periods can occur at larger T, and it does not say anything about full diagrams without a common temporal period. The '2 x prime' reading stated alongside the table is a pre-registered prediction, not a result.

source_context.heading: Registered prediction, written before reading sweep30-22.log

records.t: Exact five-cell indicator for four consecutive zero-phase right-neighbour zeros
records.st: Under an alternating centre normalized so that col_0(t) = t mod 2, with a_n = col_1(T0+2n) the zero-phase right-neighbour samples and x1,x2,... the right-hand cells at the first centre-zero time, the event a_0 = a_1 = a_2 = a_3 = 0 holds exactly when (NOT x1) AND x2 AND x3 AND (x4 OR x5), independently of x6 and x7. records.t: Nested-shift obstruction to inferring a finite-depth EMPTY verdict from an abstract nonexistence theorem
records.st: Two quantifier obstructions block the route from an abstract nonexistence theorem to a finite-depth EMPTY verdict. First, if every full diagram with eventually alternating centre had an eventually periodic neighbour, the period could depend on the diagram, and the already certified periods 4 and 6 show that eventual periodicity does not give one q shared by every accepted diagram, as a fixed-q EMPTY verdict requires. Second, even with a fixed q for all diagrams, the compactness step fails in general: let Y_R be the infinite binary words with at least R zeros between any two ones. Each Y_R contains the periodic word (1 0^R)^omega with infinitely many Diff_1 events; the safety constraints are nested, closed, shift invariant and finite-window at each R, yet the intersection consists of words with at most one 1, none of which has infinitely many Diff_1 events, so accepting witnesses do not survive the limit.
records.sc: An obstruction to a generic inference, stated on an abstract nested family of shifts. It is not a bounded-window proposal for Rule 30, not a Rule 30 counterexample, and asserts nothing about whether a Rule 30 witness exists; it only shows the extra obligations (a uniform period and a finite-depth liveness argument) that any such route must discharge.

records.t: Two-step driven boundary identity pinning three right cells whenever an observation is one
records.st: Let a_j = x(T0+2n,j) for j >= 1 be an even row to the right of an alternating centre, whose next two centre values are zero and one, and let b_j be the row after one step. Then b_1 = a_1 OR a_2, b_2 = a_1 XOR (a_2 OR a_3), and rho_(n+1) = 1 XOR (b_1 OR b_2) = NOT(a_1 OR a_2 OR a_3), by splitting on a_1. Hence every occurrence of rho_(n+1)=1 pins the preceding even row's first three right cells to zero, and a preceding row starting 000uv has next even row starting 1, u, u OR v. This is a genuine OR-dependent return mechanism, but it leaves the unrestricted farther-right tail unspecified, so a finite-state return-map claim must still prove that tail information can be discarded or summarized.

records.t: Pointwise compactness criterion for right-realizability of a prescribed rho
records.st: For one prescribed infinite rho, let E_n be the set of initial right half-rows producing its first n samples. Each E_n is a clopen cylinder set determined by 2n-1 initial cells and E_(n+1) is contained in E_n, so by compactness rho is right-realizable if and only if E_n is nonempty for every n. Consequently every unrealizable specified periodic rho has some finite obstruction.
records.sc: Pointwise compactness for one word at a time. It supplies no uniform bound on cone depth across different primitive periods, so it cannot turn the observed finite obstructions into an all-h theorem.

records.t: Finite-strip temporal periodicity and the missing uniform period-lifting lemma
records.st: Fix a width W and a rho of period h. Recording at each original time the W right cells together with time modulo 2h, and permitting a transition exactly when the internal Rule 30 updates hold, some freely chosen exterior right cell supplies the last update, and the prescribed rho and alternating centre constraints hold, gives at most 2h * 2^W states. Any genuine realization is an infinite path, hence contains a directed cycle, hence yields a temporally periodic realization of this width-W strip whose period is a multiple of 2h and at most 2h * 2^W. However the cycle and its period may change with W and the freely supplied exterior boundary need not extend one more column, so this argument produces no full diagram with one common temporal period and no torus; the missing assertion is a uniform compatible temporal-period lifting lemma, which same-period spatial orbit counts cannot replace.
records.sc: Holds per fixed width W and fixed rho period h. The conclusion is about a strip, not a diagram; the bound 2h * 2^W is a state-count bound with no uniformity in W and no claim that the strip realizations for different W are compatible.

records.t: Conditional consequence of an actually closing eventual-mask suffix graph
records.st: Given a finite collection of sound eventual masks, expand them into their finitely many concrete forbidden words and build the usual finite suffix graph. If the only recurrent components of that graph are the four simple cycles spelling the desired rho necklaces, then every actual driven rho is eventually one of those four periodic sequences: after the common burn-in every actual trace is an infinite path in the finite graph, the condensation is a finite DAG so the path eventually stays in one recurrent component, and a simple cycle makes its labels thereafter periodic. The onset of the final cycle need not have a common bound, since a path may traverse a cycle arbitrarily many times before exiting. Such a certificate would be strictly stronger than the periodic-only target, since it would also exclude the aperiodic neighbour branch under an eventually alternating centre.

records.t: Abstract shift showing a periodic-only theorem need not have a uniform finite-factor proof
records.st: A periodic-only theorem does not inherently admit a uniform finite forbidden-factor proof. Consider the shift that forbids every block 1 0^a 1 0^b 1 with b <= a. Its only periodic point is the all-zero sequence, yet it admits a non-eventually-periodic sequence whose successive zero gaps are 1,2,3,..., and every finite subset of its forbidden words misses (1 0^N)^omega for all sufficiently large N. Hence finite cone obstructions existing for every prohibited periodic word need not have a common length bound.
records.sc: An abstract counterexample about symbolic shifts, not about Rule 30; it shows only that the finite-factor route is not guaranteed to work, and asserts nothing about whether Rule 30's own obstructions happen to be uniformly bounded.

records.t: Rule 90 driven right cone realizes every prescribed observation sequence
records.st: Under Rule 90 the same two driven updates give rho_(n+1) = 1 XOR a_1 XOR a_3, with no three-zero OR pin; the identity was checked against the unchanged numeric_rho(..., rule30=False) on the same 32 five-cell seeds. Choosing all even-indexed initial cells arbitrarily and then each odd-indexed cell recursively matches an arbitrary prescribed rho, constructing an infinite right row realizing every rho, including every primitive period. It follows that no nonempty consistent sample mask can be UNSAT for Rule 90's free right cone, so the OR-dependent Rule 30 masks do not transfer to this control.

records.t: Boundary localization of the Rule 30 pin-cascade filter in the R7 strip automaton
records.st: The Rule 30 pin-cascade identity (r_t = 1 and c_t = 0 => r_{t+1} = 1) is entailed by the strip encoding at every interior modelled column pair, because the identity at column x needs the forward rule to hold at (t+1, x) whose parents include column x+1, and for interior x that column is modelled. At x = R the column R+1 is unmodelled, so the strip does not enforce it and the identity becomes free information. Measured on the rung-0 escape family, violations per column pair are 0 for -1 -> 0, 0 for 0 -> 1, 0 for 1 -> 2, and 4 for 2 -> 3 (= R); the four boundary violations sit at t = 33, 55, 77, 99, spacing 22, which is exactly the escape cycle length, i.e. once per phase slip.
records.sc: Concerns the R7 ladder strip encoding for Rule 30 at R = 3. The 0/0/0/4 counts are a finite measurement on one escape family, not a general count; the localization argument (interior entailed, outermost column not) is general to any fixed-depth strip. Says nothing about whether imposing the constraint changes any emptiness verdict.
records.nt: The prediction going in was that the filter would remove zero states everywhere; the boundary failure refutes that prediction and is what the arm produced. The boundary-pin lemma derived from this observation is already catalogued as r30 record 239a0ddb71f79ffb (RESULTS-ladder-rung1.md Lemma 1) and is therefore not re-extracted here.

source_context.heading: Arm 2 (pin cascade): the one real finding

records.t: Measured effect of the boundary pin on the rung-0 escape family and the R=3 state space
records.st: Imposing the boundary pin col_R(t) = 1 => col_{R-1}(t) = NOT col_R(t+1) on the R7 ladder cuts the reachable state count at R = 3, q = 4 from 12569 to 4915 (about 2.5x) and rejects the rung-0 escape family at letter 34, the first slip, confirmed by threading that family through the constrained automaton. The verdict nevertheless remains NONEMPTY: a new witness appears with cycle length 12 (against 22 for the old family) having 0 boundary-pin violations and 0 wedge violations, so it is admissible rather than a search artifact, and its structure displaces the slip outward into column +3, the new boundary.
records.sc: A single (R, q) = (3, 4) cell of the R7 ladder for p = 2. Shows the pin is a genuine tightening that kills one specific escape family; it does not produce an EMPTY verdict for any p >= 2 and therefore proves nothing about the prize problem. The witness cycle length 12 is BFS-shortest through the accepting SCC, not certified minimal.
records.nt: Soundness regression for the pin at T = 300 exact simulation gives 0 violations for rule 30 at R = 1..4 (150/145/163/140 antecedents) and violations at every antecedent for rule 90 (8/7/13/6). The rule-90 vacuity of this condition is already catalogued as e257d7a581a7fee7.

records.t: The 1-pin filter is not entailed by the strip construction and prunes a large state fraction
records.st: The inverse transduction INV[30](an, a, b) = an XOR (a OR b) is the forward rule at (t, x) solved for s(t, x-1), so the forward rule holds at every column from x_min + 1 up to R - 1 but not at x = R, where no col_{R+1} exists to enforce it. The pin at the rightmost modelled column is therefore free information, refuting the prior claim that it was entailed by construction. Two Rule 30 theorem forms are available, cascade (s(t,x+1)=1 and s(t,x)=0 => s(t+1,x+1)=1) and full (s(t,x+1)=1 => s(t,x) = NOT s(t+1,x+1)), with full implying cascade. Measured pruning at R = 2, k = 2: cascade at Q = 2, w = 10 takes 526 states to 323 (-39%); the full 1-pin at Q = 1, w = 01 takes 472 states to 199 (-58%). A soundness regression driving the true lone-seed letter sequence through the filter at rule 30, (R,k) in {(2,2),(3,2),(4,2),(3,3)}, both modes, gives 0 mismatches, accepted, 0 pin hits, so the constraint never rejects the real diagram.
records.sc: Pruning figures are two single cells at R = 2, k = 2, not a general rate. The soundness regression covers four (R,k) cells against the true lone-seed word only. Establishes that the filter is a genuine tightening of the encoding, not that it decides any p >= 2 case.
records.nt: The two percentages check out against the document's own table: 1 - 323/526 = 38.6% and 1 - 199/472 = 57.8%.

records.t: The pin-augmented ladder has no Rule 90 soundness control
records.st: The pin is rule-specific by design: Rule 90 violates the Rule 30 pin identity at all 7,227 of its ones, so the true Rule 90 lone-seed word is rejected by the filter (accepted = False, hits = 1 at every (R,k) tested) and the Rule 90 automaton collapses to 3 states and returns EMPTY.
