source_context.heading: Addendum 2 — exactly what the degree theorem buys for P3 (dedicated follow-up, verified)

records.t: High exact degree gives no AC^0[p] or approximate-degree lower bound for the center-bit function
records.st: The inference 'deg_2(f_t) = 2t-1, hence by Smolensky f_t needs super-polynomial AC^0[p] size' is FALSE: Smolensky's method requires inapproximability by low-degree polynomials over F_p, not high exact degree. The counterexample is AND_n, which has deg_2 = n, is a single AC^0 gate, and is approximable over F_3 to within 25% by a polynomial of degree <= 4. Two further inferences are also false: high exact degree does not imply high approximate degree (AND_n has n versus Theta(sqrt n) approximate degree, Nisan-Szegedy 1994 / Paturi 1992, and directly for this family deg_2(f_4) = 7 while the 1/3-approximate degree is 5), and low exact degree does not imply easy (PARITY has deg_2 = 1 and is not in AC^0).
records.sc: The counterexamples stand as stated; the blanket phrasing that exact degree gives NO approximate-degree lower bound was marked overstated by the verifier and is withdrawn. This refutes a proposed route from the degree theorem to circuit lower bounds, not the degree theorem itself.

source_context.heading: Addendum 2 — exactly what the degree theorem buys for P3 (dedicated follow-up, verified)

records.t: Provable inertness of the center-bit degree theorem for P3
records.st: The degree theorem is not merely unproved-to-help for P3 but provably inert: P3's input is the INDEX t, of length about log2(t) bits, whereas f_t is a function of 2t+1 unknown bits and the seed column is the single point evaluation a(t) = f_t(delta) at one fixed known input. Lower bounds on the cost of computing f_t over its whole domain therefore carry no implication for the cost of that one evaluation. The consequence that does survive is model-restricted: any algorithm family whose t-th output is forced to have algebraic degree < 2t-1 in the initial window cannot compute f_t, which is now unconditional for all t but bounds computation of the FUNCTION, not of the single-seed column.
records.sc: A structural scope statement about the arbitrary-input family, implying nothing for P1 or P2 either. It does not show P3 is hard or easy; it shows this particular theorem cannot bear on it.
records.nt: Same non-transfer conclusion as the Deva scope correction in docs/rule30/obstruction/BOUNDED-CERTIFICATE-OBSTRUCTIONS.md (r30-bco-deva-decision-tree-nontransfer).

source_context.heading: Addendum 2 — exactly what the degree theorem buys for P3 (dedicated follow-up, verified)

records.t: Ore-relation ladder interpolating between Wolfram P1 and non-2-automaticity
records.st: Let F(x) = sum_(t>=0) a(t) x^t in F_2[[x]] for the single-seed center column a = A051023, and say F admits an Ore relation of order n and height d if there are polynomials P_(-1), P_0, ..., P_n in F_2[x] of degree <= d, not all zero, with P_(-1)(x) + sum_(i=0)^n P_i(x) F(x^(2^i)) = 0 in F_2[[x]]. Put S(n) := 'F admits no Ore relation of order n at any height', and S(n,d) for the height-bounded version. Then S(0) is EXACTLY equivalent to Wolfram P1, because order 0 says F is rational over F_2(x) and a power series over a finite field is rational iff its coefficient sequence is eventually periodic; and the conjunction of all S(n) is exactly equivalent to F being transcendental over F_2(x), hence by Christol 1980 and Christol-Kamae-Mendes France-Rauzy 1980 to a not being 2-automatic. Truncating the relation to the coefficients of x^0..x^(N-1) gives an F_2-linear system that every exact relation satisfies, so a single N with trivial nullspace proves S(n,d): refutation is finite and one-sided, monotone in N.
records.sc: A reduction, not progress on P1: every rung above S(0) is unproved for A051023, and only bounded-height rungs S(n,d) are finitely certifiable. Because non-automaticity implies non-eventual-periodicity, the ladder interpolates strictly between P1 and the stronger target.

source_context.heading: The ladder

records.t: Thue-Morse witnesses that S(0) does not imply S(1)
records.st: The ladder is strict rather than a chain of equivalent restatements: the Thue-Morse series T satisfies x + (1+x)^2 T(x) + (1+x)^3 T(x^2) = 0, an order-1 Ore relation, while Thue-Morse is not eventually periodic. So Thue-Morse satisfies S(0) and fails S(1), an unconditional witness that S(0) does not imply S(1).
records.sc: A witness for the ladder's strictness in general, established on Thue-Morse rather than on A051023; it says nothing about which rungs A051023 satisfies.

source_context.heading: The ladder

records.t: Explicit bounded-width form of the order-one rung NOT-S(1)
records.st: NOT-S(1) unfolds explicitly: there exist a width d and fixed subsets J0, J1 of {0..d} such that sum_(j in J0) a(m-j) XOR sum_(j in J1, m-j even) a((m-j)/2) = 0 for all m > d, that is, a bounded-width F_2-linear relation tying a window of the center column near m to a window near m/2. S(1) asserts that no such relation exists; it is strictly stronger than P1 and strictly weaker than non-2-automaticity.
records.sc: The unfolding is an exact restatement of the order-1 Ore relation; S(1) itself is OPEN for A051023 and only bounded-height rungs S(1,d) have been certified. Novelty is claimed only as a literature-sweep result: no prior statement of S(1) for A051023 was found.

source_context.heading: The genuinely new rung

records.t: Reproduced GF(2) nullity certificates for bounded-height Ore rungs
records.st: An independent re-implementation (own matrix construction and own GF(2) elimination, with a ground-truth prefix assertion) gives: Thue-Morse at (n,d) = (1,2) nullity 0 and at (1,3) nullity 1, recovering the known witness, so the solver is tight rather than permissive; Rule 90 center at (0,0) nullity 1 and at (1,5) nullity 12, caught immediately; and Rule 30 center nullity 0 at (0,50), (0,200), (0,800), certifying S(0,d); at (1,20), (1,60), (1,120), certifying S(1,d); at (2,20), (2,40), certifying S(2,d); and at (3,20), certifying S(3,d). The arm therefore passes the Rule 90 filter, and for a structural reason: Rule 90 is F_2-linear, so by Rowland-Yassawi its columns are 2-automatic and must be caught at some finite order.
records.sc: Each nullity-0 result certifies only the bounded-height rung S(n,d) at the displayed height, never an all-height rung S(n). The wider figures the original agent reported were NOT reproduced here and are recorded as reported only: no Ore relation for A051023 at order <= 12 and heights to 570, order 0 to height 3999, order 1 to height 2665, at N = 32000, all nullity 0, with the solver calibrated by recovering relations for Thue-Morse (1,3), Rule 90 columns 0 and 5, Rule 60, Rule 150 and the regular paperfolding sequence, all at order <= 2 and height <= 6.
records.nt: Reproduction: experiments/overnight-arms/automaticity/ore_check.py.

source_context.heading: Certificates (INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED HERE)

records.t: Order-zero certificates are equivalent to a finite periodicity check
records.st: An order-0 nullity-0 certificate at height d rules out eventual periodicity of the center column for every pair (preperiod q, period p) with max(p, q+p-1) <= d. That is a real unconditional partial result on P1, but it is equivalent to a direct finite periodicity check on the prefix, so the mathematics is elementary and is not new. The new content of the ladder is the order >= 1 rungs, which are not finite periodicity checks and have no elementary restatement.
records.sc: A deliberately deflationary reading of the order-0 data; it does not diminish the higher rungs and makes no claim about them.

source_context.heading: What the order-0 certificates do and do not mean

records.t: Hadamard closure blocks any 'nonlinear rule hence transcendental' argument
records.st: The argument 'Rule 30 is a nonlinear rule, therefore its center series is transcendental' can NEVER work. Rule 30's only nonlinearity is the coefficientwise product c*r, a Hadamard product, and by Sharif-Woodcock (J. London Math. Soc., 1988) algebraic power series over F_2 are closed under Hadamard product, so the algebraic class absorbs exactly the nonlinearity Rule 30 has. What must fail instead is uniformity of degree and height under iteration, and that is where a proof has to live.
records.sc: Excludes a method class, not the target statement: it does not bear on whether the center series is in fact transcendental.

source_context.heading: Two proved negatives worth keeping

records.t: Rowland-Yassawi's linear-CA characterization yields no contradiction for Rule 30
records.st: Rowland-Yassawi does not transfer to this problem. It characterizes p-automatic sequences as columns of LINEAR cellular automata, so if A051023 were 2-automatic it would merely also be a column of some linear CA, which contradicts nothing about Rule 30. The same theorem is, conversely, the structural reason the Rule 90 control must be caught at some finite Ore order, Rule 90 being F_2-linear.
records.sc: A negative result about a proposed proof route only.

source_context.heading: Two proved negatives worth keeping

records.t: Eventually constant residuals are not necessary for a finite 2-kernel
records.st: The tempting handle 'no residual of A051023 is eventually constant, therefore the 2-kernel is infinite' is FALSE. Thue-Morse is an explicit counterexample: it has a finite 2-kernel and no eventually constant residual. So absence of eventually constant residuals carries no implication for the size of the 2-kernel.
records.sc: Refutes an inference, not any measurement of Rule 30's residuals; the observed Rule 30 residual data is unaffected and remains a lower bound only.

source_context.heading: Two proved negatives worth keeping

records.t: Theorem O: no finite prefix of the center column can imply non-automaticity
records.st: Theorem O: for every N, the sequence agreeing with a on [0,N) and 0 thereafter is eventually periodic, hence 2-automatic, with 2-kernel size <= 2N+1. Therefore no property of any finite prefix computed from a alone can imply non-automaticity or non-periodicity, and a count of distinct residuals from a prefix is exactly a lower bound on a complexity function and can never be more. Quantitatively, with A^ker(N) := min{|K_2(b)| : b 2-automatic and b agrees with a on [0,N)}, non-automaticity is equivalent to sup_N A^ker(N) = infinity; A^ker was pinned within a factor 1.08 at N = 2^16, so N terms buy a kernel lower bound of about N/8 and nothing more, ever.
records.sc: The theorem is an argument; the factor-1.08 pinning at N = 2^16 is a single measured adjunct, not part of the theorem. It bounds what finite prefix data can ever deliver and says nothing about Rule 30's true kernel. It is complementary to the ladder, whose rungs S(n,d) are finite computations settling bounded-complexity cases only.
records.nt: Reinterprets, rather than depends on, the catalogued ARM6 result 29b767d4f735d666 ('>= 8191 distinct residuals'): Theorem O says that number is a complexity lower bound and can never be more.

source_context.heading: Companion obstruction (separate lead, also verified "holds")

records.t: Refutation of the polynomial automatic-to-Ore conversion Lemma L
records.st: Lemma L, 'if a is 2-automatic with k states then F admits an Ore relation of order <= poly(log k) and height <= poly(k)', is FALSE in both halves. Height: y = x^n has h(y) = n exactly, since its minimal polynomial over F_2(x) is T - x^n, while N_2(a) = ceil(log_2 n) + 1, so for every k >= 2 the indicator of {2^(k-1)} is a k-state 2-automatic sequence of minimal Ore height exactly 2^(k-1) (Bridy, Example 2.14, arXiv:1604.08241v2, Alg. Number Th. 11 (2017) 685-712). Order: Bridy Example 2.15's Artin-Schreier family y^(2^m) - y = x has N_2(a) = m+2 and deg(y) = 2^m, forcing minimal Ore order m = k-2, linear in k rather than poly(log k). What remains proved is only the exponential conversion order <= m and height <= m*2^(2m), with m the GF(2) dimension of the span of the 2-kernel, so the bounded-height certificates do NOT dominate ARM6's rank-512 measurement.
records.sc: The refutation is generic: it does not prove that a Rule-30-specific conditional bound is impossible. The surviving possibility named in docs/rule30/AUDIT-automaticity-route-scope.md is an independently proved sequence-specific implication 'Automatic(c) => some Ore relation of order <= r0' combined with the all-height statement S(r0), or 'order <= r0 and height <= d0' combined with the finite certificate S(r0,d0); no such bound has been obtained, and a finite certificate S(r0,d0) alone does not prove S(r0).
records.nt: Refutation source read directly: experiments/overnight-arms/frontier_attack/a20_bridy_verification/bridy_verification.md, which quotes Bridy's arXiv v2 primary text. Two further facts from that file that this document does not state: the proved m*2^(2m) bound is valid but not tight, since Bridy's proof of Prop. 2.13 gives k*2^(k+1) in the state-count variable k, and PATH.md row 46 (order <= poly(log k)) and the a6 section 4 write-up (order <= m) state the order half inconsistently. A 2026-09-15 exact-count correction in that file puts the k-state monomial witness at height 2^(k-3) for the copied example while leaving the refutation standing.

source_context.heading: Historical proposed obligation — Lemma L (refuted)

records.t: Uniform Bernoulli is the unique full-support jointly invariant Markov measure at memory one and two
records.st: For m = 1 and m = 2, the unique shift-invariant memory-m Markov measure whose transition probabilities all lie strictly in (0,1) and which satisfies joint (shift, Rule 30) invariance on all blocks of length <= 6 is uniform Bernoulli(1/2). Full support is imposed algebraically by the Rabinowitsch element z * prod_w q_w (1 - q_w) - 1 = 0, whose variety is exactly the solutions with every q_w in (0,1), and a lexicographic Groebner basis of the saturated ideal decides the question outright: m = 1 (2 unknowns, 126 equations, 0.2 s) gives {2q0-1, 2q1-1, z-16} and m = 2 (4 unknowns, 126 equations, 0.9 s) gives {2q00-1, 2q01-1, 2q10-1, 2q11-1, z-256}. Both bases pin every transition probability to exactly 1/2 and neither ideal is <1>, so a full-support solution does exist; uniform Bernoulli is genuinely invariant (classical, from surjectivity), so the classification is exact and not merely an upper bound.
records.sc: Exact rational arithmetic, no RNG, but finite and per-memory: it covers m <= 2 and invariance on blocks of length <= 6 only (a necessary condition in general, which here already forces uniqueness). Memory 3 is unresolved: kill condition K2 fired, with the pre-registered sp.solve route past 40 minutes, the saturated Groebner basis at L = 6 past 110 minutes against 0.9 seconds for m = 2, and a cheaper L = 4 variant still running at write-up (L = 4 would give a weaker theorem than L = 6). There is no uniform-in-m statement, nothing rules out a non-uniform jointly invariant Markov measure of larger memory, the target rigidity statement quantifies over all shift-ergodic measures rather than finite-memory Markov ones, and even full measure rigidity would not settle P2, which concerns the measure-zero single-seed orbit.
records.nt: All mathematical figures match the artifact runs/overnight/ergodic/saturate.json exactly. That artifact used to carry "uniform_satisfies_gb": false for both m, which never contradicted the document: markov_saturate.py substituted q = 1/2 into each basis element but never substituted the saturation variable z, so the elements z-16 and z-256 could not vanish and the flag was unconditionally false. Patched 2026-09-16: z is now pinned by solving the saturation element at q = 1/2, which yields z = 16 at m = 1 and z = 256 at m = 2 from the relation rather than from a hardcoded constant, and the vacuous any(... for _ in [0]) wrapper is gone. The artifact was regenerated and the flag now reads true for both memories, agreeing with the document. Every field is unchanged except the wall-clock "seconds", which moved from 0.2 to 0.1 at m = 1 and from 0.9 to 0.6 at m = 2; the statement quotes the document's 0.2 s and 0.9 s, and a timing is a fact about a machine rather than a result. Cross-checks reported in the document: uniform Bernoulli verified invariant by direct substitution out to block length 9 (runs/overnight/ergodic/main.json records verified_to 9 for the q = 1/2 solution), the identity CA returns zero constraints, and the degenerate m = 2 component-enumeration solutions such as {q01 = 0, q11 = 1} sit on the boundary q in {0,1} and are exactly what the saturation removes.

records.t: Bernoulli-level joint invariance does not separate Rule 30 from Rule 90
records.st: In the one-parameter Bernoulli(p) family the joint-invariance constraints have solutions exactly {p = 0, p = 1/2} for the Rule 90 control, matching Rule 30's solution set {p = 0, p = 1/2}. So Bernoulli-level data does NOT separate Rule 30 from the additive control, and the separation the repository's program demands would have to come from elsewhere; this arm does not claim it.
records.sc: Figure is prose-only: it comes from experiments/overnight-arms/ergodic/markov_probe.py, whose output is not among the cited artifacts runs/overnight/ergodic/{main.json, saturate.json}, and no artifact carrying it was located, so the solver output behind it was not inspected. Beyond that, it is a control computation over the single-parameter Bernoulli family only and does not bear on the memory-m classification, where the Rule 90 comparison was not run.

source_context.heading: Result (VERIFIED, exact rational arithmetic)

records.t: Explicit logarithmic counting rate for zeros and ones of the center column
records.st: Theorem A: for the single-seed center column a(t) = s(t,0) (OEIS A051023) and every T >= 1, N_1(T) := #{t <= T : a(t) = 1} >= floor(log2(T+4)) - 1 and N_0(T) := #{t <= T : a(t) = 0} >= floor(log2(T+6)) - 2. Equivalently, a 0-run starting at time T has length <= 2*ceil(T/2)+1 and a 1-run starting at time T has length <= 2*ceil((T+1)/2)+2. This strictly upgrades the standing in-repo corollary, that the column is not eventually constant and hence has infinitely many 0s and 1s, from a qualitative statement to an explicit rate.
records.sc: Unconditional but very weak: logarithmic where the truth is plainly linear. It does not bound the density, does not show the limit exists, and does not separate Rule 30 from a sequence that is 1 only at powers of two. It is assembled on the repository's sharp-horizon result, and the proof was NOT independently re-derived in this document; only its conclusions were checked numerically, with no violation of either inequality for any T < 2^16. The accompanying meta-claim that log T is the exact ceiling of the entire method class producing it was rejected by the verifier as not following and is withdrawn.
records.nt: The verifier reproduced the sharp-horizon input by independent brute force and did not break the counting bound; its 'overstated' verdict attached to the withdrawn meta-claim, not to Theorem A. The sharp-horizon premise is cited in prose and is deliberately not wired as a depends_on, since the catalogued sharp-horizon record r30-bwh-sharp-refuted is a different (refuted) object.

source_context.heading: PROVED byproduct — Theorem A (explicit counting rate)

records.t: Observed longest runs in the first 2^20 steps of the center column
records.st: Over 2^20 steps of the single-seed center column the longest 0-run is 19 and the longest 1-run is 22, and no violation of the Theorem A counting inequalities or of either run-length bound occurs for any T < 2^16 (independent code and indexing). The true run behaviour is therefore far better than Theorem A's bound, which is logarithmic where the observed truth is plainly linear.
records.sc: Exact integer computation over a finite prefix only (2^20 steps for the run extremes, 2^16 for the inequality check); it is finite evidence consistent with Theorem A, not a proof of any sharper bound, and it says nothing about longer runs later in the column.

source_context.heading: PROVED byproduct — Theorem A (explicit counting rate)

records.t: Universal depth-four diagonal density pinning and its sharpness at depth five
records.st: Theorem 2: in the coordinates D_k[t] = s(t, B+t-k) for a finite row with right endpoint B, which satisfy the exact diagonal recursion D_k[t] = D_k[t-1] XOR (D_(k-1)[t-1] OR D_(k-2)[t-1]) with D_(-1) == 0 and D_0 == 1, for EVERY finite configuration D_k has period dividing 8 and density exactly 1/2 for k = 1, 2, 3, 4. The result is SHARP: at k = 5 exactly 16 of the 32 boundary patterns give density different from 1/2, the full k = 5 distribution over all 32 patterns being 8 patterns at 3/8, 16 at 1/2 and 8 at 5/8, with the single seed itself at D_5 = 3/8. Mechanism (odd-gate lemma): if the gate G_k = D_(k-1) OR D_(k-2) is eventually periodic with ODD weight over a period, unrolling the XOR flips the parity every period, so D_k has exactly twice that period and density exactly 1/2.
records.sc: The universal k = 1..4 statement quantifies over EVERY finite configuration and rests on the odd-gate lemma, not on a finite sample; the k = 5 sharpness is an exhaustive sweep over all 32 boundary patterns. It extends the repository's pinned diagonals (which covered k = 0, 1, 2) by two, unconditionally, in the right cone; it is the right-cone counterpart of an observation in NKS p.871 proved for the left side as Rowland 2006 Prop. 2, the density corollary and the depth-4 sharpness being the new content. It pins diagonals at fixed depth only and does not reach the center column at diagonal t.
records.nt: The adversarial verifier returned 'holds' after reimplementing the sweep by direct simulation rather than the diagonal recursion, and the document re-checked it on a third implementation after finding and correcting an indexing bug (a shrinking row array read as fixed width): D_0 density 1 as a sanity gate, k = 1..4 exactly 1/2 for all tested rows including the single seed, single-seed D_5 = 3/8, and the k = 5 distribution matching the claimed 16 exceptions exactly.

source_context.heading: PROVED — Theorem 2 (universal depth-4 diagonal pinning, and it is sharp)

records.t: Invariance over all configurations cannot force center density one half
records.st: The all-zeros configuration and the checkerboard (alternating) configuration are both exact Rule 30 fixed points, verified by direct computation: all-zeros has every column of density 0, while the checkerboard's odd-phase columns are identically 1 (density 1) and its even-phase columns identically 0. Consequently the set of F-invariant measures contains members giving the center cell probability 0 and probability 1, so sup{nu(x_0 = 1) : F_*nu = nu} = 1 and inf{nu(x_0 = 1) : F_*nu = nu} = 0. Since every weak-* limit point of the seed orbit's empirical row measures is F-invariant, NO argument built from the local rule plus invariance alone can force the value 1/2. This is a Rule-30-internal version of the Rule 90 control, ruling the family out from inside without appealing to another rule.
records.sc: The two fixed points are verified by direct computation; the obstruction itself is an argument. It rules out arguments using invariance over ALL configurations only. The natural repair, restricting to invariant measures supported on the ORBIT CLOSURE of the single seed, is NOT closed off: the agent claimed to close it, its adversarial verifier returned 'overstated' and identified that step as broken, so the repair remains open and arguments restricted to the seed's orbit closure are not excluded.
records.nt: Non-separating as expected: a verifier's linear program found the invariance bound gives max cell density 1.0 and min 0.0 for Rule 90 as well as Rule 30 at window widths 1..6, which is correct behaviour for an obstruction, since it rules a method class out for both rules. Consistent with the ergodic arm (r30-erg-markov-memory2-uniqueness): uniqueness there held only after full support was imposed, and these fixed points are exactly the degenerate boundary solutions the Rabinowitsch saturation removes.

source_context.heading: PROVED obstruction 1 — invariance alone cannot pin the density (with an OPEN repair)

records.t: Measured growth of the longest alternating block in the single-seed diagram
records.st: Whether the checkerboard lies in the seed's orbit closure is unresolved; it does if and only if arbitrarily long alternating blocks occur in the diagram. The longest alternating substring per row of the single-seed diagram measures 6, 8, 11, 15, 13, 13, 13 at t = 50, 100, 250, 500, 1000, 2000, 4000, against row widths up to 8001. That is consistent with logarithmic growth (log2(8001) is about 13), hence with unboundedness, hence with the checkerboard being in the orbit closure.
records.sc: Measurement, not proof, and the document records the question as OPEN: seven sampled rows to t = 4000, non-monotone within the sample, and proving unbounded alternating blocks is plausibly as hard as the surrounding problem. The consistency with logarithmic growth is an observation about seven data points and supports no rate claim.
records.nt: Bears directly on whether the open repair to obstruction 1 (r30-pss-invariance-cannot-pin-density) can succeed: if the checkerboard is in the orbit closure, restricting to the closure does not remove it.

source_context.heading: PROVED obstruction 1 — invariance alone cannot pin the density (with an OPEN repair)

records.t: The exact-density diagonal frontier provably stops short of the center column
records.st: Every diagonal in both cones of the single-seed diagram has a provable exact rational density: the right cone is purely periodic with power-of-two period (Rowland 2006 Lemma 2) and the left cone eventually periodic (Rowland 2006 p.15 citing Jen 1990 Thm 4). Exact densities are therefore abundant, but the center column is not among them: the universal pinning holds only to depth 4 (every finite row, k = 1..4, density exactly 1/2, period dividing 8) and is SHARP at k = 5, where the single seed itself is the explicit counterexample at density 3/8. Combined with the repository's measured ~2.4*log2(t) reach wall, the exact-density region provably does not extend to the center column at diagonal t.
records.sc: The conclusion depends on the repository's measured ~2.4*log2(t) reach wall, which is an input here and was not re-derived; the pinning and sharpness parts are the document's own Theorem 2. It closes the exact-density route to the center column and says nothing about approximate or asymptotic density arguments.

source_context.heading: PROVED obstruction 2 — the exact-density frontier does not reach the center

records.t: Maximum pinned-cut pre-period over reachable fibres exceeds the scale from n = 10
records.st: Over all 2^n binary sources W of length n and both cut values c in {2,3}, the maximum pre-period max_W tau(W,c) of the pinned-cut fibre recursion G_c is at least n + 9 at every n = 10..22; it is n + 9 or n + 10 at n = 10..15 and between 2n and 2n + 2 at n = 20..22, with measured (tau, tau - n) of (20,10) and (19,9) at n = 10 rising to (46,24) and (45,23) at n = 22 for c = 2 and c = 3. The least-squares slope of max tau over the pre-registered range n = 10..18 is 1.65 (c = 2) and 1.62 (c = 3) against the pre-registered kill line 0.9, and 2.26 and 2.25 over n = 10..22, so the pre-registered kill (K2) fires and no bound tau <= beta n + C with beta < 1 fits the maxima on this range.
records.sc: Finite and exhaustive: all 2^n wide sources, n = 10..22, both tails, two independent implementations. n = 10..18 is the pre-registered range and n = 19..22 supplementary. The kill is a finite-range statement about slopes; it excludes no beta < 1 asymptotically, only that no such bound is visible on the reachable fibres through n = 22. It says nothing about RW, (RW-alpha), SEP or PT2, which the document states are untouched.

records.t: Soundness of restricting RW to sources drawn from the actual-right language
records.st: Advancing one rho coordinate is a two-step time shift that preserves the centre phase, so a factor of a realizable trace at any offset is itself a realizable prefix and R is factor-closed. For the hypothetical period-two counterexample the endpoint is a genuine right trace beyond an artificial finite prefix, so at every sufficiently large scale the block W = e[n:2n] and its forced continuation Q_n(W) = e[2n:3n+2] are factors of a realizable trace. RW therefore only needs to exclude sources W in R_n whose forced continuation stays in R while the cut stays constant, and any superset L of R gives an upper bound on that joint run.
records.sc: A soundness argument for the restriction, uniform in n; it does not prove RW on R and does not bound the artificial prefix or the scale beyond which the trace is genuine. Membership in R is decided exactly by one CaDiCaL query on the complete right light cone.

source_context.heading: 1. Objects and why the restriction is sound

records.t: Exact decomposition of the shortened cut into a seam block and the inherited cut
records.st: For |W| = n, f = WQ, a binary prepend v of length k and a truncation of the last d endpoint symbols, the cut of the shortened word decomposes exactly as P^(n-k) I(v f[:-d]) = [P^(n-k) I(vW)] . [(P^n I(f))[:-d]], under the hypotheses 0 <= k < n and |f| - d >= n, with the first bracket holding exactly 2k cells. The proof applies the iterated rotated-Peel identity to vf, giving sigma^(2k) P^(n-k) I(vf) = P^n I(f); prefix causality identifies its first 2k output cells with P^(n-k) I(vW) and allows deleting the last d endpoint symbols and hence the last d cut cells. These statements hold for arbitrary finite words, and the verifier's two instances are controls rather than the proof.
records.sc: A uniform identity for arbitrary finite words under the stated hypotheses. It is a decomposition, not a descent: it identifies the remaining obligation without discharging it. The verifier checks it on two explicit words only.
records.nt: guarded-rw-seam-audit.json records exact_seam_plus_inherited_cut_identity true for both witnesses, with the cut decompositions 313333 = 31 . 3333 and 33222213 = 33 . 222213.

source_context.heading: 2. An exact descent and its complete missing condition

records.t: The seam condition is exactly what remains of the rotated-wedge descent
records.st: If the old cut is entirely constant c, every inherited cell of the decomposition already equals c, so the complete new obligation of the descent is precisely (SEAM): P^(n-k) I(vW) = c^(2k). There are at most two prepends to consider when k = 1 and at most four when k = 2, but each seam depends on the full ordered W, and a counterexample minimal in n and then in r would have to reject every grammar-admissible prepend. Nothing proved in the report forces one prepend to succeed.
records.sc: An exact reduction of the descent step to one condition; it does not prove (SEAM) and does not establish that any prepend passes. The descent step itself assumes the grammar condition that vW avoids 11 and 22222, which is what makes the complete new word admissible.

source_context.heading: 2. An exact descent and its complete missing condition

records.t: Bounded gap between the final two nonfinal pulls in the admissible grammar
records.st: For a complete word f = WQ of length 2n + r + 2 that avoids the factors 11 and 22222 and ends in 12a, let d be the distance from the final nonfinal pull to the preceding pull. Whenever that preceding pull exists, 2 <= d <= 5, and for n >= 4 it necessarily exists, because the final 1 cannot be the first 1 after a prefix longer than four symbols. The descent then sets k = ceil((d-r)/3) and r' = r + 3k - d in {0,1,2}, so k is 0, 1 or 2; when k = 0, truncating the last d symbols preserves n and lowers the residue.
records.sc: A grammar-level bound on words avoiding 11 and 22222 and ending in 12a, uniform in n for n >= 4. It fixes the shape of the descent step but supplies no seam.

source_context.heading: 2. An exact descent and its complete missing condition

records.t: Two exact counterexamples to the four-guard seam lemma

source_context.heading: 3. Four cut guards do not supply the seam

records.t: A descent seeded by an actual endpoint tail reaches no uniform base case
records.st: If an actual endpoint tail e satisfies I(e)_t = c for every t >= T, its true preceding symbols supply a successful seam whenever the smaller scale still has 2(n-k) >= T, and the rotated identity then makes the entire smaller cut constant, with the grammar persisting beyond the finite artificial prefix. But the descent stops at an orbit-dependent threshold determined by T and that prefix, whose sizes are unbounded across hypothetical counterexamples, so descending to these unknown base cases supplies no uniform contradiction. The remaining possible induction must either prove (SEAM) from stronger history information or reduce the unknown initial constant-tail threshold itself.
records.sc: An argument about why one specific route to a base case fails; it does not refute a descent using all cut constraints. The document's 2026-09-15 update records that the first alternative, stronger history information, is closed by RESULTS-SEAM-HISTORY-GUARDS.md, while the second alternative, reducing the initial constant-tail threshold, is untouched.

source_context.heading: 4. Why an actual prior prefix does not finish the induction

records.t: The period-two application needs RW only on the endpoint language avoiding two factors
records.st: The exact right-trace identity excludes both 11 and 00000 from the even-time right-neighbour bit trace under an alternating centre, and since endpoint symbols 1 and 2 encode right bits 1 and 0, the actual endpoint avoids 11 and 22222. The finite-rank reduction prepends only finitely many endpoint 2s and the first-infinite-tail reduction then takes a suffix, so the resulting endpoint retains both forbidden-factor conditions beyond a finite prefix even though it need not be an actual right trace at its origin. Selecting the DLP scale beyond that prefix makes the entire word f = WQ, including W, avoid both factors, so it suffices for the period-two application to exclude RW witnesses in this smaller language, whereas the stronger published RW statement allows an arbitrary binary W.
records.sc: A valid use of actual-right constraints after the artificial prefix; it does not impose them on arbitrary queues, and it weakens what must be proved rather than proving anything. The finite prefix length is not bounded here.

source_context.heading: 1. The narrower language supplied by an actual counterexample

records.t: Run inheritance under the two-symbol shift of a source word
records.st: Lemma (L1): if rho_c(W) >= 2 then Q_c(Sh_c W) = Q_c(W)[2:] and rho_c(Sh_c W) = rho_c(W) - 2, where Sh_c(W) := W[1:] . Q_c(W)[:2]. The proof is by the light cone: I(e)_t reads only e[ceil((t-1)/2) .. t] by induction from the diagonal recurrence, so Sh_c W sitting at e[n+1 .. 2n+1] has as its forcing equations the scale-n equations at rows u+2, and admissibility transfers because rows 0 and 1 are covered by the hypothesis rho >= 2.
records.sc: A uniform lemma, not a census result: it holds at every scale n and both tails c in {2,3}. It was asserted computationally on 84,744 pairs at n = 18 as a check, but the statement is proved rather than observed.

source_context.heading: 2. The two lemmas `[U]`

records.t: The literal seam condition is equivalent to run inheritance from the prepended word
records.st: Lemma (L2): for vW' admissible with W'[-3:] hard-core, P^(n-1) I(vW') = (c,c) holds if and only if rho_c(vW'[:-2]) >= 2 and Sh_c(vW'[:-2]) = W'. The reason is that the seam cells are run cells 0 and 1 of S = vW'[:-2], and both equal c exactly when W'[-2:] are S's H-forced symbols with passing pins.
records.sc: A uniform lemma at every scale, restricted to vW' admissible with the last three symbols of W' hard-core. Asserted computationally on 4,642 words over 9,022 seam evaluations at n = 18 as a check; the statement itself is proved.

source_context.heading: 2. The two lemmas `[U]`

records.t: Orphan bound above the previous scale's run and the uniform two-step run floor
records.st: Corollary (C1): a seam-passing prepend v forces rho_c(W') + 2 = rho_c(vW'[:-2]), which is at most D_(n-1)(c), so every W' with rho_c(W') > D_(n-1)(c) - 2 is an orphan admitting no seam-passing prepend, and a k = 2 step is two k = 1 steps by the cut decomposition identity. Lemma (L1) further gives the uniform run floor D_n(c) >= D_(n-1)(c) - 2, each parent with rho >= 2 having an in-grammar child; this is proved, not observed. Strictness of the floor is only computed, holding at 54 of the 60 rows n = 4..18 over both grammars and tails, the six exceptions being narrow c = 3 at n = 4, 10 and 11, narrow c = 2 at n = 18, wide c = 2 at n = 13 and wide c = 3 at n = 4, five of which still carry top orphans.
records.sc: The orphan bound and the run floor are uniform in n; strictness of the floor is a finite computation on n = 4..18 only. The equivalence of universally quantified (SEAM) with RW is noted as a triviality rather than a theorem, RW implying (SEAM) vacuously and the converse being the report's descent plus an unstated n <= 3 base.
records.nt: The document corrects an earlier wording: D_n >= D_(n-1) - 2 together with D_n >= 0 forces the floor to be strict at infinitely many n, but does not force D_n to increase; increase infinitely often would need D_n unbounded, which is measured and not proved.

records.t: A uniform-in-n guard at any level is equivalent to a bounded deepest run
records.st: Given (L1), (L2) and (C1), the guard (G_m) that at every scale n >= n0 every admissible W' with rho_c(W') >= m has a seam-passing prepend is equivalent to sup_n D_n(c) < m. By (C1) such a W' has rho_c(W') <= D_(n-1)(c) - 2, so D_n(c) >= m forces D_n(c) <= D_(n-1)(c) - 2 and with the (L1) floor gives D_n(c) = D_(n-1)(c) - 2 exactly; from n0 the run then falls by two per scale until D_n(c) < m, and once D_(n-1)(c) < m the guard forbids D_n(c) >= m again, while conversely D_n(c) < m at every large n makes (G_m) vacuous. This is (RW-alpha) at alpha = 0: it implies RW at every n >= m-2, whereas RW is consistent with the measured D_n(c) near 0.6 n and implies no constant bound. The lead of the first draft is therefore a closing reduction, not a route.

source_context.heading: 5. Route eliminated, the uniform guard, and scope

records.t: Identifying the endpoint symbols 1 and 3 in all but the last position is a quotient of the process
records.st: Lemma: let u and u' be binary words of length p with endpoint states (C,D) and (C',D'), where C has length p+1 with C[p] the last symbol and D has length p. If C[p] = C'[p], C[i] ~ C'[i] for i < p and D[j] ~ D'[j] for j < p, where ~ identifies 1 with 3, then for every s the states after us and u's are identical, and uv is in L_m(c) if and only if u'v is, for every v, m and c. The proof is that in Endpoint.peek the stored entries are read only as first arguments of CONE, with new_column[i] = CONE[C[i+1]][new_column[i+1]] and new_diagonal[j+1] = CONE[D[j]][new_diagonal[j]], and CONE[1] = CONE[3], both being (3,2,1,0), so the chains coincide entry by entry. Hence S_m(p) <= E13(p) for every m, c and horizon, and the reduced process is a deterministic automaton on reduced states.
records.sc: A uniform lemma, proved for every prefix length p, every m and both tails. It establishes only the upper bound S_m(p) <= E13(p); the matching equality is the separate finite measurement. It says nothing about whether distinct reduced states are separated at large p.
records.nt: The document concludes that the one-sided closure CONE[1] = CONE[3] of RESULTS-DIAGONAL-MEMORY.md section 8 is a full quotient of the endpoint process, compressing by a factor 0.945.

The m = 2 count at c = 2 and the m = 3 counts fall short by 1 to 5 at horizon 9 and reach the same values at horizon 12. The regular control, the same count for hard-core membership, is 3 at every p as it must be.

source_context.heading: 2. Result

records.t: Pre-registered regularity kill and the resulting DFA state lower bounds
records.st: The pre-registered kill (REG-m) fires for all six (m,c) pairs with m <= 3: S_m(11) > S_m(10), S_m(11) >= 2 S_m(8) and S_m(11) >= 0.25 E(11), with ratio S/E of 0.938 to 0.945. Consequently any DFA for L_1(c) needs at least 701 states at prefix length 11, and the extension to p = 12 and 13 at suffix horizon 7 gives E(12), E(13) = 1329, 2376 and E13(12), E13(13) = 1257, 2255, with S_1 = 1256, 2254 at c = 2 and 1257, 2255 at c = 3, so the lower bound is at least 2254 at p = 13 (2255 for c = 3, and for c = 2 at horizon 11), and at least 2192 for every m <= 3. The c = 2 shortfall of one is the horizon rather than the quotient: the unseparated pair 111112122222 against 112211222222 at p = 12 separates at suffix length 12 and the p = 13 pair at length 11.
records.sc: This is finite evidence, not a proof of non-regularity. Finite, p <= 13, horizons 9 at p <= 11 and 7 at p = 12, 13; the p = 12, 13 extension is post hoc and not in the pre-registration. Non-regularity of L_1 would not transfer to L_m in any case, and even a proved non-regular L_m would not exclude a regular over-approximation of the survivors that is empty at the required depth.

source_context.heading: Nerode residuals of the pooled run language are the endpoint states modulo `CONE[1] = CONE[3]`

records.t: Growth rate of the reduced endpoint state count with prefix length
records.st: The reduced endpoint state count E13(p) grows by a factor of 1.78 to 1.79 per symbol from p = 8, and by 1.67 to 1.87 below that, and again by 1.79 per symbol at p = 12 and 13. Since the residuals track E13 with no plateau, each further prefix length multiplies the DFA lower bound for L_1(c) by about 1.77, and the residual-to-state ratio S/E is 0.94 to 0.95 from p = 6 and 0.949 at p = 12, 13.

records.t: Periodic drive prefixes are pairwise separated with class counts doubling in the suffix horizon
records.st: The number of horizon-q Nerode classes of L_1(c) among the prefixes 1^m with m <= 1100 is 1, 4, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024 for q = 1..9, and all 1100 prefixes are distinct at q = 10, for both tails. These families are therefore finite evidence for an infinite pairwise-separated family rather than against one, and a proof along 1^m would show that for each k some suffix of length k has membership of period about 2^(k+1) along m.

The document explicitly retracts its earlier reading: the exact periodicity of these prefixes' own membership sequences, with periods 28, 28, 2, 1, 84, 28, 84, 155 for the eight drives and 1 or 4, 16, 16, 32, 32, 128 for the 2^m v family on m <= 3000, says nothing about their Nerode classes, since every a^m has the same membership in {a^n b^n}.

records.t: The single-defect source family supplies unboundedly many pairwise-separated prefixes
records.st: In the single-defect family 2^a 1 2^(p-a-1), the prefixes whose defect sits at depth a <= 4, 6, 8 at p = 12, 20, 28 share one reduced state, the state forgetting a lone early defect once it lies below about a quarter of the depth, with a_max = floor((p+5)/4) for 8 <= p <= 40, and every pair of distinct reduced states in the family is separated in L_1(c) within 3 steps at those three p. Unboundedly many pairwise-separated prefixes is exactly what a non-regularity proof of this shape needs.

The family does not account for the 1.77^p residual count, which would need about 0.8 bits per symbol, though a proof of that shape does not need it to. The separator length grows with p, passing 6 by p = 34.

source_context.heading: 4. What a no-go theorem needs, and two families read twice

records.t: The two remaining routes to a non-regularity theorem for the run language
records.st: L_m(c) is regular exactly when its Nerode classes are finite, and by the quotient lemma together with the data the classes at length p are the reduced states for p <= 11. A proof of non-regularity therefore needs either (a) separation of distinct reachable reduced states at every p together with E13(p) tending to infinity, or (b) an explicit infinite family of pairwise-separated prefixes. Neither is proved; the statement left is the separation lemma for all p, and a proof would have to track a state difference up the anti-diagonal chain through the masking cases CONE[1] = CONE[3] as first argument and CONE[1][x] = CONE[2][x] for x in {0,1}.
records.sc: An open target, not a result. What is proved is only the direction that matters for certificates: a finite-state invariant of the endpoint process can see only the reduced state, and through p = 11 the run language sees all of it. Nothing here bears on RW, (RW-alpha), SEP or PT2 except as a bound on what a bounded-memory certificate can express.

records.t: Carry-automaton completeness of the Rule 90 lone-seed context sets
records.st: Write z(t,x)=P((t+x)/2,(t-x)/2) for the lone-seed Rule 90 diagram, with P(a,b)=[a>=0 and b>=0 and (a AND b)=0] and z=0 when t+x is odd. For any context radius K, every nonzero radius-K context has an anchor offset j in [-K,K] with z(t,x+j)=1, and is generated by reading the disjoint digit pairs (u_i,v_i) in {00,10,01} of u=(t+x+j)/2, v=(t-x-j)/2. The least-significant-digit carry automaton that keeps, for every d in [-K,K], the two signed carries initially (d,-d) plus an overlap flag, together with u mod M, v mod M and 2^i mod M for M=lcm(T,q), has finitely many states and its breadth-first transition closure enumerates exactly the set of radius-K contexts occurring anywhere on the diagram, at every time and site; termination pads with 00 until both carries are fixed at 0 or -1, and the shifted predicate is one exactly when both carries are zero and no overlap occurred.
records.sc: Applies to the lone-seed Rule 90 source diagram and its radius-K same-time contexts under lookup clocks t mod T, x mod q. It fixes the input alphabet for the factor SAT encodings only; it makes no statement about Rule 30, about which lookups exist, or about other source diagrams. Requiring both carries zero is essential: overlap flags alone would wrongly accept a negative argument such as P(-1,0).
records.nt: Closure, not the representative checks, establishes the all-time quantifier; the document says so explicitly. An independent direct row evolution through time 511 reproduced the closure's context sets at radii 1 through 5 with counts 154,238,329,434,560, reported as a diagnostic cross-check only. records.t: Unique left completion of a checked right quadrant to a full two-sided Rule 30 diagram
records.st: If a field U defined at every t>=0, x>=0 satisfies the Rule 30 local equation U(t+1,x)=F30(U(t,x-1),U(t,x),U(t,x+1)) at every t>=0, x>=1, then the recursion U(t,x-1) = U(t+1,x) XOR (U(t,x) OR U(t,x+1)) applied at x=0,-1,-2,... and every t>=0 is the unique left extension: at each spatial step the required right columns already exist at every time, and the step enforces the Rule 30 equation at the current column. Together with the checked quadrant this defines a full Rule 30 diagram on t>=0, x in Z whose initial row is x -> U(0,x) and which forward determinism reproduces. Hence only local updates at x>=1 need to be checked, with no assumption of periodic farther columns and no finite strip boundary.

records.t: Clock-free state bound for the residue observation subsequence of a coordinate automaton
records.st: For a coordinate automaton with N core states reading synchronized binary digits of (t,x) most significant first, a power-of-two temporal lookup clock T=2^a and any fixed residue r, the neighbour subsequence v(n)=U(T*n+r,1) is generated by an MSB automaton with the same N core states: its transitions while reading n are the time-axis transitions delta_(bit,0), the fixed low coordinate suffix (r,1) is folded into the output function, and the spatial lookup residue is always 1 mod q, so neither lookup clock contributes a state factor. Consequently the direct MSB period bound applies with N, not N*T*q, giving the conservative constants H=2^N and P=2^N*lcm(1,...,N), and an exact inequality v(n)!=v(n+P) at some n>=H proves v aperiodic.
records.sc: Requires T to be a power of two and the observed spatial coordinate to be fixed at 1; it says nothing about odd lookup periods, where a residue lift is needed, and nothing about whether any Rule 30 realization of such an automaton exists. It supplies the observable test only.

records.t: Output-label partition criterion for eventual periodicity of a fixed MSB core
records.st: Fix an N-state MSB core with a leading-zero root self-loop, put H=2^N and P=2^N*lcm(1,...,N), let q(n) be the state after reading n from the root, and compute the exact finite relation E = { (q(n),q(n+P)) : n>=H }. An output function tau defines an eventually periodic sequence if and only if tau(a)=tau(b) on every edge (a,b) of E, equivalently if and only if tau is constant on each connected component of the undirected equality graph of E. In particular, if every edge of E is diagonal then no output function whatsoever on that core is aperiodic, and the core is excluded by fixing only its two time-axis transitions at each reachable state, independently of the low suffix and of all output labels.
records.sc: The transition table is fixed in the statement and is not inferred from a bounded prefix of any sequence; the criterion decides output labelings of one given core, not existence of a Rule 30 realization. E is computed by an exact MSB addition product retaining the two core states, a carry into the already read high digits, the digit position in P after an arbitrary common leading-zero prefix, and the significant length of n capped at N+1.
records.nt: Agreement with an independently implemented direct-MSB classifier on all 1,978 output labelings of all 252 padded transition tables at one through three states (2+32+1944 labelings over 1+8+243 tables), from direct-dfa-observation-regression.json. records.t: Exact zero-set observation condition guarded only by time-axis transitions
records.st: For a coordinate DFA with transition function delta, output lookup g[p][s][q] and time clock T=2^a, define once for all candidate cores V[p,q] = g[p][1 mod spatial][delta(q,2*(p mod 2)+1)]. Fix a proposed time-axis core on its reachable states, take its exact MSB addition closure of endpoint pairs (q(n),q(n+P)) for n>=H with H=2^N and P=2^N*lcm(1,...,N), and propagate each pair through the upper a-1 suffix bits of phase p leaving the final spatial-one transition unevaluated, giving pre-final pairs (q,r). The residue subsequence u_p(n)=s(T*n+p,1) is aperiodic if and only if V[p,q]!=V[p,r] for at least one such pair, so the zero-set observation condition is exactly the disjunction over p and pre-final pairs of (clock[p]=0 AND V[p,q]!=V[p,r]). Guarding this by the proposed time-axis transitions alone is sound: those transitions preserve the reachable axis set and every pre-final pair, and the odd-symbol transitions are arbitrary because their entire effect is already represented by V. The SAT encoding of V uses two conditional equivalence clauses per possible target of the one-hot transition, so V takes exactly the stated value for every primary assignment and is not a relaxation.

records.t: Rule 30 necessity of a one in the eventual centre period of any R1 countermodel
records.st: If the centre column of a Rule 30 right half-diagram is eventually zero, then the neighbour satisfies r(t+1) = r(t) OR s(t,2) and is therefore eventually nondecreasing, hence eventually constant and not aperiodic. Any R1 countermodel must consequently carry a one in its eventual centre period. For each canonical axis this is imposed exactly and without new variables: the left projection of the exact endpoint relation lists every state reached at coarse times beyond the uniform onset bound, and folding the low time-phase suffix through the already defined composed centre outputs gives a guarded disjunction that some actual tail state has centre label one.
records.sc: Rule 30-specific: the monotonicity primitive fails for Rule 90 because F90(0,1,0)=0, so the prune must not be applied to the Rule 90 control. The helper enforces Rule 30 and a power-of-two lookup period explicitly and must not be used for an odd-factor lookup period without its residue lift. It prunes candidates and establishes neither R1 nor P1.

records.t: Uniform nonexistence of q14/T4 dyadic-reset Rule 90-source Rule 30 factors at every radius
records.st: No Rule 30 factor exists whose finite input features come from the lone-seed Rule 90 diagram at any fixed finite collection of binary spatial/time scales, with external lookup clocks t mod 4 and x mod 14, an eventually periodic centre that is zero at phase 3 on its tail, and a neighbour that copies or complements the Rule 90 neighbour at times t=3 mod 4. records.t: Exact subset construction deciding right-surjectivity of memory-two temporal pair graphs
records.st: For a memory-two temporal pair graph whose symbols are (L_t,M_t) encoded 2L_t+M_t, whose vertices remember two consecutive symbols and whose edges E_p(a,b,c) record an overlapping triple at time phase p mod 2, right-surjectivity is decided exactly by a subset construction retaining the source vertex, the time phase, and all possible pairs of current/next right bits, which has at most 2*12*15=360 nonempty states. Every source edge filters both local updates and the target triple. An empty subset supplies a finite unliftable source path; absence of empty subsets gives a lift for every finite source prefix, and the finitely branching tree of lifts has an infinite path by compactness. This uses no online or memoryless choice of right extension. Each counterexample yields a conditional existential finite-lift constraint, necessary for every genuinely right-surjective graph, so a verified UNSAT after such refinements soundly excludes the specified graph/cycle class.
records.sc: Decides right-surjectivity for this graph presentation only; it says nothing about whether an aperiodic full Rule 30 diagram exists, and an aperiodic full diagram need not admit any finite graph presentation. There are exactly 72 possible phase-labelled edges in this family.
records.nt: Independent replay checked all 256 and 200 possible right-bit assignments across the stored cuts, confirming that with source edges enabled the actual CNF simplifies to exactly the frozen Rule 30 equations and the required target edge units for every assignment.

records.t: Aperiodicity of every odd arithmetic progression of the Rule 150 lone-seed neighbour
records.st: Let u_n = z(n,1) for the lone-seed Rule 150 diagram, so that u_(2n)=0, u_(2n+1)=1 XOR u_n and u_n = v2(n+1) mod 2. Then for every odd positive d and every residue j, the subsequence u_(dm+j) is not eventually periodic, and both values occur in it infinitely often. Proof: if it had eventual period P, put a=v2(P) and choose k>a of the opposite parity to a; because d is odd there are arbitrarily large m with v2(dm+j+1)=k, while at m+P the valuation is exactly a, contradicting that period.
records.sc: A property of the Rule 150 lone-seed source sequence only. It supplies the aperiodic selector for the label-quotient reduction and says nothing about Rule 30 itself; the Rule 150 source cannot kill R1 on its own because its centre is constantly 1, giving an empty zero set.
records.nt: The binary identities, the constant centre and the plain aperiodicity of u are already catalogued as cf862dc7f6175a1c; the generalization to every odd progression is what is recorded here, and it is the premise for r30-rlq-label-quotient.

records.t: Binary-descent completeness of the Rule 150 exact source-context closure
records.st: Rule 150 is additive with polynomial X^-1+1+X, so squaring over F_2 gives z(2t,2x)=z(t,x), z(2t,2x+1)=0, z(2t+1,2x)=z(t,x) and z(2t+1,2x+1)=z(t,x) XOR z(t,x+1). For every radius W>=1 the fine window centred at (2t+e_t, 2x+e_x) is determined by a coarse window of the same radius. Starting from all time-zero windows (one seed-containing pattern for centres x=-W,...,W plus the zero pattern at every spatial clock class) and closing the finite states (t mod T, x mod q, window) under all four binary lifts therefore enumerates exactly the contexts occurring at every time and site: every transition maps a real context to a real context, and every real context is obtained by repeatedly halving its time until time zero, with integer floor division also handling negative spatial coordinates. At the fixed centre only the spatial-bit-zero transitions are closed, the fixed site-1 patterns being the spatial-bit-one lifts of these states.
records.sc: Establishes the all-time quantifier for the Rule 150 source alphabet used by the factor CNFs; it is not a Rule 30 statement and decides no gate. The finite replays are implementation checks rather than the completeness proof, which is the binary descent.
records.nt: Independent direct XOR row evolution through time 511 reproduced all global and fixed-column pattern sets at radii 1 through 4, with global Rule 150 counts 217,364,560,812; the same check with the Rule 90 lift gives 154,238,329,434, agreeing with the carry construction recorded as r30-afa-carry-context-closure. records.t: Two-pattern A/B label quotient giving a complete R1 kill predicate for Rule 150-source factors
records.st: Write T=2^a*d with d odd and choose a power of two H>=R+1 divisible by 2^a. Frobenius gives z(Hn+p,x) = XOR_j z(n,j) z(p,x-Hj) for 0<=p<H; for centre and right-hand windows with |x|<=R+1<=H only j=-1,0,1 contribute, and since z(n,-1)=z(n,1)=u_n and z(n,0)=1, every window at time Hn+p is exactly one of two patterns: A_p (the window at time p) when u_n=0 and B_p (the window at time H+p) when u_n=1, the two possibly coinciding. On n=dm+j the lookup clock is fixed at (Hj+p) mod T while the selector u_(dm+j) is aperiodic, so a labelled output column is eventually periodic if and only if its labels agree on every such A/B pair, in which case it is purely H*d-periodic; no larger eventual period or later onset escapes these equalities. After imposing the A/B equalities for the centre, the neighbour is aperiodic on its zero set if and only if some residue has centre label 0 and unequal neighbour A/B labels.
records.sc: Complete for periodicity of every output labelling inside the chosen finite factor class over the Rule 150 lone-seed source with lookup s(t,x)=g(t mod T, x mod q, z(t,x-R),...,z(t,x+R)). It is not a bounded-window prediction of the Rule 30 neighbour from its centre history: the labelled windows belong to an auxiliary Rule 150 source. The final encoding has no explicit clock variables, fixed zero phases or neighbour-copy constraints.

records.t: Inverse-cover fixed-point operator and its conditional R1 counterdiagram consequence
records.st: Let G_a(x)_i = x_(i-1) XOR (x_i OR x_(i+1)) with prescribed x_0=a, let H be the composed driven map of a finite drive d beginning in zero repeated periodically, and observe the initial right neighbour at each complete return. Define X_0={0,1}^N and X_(n+1) = X_n intersect H(X_n intersect [0]) intersect H(X_n intersect [1]). A nonempty fixed point supplies both inverse covers, so every target in X has a predecessor in X with observation zero and another with observation one; choosing those predecessors backwards from any terminal point of X makes the sets of initial rows realizing longer observation prefixes nested, compact and nonempty, and their intersection gives a single coherent forward orbit with any chosen infinite observation word, so a provably aperiodic word yields an R1 counterdiagram. Conversely an empty X_n excludes this covering mechanism for every candidate subset of right rows, including nonsofic subsets.
records.sc: Finite stabilization is sufficient, not necessary: mere finite nonemptiness of the X_n is not a proof, although if all X_n were proved nonempty compactness would give a nonempty X_infinity with both covers persisting. The mechanism is strictly stronger than an aperiodic trace, since invertible chaotic systems can have unique predecessors and fail the cover condition, so its exclusion does not establish R1. The argument does not reverse the order of one preselected infinite past orbit, and the drive length need not be the minimal centre period.
records.nt: Independently audited. The finite representations were checked over 773 small NFAs, 9,276 all-word image equivalences, 51,076 inclusion pairs and 51,076 intersection pairs, plus 86 partial DFAs and 1,032 all-word image equivalences, with six Rule 90 covers passing (sofic-return-cover-independent-check.json). Rule 90 has the full right-row space as an immediate fixed point of the same operator.

records.t: Two-step boundary-drive return identities and the odd-ones consecutive-one prohibition
records.st: For two-step boundary drives the return observation as a function of the initial right bits (r,u,v) is exactly: boundary 00 gives r OR u OR v; 01 gives NOT(r OR u OR v); 11 gives r AND (u OR v); 10 gives NOT[r AND (u OR v)]. Consequently a zero boundary followed by an odd number of ones forbids consecutive return observations equal to one: an initial one becomes one after the zero step, zero after the first one step, and stays zero under each remaining pair of one steps. This uses the OR nonlinearity of Rule 30.

records.t: The period-two left obligation as an autonomous forward boundary condition
records.st: Pin the centre column to s(t,0) = t mod 2. At odd t the centre update c_(t+1) = l_t XOR (c_t OR r_t) forces l_t = s(t,-1) = 1, and at even t it only defines r_t = 1 - l_t and constrains the left side not at all. The left half-line i <= -1 therefore evolves autonomously under Rule 30 given that boundary column, and the rule at i = -1 gives l_(2k+1) = s(2k,-2) XOR (l_(2k) OR 0), so l_(2k+1) = 1 exactly when s(2k,-2) != s(2k,-1). The period-two hypothesis restricted to the left side is thus the single condition (L1) that the two rightmost cells differ at every even time, equivalently that column -1 is 1 at every odd time, and it is a property of the initial left word alone. Conversely a left word satisfying (L1) forever, together with a finite right word whose even-time column 1 equals 1 - l_(2k), is a period-two counterexample, so (PT2) follows if no finite word satisfies (L1) forever.
records.sc: A reformulation of the existing obligation with nothing added and nothing reconstructed: it states the obligation without the reconstruction, the four-state alphabet, the cut or the forcing, and proves no part of it. The right half-plane contributes only that the even-time column-1 word is hard-core. RW, SEP and PT2 are untouched. The source is dated 2026-09-16, was read 2026-09-16, and is untracked in the working tree, as are its scripts and logs.

records.t: Each pinned left half-line row has exactly two backward choices, not always both finite
records.st: Given the row at time t+1 on i <= -1 together with the pinned boundary, choosing l_t = s(t,-1) determines s(t,-2) = s(t+1,-1) XOR (l_t OR c_t), then s(t,-3) from s(t+1,-2), and so on leftward. Both choices of that one bit give a preimage, so the forward map is exactly two-to-one on the full sequence space and the two preimages differ only in the boundary-adjacent cell. Restricted to finite-width rows the in-degree is 0, 1 or 2, because a backward choice need not close to a finite width. This is the left-permutivity of Rule 30 read backwards.

source_context.heading: 1. Derivation

records.t: Exact halving of the survivor count through the controllable phase, and the free-running tail
records.st: Let N_w(k) be the number of width-w words, leftmost cell 1, surviving k even steps of (L1), over all 2^(w-1) such words. Then N_w(k) = 2^(w-2-k) exactly for 0 <= k <= floor((w-3)/2), the first failure falling at k = floor((w-1)/2): one bit of the seed is spent per even step while the seed bit at position -(2k+1) or -(2k+2) is still arriving at the boundary, because the leftmost cells reach column -1 at speed one and left-permutivity makes the observer's bit an affine function of the newest arriving seed bit. After that the word is free-running and the count decays slowly. The maximum number of even steps survived is M(w) = 8, 7, 8, 7, 14, 11, 13, 15, 12, 15, 16 at w = 8..18, which lies between w - 4 and w + 2, so the free-running phase after the controllable one lasts 7 to 9 even steps on this range. A period-two counterexample needs M = infinity.
records.sc: An exact finite census to width 18 only, and a description of the decay rather than a proof of any bound on it. M(w) is not monotone on this range and no growth law is established; the between-w-4-and-w+2 reading is an observation over eleven widths. Nothing here bounds M(w) for any larger w, and nothing excludes M = infinity. The source is dated 2026-09-16, was read 2026-09-16, and is untracked in the working tree, as are its scripts and logs.
records.nt: Checked in this review against the log rather than the prose: forward-boundary/forward_boundary_census_w2-18.log reproduces M(w), the first argmax word and the full survivor profile for every w = 8..15, for instance w = 12 at M = 14 with argmax 110100010101 and profile 1024, 512, 256, 128, 64, 25, 10, 8, 6, 6, 6, 3, 3, 3, 0. This M counts step 0, unlike the survivor-branching table. The 2,048 words of width 12 and 131,072 of width 18 are the enumerated populations; the sample size recorded is the largest. CORRECTION: this record first stated the halving as N_w(k) = 2^(w-1-k) for k <= floor((w-2)/2), copying the source document's prose. Both halves are wrong against the same log: N_w(0) is 2^(w-2) at every width 8 to 18, so at w = 8 the old formula predicted 128 against the measured 64, and the profile 64, 32, 16, 5 breaks at k = 3 where the old stop claimed halving still held. The corrected form holds at every width in the log. The source document carries the same error in its prose; its successor RESULTS-FORWARD-HALVING-LEMMA.md names it and proves the correct statement, catalogued as r30-fhl-halving-theorem.

source_context.heading: 2. Census
2. Census

records.t: Survivor-only branching extends the census to width 30 at square-root cost
records.st: Building level L (even) as the set of partial seeds on positions -L..-1 satisfying (L1) at steps 0 .. L/2 - 1, by extending level L-2 with two bits and filtering, exactly half of the four-fold extension survives at every level, asserted through L = 30: the condition at step k depends on positions -(2k+2)..-1 and, by left-permutivity along the diagonal, is affine with coefficient 1 in the bit at -(2k+2), so that bit is forced by the ones to its right. Counting even steps from time 0, which is one less than the full census convention, M(w) for w = 12..30 is 13, 10, 12, 14, 11, 14, 15, 13, 17, 16, 19, 20, 19, 19, 20, 20, 22, 23, 25. The free phase halves the survivors per even step for about log2 of their number and then flattens into plateaus of 2 to 6 words, its maximum length growing from 8 at w = 12 to 11 at w = 30. Cost is 2^(w/2) seeds per width, so width 40 is about a million.
records.sc: A finite census to width 30 under a stated cost model, not a bound on M(w) at any larger width. The per-level exact halving is asserted through L = 30 and supported by the left-permutivity argument, not proved for all L here. The plateau structure is an observation. The source is dated 2026-09-16, was read 2026-09-16, and is untracked in the working tree, as are its scripts and logs.

source_context.heading: 2b. Survivor-only branching to width 30

records.t: Huge fixed-family control showing the fused compiler skips updates on a compressible input
records.st: As a control the fused finite-section compiler computes Q^k(A^L) = A^L for L = 2^40 + 3 and k = 2^36 + 7 using 86 grammar nodes and one explicit leaf action, creating no L-letter word, no 2k-bit zero buffer and no enormous modulus. On this known fixed family the implementation therefore really does skip a huge number of updates on a compressible input.
records.sc: A control on a family whose answer is known in advance and chosen for its compressibility. It demonstrates a property of the implementation, not of the Rule 30 centre column, and the document states outright that it is not a Rule 30 centre shortcut. Nothing about P3 follows.
records.nt: The figure is restated in docs/rule30/RESULTS-p3-bulk-query-jumps.md, which is declared a non-claim digest, so without this record the control would have been held nowhere while both documents counted as covered. source_context.heading: 3. What the compiler costs

records.t: Uniform proof that the period-two left condition halves the forward survivor set, with the corrected width-w count
records.st: Run Rule 30 on the left half-line i <= -1 with the pinned boundary s(t,0) = t mod 2 and seed x_m = s(0,-m) for m >= 1, and let C_k = s(2k,-2) XOR s(2k,-1) be the period-two condition (L1) at even step k. Two lemmas give the result. Lemma 1 (light cone): s(t,-m) depends only on x_1, ..., x_(m+t), by induction on t. Lemma 2 (left-permutivity along the diagonal): s(t,-m) = x_(m+t) XOR g_(t,m)(x_1, ..., x_(m+t-1)). Hence C_k = x_(2k+2) XOR G_k(x_1, ..., x_(2k+1)) with G_k = g_(2k,2) XOR x_(2k+1) XOR g_(2k,1), so for each assignment of x_1..x_(2k+1) exactly one value of x_(2k+2) gives C_k = 1, and the partial seeds on -(2k+2)..-1 satisfying C_0 = ... = C_k = 1 number exactly 2^(k+1), that is level L = 2k+2 has exactly 2^(L/2) members. For words of width exactly w (x_w = 1, x_m = 0 for m > w) condition C_k forces a free bit iff 2k+2 <= w-1, so the count after C_0..C_k is 2^(w-2-k) for k <= floor((w-3)/2), and the first k at which halving is not guaranteed is k = floor((w-1)/2), the step whose new coefficient-1 bit is the fixed leftmost 1 for even w or the fixed 0 beyond it for odd w.
records.sc: A uniform proof with no restriction on k or w, replacing an assertion that earlier documents made only as a census observation. It identifies the controllable phase exactly and bounds nothing about the free phase, which is where every open question about M(w) lives. The exhaustive run is a check of the coordinate bookkeeping to k = 9 (2^20 seeds at k = 9), not evidence for the theorem. RW, (SEP) and (PT2) are untouched. The source is dated 2026-09-16 and has no companion pre-registration.
records.nt: Corrects the existing catalog record r30-fbc-controllable-phase-halving, whose statement carries the width-w count as 2^(w-1-k) with the stop at floor((w-2)/2). The census artifact forward-boundary/forward_boundary_census_w2-18.log lines 7 and 8 give N_8 = 64, 32, 16, 5 and N_9 = 128, 64, 32, 16, 10, which match 2^(w-2-k) with the stop at floor((w-3)/2) and contradict 2^(w-1-k) (which would give 128 at w = 8, k = 0). That record should be revised. The document also flags a second defect it does not depend on: the docstring of forward-boundary/forward_survivor_census.py line 4 says level L has 2^(L/2 + 1) seeds where the truth is 2^(L/2). Checker forward-boundary/halving_lemma_check.py, log halving_lemma_check_k0-9.log, all PASS, exit 0.

source_context.heading: The halving lemma of the forward form, and the bijection of its survivors with rho prefixes

records.t: Level survivors of the forward condition are in triangular bijection with free rho prefixes
records.st: On level 2k+2 of the forward (L1) construction the even-indexed seed bits x_2, x_4, ..., x_(2k+2) are determined by the odd-indexed bits x_1, x_3, ..., x_(2k+1), and rho_j = 1 - s(2j,-1) = 1 XOR x_(2j+1) XOR g_(2j,1)(x_1..x_(2j)) is affine with coefficient 1 in x_(2j+1) given the earlier bits. Therefore the map (x_1, x_3, ..., x_(2k+1)) -> (rho_0, ..., rho_k) is triangular with unit diagonal, hence a bijection of the 2^(k+1) survivors onto all 2^(k+1) binary words of length k+1. The controllable phase is thus exactly a change of coordinates carrying one free symbol per condition, which is the endpoint form's premise that the source W is free while everything else is forced. Checked exhaustively for k = 0..9: the level count is 2^(k+1), column -1 is 1 at every odd time at most 2k-1 on every survivor, and the rho prefixes of the survivors are pairwise distinct.
records.sc: Proved uniformly in k for the pinned left half-line with the (L1) condition only; the hard-core condition of the right half-plane is not imposed here. It says nothing about the free phase, where the survivors are no longer parametrized by fresh bits. The exhaustive check reaches k = 9, that is 2^20 seeds.
records.nt: The same bijection is measured independently in RESULTS-FORWARD-SURVIVOR-W40.md as a post-hoc check (seed to rho prefix injective at every even L <= 30), recorded here as r30-fsw-hardcore-level-fibonacci-counts. Log forward-boundary/halving_lemma_check_k0-9.log, rho-bijection PASS at every k = 0..9.

source_context.heading: 2. Two lemmas and the theorem

records.t: Failure of the single-flip dependency graph to carry the charge of inequality (12) at its tight word
records.st: The pre-registered statement (R-universal), that m_2(W) >= run_2(W) - [22 occurs in W] and m_2(W) >= run_3(W) - 3 for every hard-core word W, where m_2(W) is the maximum matching of forced steps j < run_c(W) into the positions i with W_i = 2 and i in D_j (single-flip dependency with the forced prefix held fixed), is false. The witness is W = 12212121212121212 at n = 17, c = 2, the sole slack-zero word of inequality (12): run_2(W) = 10, m_2 = 8, #2 = 9, one occurrence of 22, so d_univ = m_2 + credit - run = 8 + 1 - 10 = -1 < 0. The factor reading (R-factor), in which each occurrence of 22 at (i, i+1) contributes one token adjacent to step j iff i or i+1 lies in D_j, is false on the same word by the same margin, m_factor = 9, d_factor = -1. The failure is a Hall violation by inspection: over all ten steps the union of 2-positions any step depends on is {2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16}, eight tokens, because position 1, the first symbol of the 22 factor, lies in no D_j at all, so the matching is bounded by 8 and 8 is attained. Consequently a proof of inequality (12) that charges each forced step to a distinct token of the set (12) names, with single-flip dependency as the adjacency, is closed under either credit reading.
records.sc: A refutation of one proof shape, not of inequality (12), which remains an empirical inequality exact to n <= 30 by the earlier census. Finite and single-implementation: hard-core words n = 8..18, wide grammar, one definition of D_j (single flip, forced prefix held fixed), one matching routine. It does not exclude a dependency notion that is not single flip (pairs of flips, or the full Boolean dependency of the cut on the source), a token set in which the 22 factor contributes two tokens, or a charge that is not a matching; none of those is pre-registered here.
records.nt: Figures taken from charge-injection/injection_tokens_n8-18.log line 55 (n=17 c=2: min(m_2 - run) = -2, min d_univ = -1 at W=12212121212121212 run=10 m_2=8 #2=9 #22=1 credit=1 m_factor=9 d_univ=-1 d_factor=-1) and lines 56 to 58. Sample size is the word count at the two new lengths, F(19) + F(20) = 4181 + 6765. The same maximum matching of 8 on the same word is computed independently in RESULTS-DEPENDENCY-LAW.md from a full-triangle implementation (tight_word_he.py), and by the crosscheck at crosscheck/charge-injection/check_tokens.py. The crosscheck's min d_univ column differs at c = 2 for n = 8, 9, 11, 13, 15, 18 only because it includes words with run = 0; the document explains this and it is not a defect. Supersedes the open point in r30-cip-two-token-matching-fails-at-first-tight-length, which left the maximum matching at n = 17, 18 uncomputed.

source_context.heading: Charge inequality (12): the single-flip dependency graph cannot carry its charge at n = 17, the pre-registered kill fired

records.t: Exact maximum-matching census of the charge injection at lengths seventeen and eighteen
records.st: Over all hard-core words of length n = 17 and n = 18 in the wide grammar, both tails, the exact maximum matching of forced steps into the 2-positions of their single-flip dependency sets was computed for the first time. At n = 18 and both c, and at n = 17 with c = 3, every hard-core word has m_2 >= run, that is min(m_2 - run) = 0. At n = 17 with c = 2, min(m_2 - run) = -2 and exactly two words have m_2 < run: 12212121212121212 with run 10, m_2 = 8, nine 2s, one 22 factor, d_univ = -1, and 22212121212121212 with run 10, m_2 = 9, ten 2s, two 22 factors, d_univ = 0, the credit used exactly. The second word differs from the first only by a 2 at position 0, which enters D_0 and restores m_2 = 9. This resolves two earlier greedy readings: the oldest-unused greedy deficit of 1 at n = 18 was an artefact of the greedy order rather than a matching deficit, since the maximum matching saturates every word at n = 18, and at n = 17 the greedy deficit of 3 overshoots the true deficit of 2 by one. The gate against the earlier probe passed: at n = 8..16 the new script reproduces injection_probe_n8-16.log in min(m_2 - run) at both tails (0 at every n for c = 2, and -1, -3, -1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0 for c = 3) and in mean |D_j| to one decimal at all eighteen (n, c) pairs.
records.sc: Finite and exhaustive over hard-core words of length n = 8..18 only, wide grammar, one implementation of D_j and one matching routine. It is a census of the matching statistic, not evidence that inequality (12) holds at any n > 18, and the maximum matching is exact only under the single-flip dependency definition. RW, SEP and PT2 are untouched.
