source_context.heading: Charge inequality (12): the single-flip dependency graph cannot carry its charge at n = 17, the pre-registered kill fired

records.t: Closed form of a single source flip inside its own endpoint column
records.st: Let the endpoint triangle column u be the Moore machine with state (h, F) = (H_u(d), E_u(d)) reading the quotient (a, b) of column u-1, stepping h' = h + 1 + a, F' = F + h b, from the initial state (1 - H(e_u), 0) at d = -u. Flip the source symbol e_i between 1 and 2, which flips H(e_i) and keeps E(e_i) = 0. Columns u < i are unchanged by triangularity. The flip changes only the initial state of column i, from (h_0, 0) to (h_0 + 1, 0), and leaves the input word of column i unchanged. Each letter (a, b) acts affinely with linear part the shear S_b : (h, F) -> (h, F + b h); shears commute and square to the identity, so the linear part of the word read on [-i, d) is S raised to beta_i(d), where beta_i(d) = #{d' in [-i, d) : Lo(T[i-1][d']) = 0}, and the difference of the two trajectories at depth d is S^beta applied to (1, 0) = (1, beta_i(d) mod 2). Hence at every depth d in [-i-1, i]: dH_i(d) = 1; dE_i(d) = beta_i(d) mod 2; db_i(d) = 1 + beta_i(d) mod 2, so the quotient letter b flips exactly where beta_i is even; and a_i'(d) = H_i(d) (E_i(d) + beta_i(d)), that is da_i(d) = E_i(d) + H_i(d) beta_i(d).
records.sc: Uniform in i, d and the sequence, proved by the affine action of the letter alphabet; it covers only the flipped symbol's own column, not the propagation into later columns. The exhaustive gate is 386,346 cells per identity over 3,579 endpoint sequences, all binary W with n <= 10 and their forced continuations for both tails, with zero failures. It gives no bounded-state description of anything.
records.nt: Pre-registered as (P1) in PREREGISTRATION-DEPENDENCY-LAW.md. The (H, E) Moore description is from RESULTS-PSI-ANCESTRY-LAW.md section 4, re-derived in this document rather than trusted. Check counts from charge-injection/dependency-law/propagation_law_n1-10.log lines 11 to 12, ALL PASS. The (H, E) Moore machine it perturbs is the existing record 7921c4b0fba42c56 from RESULTS-PSI-ANCESTRY-LAW.md; this document re-derives it rather than trusting it, and no existing record covers the perturbation.

source_context.heading: The single-flip dependency law: (P1) and (P2) are exact and uniform, and the pre-registered kill fires at n = 4, so no step-by-step fresh-token mechanism exists

records.t: The single-flip perturbation downstream of its column is a sixteen-state transducer with a cone and an extinction rule
records.st: For columns u > i, downstream of a flip at source symbol e_i, the initial state is unchanged and the H channel is F2-linear: dH_u(d) = #{d' in [-u, d) : da_(u-1)(d') = 1} mod 2, with dH_(i+1)(-(i+2)) = 0, and dH_(i+1)(d) = sum over d' in [-i, d) of (E_i(d') + H_i(d') beta_i(d')) mod 2. The F channel is exact but bilinear: dE_(i+1)(d+1) = dE_(i+1)(d) + H_(i+1)(d) db_i(d) + dH_(i+1)(d) b_i(d) + dH_(i+1)(d) db_i(d) with db_i(d) = 1 + beta_i(d). Writing the emitted letters as da = (1 + h) dF + dh (F + dF), db = dh + dF, dh' = dh + da_(u-1), dF' = dF + h db + dh b + dh db, the pair (unperturbed column, perturbed column) at every u > i is one run of a fixed 16-state transducer on state (h, F, dh, dF), uniform in n, u and i. Two structural consequences follow. (P2.cone): (dh, dF)(u, d) = 0 for d < u - 2i - 1, since (u, d) depends only on cells with d' - u' <= d - u and the source cell has d' - u' = -2i - 1. (P2.ext): the perturbation of column u changes between zero and nonzero from depth d to d+1 only if (da, db)(u-1, d) is nonzero, because for a fixed letter the step is a bijection of the four states, so a perturbation is extinguished only by another perturbation arriving from the left and re-lit only the same way. What is explicitly not uniform is the membership i in D_j, which is the bit (dh, dF)(n+j, n) of that iterated product transducer; from column i+2 on both channels depend on the whole unperturbed column, and no bounded-window statement about it is claimed.
records.sc: A uniform derivation of the propagation identities and of the cone and extinction rules; it deliberately stops short of any bounded-state or bounded-window description of D_j membership, which the document names as the same growing-word obstruction that (PSI) meets. The exhaustive gate covers all 3,579 endpoint sequences from binary W with n <= 10 and both forced continuations: 379,188 cells for P2.H and P2.E, 347,871 for P2.Hc, 2,401,548 for P2.Hu and P2.cone, 2,084,994 cell-steps for P2.prod and P2.ext, zero failures.
records.nt: Pre-registered as (P2) in PREREGISTRATION-DEPENDENCY-LAW.md, which asked only for the H-channel parity statement at minimum; the cone and extinction rules exceed that. Counts from charge-injection/dependency-law/propagation_law_n1-10.log lines 11 to 12.

source_context.heading: The single-flip dependency law: (P1) and (P2) are exact and uniform, and the pre-registered kill fires at n = 4, so no step-by-step fresh-token mechanism exists

records.t: Refutation of every step-by-step fresh-token law behind the charge injection
records.st: The pre-registered laws (L-fresh), that every forced step j < run has a 2-position in D_j outside D_0 union ... union D_(j-1), and (L-nested), that for j >= 1 the set D_j intersected with the 2-positions is not contained in D_(j-1) intersected with them, are both false, and the pre-registered kill condition (L-fresh failing on a word whose maximum matching saturates) fires at n = 4. Witness at c = 2: W = 1212, run 2, forced 22, D_0 = {1, 2, 3} with 2-positions {1, 3}, D_1 = {1, 3} with 2-positions {1, 3}, maximum matching 2 equal to the run, and step 1 reads exactly the two 2s step 0 read. Witness at c = 3: W = 2121, run 2, forced 22, D_0 = D_1 = {0, 1, 2, 3}, matching 2. The failure is not a small-n accident: over all hard-core words with a run, (L-fresh) fails on 77 of 371 words at n = 14 with c = 2 and on 458 of 2819 at n = 18, every one of them saturating, and (L-nested) fails on 47 and 216 of the same populations. Therefore the injection of run steps into 2-tokens that inequality (12) requires exists only globally, by Hall's condition after all dependency sets are known, and no argument of the shape 'forced step j reads a 2 that steps 0 .. j-1 did not need' exists.
records.sc: Finite and exhaustive over all hard-core W with n <= 14 and n = 18, both tails, in the wide grammar, plus the tight word at n = 17. The refutation is of the named step-by-step laws only; it does not bear on whether inequality (12) is true, and D_j is single-flip dependency with the forced prefix held fixed, so a joint dependency on several flips is not excluded by the silence of the single flip. RW, (SEP) and (PT2) are untouched.
records.nt: Counts read from charge-injection/dependency-law/dependency_laws_n1-14.log (n=14 c=2 line: words 371, fresh fails 77, KILL 77, nested fails 47) and dependency_laws_n18.log line 2 (words 2819, fresh fails 458, KILL 458, nested fails 216). Sample size is the 5,444 (word, c) pairs with a run at n = 18. The sharper obstruction on the tight word, that the maximum matching is 8 for 10 steps because the flips of e_0 and e_1 are extinguished before any forced column, is recorded as r30-cit-universal-token-charge-refuted from the other document; here it is corroborated by a second implementation (tight_word_he.py, full triangle) and the D_j agree with greedy_rules_n8-18.log lines 2 to 11.

records.t: One global greedy order reaches the maximum matching on every word tested, and five fixed orders do not
records.st: Of six fixed charging orders (steps taken forward, in reverse, or by ascending |D_j intersected with the 2-positions| with ties by j, and within each step the oldest or the newest unused 2), exactly one reaches the maximum matching on every word tested: steps by ascending |D_j cap 2-positions|, oldest unused 2 within a step. It is at the maximum on all 1,992 (word, c) pairs with a run at n <= 14, on all 5,444 at n = 18, and gives 8 on the tight word 12212121212121212 at n = 17, which is the maximum. Each of the other five falls below the maximum on a named word: forward-oldest, which is the earlier probe's rule, first at 12212 with c = 3 and n = 5 and on exactly two words at n = 18 (122121212122121212 and 222121212122121212, c = 2, run 6, forced 212222, matching 6); forward-newest first at 1222121 with c = 2 and n = 7, and on 12 words at c = 2 and 4 at c = 3 at n = 18; reverse-oldest first at 2222 with c = 2 and n = 4, and 2 words at c = 3 at n = 18; reverse-newest first at 2212 with c = 2 and n = 4, none at n = 18; size-ascending-newest first at 1222121 with c = 2 and n = 7, none at n = 18. The surviving order is not a mechanism: it sorts steps by the size of sets known only after every D_j has been computed, which is a global Hall-type choice rather than a step-by-step law, and it is not used for anything.
records.sc: Empirical, and the document says so explicitly. It is a statement about maximum matchings of these particular bipartite graphs over hard-core words with n <= 14 and n = 18 in the wide grammar, plus one word at n = 17; no order is proved to reach the maximum at any larger n, and no order rescues the step-by-step mechanism that (L-fresh) killed. Status is conjectured because the claim is about all words and only a finite range was tested.
records.nt: Per-order first witnesses from charge-injection/dependency-law/dependency_laws_n1-14.log lines 30 to 79 and dependency_laws_n18.log lines 2 to 43; the 'order below the maximum matching' columns of the n = 18 lines give forward/oldest 2, forward/newest 12 at c = 2 and forward/newest 4, reverse/oldest 2 at c = 3, with size/oldest 0 at both. The pre-registration (L-order) asked whether a fixed alternative order repairs the oldest-unused rule's failures at n = 17, 18; it does, but only as a global choice. Related to r30-dpl-fresh-token-law-refuted: this order does not rescue the step-by-step mechanism that record kills.

records.t: The endpoint triangle is the pinned left half-plane in a single affine chart
records.st: For every binary endpoint word the endpoint triangle and the pinned left half-plane are the same object in one affine coordinate change: T[u][d] = 2 x(t, i) + x(t, i-1) at (t, i) = (u - d - 1, -(u + d + 2)), equivalently u = (t - i - 1)/2 and d = -(t + i + 3)/2, with the high bit the right cell of a horizontal pair. Here x is the forward configuration on i <= 0, t >= -1 with the centre pinned as x(t,0) = t mod 2 and column -1 given by l_t, extended to t = -1 by (l_(-1), c_(-1)) = (1,1). So u indexes the diagonal t - i = 2u + 1, one per endpoint symbol and two time steps each, and d indexes the anti-diagonal t + i = -(2d + 3), one per depth. The derivation is three lines from carry_action being one Rule 30 step of a horizontal pair given the pair to its right: FORWARD moves a pair one up and one right, CONE[L][R] = INVERSE[swap(L)][R] therefore moves a pair one down and one left given the pair L to its right on the lower row, and the triangle recurrence T[u][d] = CONE[T[u-1][d-1]][T[u][d-1]] is left-permutivity. The edges are T[u][-u-1] = e_u at (2u,-1) and T[u][-u] = tau_3 inverse of e_u at (2u-1,-2). The endpoint symbol is e_u = (x(2u,-1), x(2u,-2)) = (1 - rho_u, rho_u), and the boundary symbol 3 is the odd-time pair (x(2u-1,-1), x(2u-1,0)) = (1,1). This chart is the unique survivor of the pre-registered search box of 202,500 candidate coordinate changes and pair readings on all 510 binary endpoints of length at most 8, it stays the unique survivor when the t = -1 cells are excluded, and it is exact with zero mismatches on the 158,720 cells of the 1,536 binary endpoints of length 9 and 10.
records.sc: Proved for the binary endpoint alphabet {1,2} only, where the symbols are a configuration; it is a dictionary between two existing formalisms and proves nothing new about (PT2), (PSI) or (RW). The uniqueness is uniqueness within the pre-registered box, |alpha|, |beta|, |alpha'|, |beta'| <= 2 and |gamma|, |gamma'| <= 4 with four pair readings, on endpoints of length at most 8; a coordinate change outside that box is not excluded. The pre-registered kill, that no coordinate change and pair reading reproduces T, did not fire.

records.t: The four-state endpoint alphabet codes a configuration only on its binary letters
records.st: Reading a four-state endpoint symbol e_k = (h, lo) as the pair (l_(2k), l_(2k+1)) = (h, h XOR lo), the symbols 0 and 3 assert l_(2k+1) = 0, a broken pin, while the next layer still feeds the boundary symbol 3 which asserts l_(2k+1) = 1. The four-state alphabet is therefore a configuration only on {1, 2}, and the archive's four-state gate in psi_kernel.validate checks the carry algebra rather than a configuration. Quantitatively, over all 21,844 four-state endpoints of length at most 7: every cell whose pin window (the odd times 2k+1 in [u-d-1, 2u-1]) is intact agrees with the half-plane, 393,728 cells with zero disagreements, while 398,248 of the 732,520 cells with a broken pin in the window disagree, the first at e = (0,2), u = 1, d = 0, where the triangle gives 1 against the forward value 0.
records.sc: A scope limit on the dictionary, not a result about Rule 30. It states exactly where the chart holds and where it does not; it does not say what the symbols 0 and 3 mean instead, and the document states there is no identity for them. Exhaustive over four-state endpoints of length at most 7 only.

records.t: The H-forcing and the cut condition are single-cell conditions on one anti-diagonal
records.st: Under the chart, the cut cell cut_j(WQ) = T[n+j][n] is the pair at (t, i) = (j-1, -(2n+j+2)), which lies on the anti-diagonal t + i = -(2n+3), one step down-left per j, with j = 0 sitting at t = -1. The cell x(j-1, -(2n+j+2)) depends on the boundary column l up to time 2(n+j) with coefficient 1 in l_(2(n+j)) by left-permutivity along the diagonal, and not on l_(2(n+j)+1). Hence exactly one value of l_(2(n+j)), that is exactly one forced symbol Q_n(W)_j in {1,2}, makes that cell 1, which is the archive's H-forcing, and then Psi_j is the cell to its left, x(j-1, -(2n+j+3)). The tail condition reads the same way: cut_j = 2 is x(j-1, -(2n+j+2)) = 1 together with x(j-1, -(2n+j+3)) = 0, and cut_j = 3 is both cells 1. The map (l_(2k), l_(2k+1)) -> (high, low) at k = n+j is a triangular bijection because the low bit has coefficient 1 in l_(2k+1), which is why exactly one four-state symbol gives each tail and why the run stops when that symbol is 0 or 3 (the pin broken at 2k+1) or the hard-core junction is violated.
records.sc: A translation of the archive's forcing and cut into the forward chart, with no new content about either. Checked exhaustively on binary sources with n <= 8 (4,606 forced steps) and on the 3,586 endpoint-and-n splits of binary endpoints of length at most 8. It is silent about the symbols 0 and 3, where the chart does not hold.

records.t: A constant cut at depth n is exactly a finite time-zero row of the prescribed width
records.st: Because CONE[2][2] = CONE[3][3] = CONE[0][0] = 0, a constant cut cut_j = c for all j >= 1 forces T[n+j][n+m] = 0 for j >= m+1 and m >= 1, that is every cell left of the anti-diagonal at t >= 0 is 0. In the forward chart this says the time-0 row is finite with leftmost 1 at -(2n+3), of width 2n+3, when c = 2, or with leading 11 at -(2n+4) and -(2n+3), of width 2n+4, when c = 3, and every later row carries the same edge shifted left by t. Conversely a finite row of that shape has the leading edge 11 at every t >= 1, since a 10 edge becomes 11 in one step, and so has cut_j = c for every j >= 1. At j = 0 the correspondence is: with c = 2, cut_0 = 2 is exactly a finite row at t = -1 with leftmost 1 at -(2n+2); with c = 3, cut_0 = 3 is a finite row at t = -1 with leading 11 at -(2n+3), -(2n+2) and cut_0 = 1 one with leading 10; every other value of cut_0 makes row -1 eventually all 1.
records.sc: A uniform derivation from the CONE table plus a finite check: 673 instances of (endpoint, n, c) among binary endpoints of length at most 9 with cut_j = c at every available j >= 1, of which 153 also at j = 0, plus the 90 instances with c = 3 and cut_0 = 1, and 8,319 cut cells over the 4,092 seeds of the run identity. It characterises constancy of the cut, not the length of any run.

records.t: The endpoint run is the survival count of one finite forward seed
records.st: For a binary source W of length n and a tail c in {2,3}, let seed(W) be the time-0 row of width 2n+3 when c = 2, or of width 2n+4 with leading 11 when c = 3, whose cells at -1..-(2n) are determined by W through the triangular bijection with l_0..l_(2n-1) and whose cells at -(2n+1) and -(2n+2) are the unique pair making cut_0 = c, that is making the row at t = -1 finite. Then run_c(W) = S_n(seed(W)), where S_m(s) counts the consecutive k >= m at which the pin holds, x(2k,-2) != x(2k,-1), and no 11 junction occurs, that is not (x(2k-2,-1) = x(2k,-1) = 0), the junction at k = n being checked against W's last symbol and W's interior not checked, exactly as in seam_history_inheritance.admissible. The forced symbols of the endpoint form are the seed's own e_(n+j). Three independent computations agree in count and in forced word on all 4,092 pairs (W, c) with n <= 10, maximum run 8: seam_history_inheritance.run, a forward forced-pair run choosing (l_(2k), l_(2k+1)) from the pair on the anti-diagonal with no kernel call, and the survival count of seed(W) evolved forward from its time-0 row. The deepest runs D_n(c) reproduce the archive: hard-core sources match the table of RESULTS-EVENTUAL-CONSTANT-TAIL.md section 8 for n = 1..19, and all binary sources match seam_history_inheritance.controls() for n = 7..10.
records.sc: Proved as an identity of definitions and checked exhaustively only on binary W with n <= 10, both tails, in the wide grammar; the D_n tables extend to n = 19 for hard-core sources. It converts the run into a forward statistic and bounds nothing: no growth law for D_n follows from it. The wide grammar admits sources containing 11, which the right half-plane excludes, and D^wide exceeds D^hc at n = 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, so any positive bound should be stated on D^hc.

records.t: Two-sided sandwich relating the hard-core forward census maximum to the archive's deepest run
records.st: With w = 2n+3 for c = 2 and w = 2n+4 for c = 3, and M_HC(w) the maximum over width-w seeds of S_0 under the pin and the hard-core junction in this document's convention, the hard-core forward census and the archive's deepest run D_n^hc(c) satisfy n + D_n^hc(c) <= M_HC(w) <= n + 2 + D_(n+1)^hc(c), so free_HC(w) = M_HC(w) - (n+1) lies in [D_n^hc(c) - 1, D_(n+1)^hc(c) + 1]. The three differences between the census statistic and the run are exactly: the run starts at k = n rather than k = 0, the run adds the hard-core junction, and the run sees only seeds whose row at t = -1 is finite, which one shift by an endpoint symbol removes at the price of one scale. The sandwich holds exhaustively over all 2^(w-1) seeds at every width w = 5..18 with both bounds attained at some widths, and against the sibling hard-core census to width 40 in the form n + D_n^hc(c) <= M_hc(w) + 1 <= n + 2 + D_(n+1)^hc(c) at all 29 widths 12..40, where M_hc is the sibling's survivor-convention maximum, one condition fewer, verified equal after the offset at the overlap widths 12..18. One side is attained at 22 of the 29 widths, the lower bound at w = 12, 18, 19, 22, 23, 24, 27, 28, 31, 35, 37, 39, 40, the upper at w = 14, 16, 17, 20, 22, 24, 26, 30, 32, 34, 36, 39, and both at w = 22, 24, 39. The transfer is therefore two-way for the hard-core statistic: a bound D_n^hc(c) <= B(n) for all n gives free_HC(w) <= B(n+1) + 1, and a bound free_HC(w) <= B'(w) gives D_n^hc(c) <= B'(2n+3) + 1 for c = 2 or B'(2n+4) + 1 for c = 3.
records.sc: Finite: the sandwich is checked, not proved for all widths, exhaustively to w = 18 from this script's own enumeration and to w = 40 against an inherited census that was read and not rerun. D_n^hc is this script's own to n = 19. The sandwich holds only for the hard-core statistic M_HC; it does not control the unfiltered census maximum M(w). Conventions matter: free here is M_HC(w) - (n+1), one more than the sibling documents' convention, and the width-40 form carries an explicit +1 offset on the inherited M_hc.

records.t: The forward free phase is not bounded by eleven steps through width forty
records.st: The pre-registered hypothesis (H2), that free(w) <= 11 for all w <= 40, is false and its kill fired. In the convention free(w) = M(w) - (ceil(w/2) - 1), with M(w) the maximum number of even steps of the pin condition (L1) survived counting from time 0 by a width-w seed, the values for w = 12..40 are 8, 4, 6, 7, 4, 6, 7, 4, 8, 6, 9, 9, 8, 7, 8, 7, 9, 9, 11, 11, 16, 11, 14, 13, 12, 15, 15, 18, 16. The maximum is 18 at w = 39, and free exceeds 11 at w = 32 (16), 34 (14), 35 (13), 36 (12), 37 (15), 38 (15), 39 (18) and 40 (16), against 11 at w = 30. The ratio free(w)/w is about 0.46 at w = 39 against 0.37 at w = 30, with no plateau in sight, consistent with the archive's D_n(c) growing about 0.3 n. The census gate against the width-30 log passed field by field, and the level construction reached level L = 40 with 2^20 seeds.
records.sc: A finite census to width 40 only, and the outcome the pre-registration itself named as expected. It refutes the bound 11 on this range and bounds free(w) from below by 18 at w = 39; it establishes no upper bound at any width and nothing about w > 40. A period-two counterexample needs free infinite, so nothing here moves (PT2). The convention counts even steps from time 0 as the width-30 log does, one less than the width-18 census and one less than the dictionary document's convention.

records.t: The hard-core condition adds no free steps at the extremal seed of width twenty
records.st: The pre-registered hypothesis (H3), that free_hc(w) <= free(w) - 2 at every w >= 20, where free_hc and M_hc impose both the pin condition (L1) and the hard-core condition on the even-time column -1 word at every even step, is false and its kill fired at w = 20. There free_hc(20) = free(20) = 8 and M_hc(20) = M(20) = 17, attained by the same first argmax 11010001010101000001, whose rho word rho_0..rho_17 = 212222212212212221 has no factor 11 and so is hard-core over its whole life. The same coincidence holds at w = 16, below the pre-registered range, with free_hc = free = 4 at argmax 1000000100010101 and rho = 222122212222. At every other width in 12..40 the hard-core filter does shorten the free phase, by free_hc - free of -8, -3, -4, -5, 0, -3, -5, -3, 0, -4, -3, -7, -4, -3, -3, -4, -6, -4, -6, -6, -10, -5, -8, -5, -7, -7, -9, -11, -9 for w = 12..40, that is by 3 to 11 steps wherever it bites, and no plateau word of any width 30..40 has a hard-core rho word (0 of 8, 26, 21, 83, 48, 26, 120, 12, 12, 12, 52 at w = 30..40). The honest form of the hypothesis is therefore that the right half-plane's condition costs 3 to 11 steps on w = 21..40 and 0 at w = 16 and w = 20, not that it always costs at least two.
records.sc: Finite, w <= 40, left half-line only, with the right half-plane represented solely by the hard-core reading of the even-time column -1 word; no cut, no four-state alphabet, no forcing, no reconstruction. The refutation is of the stated inequality at one width, by one witness word. Whether free_hc is bounded is not answered on this range: it reaches 8 at w = 20, 35 and 37 and 7 at w = 39 and 40.

records.t: Hard-core level counts are Fibonacci because the controllable phase is a coordinate change
records.st: Under the pin condition (L1) alone, the level-L count is exactly 2^(L/2) at every even L <= 40, asserted level by level in the construction with L = 40 holding 2^20 = 1,048,576 seeds. Under (L1) together with the hard-core condition imposed at every even step from step 2 on, the level counts at L = 4, 6, ..., 40 are 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, 34, 55, 89, 144, 233, 377, 610, 987, 1597, 2584, 4181, 6765, 10946, 17711, that is the Fibonacci numbers F(L/2+2), which is exactly the number of hard-core binary words of length L/2. The reason is a post-hoc check that the map from a level-L seed to its rho prefix rho_0..rho_(L/2-1) is injective at every even L <= 30, hence bijective onto all of {0,1}^(L/2): the controllable phase is a change of coordinates carrying one free bit per even step, so imposing the hard-core condition on it removes nothing structural, only the non-hard-core rho prefixes. Everything the census measures is therefore in the free phase.
records.sc: Finite: the (L1) level counts are asserted through L = 40 and the hard-core counts measured there; the seed-to-rho injectivity was checked only at even L <= 30. The Fibonacci identification is an observation about counts, not a proof for all L, although the bijection it rests on is proved uniformly elsewhere. It says nothing about the free phase, which is where the open questions are.

records.t: The last surviving seeds of a width form families sharing a long rho tail
records.st: The plateau words of a width, the seeds alive at each of the last three nonempty free levels, share no common suffix as seeds: the longest common suffix is empty at every width 30..40, because the rightmost cell l_0 takes both values within every plateau. In the rho coordinate they are highly structured instead. At the flat plateaus all 21 plateau words of w = 32 agree on rho_6..rho_31, a shared tail of 26 of 32 symbols equal to 22112121121221111112211121, and all 12 of w = 39 agree on rho_5..rho_37, a shared tail of 33 of 38 symbols equal to 221112221211221212111112212222121. These are single families differing only in the first five or six rho symbols, which is exactly the coordinate that the controllable phase leaves free, and their seed words share only a short left prefix because the seed-to-rho bijection scrambles the right end. A bound on the free phase must exclude that tail, and the tail is a property of the rho word rather than of the seed.
records.sc: A structural observation over widths 30..40 only, with the flat plateaus at w = 32 (21 words at six consecutive levels) and w = 39 (12 words at three) carrying the long shared tails; at w = 31, 33, 34, 35, 36 and 40 the plateau words share no rho tail at all and the common seed prefix is the single symbol 1. It proves nothing and is not used to bound anything. The right-suffix-extension check reported alongside is uninformative by construction, since the rightmost 12 cells of any (L1) survivor range over exactly 64 words and the plateau words of widths 12..29 already cover all 64.

records.t: Closed form of the endpoint state after a constant prefix, and the resulting memberships
records.st: For sym in {1, 2} and m >= 1, after the endpoint word sym^m the state holds T[m-1][d] = sym when m + d is even and sym XOR 3 when m + d is odd, for every d in [-m, m-1]. Both halves of the column alternate, the phase is the parity of m, and nothing else about m is stored. The proof is induction on m with two CONE entries per symbol: CONE[sym XOR 3][sym] = sym XOR 3 and CONE[sym][sym XOR 3] = sym, that is CONE[2][1] = 2 and CONE[1][2] = 1, so the two-letter transducer reading (sym, sym XOR 3) from state sym XOR 3 emits (sym, sym XOR 3) and returns to sym XOR 3; the base is T[0][-1] = sym and T[0][0] = BOUNDARY[sym] = sym XOR 3. Corollary: the last column of sym^m s reads m periods of (sym, sym XOR 3) from state s XOR 3, so cut(sym^m s) = P_sym^m(s XOR 3) with P_1 = CONE[2] after CONE[1] = (0 1)(2)(3) and P_2 = CONE[1] after CONE[2] = (0)(1)(2 3). Hence cut(1^m 1) = 2 which is inadmissible after a 1, cut(1^m 0) = 3 which is not binary, and cut(1^m 2) lies in {0,1}, so 1^m is in neither L_1(2) nor L_1(3) for any m >= 1; while 2^m is in L_1(2) iff m is even and in L_1(3) iff m is odd. The pre-registered kill's first clause, that the transducer state does not return over a period, did not fire.
records.sc: Proved for all m >= 1 and both constant symbols, with a cell-by-cell check against psi_kernel.Endpoint for m <= 200. It is a statement about the wide language only, since 1^m contains the factor 11 and is not hard-core; 2^m is a control rather than a probe, being realizable only to length 4. It establishes no separation and no non-regularity.

source_context.heading: Non-regularity of L_1(c) along 1^m: closed form, separating suffixes to level 17, and the exact gap

records.t: After a constant prefix the suffix reads a position in one length-independent periodic triangle
records.st: Define the triangle U by U(-1, e) = 1 + (e mod 2) for e >= 0, U(j, -j-1) = v_(j+1), U(j, -j) = v_(j+1) XOR 3 for 0 <= j < q, and U(j, e+1) = CONE[U(j-1, e)][U(j, e)] for e >= -j, for a suffix v = v_1 .. v_q. Then after 1^m v the endpoint triangle satisfies T[m+j][d] = U(j, d + m) for 0 <= j < q and -(m+j)-1 <= d <= m+j, by induction on j using the closed form on 1^m for the base, and the cut of 1^m v s is the single cell U(q, 2m + q) where column q is built from the symbol s. Since the tower (U(0,e), ..., U(q-1,e)) at position e determines the tower at e+1 given e mod 2, and every step is a permutation of the fibre, the tower is purely periodic from e = 0. So the endpoint state after 1^m v is the window [-q, 2m+q) of column q-1 of an m-independent periodic object, the only m-dependence is the window's right end, and the length m is observed as a position advancing by two per unit of m rather than as content. The measured horizon-q class counts 1, 4, 16, 32, ..., 1024 of the earlier residuals document are the periods of these columns.
records.sc: Proved for all m and all suffixes v, and checked against the oracle on 6,048 triples (m, v, c) with m <= 24 and |v| <= 6. It reduces the separation question to the content of one periodic column between two cut positions; it does not by itself separate any pair of lengths.

records.t: Membership as a D8 letter product, the exact complement between tails, and the separation criterion
records.st: Modelling a cell x as the point (h, F) = (H(x), E(x)) of F_2^2 with E = 1 + H + Lo, each cell acts as the affine map (alpha, beta, gamma) = (1 + (1+h)F, h + F, 0) and the group generated is D8 with centre z = (0,0,1); CONE[x][y] equals the letter of x applied to y for all sixteen pairs. Column q of the reduction triangle starts at U(q, -q) = s XOR 3 and reads column q-1 over [-q, 2m+q), so U(q, 2m+q) = Pi_m applied to (s XOR 3) with Pi_m the D8 product of the letters of column q-1 over that window. Pi_m is a bijection of the four cells, so exactly one symbol s gives each tail. For a suffix v ending in 2 the membership function is f_c(m) = [F(Pi_m inverse applied to c) = 0], and for v ending in 1 it is f_c(m) = [Pi_m(1) = c]. Since Pi_m inverse is affine with linear part fixing (0,1), one has Pi_m inverse of (1,1) equal to Pi_m inverse of (1,0) plus (0,1), so f_3 = 1 - f_2 exactly for every suffix ending in 2 and one suffix separates for both tails at once. Separation criterion: for m < m', writing Pi_(m') = D Pi_m with D the product of the 2(m'-m) letters of column q-1 over [2m+q, 2m'+q), and Pi_m = (alpha, beta, gamma) with D inverse of (1,0) equal to (h', F'), the two lengths differ in membership iff F' + beta(Pi_m)(h' + 1) = 1. In particular the stretch separates whenever D maps cell 3 to cell 2, never when it fixes cell 2, and otherwise h' = 0 exactly when beta(Pi_m) = F' + 1.
records.sc: A uniform derivation from the affine model, with the complement identity checked on every suffix ending in 2 of length at most 7 for m < 128. The criterion characterises separation in terms of the content of a periodic column between two cut positions; it does not exhibit any separating family, and it says nothing about suffixes ending in 1 beyond the membership formula.

source_context.heading: Non-regularity of L_1(c) along 1^m: closed form, separating suffixes to level 17, and the exact gap

records.t: Certified anti-periodic suffixes to level seventeen and a DFA lower bound of two to the eighteen states
records.st: For every level a = 4..17 there is an explicit suffix A[a] of length a, namely 2112, 21112, 212112, 2111112, 21111112, 211111112, 2211111112, 21111121112, 221111111112, 2111112111112, 21211111111112, 211121111111112, 2111211111111112 and 22111111211111112, which is anti-periodic at 2^a: f_c(m + 2^a) != f_c(m) for all m >= 0 and both tails c. Each is certified by a tower recurrence plus an exhaustive check over one period: the least even P with tower(P) = tower(0) over columns 0..q-1 gives U(j, e+P) = U(j, e) for all e >= 0; the product Phi of column q-1's letters over [0, P) satisfies Pi_(m + P/2) = Phi_m Pi_m with Phi_m a cyclic rotation of Phi, hence conjugate to it, so L = (P/2) ord(Phi) is a period of f_c; and the check covers all m < L. The column periods P run 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 8192, 16384, 65536, 131072, 262144, with L equal to P except at a = 13 and 14 where L = 2P. For a <= 3 every suffix has membership period dividing 16, and two covering sets of six suffixes each give 16 distinct signatures over m mod 16, one for each tail, with no set of five sufficing. Theorem: for c in {2,3} and all m != m' with m != m' mod 2^18, the prefixes 1^m and 1^(m') are Nerode-inequivalent for L_1(c), since a = v_2(m'-m) <= 17 and either the mod-16 table applies or A[a] flips membership an odd number of times. Hence every DFA for L_1(c) has at least 2^18 = 262144 states.
records.sc: A finite theorem: it separates every pair of prefix lengths not congruent mod 2^18 and says nothing about a pair that is congruent, so it does not prove non-regularity. The certificates are exhaustive checks at fixed a over one membership period, not an induction on a, and the search for A[a] ranged only over the families 2 1^n 2, 2 1^i 2 1^j 2, 2 1^i 2 2 1^j 2 and, at level 17, 2 1^i 2 1^j 2 1^k 2; the listed suffixes are the first certified in that order, not the only ones. 1^m probes the wide language only, since it is not hard-core.
records.nt: Certificates at nonregularity/ones_separation.log lines 67 to 94; the level-17 line gives A[17] = 22111111211111112 with P = 262144, Phi = (1,0,0), ord 2, L = 262144, checked for all m < 262144. Sample size is that period. The rule v(m, m', c) additionally separates all 4032 pairs with 1 <= m < m' <= 64 under the Endpoint oracle with |v| <= 5 (line 95). This supersedes the finite DFA bound in r30-srs-reg-kill-and-dfa-lower-bound, which reached 2254 states at prefix length 13; the document's phrase 'up from the measured 1100' cites the older 1100-prefix figure of r30-srs-drive-prefixes-separate and understates the archive's own best prior bound.

source_context.heading: Non-regularity of L_1(c) along 1^m: closed form, separating suffixes to level 17, and the exact gap

records.t: No uniform mechanism carries the separating family past a fixed level, so non-regularity stays unproved
records.st: The pre-registered kill fired in its second clause: a periodic closed form on 1^m exists, but no separating family for all pairs follows from it, so the theorem that L_1(c) is not regular is not proved. The naive family 2 1^(a-2) 2 fails to be anti-periodic at a = 6, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16 and 17, and among the two-inner-2 candidates the certified count falls to 3, 1, 1, 0 at a = 14, 15, 16, 17, so level 17 required widening to three-inner-2 words, of which 6 of 105 certify. The one-period maps Phi_k of the columns along 2 1^k for k = 0..10 are (1,0,1), (1,1,0), id, z, (1,0,1), z, (1,0,0), z, z, id, (0,1,0), with orders 2, 4, 1, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 1, 2 and column periods 4, 8, 32, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 2048: the identities at k = 2 and k = 9 stall the tower, and the maps take every conjugacy class of D8 as the suffix grows, so no period or self-similarity is visible and an induction on a would need an invariant of bounded size that the data show does not exist within the families tried. The missing statement is (G): for every a there is a suffix v whose membership function is not 2^a-periodic. Two sub-steps are open. (G1) unbounded tower period: along 2 1^infinity the tower period is bounded iff some column U(j,.) with j >= 1 is ground on e >= 0, and locally column j+1 is ground iff column j has no cell 0 and no cell 2 at positions e congruent to j+1 mod 2; no invariant is known that forbids this, and the per-period counts of 0-cells 1, 1, 8, 6, 15, 30, 57, 112, 246, 522, 532 are positive but follow no rule. (G2) observability: cells 1 and 3 emit the same letter, so the tower can differ at two positions without the difference reaching the cut, and the certificates say it always does through level 17 with no argument why.
records.sc: An explicit obstruction rather than a result. The witness data cover the family 2 1^k only for k <= 10 and the certified-candidate counts only the four suffix families searched, so the absence of a uniform mechanism is established for those families and not in general. (G1) is proved only as an equivalence, with the sufficient condition unproved in either direction, and (G2) has no argument at all. Nothing here bears on P1; the pre-registration classes the result as a no-go theorem for finite-state certificates of the run language.
records.nt: Failing levels of the naive family from nonregularity/ones_separation.log lines 71 to 93; the witness line 108 gives the Phi_k list, the orders and the column periods, and the level-17 line 93 gives 6 of 105 certified after widening to three inner 2s. Sample size is the level-17 candidate count. The document's section 2.8 cites lines 97 to 107 for the ground-column check and line 108 for the witness, while its abstract cites lines 97 to 108 for both; the figures are the same.

records.t: Period-28 closed form for the whole endpoint state after (12)^k, proved by induction for every k >= 2
records.st: Let D = 2120030303000312031112300323, a word of length 28 read with indices mod 28, and let Endpoint be the psi_kernel state after appending W = (12)^k, with L = n = 2k. Then for every k >= 2 the state satisfies S(k): column[i] = D[(2k - i) mod 28] for i = 0..2k and diagonal[j] = D[(2k + j) mod 28] for j = 0..2k-1, equivalently T[2k-1][d] = D[(2k + d) mod 28] for every depth -2k <= d <= 2k-1. So the column and the anti-diagonal are not two objects over a fixed bottom but one period-28 sequence read in the depth coordinate, and appending the block 12 is the shift D[t] -> D[t+2] on it. The proof is an induction: the base S(2) is column = 0 0 2 1 2 = D[4] D[3] D[2] D[1] D[0] and diagonal = 0 3 0 3 = D[4..7]; the step S(k) => S(k+1) is discharged by finite state returns of the two-append lockstep transducer STEP((x_1,...,x_m), z) = (CONE[z][x_1], CONE[x_1][x_2], ..., CONE[x_(m-1)][x_m]), namely three bottom-cell identities plus one-period outputs and the return sigma(28) = sigma(0) = (2, 2) for the column, and fourteen checks, one per residue r = k mod 14, each verifying the outputs over one period and the return tau(28) = tau_0(r) for the anti-diagonal. Since the transducer input D[t mod 28] is 28-periodic, the checked period extends to every t and every k at once.
records.sc: The pure alternating sources W = (12)^k only, k >= 2, a measure-zero family among sources; it is a statement about the endpoint state, not about (PSI), RW, (SEP) or (PT2), and nothing off the family follows. The quantification over k is complete (an induction, not a finite range), but the induction step is discharged by machine-checked finite state returns rather than by hand, and it rests on one implementation, psi_kernel.py, gated against its reference by validate() and not independently re-implemented. The mirrored family (21)^k is not treated here.
records.nt: Figures from alternating-family/psi_alternating_proof.log: D and its period on line 1, CONE = ((0,1,3,2),(3,2,1,0),(3,2,0,1),(3,2,1,0)) and BOUNDARY = (3,2,1,0) on line 2, the direct check S(k)_direct_k=2..200 on line 6, the three column checks on lines 7 to 9, and the fourteen anti-diagonal state returns with their seeds tau_0(r) on lines 10 to 23; the same checks pass identically in psi_alternating_proof_depth7.log. This discharges the conjecture recorded as r30-alt-pure-family-closed-form, which is status conjectured on the finite range k = 2..60 and whose scope names exactly this proof as what was missing. D is the block of that record rotated by four: the earlier document's D'[t] = D[t + 4]; there is no separate fixed bottom.

source_context.heading: 1. Objects

records.t: The first six cut cells after (12)^k are a function of k mod 448, with a proved period bound of 896
records.st: Fix a pattern S = (s_1, ..., s_6) in {1,2}^6 appended after W = (12)^k and let V_S(k) be the vector of the six cut cells T[2k+l][2k], l = 1..6. Running the six appends in lockstep gives one machine on {0,1,2,3}^6 whose column pass starts at sigma_S(0) = column_init(S) and reads D[t mod 28] for t = 0..2k-1, and whose anti-diagonal pass starts at tau_S(0) = sigma_S(2k) and reads D[(2k+j) mod 28] for j = 0..2k-1, ending at V_S(k) = tau_S(2k). Each STEP(., z) is a triangular bijection of {0..3}^6 because every CONE row is a permutation, so the one-period map F_phi given by 28 successive STEPs from phase phi is a permutation; its order is 64 at all fourteen even phases. Hence for k' = k + 14q both passes differ by q applications of a one-period permutation, and with q = 64 both are the identity, giving V_S(k + 896) = V_S(k) for every pattern S and every k >= 2, with no excluded residues and k_0 = 2. The H-forced pattern is determined cell by cell from these vectors, so the six forced symbols, the six cut cells and the six defect bits are all 896-periodic in k. The census recomputing all of this from Endpoint over k = 2..1793, two full periods, confirms V(k + 896) = V(k) directly and sharpens the minimal periods to 448 for the six cut cells, 224 for the six forced symbols, 28 for k_E(2) and 224 for k_E(3); a 448-periodic block of length 896 makes the whole 896-periodic sequence 448-periodic.
records.sc: Depth six only: the first six forced appends after the pure alternating source (12)^k, k >= 2. The period bound P_0 = 896 is proved for all k; the sharper minimal periods 448 and 224 are read off a census over two full periods and are exact for that reason, not extrapolated. The lemma says nothing about cut cells at depth seven or beyond, nothing about any source off the family, and nothing about RW, (SEP) or (PT2). One implementation (psi_kernel.py), not independently re-implemented.

source_context.heading: 2.2 The six cut cells are a function of k mod 448, for every k >= 2

records.t: The pre-registered bound k_E(3) <= 5 on the alternating family is false at k = 144 (mod 224)
records.st: The bound pre-registered in PREREGISTRATION-PSI-ALTERNATING-PROOF.md, that the constant-cut run k_E(c) of the H-forced continuation of W = (12)^k is at most 5 for both tails c in {2,3} at every k >= 2, is false for c = 3. Over the census k = 2..1793 the histogram of k_E(3) is {0: 768, 1: 384, 2: 224, 3: 208, 4: 128, 5: 72, 6: 8}: eight values of k, exactly the residue k = 144 (mod 224), namely k = 144, 368, 592, 816, 1040, 1264, 1488, 1712, have all six inspected cut cells equal to 3 (low bit 1), so k_E(3) >= 6 there, and the check k_E(3)<=5_all_residues_mod_448_and_k=2..1793 fails with max = 6. The witness run of psi((12)^144) in full gives forced prefix 21212222, cut cells 3 3 3 3 3 3 2 3, defect word 111111011000, k_E(2) = 0, k_E(3) = 6 against n + 2 = 290; the residue mate k = 368 gives forced prefix 21212212 and the same eight cut cells with k_E(3) = 6 against n + 2 = 738. The bound was a census artifact: the earlier census stopped at k = 60, k_E(3) has minimal period 224, so it saw 59 of 224 residues and missed the one on which the value is 6. The depth-six script exits 1 with KILL FIRED and was not extended past its pre-registered depth of six cells.
records.sc: Refutes the numeric bound k_E(3) <= 5 only. It does not refute (PSI) on the family: at k = 144 the run 6 is far short of the requirement n + 2 = 290, and the companion bound k_E(2) <= 3 survives with max 3 over the same census, attained at k = 22, 25 (mod 28). It also does not refute the structural claims: the pre-registration's own two kill conditions, a transducer state that fails to return after one period and a cut sequence that is no function of k mod P for any P <= 448, did not fire. The counterexample is exact integer computation on one implementation (psi_kernel.py), and the earlier finite record r30-alt-pure-family-cut-run-slack, which reported k_E(3) in 0..5 for k <= 60, is correct on its own range and wrong only as an extrapolation.

records.t: Depth-seven rerun: k_E(2) <= 3 and k_E(3) <= 6 for every k >= 2, so (PSI) holds on the alternating family
records.st: For every k >= 2 the H-forced continuation of W = (12)^k has k_E(2) <= 3 and k_E(3) <= 6, so (PSI), the requirement k_E(c) < n + 2 = 2k + 2 for both tails, holds on the pure alternating family at every k >= 2 with slack 2k - 4 at c = 3. The argument is the depth-six machinery at DEPTH = 7: the one-period map on 4^7 states is a permutation of order 128 at all fourteen even phases, so by the same lockstep argument the first seven forced symbols, cut cells and defect bits are a function of k mod 1792 for every k >= 2; the bound is then a finite check over one period. The census over k = 2..3585, two full periods, confirms the periodicity from the kernel, gives minimal period 896 for the seven cut cells and 448 for the seven forced symbols, keeps k_E(2) at period 28 and k_E(3) at period 224, and reports maxima 3 and 6 over all residues, with histograms k_E(2) {0: 2048, 1: 512, 2: 768, 3: 256} and k_E(3) {0: 1536, 1: 768, 2: 448, 3: 416, 4: 256, 5: 144, 6: 16}: k_E(3) = 6 on 16 of 3584 values, the residue 144 (mod 224), and never 7. Spot checks at k = 6344, 7777, 10000 built symbol by symbol in the kernel agree with the residue prediction. The run was pre-registered the same day in PREREGISTRATION-PSI-ALTERNATING-DEPTH7.md with this bound and these kills stated before it; none fired, and the script exits 0 with all 33 checks passing.

source_context.heading: 6. Depth seven: the theorem

records.t: Dyadic-lag correlations on the centre column show no drift through 2^29
records.st: With R_N(h) = sqrt(N)*C_N(h)/(N-h) on the singleton centre column and D = {2^a - 2^b : a > b >= 0}, the quantity max_(h in D) |R_N(h)| over all 211 dyadic lags h <= 2^20 has log-log slope -0.0084 against N across eight nested prefixes N = 2^22 to 2^29, a factor 128 in N. No dyadic lag has |C_N(h)/(N-h)| above 1e-3 at any of the three largest prefixes; the three largest at N = 2^29 are 1.39e-04 at h = 24, 1.32e-04 at h = 32,760 and 1.07e-04 at h = 28, none holding its sign across the ladder. Against 211 seeded non-dyadic control lags of the same magnitude the dyadic-to-control ratio of max |R| at the top rung is 1.133. All three pre-registered kill conditions, set at slope 0.25, at 1e-3 and at ratio 2, were silent.
records.sc: A finite measurement that can refute the hypothesis it tests and cannot confirm it: limsup_N C_N(h)/N <= 0 is asymptotic and eight prefixes of a half-billion-bit cache decide nothing about the limit. The eight rungs are nested and so are not independent trials, and the control is a calibration rather than a statistical rejection rule. It gives no bound on liminf D_N(h)/(N-h) at any lag, makes the remaining estimate no easier, and bears on no prize problem. The lag set is capped at h <= 2^20, so nothing is measured about larger dyadic lags. The source and its artifact are untracked in the working tree at the time of extraction.
records.nt: Original computation of this review, pre-registered in experiments/rule30/PREREGISTRATION-dyadic-lag-drift.md before the script existed; the ladder was amended from a 2^20 start to 2^22 before any correlation was computed, because at N = 2^20 the largest lag left zero span, and the amendment is recorded in the pre-registration. The source is the wdr_billion.bin cache at payload offset 239, used-payload sha256 c46e9665..., with the first 29 centre bits checked against 11011100110001011001001110101 before anything was computed. C_N(h) = (N-h) - 2*M_N(h) is exact integer arithmetic; only the sqrt(N) normalization is floating point. The LEVEL of these correlations is validation of a settled empirical fact, the centre column having been Mathematica's original pseudorandom source, and is not claimed as a finding; only the drift is new. Calibration, recorded but not claimed as a result: the dyadic median |R| sits at 0.62 to 0.69 at every rung against a half-normal median of 0.6745, and the max over 211 draws at 2.6 to 4.0 against an expected max of about 2.9 for 211 standard normals, so the normalized correlations behave like unit-variance noise in both families.

source_context.heading: 3. Result

records.t: The dyadic lag family is not distinguishable from generic lags on the centre column
records.st: At every one of the eight prefixes N = 2^22 to 2^29, the distribution of |R_N(h)| over the 211 dyadic lags h <= 2^20 overlaps the distribution over 211 seeded non-dyadic control lags of the same magnitude: dyadic medians run 0.6160 to 0.6942 against control medians 0.6482 to 0.7761, and dyadic maxima 2.5616 to 4.0188 against control maxima 2.7261 to 3.8446, with neither family dominating the other at any rung. The centre column carries no structure at the dyadic lags that it does not carry at generic lags of the same size.
records.sc: A negative about visible structure at one lag cap and one horizon, not a theorem. Two distributions overlapping is a failure to distinguish them, not a proof that they are the same, and no test statistic or rejection rule is applied. It says nothing about dyadic lags above 2^20 and nothing about the infinite orbit.

source_context.heading: 4. What this does and does not mean

records.t: Sup-deviation decay slope sits inside the i.i.d. seed range at every tested block length
records.st: At the registered T = 2,000,000, the least-squares slope of log2 S(L,W) against log2 W over W in {2^12, 2^14, 2^16, 2^18, 2^20} lies inside the range spanned by 20 i.i.d. null seeds at every tested L: L=1 gives -0.473 in [-0.658, -0.364], L=2 gives -0.518 in [-0.622, -0.383], L=4 gives -0.581 in [-0.629, -0.399], L=8 gives -0.518 in [-0.594, -0.490] and L=12 gives -0.563 in [-0.657, -0.551]. Seed-range containment is a descriptive comparison, not the pre-registered test: the pre-registration's consistency branch asks for a slope in [-0.65, -0.35] at each L <= 8, which -0.473, -0.518, -0.581 and -0.518 satisfy, and its disconfirming plateau criterion asks for a slope above -0.25, which no L reaches.
records.sc: A measured single-run outcome, not a proof and not an inference to ergodicity. One column, one run, T = 2,000,000, 20 numpy null seeds. A block-frequency diagnostic has power only to disconfirm; the document's own status line calls it measured and diagnostic only and says it proves nothing about P2 in either direction. Each slope is a five-point regression. The pre-registered decision rule covers L <= 8 only, so L = 12 is reported outside it. The sup over depth uses 10 depths at W <= 2^18 and 9 at 2^20, so the pre-registered floor of 8 depths per window holds at every W and the largest-window end of each regression is no longer the weakest by depth count.
records.nt: Merged from five per-L sections that state one claim at five values of L. At L=12, W=2^12 the Rule 30 value 1.469e-03 equals the seed minimum exactly, which at 4,096-sample resolution is quantization rather than a coincidence worth reading. Restated 2026-09-16 from the registered T = 2,000,000 run; the superseded T = 1,100,000 values were -0.483, -0.532, -0.607, -0.518 and -0.571, also all inside their seed ranges.

source_context.heading: L = 1: S(L, W) = sup over depth of max-block deviation

records.t: All three pre-registered disconfirming criteria are silent at the registered T = 2,000,000
records.st: None of the three criteria fixed before the run fires. Criterion A, a deepest-window frequency drift with |z| > 3 at two or more W >= 2^16, has count 0, the largest tabulated |z| anywhere being +2.20 at t0 = 4,096, W = 2^14. Criterion B, some L <= 8 with slope above -0.25 and both of the two largest W exceeding the seed maximum, fires for no L, and cannot: no cell at W = 2^18 or W = 2^20 exceeds its seed maximum at any L. Criterion C, four or more of the 25 (L,W) cells exceeding the 20-seed maximum, sees 2, at (L=2, W=2^14) and (L=4, W=2^12).
records.sc: A non-firing outcome proves nothing. The document's own pre-registration states in advance that this branch cannot certify convergence of any invariant measure's marginal, and the phrase the document uses for the verdict, consistent with unique ergodicity, is explicitly qualified there as proving nothing. One column, one run, T = 2,000,000, 20 numpy null seeds. A block-frequency diagnostic has power only to disconfirm; the document's own status line calls it measured and diagnostic only and says it proves nothing about P2 in either direction. The 2-of-25 tally is one realization against a design expectation of about 1.2 and ignores correlation between cells sharing an L or a W. A plateau appearing only beyond t0 = 2e6 or beyond W = 2^20 is untestable here.
records.nt: Criterion A's deepest window at W = 2^20 now starts at t0 = 951,424, 47.6 percent into a column of 2,000,000, against t0 = 51,424 and 4.7 percent in the superseded T = 1,100,000 run. The single large-W exceedance that the superseded run placed in that same weakened cell, L=8 at W=2^20, does not survive the registered run: Rule 30's statistic there is 2.479e-04 in both runs and the null's seed maximum rises from 2.441e-04 to 2.613e-04 once each null seed takes its sup over 9 depths instead of 5.

records.t: The diagnostic pipeline flags every cell of the Rule 90 control column
records.st: Run unchanged on the Rule 90 lone-seed centre column, the pipeline flags all 25 (L,W) cells. For every cell the minimum and the maximum of D(L,W,t0) over t0 >= 1 both equal 1 - 2^-L exactly, that is 0.500000, 0.750000, 0.937500, 0.996094 and 0.999756 for L = 1, 2, 4, 8 and 12, each far above the matching null seed maximum, for instance 0.996094 against 2.613e-04 at L=8, W=2^20. The t0 = 0 column sits strictly below, 0.499756 at L=1, W=2^12 rising to 0.499999 at W=2^20.
records.sc: A soundness control on the pipeline, carrying no information about Rule 30. It shows only that the pipeline detects a maximally degenerate, eventually all-zero column; it does not calibrate sensitivity to a subtly non-equidistributed column, which is the failure mode that would matter for Rule 30. Its mathematical prediction is the separate catalogued lemma 384de53cf82ab104; this record is the empirical fact that the pipeline acted on it.
records.nt: The t0 = 0 entries falling one bit below 1 - 2^-L is exactly what a column that is 1 at t=0 and 0 afterwards produces, so the control corroborates 384de53cf82ab104 rather than merely coexisting with it. Re-verified unchanged on the registered T = 2,000,000 run; only the null seed maxima it is compared against moved.

source_context.heading: Rule 90 control: D(L, W, t0) must equal 1 - 2^-L for every t0 >= 1

records.t: The first orbit-closure run deviated from its frozen protocol in three ways, since corrected by re-running the protocol
records.st: Three deviations between the document's frozen pre-registration and the run of 2026-08-30 it originally reported, none of them recorded as an amendment at the time. First, the pre-registration sets a target length T >= 2,000,000 and that run used T = 1,100,000, 45 percent short, justified in its run header as the smallest length admitting the full window ladder. Second, the pre-registration guarantees every W at least 8 depths including the deepest the column allows; counted from the per-depth tables the depths per W were 10, 10, 10, 9 and 5 for W = 2^12 through 2^20, so the guarantee failed at W = 2^20, where the deepest start was t0 = 51,424. Third, the frozen reproduction block reads --steps 2000000 while that run line read --steps 1100000, so the documented reproduction command did not reproduce the reported run. Closed 2026-09-16 by running the registered protocol at T = 2,000,000, not by amending the pre-registration: depths per W are now 10, 10, 10, 10 and 9, the reproduction block is now the command that produced the tables, and the pre-registered verdict is unchanged.
records.sc: A defect report about protocol fidelity in one document, not a mathematical result and not a refutation of its measurements. It did not say the reported numbers were wrong; it said the largest-window end of every statistic in the document rested on fewer depths than the protocol promised, and that the reproduction command as written reproduced a different run. Both conditions are now false of the document, and the record is retained as the history of the deviation and its correction.
records.nt: Consequential rather than cosmetic, and the registered re-run bore that out. The one large-W seed-max exceedance behind criterion B and criterion A's deepest-window test both landed in the W = 2^20 cell, the cell the depth shortfall weakened; on the registered run that exceedance is gone, leaving 2 of 25 rather than 3, because the null's seed maximum there rose from 2.441e-04 to 2.613e-04 while Rule 30's statistic held at 2.479e-04. The depth counts were derived from the per-depth tables, not stated by the document. The generator itself is checked, the document recording its first 30 terms against OEIS A051023, and the cached T = 2,000,000 columns agree byte-for-byte with the T = 1,100,000 ones on their shared prefix.

source_context.heading: Protocol deviation and correction

records.t: No individual dyadic lag up to 2^20 drifts against matched controls to N = 2^29
records.st: Computed separately for each of the 211 dyadic lags h <= 2^20 on eight nested prefixes N = 2^22..2^29, the Theil-Sen slope of log2|R_N(h)| against log2 N has median -0.007 over the dyadic family against -0.011 over 211 matched non-dyadic controls, quartiles -0.168/0.165 against -0.203/0.150, and maxima 0.867 against 0.720. A persistent correlation at a lag gives slope 0.5. Exactly one dyadic lag exceeds the control slope ceiling against a null expectation of 0.995 and a kill at 7, and the permutation p-value for a shift in the median slope is 0.888 against a kill at 0.01. Both pre-registered kills were silent.
records.sc: Proves nothing about the limsup hypothesis. A finite measurement against an asymptotic hypothesis: it can refute and cannot confirm. Nested prefixes are not independent of one another and all lags are evaluated on one sequence, so the kills are screens for a gross difference between two lag families, calibrated under exchangeability of those families, and their p-value is not a test of the asymptotic claim. The single exceeding lag h = 1,048,568 = 2^20 - 2^3 is an artifact of a near-zero first-rung cell and its |R_N| series decreases over the top four rungs, so it is not a candidate counterexample. The level of the correlations is validation of a settled empirical fact, not part of this claim.
records.nt: Closes the blind spot of r30-dld-no-drift-to-2-29, which tracked only the maximum over the family: at N = 2^29 the noise scale 1/sqrt(N) is 4.3e-05, so a lag could climb twenty-fold off the floor without moving the maximum or crossing that run's 1e-3 persistence threshold. Calibration kept out of the statement: dyadic median |R_N| is 0.616 to 0.694 across all eight rungs against a half-normal median of 0.6745, flat.

source_context.heading: 3. Result

records.t: Dyadic lags between 2^20 and 2^23 are not distinguishable from generic lags
records.st: For the 66 dyadic lags with 2^20 < h <= 2^23, smallest 1,572,864 and largest 8,388,608, measured on five nested prefixes N = 2^25..2^29 where every such lag keeps a span of at least 3N/4, the dyadic maximum of |R_N(h)| at N = 2^29 is 2.378 against 2.493 over 66 controls drawn from the same interval, a ratio of 0.954 against a specialness threshold of 2.0, and no dyadic lag in the range holds |C_N(h)/(N-h)| > 1e-3 at the top three rungs, the largest being 1.03e-04 at h = 3,670,016. Both pre-registered kills were silent.
records.sc: These lags had never been measured, so this is a first look rather than a confirmation. A finite measurement against an asymptotic hypothesis: it can refute and cannot confirm. Nested prefixes are not independent of one another and all lags are evaluated on one sequence, so the kills are screens for a gross difference between two lag families, calibrated under exchangeability of those families, and their p-value is not a test of the asymptotic claim. No drift kill is registered here at all: five rungs give regressor sum of squares 10 against tier A's 42, so a per-lag slope over this range carries roughly twice the sampling spread and the tier-B slopes in the artifact are descriptive only. The ceiling moved from 2^20 to 2^23 and did not go away; the cache holds 1,000,000,848 payload bits, so 2^29 is the largest prefix available and any further extension needs new trajectory computation.
records.nt: The dyadic family is marginally quieter than the controls rather than louder, which is the opposite direction from a specialness claim and is not significant at 66 draws; recorded so a later reader does not mistake the sign for a finding.

source_context.heading: 3. Result

records.t: An absolute per-lag slope threshold is uninformative on this measurement
records.st: The log-log slope threshold of 0.25 that r30-dld-no-drift-to-2-29 applies to the maximum over the dyadic family cannot be carried over to per-lag slopes: of the ten largest tier-A Theil-Sen slopes, 10 of 10 dyadic and 10 of 10 control slopes exceed 0.25, so a fixed cutoff there fires on both families identically and separates neither. Separately, least squares on log2|R_N(h)| is not usable as the per-lag statistic: the control family's OLS maximum is 2.439 against a Theil-Sen maximum of 0.720, manufactured by a single floored cell where |R| fell below 2^-30, and least squares would have reported that as the headline drift.
records.sc: A statement about how a measurement of this shape must be designed, not about Rule 30. It says a per-lag kill must be calibrated against a control family and that the slope statistic must be robust to a near-zero cell; it does not say what any such measurement will find, and it does not transfer to a ladder with a different rung count, where the sampling spread differs.
records.nt: Recorded because the archive's larger asset is its map of what not to re-derive. Written into the pre-registration as the reason the kills were stated distributionally, before the run; the run then measured the exceedance count at 1 against the null expectation of 0.995.

source_context.heading: 3.2 Why the kills were registered distributionally

records.t: Exponential literal word length against linear guard evaluation for the balanced defect family
records.st: Expanded literally in the primitives A, A^-1 and tau_0, the balanced defect E_d has word length obeying L_0 = 1, L_(d+1) = 4 L_d + 4, so L_d = (7*4^d - 4)/3. The normal form stores d instead and evaluates one guard, which for a supplied input prefix reads at most 2d-2 input bits and costs O(d) Boolean work. On zero input the guard is always true, E_d(0) = 2^(2d) so bit_k(E_d(0)) = 1 exactly when k = 2d, and the implemented zero_marked(d,k) compares binary integers at O(log(d+2)+log(k+2)) bit work, constructing neither 2^(2d) nor a large mask; the large-index control runs d = 10^1000 and checks positions 2d-1, 2d and 2d+1 at those costs.
records.sc: A costed evaluator for this expression family alone, and no bound on P3. Index arithmetic is charged separately and producing a complete output integer charges its length, so creating the bit 2d from zero still takes linear output space; the document states outright that the normal form is not a constant-cost operation on an arbitrarily long unread input. No collection of the actual norm into this family is established, and conjugation retains the unresolved part, (A^j E_d A^-j)(0) = 4^d A^j(1), so the singleton index j is not reduced.
records.nt: The exponential-to-logarithmic gap is the document's headline and was held by no record while the file counted as covered with three. Consistent with r30-p3-defect-derived-series-matrix rather than in tension with it: that obstruction concerns faithful representations of entire defect groups and does not forbid compact evaluation of particular group elements.

source_context.heading: 3. The reduction is substantial, and its costs are explicit

records.t: Adjacent cancellation does not extend to nonadjacent conjugate pairs
records.st: Refuted proposal: adjacent-defect cancellation extends to arbitrary conjugate pairs. With F_i = A^i E_2 A^-i the adjacent commutators satisfy [F_(i+1), F_i] = A^i E_3 A^-i and all fix odd inputs, but on the saved actual singleton row y = A^8(1) = 102849 the nonadjacent commutator gives [F_3, F_1](y) = 102465, with y XOR [F_3,F_1](y) = 2^7 + 2^8, which changes the actual time-eight centre readout at bit eight from one to zero. Composition is the ordinary convention of the document's section 1.
records.sc: An exact witness on one actual odd singleton input, refuting a rewriting rule rather than a class of algorithms. It does not assert that this commutator occurs uncancelled in the ordered actual norm, and it bears on P3 only by excluding one simplification.
records.nt: Distinct from r30-p3-balanced-defect-normal-form-collection, which refutes dropping shuffle corrections from the six-swap P8 collection in the actual norm and names the n=13 and n=14 readouts. This is the nonadjacent-pair identity with its exact values, and neither 102465 nor the XOR mask appears in that record or any other.

source_context.heading: 5. Adjacent cancellation does not permit arbitrary collection

records.t: No mechanical detector separates extracted from unextracted sections in this archive
records.st: Two candidate detectors for claim-level coverage debt were built over the 5,046 indexed source sections and both fail. A regex for this archive's own claim vocabulary fires in 37.4 percent of the 1,522 sections that received a record and 36.4 percent of the 3,524 that did not, a discrimination of 0.010. A detector for distinctive measured figures appearing in no record fires in 16.2 percent against 11.2 percent, and ranks per-row data tables and witness bitstring listings highest, which are exactly the sections a record is correctly not expected to hold cell by cell. The ranking that shipped instead, substantive sections per record, is not a claim detector: reading its top three files gave one false positive at rank 2, a synthesis index whose claims are correctly held at the reports it summarises, and two true positives, one of which sat at rank 123 and was reached by following a link rather than by the ranking.
records.sc: A measured statement about detectors on this corpus at 1,905 records, not a theorem and not transferable to another archive. It does not bound the remaining coverage debt, does not certify any file as covered, and says nothing about Rule 30. Three files of 493 were read.
records.nt: Both times coverage debt has been found here, it was found the same way: a figure restated in a second document, traced back to an origin holding no record. That produced r30-p3-fused-section-blocks-fixed-family-control and r30-p3-balanced-defect-normal-form-cost. The verdicts on the three audited files are carried in screen_claim_coverage.py's AUDITED ledger so a persistent false positive is not re-audited.

source_context.heading: 1. Two detectors were built and both failed

records.t: No fixed-width chronological window determines the index-15 guarded lift outcome
records.st: Keying the depth-13, 14 and 15 index-15 guarded-lift survivors by their newest k temporal pairs, the least k making the (reachable, live) outcome a function of the key is 11, 12, 13 respectively, which is n-1 at every layer. The pre-registered width-6 quotient is mixed in every layer (K1 fires), and k_min strictly increases across the three layers (K2 fires).
records.sc: Finite consistency check on the three saved guarded-lift layers only; not a statement about depth 16 or beyond, and not a refutation of every possible finite quotient of the lift.

source_context.heading: 4. The four unresolved joints

records.t: The index-15 guarded lift outcome does not factor through cycle monodromy or the guard mask
records.st: On the three saved guarded-lift layers, keying survivors by (cycle monodromy of the lifted transport, guard mask) still leaves 8 of 27, 14 of 30 and 20 of 32 classes mixed, and the reachable sheet set is a single monodromy orbit for only 17 of 125, 48 of 216 and 54 of 351 survivors. Separately, live sheets equal reachable sheets passing the guard mask, but this holds by definition: cover liveness and the mask evaluate the same guard predicate, so it carries no reachability information.
records.sc: Exploratory finite check on the three saved layers; rules out this specific candidate mechanism for the reachable set, not every possible one.

source_context.heading: 4. The four unresolved joints

records.t: The body2 transport automorphism has no small finite nucleus through power 11
records.st: Each 13 block of the index-15 family acts on the temporal tape as one tree automorphism g. The minimized automaton of g^n has 9, 42, 169, 618, 2115, 6904, 21880, 67620, 205416, 614415 and 1811799 states for n=1..11, and every state lies on a cycle. Since every cyclic state must belong to the nucleus of any contracting group containing g, this is a proved lower bound of 1,811,799 elements on such a nucleus. Neither the power closure nor the whole-group nucleus iteration closed within a 10-minute budget, and g shows no sign of finite order through tree level 10 (orders 2,4,16,32,32,128,256,512,1024,2048).
records.sc: A lower bound through n=11 only; not a proof that no finite nucleus exists at any n, and not a compression of the guarded lift even if one did, since the lift outcome does not factor through monodromy.

source_context.heading: 4. The four unresolved joints

records.t: A leading defect immediately before another defect is absorbable at gap>=2
records.st: For every k>=2 and every finite four-state suffix v, F^(k+2)(1 2^k 1 v) = F^(k+2)(2^(k+1) 1 v): a leading defect followed by k twos then another defect is exactly interchangeable with a plain 2, with no trailing padding required. Proved for every k>=2, not just a tested range: the pure-2 background is a fixed point of the morph (BOUNDARY[2]=1, PHI[2][1]=2, PHI[1][2]=1 form a 2-cycle, giving morph(2^n)=2^(n-1) for every n), and inverse_terminal/peel/terminal are each local enough that morph(2^k 1) and morph(2^(k+1)) agree at position 0 for every k>=2. The boundary cases k=0 (adjacent defects) and k=1 need padding 5 and 1 respectively, both sharp, verified as finite exact certificates.
records.sc: Resolves one narrow interrupted-run case with a genuine all-length proof for k>=2: two defects with gap>=2. Says nothing about three or more independently-spaced defects, the full RW/DLP hard-core source language, or a formal reduction to DLP/RW/SEP.

source_context.heading: 1. The lemma

records.t: The index-15 guarded lift outcome does not factor through a free-group cancellation invariant
records.st: Decode each saved depth-13, 14, 15 index-15 guarded-lift survivor column into its original high bit and ordered temporal pairs, exactly as the accepts() guard evaluator does. Reduce the pair sequence in the free monoid where adjacent pairs 1 and 2 annihilate, and take the invariant (residue length, XOR parity of the residue, original high bit). Keying the saved survivors by this invariant leaves 17 of 22, 22 of 22 and 23 of 24 classes mixed at old depths 12, 13 and 14 respectively.
records.sc: Exploratory finite check on the three saved guarded-lift layers only; rules out this specific candidate invariant, not every possible one.

source_context.heading: 4. The four unresolved joints

records.t: B-power doubling in t does not coarsen to the halved spatial site index
records.st: Candidate: digit_i of B^(2t)(0) is a function of digit_(i//2) of B^t(0) alone, modeled on the shift-commutation used in the alternating-guard classification. Refuted: the same digit_(i//2)(B^1(0)) value already maps to two different digit_i(B^2(0)) outcomes, and the count of mixed classes grows with t through t=18. The oracle used first reproduces exactly the four saved B-power rays and the site-1 high-bit collision at old times 0 and 4, and the Y_r rise/fall identity, as implementation controls.
records.sc: Rules out this specific coarsening candidate for the missing sublinear constructor; does not rule out a recursion keyed on a wider window or on the actual predecessor-word certificate.

source_context.heading: 5. 2026-09-18: a time-doubling candidate, killed

records.t: Measured high-bit invariance runs exceed a random-column control but do not grow with depth
records.st: For the real zero-seed orbits B^t(0) and C^t(0), the maximal empirical run length K with high(g^(a+2K)(0))_i = high(g^a(0))_i for some starting time a, scanned over t<=2200 and sites i<=2198, has mean K rising from about 7 near the origin to a plateau around 17 by site 50, staying at that plateau (16-18 mean, under 40 maximum) through site 2198 for both generators. The disconfirming control is the identical scan against an i.i.d. random bit column of the same shape: it plateaus too, at a mean around 9.5 (max 20), stable across seeds. The real plateau is consistently about 1.8 times the random plateau, so it is not a sampling artifact of a structureless column, but it still does not grow with site index over the tested range. This upper bounds what any correct guard-satisfying certificate of the rise-chain-transparency theorem could exploit, since guard-satisfying invariance is a special case of raw high-bit persistence.
records.sc: A finite empirical scan up to depth 2200, not a proof that K stays bounded for every n. If the plateau holds at all depths, this specific certificate mechanism gives at most a constant per-query saving and cannot alone yield a sublinear P3 algorithm; it does not exclude other mechanisms.

source_context.heading: 5. Measured chain lengths do not grow with depth, and exceed a random control

records.t: The low-bit nonzero-count identity does not telescope across two sites
records.st: Equation (4) gives an unconditional closed form: low(digit_i(B^N(0))) equals the parity of #{s<=N: digit_(i-1)(B^s(0))!=0}, verified against 89,400 direct cases with zero mismatches. Testing whether that running parity at site i is a function of the running parity at site i-2 alone is mixed at every one of 80 tested sites, with zero exceptions. Algebraic inspection of the bitplane equations (1) explains why: whether digit_i of the output ray is zero depends on the same-time output at site i-1 and the same-site input from the previous time step, an inherently two-dimensionally coupled dependency, not a telescoping one-site count.
records.sc: Rules out this specific two-site coarsening of the count; the exact low-bit identity itself remains a real, unconditional result, just not one that escapes the site-time coupling by itself.

source_context.heading: 6. Two further candidates, both killed

records.t: The light-cone periodic tail of B^N(0) never reaches the actual query site
records.st: B^N(0) is spatially eventually periodic (period 16, stable from N=300 through N=2000 tested), an information-front effect: the scan automaton fed constant-zero input past its front settles into a small limit cycle. The onset site scales linearly with N at a measured ratio between 1.5 and 1.65 (N=100 through N=2000). The singleton query site h-1 at depth N=h+1+e has site-to-depth ratio about 1, strictly below the measured onset ratio at every tested N, so the periodic tail never reaches the query site; the region of interest is always inside the transient.
records.sc: A finite empirical measurement of period and onset ratio up to N=2000, not a proof for all N. It explains why a spatial-periodicity shortcut cannot help this route rather than proposing one to test further.

source_context.heading: 6. 2026-09-18: a real spatial-periodicity effect that cannot reach the query site

records.t: Width-26 right-seed census: maximum zero run 44 against fair-coin expectation 36.3, two seeds at or above line+3
records.st: Streaming census over all 2^26 right seeds at M=4096 (forward-boundary/census_scale.py, six parts): 32,341,063 distinct traces of 67,108,864 seeds. The longest zero run Z of the reconstructed row has maximum 44 (seeds 2d3e775 and 1d3e775 in hex, tail 0), median 11, p90 14, p99 17, and the longest tail run is 25 (seed 32c56f7). The fair-coin expected maximum over 32,341,063 independent samples of length 4096 is 36.3 (P(max>=44)=0.0037) and the line log2(NM) is 36.9, so exactly 2 seeds reach line+3.
records.sc: One width and one M. Distinct traces share prefixes, so they are fewer than N independent samples. A measurement of the wall-trace zero-run margin of right seeds, not a theorem about any period, and not a bound for other widths. Supersedes the earlier statement that no seed at any width reaches line+3, which held only through width 24.
records.nt: 14.56 CPU hours on six workers. census_scale.py was validated at width 16 against the full instrument (max 26, 31,779 distinct, tail 17). Expected values from strengthen/faircoin_widths.py (faircoin_widths.log). Folded into the period-two paper by commits b41b8c3 and 3b59035.

records.t: The six width-26 and width-28 seeds at line+3 share one 24-bit prefix and form a local tail cluster, not a family
records.st: All six flagged seeds share the low 24 bits 0xd3e775 (cells 1..24) and differ only in the width-extension bits (cells 25..28). Of the 16 settings of those four bits at width 28 with the prefix fixed, exactly 4 give Z=44 (nibbles 0001, 0010, 0110, 1010, the flagged seeds and no others) and the other 12 give Z between 9 and 14. The hot set is not closed under XOR (0001 xor 0010 = 0011 is not hot). At width 26 only nibble values 0..3 are reachable and exactly 1 and 2 are hot, matching the census's two flagged seeds.
records.sc: One prefix, one width. Shows that this cluster is a local concentration of fair-coin-tail events and gives no evidence of a width-invariant or growing family. Does not show that no other prefix carries a family.

records.t: Exhaustive period-two horizon for rows of support radius w up to 10
records.st: Over all 2^(2w+1) rows of support radius w (the zero row included, both phases of 0101... counted), the longest prefix of the centre column that alternates has length 7, 7, 7, 7, 9, 10, 10, 15, 17, 17 for w=1..10, attained by 1, 1, 1, 2, 7, 11, 67, 3, 1, 2 rows. In the paper's convention H(2,w) is this length (the horizon index is the length minus 1), so H(2,w)-w = 6, 5, 4, 3, 4, 4, 3, 7, 8, 7.
records.sc: Finite computation for w<=10. Proves nothing for larger w and no bound of the form w+constant. Compare H(1,w)=w+2 exactly, which the period-two data do not follow.
records.nt: Also reproduced by an independent numpy implementation and by an unpublished draft by N. Berzai (2026-09), which reports the same table and the same constant-case tables. The repository script is the source.
