records.t: The wall trace conjugates the zero-wall step F on {0,1}^N to the full one-sided 2-shift
records.st: Let c(x)_t = F^(t+1)(x)_1 for the zero-wall step F on one-sided sequences. Then c o F = sigma o c, and c is continuous and bijective by left-permutivity, hence a homeomorphism. F is therefore topologically conjugate to the full one-sided 2-shift, F is two-to-one, h_top(F)=log 2, and the natural extension is the two-sided full shift (the Smale horseshoe on its invariant set). Every conjugacy invariant of F (horseshoe braid types, template linking data, kneading data) is an invariant of the full shift and carries no information about S3.
records.sc: Whole-space statement; the corpus had recorded only the restriction (X_inf, F^2). The Rule 30 content sits entirely in the coordinate change c and the countable set c(Fin), which the conjugacy class does not determine. h_top(F)=log 2 does not conflict with the bound h(R)<=0.124 because R is the language of the single actual trace, not of (F,{0,1}^N). Nothing here narrows (PT2).
records.nt: Standard (Hedlund line) argument stated for the whole space. Finite check on all x of length 16 (refute_knot-theory_extra.log X2). Refutation pass of attempt-knot-theory.md, 2026-09-18.

records.t: The wall-trace section count is at least n+1 at every depth, so c is not finite-state
records.st: Let count(n) be the number of distinct sections of the wall trace c at prefix depth n. Lemma U-a: for prefixes u, v of any lengths, the sections g|_u and g|_v are equal iff Phi_u = Phi_v, where Phi_u(y)=F^|u|(uy). Lemma U-b: if x is finite and nonzero with last 1 at p, then F^t(x) has its last 1 at exactly p+t. Theorem: count(n)>=n+1, using the prefixes 0^n and 0^(p-1) 1 0^(n-p) for p=1..n. So c has infinitely many distinct sections and no finite automaton computes c.
records.sc: Linear lower bound only. The measured growth is exponential (ratios near 5/3) but exponential growth is not proved. Closes the automaton-group arm of the knot-theory bridges as a theorem. Does not address (PT2) or S3 itself.
records.nt: Finite checks: U-b on every nonzero u of length <=14 and t<=20; the n+1 classes are distinct under the exact criterion for n=1..10 (refute_knot-theory_unbounded.log).

records.t: The Rule 30 braidings R1 and R2 on cyclic columns have image 3^n and violate Yang-Baxter for every n from 2 to 12
records.st: Two braidings built from Rule 30 on cyclic columns of length n have image exactly 3^n (T(a,b)[t] ignores b[t] where a[t]=1, and the sum over a of 2^(zeros of a) is 3^n), so neither is invertible. records.t: The claim that every knot-theory bridge from Rule 30 to S3 is shut by missing invertibility or finite-stateness is refuted as an argument
records.st: The attempt-knot-theory.md claim that the pseudo-Anosov, biquandle and kneading/template/automaton-group bridges are all closed at their entry conditions is refuted as an argument. F is conjugate to the full 2-shift, so bridge 1 is open but empty (the horseshoe), the kneading and template arms of bridge 3 close for the same reason and not for lack of finite-stateness, and bridge 2 over-generalises from two specific braidings. Only the automaton-group arm needs finite-stateness, and it is now closed as a theorem. The attempt's conclusion that no S3 information comes out of the three bridges survives on the corrected grounds.
records.sc: Verdict on one attempt document and its diagnosis. The literature attributions in the attempt are carried forward unverified. Nothing here narrows (PT2).

records.t: Exponential growth of the wall-trace section count is not proved, and the outward-edge method does not reach it
records.st: count(n)>=mu^n for some mu>1 is open. The measured ratio falls slowly, from 1.671 at n=15 to 1.651 at n=22 (r30-s3-section-count-exact-n22), and the distinguisher y=0^inf alone separates 1, 2, 4, 6, 11, 17, 28, 47, 80, 130, 205, 343, 571 classes at n=0..12. Negative findings: same-section prefix pairs differ up to bit n-1 for n=3..11, so no outer-bit agreement lemma exists; sparse prefix families are not section-injective (first collisions at n=4, 8, 8 for gaps 2, 3, 4); image counting |F^k({0,1}^n 0^inf)| keeps shrinking in k and cannot give the bound; backward-tree tails number 1305 at n=14 against 1548 for the image count; there is no linear-algebra separation in the GF(2) algebraic normal form.
records.sc: A negative result about one method (Lemma U-b with image and tail counting); the exponential bound may still hold. It needs control of the damage front on Rule 30's non-permutive side at a sub-unit speed, a Lyapunov-exponent style statement that is not proved. A Cauchy-Schwarz heuristic, not a computation, predicts mu near 2^0.62=1.54.
records.nt: Prior-art search 2026-09-18 found no source counting sections of a CA trace map or treating Rule 30's trace map as a transducer, and no rigorous bound on Rule 30's non-permutive-side damage speed (the 0.2428 figure is Wolfram's measurement, NKS p. 949 note). Neither the section-count sequence nor the distinct-row sequence I(n) = |F^n({0,1}^n 0^inf)| (1, 2, 4, 6, 11, 17, 28, 47, 80, 130, 205, 343, 571, 935, 1548 for n=0..14) is in the OEIS (searched 2026-09-18). Nearest named quantity: automaticity (Shallit-Breitbart 1996, not opened), where count(n) >= n+1 exceeds Karp's (n+3)/2 bound for nonregular languages.

records.t: Wall-trace sections are decided by the hypotenuse and masked inner diagonals of the prefix's own zero-wall diagram
records.st: For prefixes u, v of length n, write B_t(u) = F^t(u)_(n-t) for t=0..n-1 and C_t(u) = F^(t-1)(u)_(n-t) for t=1..n (C_n is the wall cell, 0). Then g|_u = g|_v iff B_t(u) = B_t(v) for all t and C_t(u) = C_t(v) for every t with B_(t-1) = 0. So count(n) equals the number of distinct signatures (B, C restricted to B_(t-1)=0) over u in {0,1}^n, computable in O(n^2) per prefix and independent of the continuation y.
records.sc: Exact characterisation at every depth n, via the exact section criterion (sections agree iff F^n(uy) = F^n(vy) for all y). The proof tracks damage leaking out of the prefix triangle through three boundary cells, and uses permutivity in a fresh y bit to push a damaged front to time n. It says nothing about the growth rate of count(n).
records.nt: Finite corroboration in refute_knot-theory_triangle_N22.log: T1 signature partition equals the exact 2n-criterion partition on all prefixes for n=1..10; T4 equal signatures have equal children signatures on all prefixes for n=1..16. Supersedes the lookahead n+1 lower bounds (n=15..21) and the separating-window measurement w(n) as ways to decide section equality; both were in the source's 2026-09-18 follow-up pass and are not catalogued separately. Fourth follow-up pass of the refutation of attempt-knot-theory.md, 2026-09-18.

records.t: The rises of rho are dense on the measured prefixes of B^h(0), so a sparse rise index is no shortcut; no lower bound on the last-rise query follows
records.st: rho (rising edges of A=low(B^h(0))) has density 0.150, 0.250, 0.214 and 0.249 on the four measured prefixes, digits/h = 400/40, 2000/100, 2000/500 and 4000/1000, with maximum gap between consecutive rises 8, 10, 10 and 13. The rises are not sparse on that range, so a summary that stores or skips between rise positions is not sublinear there. No lower bound follows. B^h(0) is eventually periodic for every h, being the image of the constant word under a three-state Mealy machine, and r30-p3-session-limits-supplement-spatial-periodicity-out-of-reach measures that tail; most of each prefix measured here lies in it; and on it the rises have positive density with gaps bounded by the period while the last rise before any position is O(1) arithmetic from the period word. Positive density with bounded gaps therefore does not force Theta(h) work. The 2026-09-18 statement that the gaps stay in single digits and that no index can answer a last-rise query in o(h) is withdrawn.
records.sc: A finite measurement on four prefixes with h <= 1000, recomputed 2026-09-21 with identical counts. Refutes only a sparse or skip-list summary of rho's rise positions on that range. It is not a lower bound on any constructor: building the last rise at position h-1 and the range parity from binary n in o(h) work is the open obligation of node p3_control_construction and is untouched. The split of the counted rises between head and tail in the source (head density 0.25 to 0.27) is an in-session recomputation with no saved artifact; the tail itself is the measured object of the record named in the statement. Does not address whether A itself (not just its rise mask) admits a sublinear representation via the Phi conjugacy or K-automaton of section 4 of the implicit-boundary doc.

records.t: LZ77 factor counts of the first n base-four digits of B^n(0) match a random word at n = 64..1024; no grammar lower bound follows
records.st: The self-referential LZ77 factor count of the first n base-four digits of B^n(0) (p3_itinerary_conjugacy.k_prefix, state 'B', n steps from 0) is 29, 52, 85, 145 and 253 at n = 64, 128, 256, 512 and 1024, against 30, 50, 90, 145 and 256 for one i.i.d. quaternary draw per length (random.seed(0)) and 5 for a period-4 control. The real count is within 6% of the random draw at each length and z/n falls from 0.453 to 0.247 for both; over 20 draws, recomputed 2026-09-21, the control ranges over 29-35, 49-55, 80-90, 143-152 and 252-262 and the real count lies inside every range. The five rows are five different words, each inside the aperiodic head of B^n(0), and the measured object is the digit word, not the binary low field A of the implicit-boundary document. Since z <= g for a straight-line grammar producing a string, a plain grammar producing the n = 1024 word has at least 253 rules. No sublinearity statement follows: the saved output records flat_or_growing_ratio false, and every length-n word over a fixed alphabet has a grammar of O(n/log n) rules through its LZ78 parse, which is o(n), so matching a random word is not evidence that no grammar is sublinear. The quaternary evaluator of RESULTS-p3-implicit-boundary-investigation.md section 4 is not bounded by this count, its grammar being over the chronological A/B/C generator word and not over the digit word. The 2026-09-18 statement that this rules out every grammar construction is withdrawn.
records.sc: A finite measurement on five words with n <= 1024 and one random draw per length. Refutes only the hope that LZ77 finds in these digit words the repetition it finds in a periodic word. It is not a lower bound on any grammar, evaluator or algorithm and does not close the Phi conjugacy / K-automaton route. The 20-draw spread and the prefix comparison are in-session recomputations with no saved artifact. Does not address the binary low field A alone, grammars with repetition nodes, a representation that answers the singleton query without producing the digit word, the rise mask (for which r30-p3-two-time-rise-density-refuted is likewise no lower bound), or the unrestricted no-sublinear-algorithm question, which stays open.

records.t: Prefix lemma: the pin at period two holds through T exactly while the left row agrees with the reconstruction xhat(y)
records.st: Let W be a finite left row (W_m = s(0,-m), zeros beyond its width), y a finite right seed, and evolve (W,0,y) by plain Rule 30 with no boundary. Then for every T>=1, s(t,0) = t mod 2 for all t<=T iff W_m = xhat_m(y) for all m<=T, where xhat(y) is the left row reconstructed by left permutivity from the trace rho_k(y) = s(2k,1) of the right half-line driven by the pin. Consequently the pin holds forever iff W = xhat(y), so (PT2) at period two is exactly the statement that xhat(y) has infinite support for every finite y, and the pin survival of every finite configuration is a zero run of one reconstructed row.
records.sc: Period-two pin only. Proof is an induction on T using Lemma 2 of RESULTS-FORWARD-HALVING-LEMMA.md (the catalog holds that document's main theorem as r30-fhl-halving-theorem); finiteness of y is never used. Proves no exclusion by itself: it converts (PT2) into the infinite-support question for xhat(y).
records.nt: Section 10 of the source: referee pass on the two lemmas found both HOLD (crosscheck/verify-0916/margin/REFEREE.md; two write-up corrections adopted), and an independent second implementation (crosscheck/right-seed-margin/rcheck.py, 100 of 100 prefix-lemma gate, 300 of 300 random pairs failing the pin at exactly the first disagreement).

records.t: A finite right seed with an eventually periodic trace has no finite left partner keeping the pin
records.st: If rho(y) is eventually periodic then no finite left row keeps the period-two pin against y. Sketch as written: if (W,0,y) kept the pin forever, W is nonzero, column -1 is l_t with l_(2k) = 1 - rho_k and l_odd = 1, so l has the even period P = 2p from t_0 = 2k_0; by left permutivity every left column is P-periodic for t >= t_0; but Rule 30 moves the left edge of the finite W one cell per step, so a far column takes value 0 at time m - w_L - P and 1 at time m - w_L, congruent mod P, a contradiction.
records.sc: Uniform in the width of y and in the seed; this is the Jen 1990 / Kopra argument for two adjacent eventually periodic columns applied to the pin and its forced neighbour. It excludes (PT2) only for seeds whose trace settles; a counterexample needs a right seed whose trace never settles, and the source reports no sign that every trace settles.
records.nt: Labelled [U] in the source. Rests on the external two-adjacent-columns theorem of Jen and Kopra, applied as in the source. The 377 certified seeds satisfy (PT2) by this lemma alone; the period-7 xhat computation for them is a confirmation.

records.t: Backward depth recurrences for the episode scan fields A_d(n) and B_d(n)
records.st: At time n within an episode of original length r, with depth d measured inward from the current terminal end, A_d(n) = a_(r+n-1-d)(n) and B_d(n) = b_(r+n-1-d)(n). records.t: Proposition A: if the lone-seed centre column is eventually periodic then its zero set Z is infinite and r restricted to Z is not eventually periodic
records.st: Let S* be the lone-seed Rule 30 diagram, c*_t = S*(t,0), l*_t = S*(t,-1), r*_t = S*(t,1), Z = {t : c*_t = 0}. If c* is eventually p-periodic then (i) l* is not eventually periodic (by the identification of the true left half-plane with the driven one and the left-column theorem), (ii) Z is infinite (otherwise c*_t = 1 for t >= t2 gives l*_t = 0, eventually periodic), and (iii) r*|Z is not eventually periodic: with k the number of zeros of c* per period p, the enumeration of Z satisfies z_(i+k) = z_i + p for i >= i0, so an eventually periodic r*|Z with period q would force l* to be P-periodic with P = qp, contradicting (i). Hence R1 (if c* eventually periodic then r*|Z eventually periodic) is equivalent to P1.
records.sc: Lone seed only. Uses the theorem c4526cb8dfb7eb13 for the left-column aperiodicity step. Numeric gates in the source: CHECK6 identifies the true left half-plane with the driven one cell for cell to T=3000 (9,012,003 cells, 0 mismatches); CHECK7 exercises the enumeration and periodicity algebra on 312 synthetic drives, 0 failures.

records.t: Width-16 right-seed margin: the longest zero run of xhat is 26 at M=4096, the extremes of a fair coin, with a body carrying the shields
records.st: Over all 2^16 right seeds of width 16 (31,779 distinct traces to k=2048), the longest zero run of xhat_1..xhat_M has maximum 26 at M=4096 (p99 17, p90 14, median 11), against maxima 28, 29 and 27 for the fair-coin, hard-core and no-11-no-00000 nulls; the maximum grows by 0, 3, 2, 1 per doubling of M from 256, the longest tail run is 17, and no seed is a counterexample candidate (pre-registered bound 32). Against the exact longest-run law of a fair coin of length 4096 (mean 11.33, median 11, p90 14, p99 17) the maximum, median, p90 and p99 match (P(max >= 26) = 0.62) but the distribution does not: chi-square 1,100 on 16 degrees of freedom, of which 972 come from 105 seeds with Z <= 7 (against 9.4 expected, the periodic-trace seeds whose xhat has period 7) and the rest from an excess at Z = 14, 15 (+7.9 and +4.6 standard units) and deficits at 11 and 13; the fair-coin and hard-core models pass the same test (chi-square 10 and 20 on 17 degrees of freedom, p = 0.90 and 0.27) and the two-factor model does not (chi-square 32, p = 0.016). Extension: width 18 at M=4096, 126,762 distinct traces, maximum 28 against a fair-coin expected maximum 28.3, tail 17; width 20 at M=2048, 505,964 distinct, maximum 26 against 29.3 (P(max <= 26) = 0.022), tail 21; width 16 at M=8192, maximum 26 (expected 27.3), tail 16.
records.sc: Widths 16 to 20 here; the streaming census at widths 22 to 30 is r30-rsm-census-w26-margin and its siblings, and at widths 26 and 28 seeds do reach line+3, so the sentence that the extremes are fair-coin deep and never deeper held only through width 24. A measurement of the wall-trace zero-run margin, not a theorem about any period. Distinct traces share prefixes, so they are fewer than N independent samples.

records.t: Triangular bijectivity of the endpoint-to-inverse-cut prefix map
records.st: For every endpoint word e over the four states and every t>=0, with e_0,...,e_(t-1) fixed, the map e_t -> I(e)_t is a permutation of the four states (the newest cut cell is a permutation of the new endpoint symbol, inductively because phi(l,.) is a permutation of the right argument). records.t: The guarded lift of a four-cycle has translation monodromy at the next depth
records.st: Let C be a first-return cycle of depth-n guard survivors with total word W, M its monodromy on the depth-(n+1) pair and O an M-orbit, so the survivors over O lie on one lifted cycle traversing C |O| times. If |O| = 4, that is M is a four-cycle, the lifted monodromy on the depth-(n+2) pair has t = 0, so it is a translation and never a four-cycle; if |W| is even it is the identity or the central translation (a,b) -> (a+1,b). If |O| = 2 and O is closed under adding (1,0), the lifted monodromy is a translation when |W| is even. Proof: at each symbol the traversals carry one transported copy of O, the next layer's coefficients there are t = 1+U' and c = U OR V', and summing over the (1,0)-pairs gives a per-symbol t-sum of |O|+|O|/2 and, for |O| = 4, a c-sum of 1; t and c add under composition. Hence the order-four reproduction mechanism never acts at two consecutive depths of one lineage.
records.sc: Every depth of a guarded lift built on the triangular extension; the even-length clauses cover the body (13) of index 15. It constrains where four-cycles can occur and does not bound the survivor tree or decide mortality. Checked with no violation on all 82 and 134 child cycles of the two saved index-15 generations and on every column of the pure (13) block through depth 8, all at even word length. An exhaustive two-layer enumeration under arbitrary lower constants realizes at even length every combination the lemma does not exclude, and at odd length confirms the parity-free clause: every four-point orbit lifts to a free reflection, while every two-point orbit closed under (1,0) lifts with t = 1, so the even-length hypothesis of that clause is needed.

records.t: Every seam entry at a guarded-lift layer has one type, fixed by the first-star monodromy
records.st: In the guarded lift of 213(13)^a1213(13)^b03 let P_n be the first-star period at depth n, h_d the action of (13)^(P_(d-1)) on the depth-d pair over the prefix column, and O_d the h_d-orbit of that column's pair, so P_d = |O_d| P_(d-1). The |O_d| new phases over any old phase with an entry enter G_(d-1) at one vertex, with pairs g(O_d) for one group element g. Every group element fixes the direction (1,0), so at each layer all entries are points, all are z-pairs {x, x+(1,0)}, all are guard lines (the four accepted sets of the balanced guard lemma) or all are the fibre. Hence every cycle of G_(d-1) receives an entry; at a z-pair layer every old survivor has a child and at a fibre layer exactly two; a survivor dies only when its reachable set lies in the guard line disjoint from its accepted line, so survivors on cycles with monodromy z or a four-cycle never die and fixing-reflection cycles lose survivors only at point layers. From the prefix orbit alone, for d <= 24: fibre at 2, 8; z-pair at 3, 12, 17, 18, 24; guard line at 4, 5, 13-15, 19-22; point at 6, 7, 9-11, 16, 23.
records.sc: Every depth of the index-15 guarded lift; the proof uses only the triangular extension lemma. Validated on layers 5-16, eleven of them from a pre-registered rerun of the unmodified lift from the exhaustive depth-4 base, independently checked, including the predicted |G_7| = 31 and no deaths at the z-pair layer 12. cap18_entry_supply.py computes the schedule from one pass over the depth-24 prefix orbit and checks it against layers 5-16 and the exhaustive first periods at depths 4, 8, 12 and 16. It says where deaths can occur; it does not bound the survivor tree or decide mortality. That a cycle's reachable pairs are the monodromy closure of its entries is true by construction and is not part of the claim.

The candidate inductive invariant, that each has a child on such a cycle, fails in 9 of the 10 registered generations G_4 to G_5 through G_13 to G_14: 143 of 205 parents fail, 88 of 123 out of sample, against 103.8 expected under the registered independence floor and 126.0 under the corrected one. records.t: P2 route 1 (shell seam) can enter Rule 30 only through the adjacent-block cross term, so it is a carrier for routes 2 and 3
records.st: Writing a level-(k+1) piece as a concatenation uv, the four-coordinate law gives I(uv) - I_u - I_v = n_v D_u^2 + 2 D_u A_v. The law is an identity on arbitrary signed words, so any bound derived from it alone also holds for the all-ones word; and the halves [2^(k+1), 3*2^k) and [3*2^k, 2^(k+2)) of shell k+1 are not shells, so bounding the cross term from the halves' own bounds is the triangle inequality over aligned blocks and needs sum |D| over the 2^(K-j) aligned blocks of shell K to be o(2^K), which is stronger than P2. Hence the only place Rule 30 can enter route 1 is an estimate of how D_u and A_v of adjacent aligned blocks are coupled through the spacetime between them, which is route 2's residual or route 3's boundary term. The P2 readout (n, D, A, I) is strictly coarser than the P3 centre-bit readout (+--+ and -++- both have summary (4, 0, 0, 2)), so route 1 is not route 4 in disguise. An exact compressed seam would only compute (D, A, I) faster and bounds nothing.
records.sc: A reduction of a proof route, not progress on P2. The full seam (Hashlife node DAG) is measured superlinear, n^1.57 fit through n = 8192 (finite evidence), and a bounded seam would make the centre column 2-automatic (not proved false). Whether a level-growing congruence on the reachable lone-seed node DAG refining the summary compresses it is unmeasured.

records.t: Rule 30 has no spatially twisted local additive conservation law of window <= 11 for any periodic weight of period 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 or 8
records.st: For every window m = 1..11 and every twist omega of order p in {1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8}, the solution space of rho(y_0..y_(m-1)) - rho(x_1..x_m) = J(x_0..x_m) - omega J(x_1..x_(m+1)) for Rule 30 has density dimension exactly 2^(m-1), the trivial twisted coboundaries (66 of 66 rows). The rank is exact over GF(1000000009), where omega has order p; a rank mod a prime above q is at most the rank over Q(omega), so a trivial count mod q certifies the trivial count. By a Vandermonde argument over shifts this covers every periodic weight of those periods, the quarter-wave sin(pi i / 2) included; every primitive root of each order was also run explicitly through m = 9 (108 rows, all trivial). Controls: Rule 184 untwisted gives 2^(m-1)+1, Rule 204 gives 2^m at p = 1, 3, 4, and Rule 236 at p = 4 has excess 1, 2, 3 at m = 2, 3, 4, a genuine twisted law; the solver's null vectors are conserved under direct summation on random finite rows. So a route-3 identity x_0 - 1/2 = Phi(x^(t+1)) - Phi(x^t) + (cone-edge boundary terms) with local twisted Phi cannot remove the interior current.
records.sc: Windows <= 11, twists that are roots of unity of orders 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 only. Says nothing about growing windows, history-dependent or non-additive invariants, temporally twisted invariants Phi(Fx) = lambda Phi(x), or identities valid only on the lone-seed orbit rows, which need not decompose into local equations. records.t: The guarded-lift survivor mass halves exactly at z-pair and fibre layers and on z or rotation cycles
records.st: Weight each depth-n column of the guarded lift of 213(13)^a1213(13)^b03 by the parameter pairs that reach it (a uniform modulo the first-star period P_n, then b uniform modulo that phase's body2 orbit length). The mass mu_n of G_n is then the limiting fraction of pairs a<2^i, b<2^j surviving n guards, and the family is uniformly mortal exactly when some mu_n = 0. A new phase puts uniform mass on the monodromy orbit of its transported entry pair, the new phases over one old phase enter at one vertex with pairs g(O_(n+1)) (entry-supply lemma), and every group element commutes with adding (1,0), which maps each guard line to its complement. Hence if layer n+1 has z-pair or fibre entries, or a column's cycle has monodromy z or a rotation, exactly half of that column's mass survives, and mu_(n+1) = mu_n/2 at every z-pair and fibre layer. Per old phase and column the kept fraction is exactly 1/2 at z-pair and fibre layers and for z or rotation monodromy. At guard-line layers it is 1/4 or 3/4 for fixing reflections, 1/2 for free reflections unless the entry line is one of their orbits (then 0, 1/2 or 1), and 0, 1/2 or 1 for the identity. At point layers it is 1/2, 0 or 1 for fixing reflections, 0, 1/2 or 1 for free reflections and 0 or 1 for the identity. Mass can vanish only at guard-line and point layers, on identity and free-reflection columns, and at point layers also on fixing reflections.
records.sc: Every depth of the index-15 guarded lift. The proof uses only the entry-supply, balanced guard and triangular extension lemmas, none specific to index 15, but it has been checked only on index 15: cap18_survivor_mass.py asserts every case on every old phase at every column of layers 5-16, with 942 phase-columns deviating from 1/2 at guard-line and point layers as the control that the checks are not vacuous. It says where the mass must halve. It gives no lower bound at guard-line or point layers and decides neither uniform nor individual mortality.

records.t: Index-15 survivor mass equals the lifetime census exactly through depth 16, within 0.875 to 1.301 times 2^-n
records.st: For 213(13)^a1213(13)^b03 the survivor mass mu_n computed from the guarded lift equals the fraction of the pre-registered census box a<2^11, b<2^16 that survives n guards, as exact rationals at every n = 4..16. The box is exact there because P_16 = 2^11 and every survivor-carrying body2 orbit has length at most 2^16. For n = 1..16, 2^n mu_n = 1, 1, 1, 0.875, 0.875, 0.906, 1.063, 1.063, 1.047, 1.188, 1.242, 1.242, 1.301, 1.289, 1.275, 1.227 (mu_16 = 2513/2^27). The kept fraction was exactly 1/2 at the fibre layer 8, the z-pair layer 12 and the guard-line layer 5. At the other guard-line and point layers it ran from 0.481 (layer 16) to 0.586 (layer 7). Per old phase and column, the kept fractions 0 and 1 occurred about equally often (205 and 186 at layer 16), and columns on z or rotation cycles held 18 to 50 percent of the mass. The census's record rising one step per doubling of its box is 2^n mu_n staying near 1. The per-layer sums mod 2 of the cycle coefficients t and c are not forced: both values occur.
records.sc: Exact finite computation through depth 16. Past it only the exact halving at z-pair and fibre layers is known, which gives mu_17 = 2513/2^28 and mu_18 = 2513/2^29. The data are consistent with unbounded lifetimes and prove nothing about them.

records.t: Clocked quarter-wave boundary corrections are refuted at every radius where the lone seed repeats a phase-matched centre window, and vacuous above, for every period through 16 at T = 2^20
records.st: For K_t - rho_(t mod p) = h_((t+1) mod p)(W_r(t+1)) - lambda*h_(t mod p)(W_r(t)) on the first 2^20 lone-seed rows with K_t computed from q_i on the full row: a phase-matched repeated window pair with unequal K refutes it for every h_a, rho_a and lambda, phase-dependent lambda_a included, at every r <= r_pair(p), with r_pair(p) = 18, 18, 16, 17, 17, 16, 17, 15, 16, 15 for p = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 12, 16. At every p the kill reaches the last radius at which any phase-matched repeat exists, so no radius has repeats and survives; above it nothing repeats and the identity is satisfiable trivially. Every horizon is within 2 of the pre-registered budget law (2r+1 or 2r+3) + log2(p) <= 2*log2(T) - 1 and within 2 of the null model, the per-radius phase-matched repeat population tracks the null to between 0.882 and 1.058 over r = 8..14, and the rate of equal K at phase-matched repeated pairs shows no excess at any period: at r = 9 the orbit-minus-null difference in Poisson sigma is +0.30, +0.41, +0.94 and +0.69 at p = 4, 8, 12 and 16, against -0.16, -1.56, +0.77, -0.10 and -1.33 at the controls p = 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 and -1.26 at p = 1. records.t: Boundary corrections reading up to thirteen past windows are refuted to the same radius as memoryless ones, and the radius-18 refutation holds for every support shape inside that neighbourhood
records.st: Two results on the first 2^20 lone-seed rows, for K_t - rho = h(W(t+1)) - lambda*h(W(t)) with K_t computed from q_i on the full row. (S) If (s, t) is a killing pair at radius R, meaning W_R(s) = W_R(t), W_R(s+1) = W_R(t+1) and K_s != K_t, then every h reading only cells in [-R, R] of one row is constant on {s, t} and on {s+1, t+1}, so the identity is refuted for that h for every lambda and rho whatever the shape of h's support: off-centre window, masked or sparse subset, weighted sum, parity, or a half-row sum truncated to the neighbourhood. At R = 18 the orbit supplies such a pair, times 544690 and 987828 with currents 54 and 474, and all 361 off-centre windows with |c| + r <= 18 agree at both times and both successors while the two rows differ only at cells of absolute value 19 to 30. (H) A correction reading the last d windows of radius r is a function of the single window of radius R = r + d - 1 at the earliest of those times, by the Rule 30 light cone, so the class is the same instrument with the current lagged by L = d - 1. Over lags L = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, that is depths 1 to 13, scanned on a common time range of 1,048,563 so the window data is bitwise identical across lags, r_pair = 18, r_one = 18 and r_half = 19 at every lag, equal to the birthday prediction and to the null at every lag, so orbit minus null is 0 throughout. From r = 14 upward every repeated window pair is a killing pair at every lag (352, 82, 23, 4, 2 pairs at r = 14..18, none at 19), so no radius has repeats and survives. The lag does move the instrument: killing_pairs at r = 9 ranges over 303,655 to 303,702 across the ten lags while repeated_pairs is identical at 304,018. The rate of equal lagged current at repeated pairs at r = 9 shows no excess at any lag, (o-n)/sqrt(o+n) running from -1.50 at L = 5 to +1.18 at L = 6 against a pre-registered Bonferroni flag of 3. Consequence, for the measured depths d <= 13 only: a depth-d correction at radius r is refuted whenever r + d - 1 <= 18, and by (S) applied at each tested lag, where both radius-18 pairs are killing, the refutation there covers every support shape inside that neighbourhood and not only windows. Depths above 13 are not covered: (S) separates a pair by K_s != K_t, so at lag L it needs K_(s+L) != K_(t+L), which is measured only for L <= 12.

records.t: Pre-registered census measures the index-15 survivor mass at layers 19 and 20, the first two the halving lemma leaves open, finding kept fractions 0.5042 and 0.4991 and lifetime 36
records.st: Pre-registered in experiments/rule30/PREREGISTRATION-cap18-mass-census-depth20.md. A census of 213(13)^a1213(13)^b03 over the nested grid a < 2^13, 2^14, 2^15 against b < 2^19, 2^20, 2^21, one sweep per a and 2^36 pairs in the largest box, reproduces the committed mu_n for every n <= 18 in all nine boxes with no member reaching the step cap of 96. Layers 19 through 22 carry guard-line entries, where the survivor-mass lemma gives no lower bound. At layer 19 all six boxes covering P_19 = 2^14 agree: mu_19 = 10137/2^32, a kept fraction of 10137/20104 = 0.5042 and 2^19 mu_19 = 1.2374. That is the pre-registered (Y) on the band [11/25, 27/50]. At layer 20 the pre-registered verdict is (I): b < 2^19 undersamples P_20 = 2^15 and the covering boxes disagree, a < 2^15 with b < 2^19 giving 5055/2^32 against 20239/2^34 from the two that saturate. Post hoc only, those two agree on mu_20 = 20239/2^34, a kept fraction of 20239/40548 = 0.4991. The pre-registered half-sample prediction fired as a kill (K): the a < 2^13 boxes carry half the depth-19 phase classes and put k_19 at 0.4906 and 0.4894 against the true 0.5042, missing by 0.0136 and 0.0149 where 0.01 was allowed, so their exploratory fractions past depth 18 are not a guide to the mass at that precision. The covered box replaces them: 2^n times the surviving fraction in a < 2^15, b < 2^21 stays between 1.230 and 1.295 at every depth 19 to 30, against the 1.18 to 1.75 the half-sampled boxes drifted through. The record lifetime rose to 36 at the least pair (31051, 1202824), pre-registered (Y) against a floor of 35, so G_36 is nonempty and a common-depth certificate for index 15 needs depth at least 37, against the 35 the layer 17-18 census gave.
records.sc: One family, index 15, and one census program. The mass is exact only where the boxes cover both P_n and every survivor-carrying orbit and then agree, which is n <= 19 here; mu_20 is post hoc in THIS run and rests on two of its boxes, not on a pre-registered verdict, and no box here covers P_21 = 2^16; r30-cap18-index15-mass-census-layer-21 later confirmed the same mu_20 with a pre-registered verdict over four covering boxes, so the value stands and only this run's standing for it was provisional. Fractions past the covered depth are exploratory and are not the mass. Only the lifetime record is independently reproduced, by the frozen panel/cert33.py replay on the explicit 2467759-symbol word; mu_19 and mu_20 are one program's arithmetic agreed across boxes, and the agreement of several unsaturated boxes on a wrong value was pre-registered as possible and is not excluded by the run. D was not computed for the record pair. Kept fractions near one half decide neither uniform nor individual mortality: the lemma's floor is s_n mu_n/2 and the census carries no column classes, so it cannot measure s_n at all.
records.nt: Reproduce with `uv run --offline --no-project --with numpy python cap18_mass_census_grid.py --workers 6` from experiments/rule30, 27 minutes. Layers 21 and 22 need --a-exps 15,16 --b-exps 21,22; cap18_lifetime_census.py's rectangle() cannot reach them, since it holds the whole box as one int16 array.

records.t: Index-15 survivor mass on z and rotation columns is supplied by every present monodromy class at depths 13 and 14, and losing a whole class at depth 12 did not empty it
records.st: Exploratory and not pre-registered. cap18_class_flow.py follows the kept mass from every depth-n column of the index-15 guarded lift onto its children and classifies both ends, for parents at depths 4 to 14 and children at 5 to 15. Writing s_(n+1) for the share of the depth-(n+1) mass on z and rotation columns, the quantity the survivor-mass lemma's floor mu_(n+1) >= s_n mu_n/2 depends on, s_n ran from 0.1765 at n = 7 to 0.5000 at n = 5 over n = 5 to 15, and was 0.4089 at n = 15, the deepest measured. How many of the five classes present (center, fixing reflection, free reflection, identity, rotation) supply it rises with depth: one at depths 4 and 5, two to four through 12, and all five at 13 and 14. At depth 14 every present class sends between 0.2985 and 0.4390 of its kept mass to a z or rotation child and no single class supplies more than 0.3333 of the total, giving s_15 = 0.4089; at depth 13 the weakest sends 0.1556 and the largest feeder supplies 0.4779, giving s_14 = 0.2917. Depth 12 is the sharp case the other way: the fixing reflections sent nothing at all and the other four sent 0.1038 to 0.6154, and s_13 was still 0.2387, so losing a whole class did not empty the z and rotation columns. Two controls hold exactly at every depth: the children of center and rotation columns stay inside the section 7 lift lemma, and the flow into a depth reproduces that depth's own column masses as exact rationals, so s_(n+1) is computed twice by different routes.
records.sc: Index 15 only, parents at depths 4 to 14, guarded survivors only. A share here is of the kept mass at that depth, so it is what the guards actually passed and not what the two-layer algebra permits; read forward, that enumeration is permissive, letting every parent class but a four-traversal rotation at odd word length have a center or rotation child over arbitrary incoming constants. Exploratory with no pre-registration, so no prediction was at risk and nothing here is a verdict. Two depths with all five classes feeding is not a trend and gives no lower bound on s_n at any depth past 15. That bound is structural, not a choice of range: classifying the depth-n columns needs the cycles saved in layer n+1, whose `old` set they are, so s_16 needs layer 17, which was the continuation that hit the transport-cache cap and is now complete, putting s_16 at 0.4274 (r30-cap18-index15-self-sufficient-share-depth18). It therefore does not decide uniform mortality, which needs s_n = 0 at some layer, and it is consistent with s_n vanishing at any deeper layer.
records.nt: Runs in about 2 seconds from the saved entries and cycles of capacity18-guarded-base4.json and capacity18-guarded-16.json, whose digests the artifact pins along with those of cap18-entry-supply.json and cap18-entry-supply-16.json, and re-running it reproduces the committed artifact byte for byte. That is determinism, not independent reproduction: it is the same program over the same inputs. The artifact declares itself exploratory_not_preregistered_no_claim in its status field.

records.t: Pre-registered census measures the index-15 survivor mass at layer 21, gives layer 20 a pre-registered verdict, and reaches lifetime 37, with all five predictions confirmed
records.st: Pre-registered in experiments/rule30/PREREGISTRATION-cap18-mass-census-depth21.md. A census of 213(13)^a1213(13)^b03 over a < 2^15, 2^16 against b < 2^21, 2^22, 2^38 pairs in the largest box in 1.82 hours, reproduces the committed mu_n for every n <= 18 in all four boxes with no member reaching the step cap. All five pre-registered predictions hold. (P1) mu_19 = 10137/2^32 reproduces under the new a < 2^16 and b < 2^22 ranges, so the layer-19 mass does not depend on the box that first measured it. (P2) all four covering boxes agree on mu_20 = 20239/2^34, kept fraction 20239/40548 = 0.4991, which the previous census could give only post hoc behind a pre-registered (I); layer 20 therefore loses its post hoc mark. (P3, P4) layer 21 is new: mu_21 = 20457/2^35 from the two boxes covering P_21 = 2^16, a kept fraction of 20457/40478 = 0.5054 and 2^21 mu_21 = 1.2486, inside both the [11/25, 27/50] band that judged layers 19 and 20 and the tighter [49/100, 53/100] registered as the riskier claim. (P5) the record rose to further lifetime 37 at the least pair (21781, 2338078), so G_37 is nonempty and a common-depth certificate for index 15 needs depth at least 38. Separately, the record's growth law is not the one either census pre-registration assumed: over the dyadic maxima of every box measured, 2^0 to 2^27 in the lifetime census and 2^32 to 2^38 in the two grid censuses, 18 of the 33 single doublings add nothing and the plateaus reach three doublings (max_ell 19 from 2^15 through 2^18, 34 from 2^32 through 2^35), the largest box here being one of them since a < 2^16, b < 2^22 finds the same 37 at the same pair as the half-size a < 2^15, b < 2^22. The average slope is 0.91 steps per doubling from 2^27 to 2^38 and 0.92 from 2^0 to 2^38, with the exponents 28 to 31 unmeasured, so one step per doubling is a trend and not a per-doubling fact.
records.sc: One family, index 15, and one census program. Exact only where a box covers both P_n and every survivor-carrying orbit and the covering boxes then agree, which is n <= 21 here; no box covers P_22 = 2^17. At depths 19 and 20 both b ranges exceed the b < 2^20 that already saturated depth 20, so their agreement there is guaranteed in advance and P1 and P2 test the a range rather than b saturation; depth 21 is the only layer in this run where b saturation is live, b < 2^21 being the smallest range that can saturate it. Two unsaturated b ranges agreeing on a wrong value was pre-registered as possible and is not excluded. Nothing here is independently reproduced: it is one program's arithmetic agreed across boxes, and the record pair was not replayed. D was not computed for it. A kept fraction near one half decides neither uniform nor individual mortality, and the census carries no column classes, so it cannot measure s_n, which is the whole content of the survivor-mass lemma's lower bound.
records.nt: Reproduce with `uv run --offline --no-project --with numpy python cap18_mass_census_grid.py --a-exps 15,16 --b-exps 21,22 --band-depths 19,20,21 --workers 6 --output cap18-mass-census-21.json` from experiments/rule30, 6564 s measured. --band-depths is load-bearing and defaults to 19,20, so omitting it measures nothing new; a run naming only 21 and 22 fails the exact_through >= min(band_depths)-1 assert because the committed mass stops at 18. The artifact's P3_half_sample_predicts_k19 block is a recomputation of a kill already settled by the depth-20 census, not a fresh prediction. records.t: Window-wise SAT exclusion of q=3 odd-mask period-bound violations at N=3 to 6
records.st: For q=3 no reachable binary MSB machine with a root self-loop and N states agrees with a free least-period-p sequence v on u(3n+r)=v[n mod p] at every n>=2^N whose 3n+r stays below 2^L, taken over N=3,4,5,6 at L=11,12,13,14, all r in {0,1,2}, and the 24 periods p<=64 whose a+b equals N+1 or N+2 and which therefore violate a+b<=N (N=3 {5,6,8,12,16}; N=4 {5,10,12,16,24,32}; N=5 {7,10,20,24,32,48,64}; N=6 {7,14,20,40,48,64}): all 72 runs are UNSAT under pysat Cadical. So for these p no eventually periodic mask whose onset is at most 2^N violates the sharp period bound, and the exclusion is strictly stronger than the statement needs, since it also excludes machines that are periodic only inside the window.
records.sc: q=3 only, the 24 listed periods, p<=64, and L exactly as stated. The binding restriction is the encoding's floor: u(3n+r)=v[n mod p] is pinned only from n0=2^N, so a violating mask is excluded only if its onset is at most 2^N. That floor sits far below the a priori LSD onset bound for the composed machine, which reaches 96 states at N=5 and so bounds onset by 2^96, and it was measured non-binding only at N=3 (largest mask onset 1 over all 456 eventually periodic of 1,080 subsequences, against a floor of 8) and at N=4 (largest 2 over 798 eventually periodic in a seeded 4,000 of 39,168, against a floor of 16), both with window_unresolved 0. For N=5 and N=6 that is extrapolation from smaller N and not evidence. The N=6 onset-violation case is not covered here and is inconclusive; see r30-msbk-n6-onset-sat-artifacts. No Rule 30 content.
records.nt: Non-vacuity is established rather than assumed, which matters because a vacuously unsatisfiable encoding would produce the same 72 UNSAT lines. Positive controls at the tested modulus q=3: the largest a+b<=N period, p=2^(N-1), at each of the four (N,L) pairs the table uses (p=4 at N=3 L=11, p=8 at N=4 L=12, p=16 at N=5 L=13, p=32 at N=6 L=14) and at all three r, twelve runs, all SAT in at most 1.0 s with a reachable machine and an exactly eventually periodic mask. Negative controls at q=1, N=4: p=8 (a+b=4) SAT, p=12 and p=16 (a+b=5) UNSAT, as the theorem requires. Covering all three r is what makes an UNSAT at r=1 or r=2 mean what it does at r=0, since r enters the window bound, the u(qn+r) offset and the onset selector. PROVENANCE WARNING on the 84-record sat-mask-results.log: it predates the exact reachability and mask-periodicity check, emitted machine_reachable as a hardcoded constant rather than a computed value, and carries no mask_eventually_periodic field at all. Both are carried only by the three recheck records in sat-controls.log. Do not read the logged machine_reachable as a computed result. Line-delimited evidence is fingerprinted here rather than in proof_and_checker_artifacts, because validate_proof_artifacts parses every saved_artifact path as a single JSON document and these are one object per line or plain text: sat-mask-results.log sha256 4e95c5135663294fc5a7ed20027e9da03b5d39cbb1cb84b9ee34d6309d653fcb, sat-controls.log sha256 51f0db07b239799f9357b07fc7cb7282f4e2b77202024b807c184f9a179f9e66, sat_jobs.txt sha256 dc05ec4ee3a27da2ba7ac41c8044a085498399bb3725edc09ea7df0fa023366a.

records.t: The three N=6 onset SAT witnesses are aperiodic artifacts, and excluding them needs L=19, 15 and 16
records.st: At N=6, q=3, L=14 the three onset-violation runs, which pin u(3n+r) to period P_sharp=480 from n=2^6 while forcing a mismatch at some n in [H_sharp, 2^6), returned SAT at every r in {0,1,2}, but each returned machine composes to an exactly aperiodic mask under the composed LSD machine with all six states reachable, so none is a counterexample to the sharp period bound. Measured against its own window, whose top is 5,462 at r=0 and 5,461 at r=1,2 and whose last fully constrained index is top-480-1, that is 4,981 and 4,980: each witness's mask first breaks 480-periodicity at n=168,457, 5,345 and 19,908, every one of them above its last fully constrained index. Excluding a witness needs 3(n+480)+r back inside the window, so L would have to reach 19, 15 and 16 respectively.
records.sc: This leaves the N=6 onset case inconclusive rather than settled either way. The witnesses are artifacts of a window holding only about 11 periods of length 480, and nothing measured here bounds where a fresh search at a larger L would place the next break; that search has more freedom than this one, not less. Two of the three predictions pre-registered in the onset_witness_break.py docstring fired. P1, registered as n_break >= top for all three, fired on r=1 at 5,345 against top 5,461; the registered threshold was wrong and not the encoding, since periodicity binds only where both n and n+480 carry a constraint, and it was amended after the run to top-P-1 with the original preserved as registered. P2, registered as a KILL for the "rerun at L=15" lever on any L_needed>15, fired on r=0 and r=2 at L_needed 19 and 16, so that lever is retired rather than deferred and no replacement lever is registered. P3 split 2-1 against its treadmill reading: against 2P=960 the gaps are 162,995, -116 and 14,447. No Rule 30 content.
records.nt: Neither n_break nor the P1 amendment rests on a single code path: both n values at each break were read by the MSB reader and by the composed LSD machine, which agree on every n<3000 and on both sides of each break. Measured past the last constrained index, r=1 breaks after 365 terms, under one period, which is a solver putting the break wherever it is cheapest, while r=2 breaks 31 periods past and r=0 340 periods past, which is not; so a break can sit either just outside the constrained range or far beyond it. Cost of the retired lever: L=19 carries 32x the state variables of an L=14 run that already cost 12.3 hours in period mode at this N (p=64, r=0). The recheck in sat-controls.log re-ran the exact classifier over the three SAT records of sat-mask-results.log, finding all six states reachable and all three masks exactly aperiodic, with the r=0 record agreeing machine-for-machine with an independent reproduction of that run. Line-delimited evidence is fingerprinted here rather than in proof_and_checker_artifacts, because validate_proof_artifacts parses every saved_artifact path as a single JSON document and these are one object per line or plain text: sat-mask-results.log sha256 4e95c5135663294fc5a7ed20027e9da03b5d39cbb1cb84b9ee34d6309d653fcb, sat-controls.log sha256 51f0db07b239799f9357b07fc7cb7282f4e2b77202024b807c184f9a179f9e66.

records.t: The guarded RW prefix erasures coalesce one step before their displayed cutoff at k=1 and k=3, and exactly at it for k=0, 2 and 4
records.st: RESULTS-rw-defect-cocycle.md displays each guarded erasure at the length of its own prefix: identity (1) at F^(4k+3), (3) at F^7, (11) at F^8. The depth at which the two images coincide is a second parameter, fixed by neither the erasure theorem nor the sharp padding f(k) of (10). From J(wv)=J(w)M_w(J(v)) and J(F(u))=J(u)[1:], F^d(left v)=F^d(right v) holds for EVERY four-state suffix v exactly when M_left bisimulates M_right and J(left)[d:]==J(right)[d:], both exact finite checks, so the resulting depth is all-length in v rather than a census. For the sharp-padding rules 2^k 1 2^(f(k)+2) against 2^(k+f(k)+3), the coalescence depth is 3, 3, 7, 7 and 11 at k=0,1,2,3,4 against displayed depths 3, 4, 7, 8 and 11. So k=1 and k=3 are valid one F-step earlier than published and k=0, 2, 4 are already sharp. Each depth is sharp and not merely sufficient: one step earlier the EMPTY suffix already separates the two words, with images 00 against 22 at k=1 and k=3 and 0 against 2 at k=0, 2 and 4. The bisimulation closes at 141, 517, 18619, 57741 and 1555372 pairs.
records.sc: k <= 4. The erasure identity itself is the published theorem and is not reproved here; only its depth is computed. For k >= 5 the exact bisimulation passes 2,000,000 pairs without closing under a cap set to bound memory, so no depth is asserted there: granting the published all-k theorem the J comparison alone gives depth equal to the displayed cutoff at k=5,6,7, but that inherits the theorem rather than certifying it and is not claimed. Earlier coalescence matters only where a guard must survive to a stated depth. No RW separator, SEP certificate, period-two exclusion or normalization of the source language follows, and the interrupted-run gap is untouched.
records.nt: Reproduce with `uv run --offline --no-project python erasure_depth.py 4` from experiments/rule30/keep-the-real-constraints-in-the-weakest, about 21 s, single-process, almost all of it the k=4 bisimulation. Raising the argument past 4 needs a memory bound first: k=5 exceeds 3.4M reachable pairs. endpoint_section_machine.bisimilar defaults to cap=20000 and refuses rather than guessing, which is why k=3 needs the cap raised; it is the guard working, not a defect.

records.t: The fixed-depth survival Hankel rank grows at c=3 exactly as at c=2, so the automaton kill is not an artifact of one constant
records.st: Section 5b measured the Hankel rank of H_d[u,t] = [alive(ut) >= d] over hard-core u,t at c=2 only, and SEP quantifies over c in {2,3}. At c=3 and d=1 the ranks for L=2..9 are 4, 7, 11, 17, 26, 39, 60, 92, against 3, 6, 11, 17, 26, 39, 60, 92 at c=2. The two agree exactly from L=4 onward and differ only at L=2 and L=3, and the c=3 rank grows at the same rate of about 1.5 per symbol with no saturation in range. Depths d=2..6 carry the same shape. So the recorded kill of a small source automaton deciding survival of the forced RW continuation to a fixed depth holds at both constants SEP quantifies over, not at one.
records.sc: Ranks measured to L=9 and d<=6, for c=3, over hard-core u and t. That the rank never saturates remains extrapolation, exactly as in the c=2 record this extends; widening the constant does not widen the horizon. It closes one automaton per fixed depth in source coordinates as a route to an inductive family, at c=3 as well as c=2, and settles nothing about RW, SEP or period two.
records.nt: Reproduce with `uv run --offline --no-project python hankel_depth.py 3 9 6` from experiments/rule30/keep-the-real-constraints-in-the-weakest, a few minutes single-process. The script takes c as its first argument and only the c=2 log existed before this run.

records.t: Three qualifying maximal-drop steps below n=18 were already in the published census and all three inherit, taking the section 4b converse to nine trials
records.st: RESULTS-BINARY-WEDGE-HORIZON.md:347 states that every step with M(n+1,c)=M(n,c)-2 also has Q(n+1,c)=Q(n,c)[2:], with an unrestricted kill condition, but section 4b tested only 18 <= n <= 26 and the frozen-inequality extension added 29->30. The published census already contained three qualifying steps below n=18 that were never examined: n=15->16 at c=3 with M 16->14, n=5->6 at c=3 with M 8->6, and n=6->7 at c=2 with M 9->7. All three inherit exactly, and all three carry a single distinct Q on each side, so the strong form holds there as well, where it had failed at 18->19 c=3, 22->23 c=3 and 29->30 c=2. Control: every M printed matches the published census at its (n,c), which fires against the census rather than against the continuation pass that produced the Q values. Separately, 29->30 at c=3 is not a trial and must not be swept: M_3(29)=M_3(30)=24 is a drop of zero, so it never satisfied the hypothesis.
records.sc: Nine trials unrestricted, or seven inside the n >= 7 regime where (BWH+) is true, since n=5->6 and n=6->7 straddle the region in which it is false (M_3(5)=8, M_2(6)=9). Computed, not proved: nine trials are no more a law than the original six, and the converse remains a conjecture about maximisers. (BWH+) is unchanged and still conjectured. The next genuinely new trial needs M_c(31), about 6500 s single-core, so this exhausts what the existing census can answer.

records.t: The k=2 sparse-high family has at most 12 repeats for r <= 1000, which does not tighten the epsilon restriction the single far witness already forces
records.st: RESULTS-sparse-high-history-obstruction.md:176-179 states that a uniform conditional positive-rate estimate on k=2 rows is equivalent to a uniform repeat bound on that family, and that no such bound is established; the family had one measured member, r=46735 with D=18. Sweeping it exhaustively in r and in the hole position for 3 <= r <= 1000, which is 1,994,004 evolutions because the rank theorem leaves at most four effective originals per (r,p), the maximum is D=12 at r=740, hole 473, with N=17 and tape 11011000000111111. Max D by range is 6 at r<=120, 10 at r<=400 and 12 at r<=1000. The necessary c=1 bound at that maximum is 2/D = 1/6, WEAKER than the 2/18 = 1/9 the single far member already forces, so a dense sweep three orders of magnitude below it does not tighten the restriction and on this evidence will not: D grows slowly and erratically, roughly doubling over a factor of eight in range. What it does settle is that no member in range has D >= r, so nothing in the family threatens H_sharp (D <= r-1) at a length the exhaustive census cannot reach.
records.sc: Exhaustive in r and hole position for 3 <= r <= 1000 and nothing past it. The known D=18 member sits at r=46735 and no dense sweep of this shape reaches that regime, so none of this is evidence about it; the 'no uniform bound established' gap is now a gap above r=1000 rather than a gap everywhere. Repeat budget, mortality and P1 are untouched.

records.t: Extending the fixed-window domain from j+l<=k/2 to j+l<=k keeps every l>=2 minimum strictly positive but cuts the l=2 margin by a factor of six
records.st: (P2-C) is stated on j+l <= k/2, while RESULTS-p2-flexible-scale-audit.md:194-201 puts the M/N-minimizing scale ABOVE k/2 at every large k (j=18 at k=28), so the stated domain excludes the scales where the seed's cancellation sits. Recomputed on the stored shells with verify_fixed_window.py's own formula, the minimum relative loss on j+l<=k is 19/188 = 0.101064 at (9,7) for l=2, 67/236 = 0.283898 at (9,6) for l=3, and 23435591/34213680 = 0.684977 at (23,19) for l=4, against 5/8, 1611/1940 and 3711/4040 on j+l<=k/2. So l>=2 pure contraction with C=0 survives the extension on k<=28, the minimum staying strictly positive, but the l=2 margin falls by a factor of 6.2. The control is that the same code over the published domain returns the published minima exactly, asserted at run time. A third fact falls out at l=1: the extended domain admits (k,j)=(3,2) with E=[8,8,0,0], where the loss ratio is zero only because the denominator is. Excluding that degenerate pair leaves exactly two genuine zero-loss pairs with E_j > 0, (2,0) and (11,10), independently reproducing RESULTS-p2-ordered-energy-audit.md:147-155; (11,10) lies outside j+l<=k/2, which is why the l=1 refutation record carries a one-element witness set while that table has two.
records.sc: Stored seed shells k <= 28 only. 19/188 is NOT a candidate eta: every dip sits within three or four levels of k where the block count N/2^j is between 4 and 16 ((9,7) has four blocks), the regime RESULTS-p2-flexible-scale-audit.md:227-229 discounts for its own four-block witness, and the per-shell l=2 extended minima are erratic in k with no trend and no zero. records.t: The aligned-block absolute-sum profile of the Rule 30 shells follows the exact simple-random-walk law to 2.25 percent through shell 28, so the triangle-inequality branch of route 1 survives the measured data
records.st: Pre-registered in experiments/rule30/shell-maximum-o-n/PREREGISTRATION-aligned-block-seam.md, written before seam_profile.py existed and with the band calibrated against the iid control before any Rule 30 number was read. For the lone-seed centre column and shell K = [2^K, 2^(K+1)), let L(K, j) be the sum over the 2^(K-j) aligned blocks of length 2^j of the absolute block sum, and let m_j = n C(n, n/2) / 2^n with n = 2^j be the exact mean absolute displacement of a simple random walk of n steps. With r(K, j) = L(K, j) / (2^(K-j) m_j), over every K = 10..28 and every 1 <= j <= K - 12, that is every depth with at least 4096 blocks, 136 pairs in all, max |r - 1| = 0.0225. The iid control over the same construction gives 0.0196 over 78 pairs, the all-ones control 79.2170 and the biased control P(+1) = 1/2 + 1/k gives 5.6663; the last two are pre-registered kills of the screen and both fire. The deviation shrinks with block count as sampling predicts: at j = 4, r is 1.0741 at K = 10 and 1.0002 at K = 28. Hence on the measured shells L(K, j)/2^K equals sqrt(2/(pi 2^j)) to within 2.3 percent. Section 6.1 of the cross-review requires L(K, j) = o(2^K) for the triangle inequality over aligned blocks to bound the adjacent-block cross term from the halves' own bounds, and the measured profile satisfies that at every measured pair, so the data does not kill that branch.
records.sc: Exact integer counts on the complete shells k = 10..28 of the centre column and on depths with at least 4096 blocks; no asymptotic statement and no bound on M_k. A finite profile satisfying o(2^K) at each measured K is not the uniform statement the branch needs, and nothing here produces the cross-term estimate that r30-p2-route1-reduces-to-adjacent-block-cross-term identifies as the only place Rule 30 enters route 1. What the screen measures is fixed by its controls: the biased control satisfies P2 and still fails the screen by 57 times the band, so S1 is a bias screen at the aligned-block level and passing it says the shells carry no block-level bias through K = 28, not anything about P2. r(K, 0) = 1 identically is structural, L(K, 0) = 2^K and m_0 = 1, and is excluded from the screen rather than counted; the first run counted those 19 structural entries and reported 155 pairs where 136 were measurements, which changed no maximum and no verdict.
records.nt: Reproduce with `uv run --no-project --script seam_profile.py --kmax 28 --out seam-profile.json` from experiments/rule30/shell-maximum-o-n: 10.74 s and 9.53 s real on two runs, peak resident 2,116,304,896 and 2,121,973,760 bytes, both producing an identical artifact since every control is seeded from SEED = 20260920. seam_profile.py is an independent second implementation of shell_screen.py's inline carry, accumulating (n, D, A, I) by the four-coordinate law over 2^24-bit chunks, and it reproduces the recorded M, u_star, D and I exactly at every complete shell or aborts. The cross-chunk fold that builds L above depth 24 runs only at k = 25..28 and was checked against a direct unchunked fold of the same bits at k = 25 and k = 28.

records.t: The half-seam coupling of the Rule 30 shells changes sign over k = 10..28, and the first half of shell 16 has signed sum exactly zero
records.st: Pre-registered as screen S2 in experiments/rule30/shell-maximum-o-n/PREREGISTRATION-aligned-block-seam.md. For the two halves u, v of shell k+1, the four-coordinate law gives I_(k+1) - I_u - I_v = 2^k D_u^2 + 2 D_u A_v, whose first summand depends on u alone, so the only genuine coupling between the halves is Y_k = 2 D_u A_v. Over k = 10..28 the sign of Y_k is - + - + - - 0 + - + - - + + - - - - -, which is not constant, so the screen is not refuted. The zero at k = 16 is exact and not a rounding artefact: the first half of shell 16, t in [65536, 98304), has signed sum exactly D_u = 0, verified by a separate direct read of the same bits; the second half carries the whole shell total -356. The all-ones control gives Y_k > 0 at every k and is refuted, as pre-registered, and so is the biased control. The prefix area A_k is recorded for k = 10..28 in the same artifact and is the quantity no earlier run serialized: shell_stats returns length, M, u_star, D, I and no area, and p2_dyadic_shell_probe.py carries the law but no area field and stops at k = 18. Reported without a screen, because the iid control shows neither concentrates: X_k / I_(k+1) runs from -0.737 at k = 12 to 0.828 at k = 22, and A_k / 2^(3k/2) from -0.464 to 1.042.
records.sc: Exact integer counts on the complete shells k = 10..28 of the centre column. A sign pattern over nineteen shells is not an asymptotic statement and bounds nothing; it removes only the reading in which the two halves couple coherently at every scale. The screen was registered because a constant sign is the shape a route-1 bound would have to defeat, and its null probability under the iid control is about 2^-10, measured as not constant in any of five control trials over eleven shells.
records.nt: Same run and same artifact as r30-p2-aligned-block-profile-random-walk-law; the script asserts at every k that the two half summaries compose to the whole shell and that I_u + X_k + I_v = I_(k+1), and re-checks the four-coordinate law exhaustively over all 3969 pairs of signed words of lengths 0..5 before using it.

records.t: The seed's only sub-quarter mesoscopic loss is still the one at t=20 after extending the census eight times further, to t=65536
records.st: The refutation of a uniform mesoscopic loss delta >= 1/4 on the seed rests on a single exception, delta = 17/84 at t=20, L=4, and its own scope leaves an eventual version alive. quarter_wave_seed_loss_scan.py caps its CLI at t=8192 as a declared audit scope while scan() is horizon-parametric, so the same engine reaches further without modification. Over every integer 16 <= t <= 65536 and every dyadic L with 4 <= L <= floor(sqrt(t)), which is 371,383 row-scale cases in 253 s single-process, there is exactly one violation of delta >= 1/4 and it is still t=20, and there is no violation below 1/8, so the eta = 1/8 worked example of the certificate-search document is not threatened in this range. The five published per-scale minima reappear unchanged as a prefix at the same argmin times and the t=20 scalar witness assert fires on every run, which is the control: the same function over the published horizon returns the published table. The extension adds two scales: L=128, whose minimum over its admissible times (16384 <= t <= 65536) is 1277803/3130268 = 0.408209 at t=20858, and L=256, which is admissible only at the single census row t=65536 (since the census domain is 4 <= L <= floor(sqrt(t)) with t <= 65536, and floor(sqrt(t))>=256 forces t=65536) and reads 8478921/15982336 = 0.530518 there, not a minimum over any range.
records.sc: Finite census over 16 <= t <= 65536 and dyadic L <= sqrt(t); nothing is extrapolated past it and no all-time seed loss bound is proved or refuted. This is the lower-payoff outcome and was the likelier one: the T=131072 dyadic ladder already sat at delta_L ~ 0.49-0.51 across every mesoscopic L, so only a violation would have been informative. What it buys is that the t=20 exception is isolated over three orders of magnitude rather than one. It buys nothing toward P_t = o(t) and cannot: the proved loss floor summed over dyadic L up to L_J = o(t) is O((L_J/t)^2) -> 0, so positivity of loss is not the missing certificate, and any coefficient below 1/4 needs a constant depending on the entire initial row.

records.t: First measurement of the seed's single-interval deficits: D_+ + D_- saturates at exactly the shell's signed sum, and the collection maximum exceeds one interval by up to 30x below the crossover radius
records.st: D_+(R) and D_-(R), the largest single-interval deficits this node's target is about, had never been computed on the seed at any (k,R): the only stored deficit was the k=20, R=1024 neighborhood certificate and the only other D_pm in the tree belongs to a 24-symbol artificial word. Writing d_+([a,b)) = f(b) - g(a) with f(b) = P_b - Q_min(N,b+R) and g(a) = P_a - Q_max(0,a-R) makes each exact maximum a single O(N) pass with a running minimum, and clamping the prefix index rather than special-casing the ends is what reproduces the stored certificate's D_+ = 814. Three exact facts over shells k=10..24 and R=2^j. (i) For R past a shell-dependent point D_+ + D_- equals |sum z| EXACTLY, at all fifteen shells, the smaller deficit reaching zero and the larger holding at the global imbalance; so at fixed k the target quantity is eventually constant in R and all the content is in where the decay happens. (ii) The first dyadic R with D_+ + D_- <= R stays within [0.707, 2.828] of sqrt(N) at every shell, four grid steps, which is the scale at which sqrt(N) is already killed as a canonical schedule. (iii) The ++++---- kill's mechanism is real on the seed and is radius-dependent: at the nine (k,R) rows carrying a stored U_R, Delta_+ exceeds D_+ by up to 30x below the crossover (k=20, R=8: 45337 against 1515) and equals it at and above (k=20, R=1024: 814). The stored certificate reads as single-component because it was taken at that shell's crossover. Separately, the explicit packing factor the success criterion asks for is slack by 32x to 1858x against the actual U_R, growing with k at fixed R, so proving the single-interval bound would still not deliver the collection bound through that inequality at realistic constants.
records.sc: Exact over k=10..24 and R=2^j, 3<=j<=k-2, and nothing past it. D_pm are exact; Delta_pm exist only at the 19 rows where a stored U_R does and are derived from it, not recomputed. THE RADIUS IN THE TARGET IS ONE A PROVER CHOOSES, so a fixed dyadic grid is evidence neither for nor against D_+ + D_- = o(R) and no grid value is a counterexample; the crossover ratio is quantized to powers of sqrt(2) because R* is dyadic and sqrt(N)=2^(k/2), so the band is a resolution limit and not a fitted constant, and fifteen points are not a law. P2 and the matching node are unchanged and the node stays conditional. Shells are read from a gitignored payload no script in this chain regenerates; the bit offset it is read at was re-derived against 8192 regenerated centre-column bits on every run rather than inherited.

records.t: The seed's dyadic tree energy H_k stays within a factor of 1.73 of its random-sign value (k+1)N at every shell through k=28, re-derived from the payload by a second code path
records.st: E_(k,j) is the sum of squared aligned block sums of length 2^j over shell k and H_k = sum_(j<=k) E_(k,j); H_k/N^2 -> 0 is equivalent to P2 and M_k^2 <= (k+1)H_k is proved, so H_k is the quantity the ordered-energy node's target is about. The per-level energies are NOT new: experiments/rule30/p2-cross-science-explore.json has stored every E_(k,j) for k <= 28 since at least 2026-09-17. What had not been written down is H_k itself past k=20 and three facts about it. Over k=8..28, H_k/((k+1)N) stays in [0.674, 1.727], minimum at k=11 and maximum at k=9, and (k+1)N is the expected value of H_k for independent fair signs, so the seed's dyadic energy sits at the random-sign scale, about N/log N below the o(N^2) threshold; at k=28, H_k/N^2 = 1.017e-7. H_k/N^2 strictly decreases at every step from k=9 to k=28. And argmax_j E_(k,j) = k, so that max E = D_k^2, at exactly k=9, 13, 17, 23 and 26, the shells with the largest signed sums relative to N. The computation is a second code path: a chunked fold over the payload that agrees with the sum of the stored E arrays at every k=8..28, where those arrays had been independently cross-checked only through k=12, and that reproduces the seven published H_k at k=8,10,...,20 as exact integers.
records.sc: Exact over shells 8 <= k <= 28 and nothing past it; k=29 needs 2^30 centre bits and the only cache holds 1e9. The agreement with the stored arrays is independent of the code that wrote them but NOT of the payload: both read the same cache, verified against a regenerated centre column only on its first 8192 bits, which this run re-derives each time. The success criterion H_k = O(N^(2-eps)) is asymptotic and no finite table reaches it; sitting at the random-sign scale through k=28 is what a proof would have to explain, not evidence one exists. The band moves by a factor of 2.6 with no trend, so no constant is fitted. The node stays conjectured. source_context.heading: 2. Result

records.t: A CEGIS walk of 152 N=6 q=3 onset machines puts the median window exponent needed to exclude one at 17 to 19, and only L=20 reaches all of them
records.st: Pre-registered in the onset_cegis_probe.py docstring, committed before the first run. The probe enumerates the family the three N=6 q=3 L=14 onset SAT witnesses came from: solve, read the machine, classify its mask with the same exact composed-LSD classifier sat_mask_search.verify uses, measure the first n >= 2^6 at which the mask breaks 480-periodicity, block that machine, re-solve. The blocking clause is the negation of the certified implication cube, the selected transition literals of the states reachable from state 0 plus their signed output literals, so one clause kills every completion of the unreachable states, and all 120 relabellings fixing state 0 are blocked with it. Under a 2,700 s wall-clock cap per residue the loop returned 47 machines at r=0, 44 at r=1 and 61 at r=2: 18,240 blocking clauses, 8,143 solver seconds, 21.7M conflicts. All 152 are distinct core signatures, all have six reachable states, and all have exactly aperiodic masks, so no in-window witness appears; every break sits above its own last fully constrained index, the r=1 minimum of 5,345 lying below top=5,461 but above 4,980 as the amended P1 of r30-msbk-n6-onset-sat-artifacts allows. n_break runs 11,899 to 220,886 at r=0 (median 24,278), 5,345 to 255,838 at r=1 (median 54,861) and 6,801 to 232,536 at r=2 (median 40,297), and the three committed break points 168,457 / 5,345 / 19,908 all reappear as members. L_needed = bitlength(3(n_break+480)+r), the smallest window exponent reaching the break, has median 17, 18 and 17 weighted by machine and 19, 18 and 18 over the distinct break values, against the registered KILL threshold of 17. Counting instead of averaging: L=15 excludes 13 of the 152 and none at all of the 47 at r=0, where the cheapest break needs 3(11,899+480) = 37,137 against a window of 2^15 = 32,768; L=16 reaches 58, L=19 reaches 138, and only L=20 reaches all 152, at 64x the state variables of the L=14 runs. The registered treadmill reading is refuted at all three residues: 0 of 47, 8 of 44 and 0 of 61 breaks lie within 2P=960 of the window top, and the smallest gap at r=0 is 6,437, more than thirteen periods out.
records.sc: This is a capped enumeration and it excludes nothing. All three runs stopped at the wall-clock cap, never at UNSAT; a blocking clause adds no window, so every model returned still breaks outside L=14, and the standing is that of r30-loc-class-search-unknown, whose own scope line reads that no conclusion follows from a resource cap. What is killed is a lever, not the N=6 onset case, which stays inconclusive. The sample is also narrower than 152 suggests, and the narrowing was not predicted: the 47 machines at r=0 carry only 8 distinct break values, 44 at r=1 carry 15 and 61 at r=2 carry 13, so the effective sample for the distribution is 8, 15 and 13. The narrowing is not the machines being redundant presentations of each other, which was the first thing checked and is refuted: run through census.minimize, all 152 are already minimal at six states and all 152 are distinct as minimal machines, so the orbit blocking did enumerate 152 genuinely different behaviours and the machine count is not inflated by non-minimal copies. n_break is therefore a coarse invariant, many-to-one on distinct minimal machines rather than a fingerprint of one, the map running one way only: each minimal machine has a single break, and several minimal machines share one. The machine-weighted medians are therefore weighted by how often Cadical returned each cluster rather than by anything about the family, which is why the distinct-value medians are reported beside them; the KILL holds under both readings and under the count, which needs no weighting at all. No registered prediction measured break diversity, so the clustering is exploratory and nothing here says the 8 values at r=0 are all of them: they are reproducible rather than asserted. Three runs before the registered one, all at N=6 r=0 and all discarded, found 49,036, 11,899 and 168,457 at seed 999 with phases over the machine, 24,278, 110,203 and 168,457 at seed 999 with phases over the free period sequence too, and 220,886 at seed 7, every value inside the seed-30 set; seed 999 with no phase randomization at all returned 168,457 twice and 41,754, which is outside it. So the set is seed-robust and demonstrably not closed, at nine values and counting. The three residues share no break value. Q6b, which measures core diversity and not break diversity, held at exactly its registered floor of 4 of 18 at r=0, clearing it by nothing. q=3, N=6, L=14 and the sharp period 480 only. No Rule 30 content.
records.nt: Reproduce with `uv run python onset_cegis_probe.py --r 0 --max-iters 100 --max-seconds 2700 --seed 30` from the results directory, once per residue; the caps bind on wall clock, so a rerun on a different machine returns a different number of members of the same family rather than the same list. What is checked against something the probe did not write: the encoder split is asserted against the committed (vars, clauses) of two logged runs before anything else, sat-mask-results.log line 1 at 6183/22527 and sat-controls.log line 8 at 98446/654828, both exact; and the numpy mask evaluator, which replaces a census.value scan that would cost a minute per iteration, is replayed against onset-witness-break.json and reproduces all three committed breaks exactly on n_break, window_top, last_fully_constrained_n, gap and L_needed. Iteration 1 of each run additionally re-derives its own break through onset_witness_break.row, the census.value path, and agrees on all five fields. The soundness invariant behind the blocking, that two assignments agreeing on the reachable core have the same mask, is asserted per iteration in three parts rather than argued: core closure, invariance under re-deciding every state outside the core, invariance under a random relabelling. Cadical153 cannot be interrupted in this pysat build, interrupt() and clear_interrupt() both raising NotImplementedError, so each solve carries a 2,000,000 conflict budget instead and solve_limited's None return is separated from False before anything reads it; reading None as UNSAT would have reported a resource cap as a real exclusion. Phase randomization covers the machine variables only, and the comparison is measured rather than asserted (onset_phase_cost.py, onset-phase-cost.json): three scopes over one N=6 r=0 instance at one seed, run strictly sequentially, give 85.6 s per solve with phases over t, o and the 480 free period variables, 39.4 s over t and o alone, and 4.6 s with no randomization, whose three solves are 13.79 s then 0.03 and 0.04. Cost alone would choose the last, and what rules it out is diversity: both no-randomization and the full scope returned a fresh core signature carrying a break they had already produced, while t and o alone returned three distinct breaks from three distinct cores, which is the neighbourhood the registered Q6b exists to catch. An earlier measurement of the same comparison gave 168 s against 30 s; it was taken under load from concurrent sessions, so the ratio, 2.2x here, is the claim and the absolute seconds are context. The onset_cegis_probe.py fingerprint below is the file as of this amendment; the only change since the 152 runs is that comment, which quoted those superseded figures and now points at the artifact instead. Line-delimited evidence is fingerprinted here rather than in proof_and_checker_artifacts, because validate_proof_artifacts parses every saved_artifact path as a single JSON document and this one is an object per line: onset-cegis-probe.jsonl sha256 513be623cfaaa75617ce10957debe5fcc48731170d81fed79f66a3915d200937.
