records.t: The guarded capacity language's number of free repetition parameters is max{n : 2*3^n <= K} at every cap K = 1..1460, confirmed by three predictions made before the data that tested them
records.st: The capacity route's kill rests partly on the language's dimension expanding with the cap, and the tracked evidence was two points, one independent repetition parameter at cap 17 and two at cap 32. Running the same decompose() and verify_language() at every cap, the first cap carrying d parameters is 1, 6, 18, 54, 162, 486, 1458 for d = 0..6, which is 2*3^d, and the parameter count equals max{n : 2*3^n <= K} at every cap K = 1..1460 with zero exceptions, a step function in log_3(K/2) with no dips; verification.all_lengths holds at every cap. Three steps were predicted before any data reached them: first_cap(4) = 162 and first_cap(5) = 486 after the sweep to K=64, and first_cap(6) = 1458 after the sweep to K=500, each written down with its kill before running further, and all three held. The step at 18 agrees with r30-cap18-language-frontier. So the kill's precondition is confirmed and quantified: dimension grows without bound through K=1460, so an argument needing a bounded number of independent parameters across all capacities is dead through that range, but it grows only logarithmically, leaving floor(log_3(K/2)) parameters to control at capacity K.
records.sc: Exact at every cap 1 <= K <= 1460 and nothing past it. The law has three out-of-sample confirmations and is still measured, not proved for all K; its next step at K=4374 is predicted and not run. A dimension count describes the language's shape and bounds nothing: the node needs a finite B(K) for every K, and this is not one. The cap-18 seams worked in another session are untouched.

Running the same decompose() and verify_language() at every cap K = 1..500, the first cap carrying d parameters is 1, 6, 18, 54, 162, 486 for d = 0..5, which is 2*3^d, and the parameter count equals max{n : 2*3^n <= K} at all 500 caps with zero exceptions, so it is a step function in log_3(K/2) with no dips. verification.all_lengths holds at every cap. Two predictions were written down after the sweep to K=64 and before running further, first_cap(4) = 162 and first_cap(5) = 486, and both held. The step at 18 agrees with r30-cap18-language-frontier. So the kill's precondition is confirmed and quantified: dimension grows without bound on this range, so an argument needing a bounded number of independent parameters across all capacities is dead through K=500 rather than on one step, but it grows only logarithmically, leaving floor(log_3(K/2)) parameters to control at capacity K.
previous_record.scope: Exact at every cap 1 <= K <= 500 and nothing past it. The law is measured with two out-of-sample confirmations, not proved for all K; its next step at K=1458 is predicted and not run. Running the same certify() to J=64 on a spacetime 72 columns wide instead of 40, with j* asserted unchanged against each stored row, every seed first reproduces its stored J=32 verdict and state count exactly (124, 96, 89, 96, 344). Then 20dc (j*=18), 9b6a (j*=18) and a0dc (j*=16) close at J=44 and 60dc (j*=16) at J=48: the reachable state set closes with no violation below the cap, certify()'s exhaustive outcome and a machine-checked certificate for that seed at that buffer. That strengthens rather than weakens RESULTS-RIGHT-SEED-MARGIN.md:321-325, which says no period-5 block with j* <= 12 is a robust shield at buffer 16: its only member in this family now fails through buffer 60, while robust period-5 shielding appears here only for j* = 16 or 18.

records.t: The quarter-wave current's excess over 1/2 is not the time-difference of any additive phase-periodic window functional on the seed orbit, for windows up to 8 and phase periods 1, 2, 4, over the whole half-row or row
records.st: If K_t - 1/2 were an exact time-difference of a local functional on the orbit, the current sum in A(T) - T/2 = P_T + sum_(t<T)(K_t - 1/2) would telescope. The history-window kill closes every bounded window inside radius 18 and names untruncated half-row sums as what survives; the seam-routes kill covers laws on every input and says nothing about identities holding only on the orbit. Taking Phi(x) = sum_i rho(i mod p, x_i..x_(i+m-1)) with rho(.,0^m) = 0 over every window start i >= 0 (right half-row) or every start (full row), the condition for t < T is one linear system in p(2^m - 1) unknowns. At T = 2048 it is inconsistent for every m = 1..8, every p in {1,2,4}, on both supports, the largest system being 1020 unknowns against 2048 equations, decided by rank of A against [A|b] modulo two independent 31-bit primes that agree. Inconsistency at T holds at every larger T. Positive control: by x_0 = P(Fx) - P(x) + K(x) the target K - x_0 is exactly -(P(Fx) - P(x)), and P is additive with a phase-4 weight on the right half-row, so that system must be consistent at p=4; it is, and it is correctly inconsistent at p=1 and p=2 where no phase-4 weight is expressible. K and P also match the audit's scalar_current and scalar_potential at every t < 128, and a planted random rho is recovered. Proved, not only computed: exact_certificate.py extracts, for each support, an integer vector y zero off a row set S with y^T A = 0 and y^T b != 0 checked in exact integer arithmetic, which shows the system has no rational solution however y was found. A window-m, phase-p functional with p | 4 and m <= 8 equals a window-8, phase-4 functional over the same starts, so the (m=8, p=4) certificate on each support proves all 24 systems there: 639 rows with entries up to 394 digits on the half-row, 513 rows with entries up to 360 digits on the full row, both in exact-certificate-m8-p4.json.
records.sc: Seed orbit t < 2048, and therefore every larger horizon, windows m <= 8, phase periods p in {1,2,4}, right half-row and full row; proved over Q by exact integer certificates. It closes only that sub-family of the surviving lever. Not closed: windows longer than 8; phase periods other than 1, 2, 4, including 8 and 16; non-additive functionals; functionals of history rather than the current row; scale- or time-dependent coefficients. A positive answer would not have been success either, since a telescoping Phi over a row of width 2t is O(t), not o(t), without further control.

records.t: Pre-registered census measures the index-15 survivor mass at layers 22 and 23, extends the b saturation law one threshold, and reaches lifetime 46, with all nine predictions confirmed
records.st: Pre-registered in experiments/rule30/PREREGISTRATION-cap18-mass-census-depth23.md and read by rule by resolve_cap18_depth23.py, committed before the artifact existed, with all fifteen self-checks passing. The unmodified cap18_mass_census_grid.py over a < 2^16, 2^17 against b < 2^23, 2^24, 2^41 pairs in the largest box in 15.4 hours on six workers, reproduces the committed mu_n for every n <= 18 in all four boxes with nothing censored. All nine pre-registered predictions hold. (P1-P3) mu_19 = 10137/2^32, mu_20 = 20239/2^34 and mu_21 = 20457/2^35 reproduce exactly under the new a and b ranges, over four covering boxes each. (P4, P5) layer 22, a guard line at P_22 = 2^17: mu_22 = 81869/2^38, kept fraction 81869/163656 = 0.5003, 2^22 mu_22 = 1.2492, inside [11/25, 27/50] and [49/100, 53/100]. (P6, P7) layer 23, the first point layer past 16: mu_23 = 10173/2^36, kept fraction 40692/81869 = 0.4970, 2^23 mu_23 = 1.2418, inside the point-layer band [0.48, 0.59] and the guard-line band [0.44, 0.54]. (P8) b < 2^23 and b < 2^24 agree through depth 23 and first disagree at 24 in both a ranges, so the b saturation law extends one threshold. (P9) the record reached lifetime 46 at the least pair (81664, 16385540) in a < 2^17, b < 2^24, against a registered floor of 38, so G_46 is nonempty and a common-depth certificate for index 15 needs depth at least 47. The dyadic maxima are 37 at 2^39, 39 and 40 at the two 2^40 boxes and 46 at 2^41, a gain of six over one doubling after a plateau at 37 from 2^38 to 2^39.
records.sc: One family, index 15, and one census program. Exact only where a box covers both P_n and every survivor-carrying orbit and the covering boxes then agree. The nested grid is a < 2^16, 2^17 against b < 2^23, 2^24, four boxes and 2^41 pairs in the largest, and its coverage is asymmetric in a way the pre-registration fixed in advance: at depths 19, 20 and 21 four boxes cover P_n and their agreement is a genuine out-of-sample test of the a range, a < 2^17 never having been run, and of nothing else, while at depths 22 and 23 only a < 2^17 covers the period. Both b ranges exceed the threshold that already saturates depth 22, so DEPTH 22 HAS NO LIVE CROSS-CHECK OF ANY KIND: its two boxes are guaranteed to agree in advance, that agreement tests neither the a range nor b saturation, and its content is the value and the band, nothing more. Depth 23 is the only layer in this run where anything is live, b < 2^23 being the smallest range that can saturate it. Two unsaturated b ranges agreeing on a wrong value was pre-registered as possible and is not excluded. Layer 24 is not measured and cannot be by this program, which needs a < 2^18 for P_24 = 2^18 and refuses a z-pair layer as a band depth outright; mu_24 = mu_23/2 and k_24 = 1/2 follow from the survivor-mass lemma at the cost of one inherited dependency, that depth 24 is a z-pair layer, which is read from the first-star schedule record and not recomputed here. Layer 25 is out of reach at practical cost: a guard line at P_25 = 2^19 needs a < 2^19 and b < 2^25, 2^44 pairs, about 4.8 days and about 16 GB across six workers, so this run is the last layer of index 15 the grid census reaches and the frontier past it belongs to an instrument that does not exist yet. THE CENSUS CARRIES NO COLUMN CLASSES, SO IT CANNOT MEASURE s_n AT ALL, and s_n is the whole content of the survivor-mass lemma's lower bound mu_(n+1) >= s_n mu_n / 2: a kept fraction near one half at 22 or 23 is consistent with s_n being anything positive and equally with s_n = 0 at any layer past 15, which is where every available instrument stops, since classifying the depth-n columns needs the cycles saved in layer n+1, whose `old` set they are, so s_16 needs layer 17, which was the continuation that hit the transport-cache cap and is now complete. Neither uniform nor individual mortality is decided by any outcome here. Nothing is independently reproduced: it is one program's arithmetic agreed across boxes, at depths 22 and 23 across two boxes the pre-registration registers as guaranteed to agree at 22, and the record pair is not replayed by this run. D was not computed for it.

records.t: Refuted: that measuring s_n at more layers is an instrument for deciding the capacity-18 index-15 route
records.st: Route p1-cap18's next_action names s_n past depth 15 as the instrument that would decide the route. The two capacity-18 two-parameter families with a nondegenerate uniform mortality certificate, the third of the three closed seams being index 12 which closes at depth 4, now have their s_n profile computed from their exhaustive depth-4 base to the empty layer. Index 5, empty at depth 23: s_n = 0 at depths 4, 7, 9, 11, 12, 13, 16, 20, 21 and 22, and s_n = 1 at 5, 6, 8, 10, 14, 15, 17, 18 and 19. Index 27, empty at depth 16: s_n = 0 at depths 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 14 and 15, and s_n = 1 at 11, 12 and 13. s_n = 0 is necessary for layer n+1 to empty, by the survivor-mass lemma and corollary 3, and it occurs nineteen times across the two families; seventeen of the nineteen are false alarms, index 27 carrying s_n = 0 through seven consecutive depths 4 to 10 and surviving all seven. In the other direction index 5 has s_n at its maximum value 1 at depth 19 and is empty at 23, so the strongest possible positive reading of the quantity is compatible with death four layers later. No prefix of s_n measured on either family whose answer is known announces the layer that kills it, so measuring further layers of it for index 15 is not evidence for unbounded lifetimes. A layer with s_n = 0 would still be evidence in the other direction, since it is necessary for the next layer to empty, which is what route p1-cap18's target field already says; what this removes is the reading of a positive s_n as support. No immortal family is in the control set, because none is known.
records.sc: What is refuted is a methodological claim about an instrument, not a mathematical statement. The survivor-mass lemma and corollary 3 are untouched and still proved; s_n = 0 at some layer remains necessary for uniform mortality and a uniform positive lower bound on s_n would still give unbounded lifetimes. Nothing here says index 15 is or is not uniformly mortal. The controls have two defects that bound how far this carries and neither can be removed with what exists: indices 5 and 27 are two of the three seam-intertwined families, so each is effectively one-parameter and their survivor sets never exceed 8 and 2 columns; at every depth of both controls the whole survivor mass sits in a single monodromy class, so s_n there is not a share at all but an indicator of which class the family's one surviving orbit is in, and it takes only 0 and 1, where index 15's runs between 0.2387 and 0.4274 over depths 12 to 18 at 125 to 1487 columns, 0.1765 at depth 7 in the committed cap18-survivor-mass.json, and index 8's between 0.2089 and 0.5000. The third closed seam, index 12, closes at depth 4 and is degenerate. No mortal non-intertwined two-parameter capacity-18 family is known, so this is the whole available control set. The claim this refutes is the presumption that a mortal family announces itself in s_n before the layer that kills it, which is false wherever it can be tested; it is not a claim that s_n behaves the same way on a non-intertwined family.
records.nt: P3 of the registration asked whether index 5's s_n decays gradually and registered at least two consecutive layers with 0 < s_n < 0.10 before the first 0. Its literal band could not be reached on either control, because every control layer carries its whole mass in one monodromy class, so s_n is 0 or 1 and never in between; registering a band without checking it was attainable is a design error in the registration. The OUTCOME P3's kill was written to catch did occur, and its registered consequence stands as written: both controls hold s_n at its maximum within four and three layers of the layer that empties them, so index 15's flat s_n is not evidence for unbounded lifetimes.

records.t: A capacity-18 seam that dies and one that does not share a first-star schedule exactly, so the schedule is not what decides
records.st: cap18_entry_supply.py's first_star_schedule depends only on the prefix and body1. Index 5, 21213(13)^a031(31)^b303, and index 8, 21213(13)^a1213(13)^b03, share both, so their schedules are identical by construction, and the two computed schedules agree in period and entry type at every layer 1 to 20. Index 5 empties at depth 23 with a verified uniform mortality certificate; index 8 has 7140 surviving columns at depth 18 and gained survivors at every layer. Their survivor ratios over the shared layers 10 to 18 are 0.875, 1.000, 0.571, 1.000, 0.500, 1.000, 1.000, 0.500, 2.000 for index 5 and 1.556, 1.679, 1.687, 1.708, 1.246, 1.439, 1.628, 1.291, 2.000 for index 8: equal at exactly the z-pair layers (1) and the fibre layer (2), where the entry-supply lemma forces the value, and different at every guard-line and point layer, where the lemmas leave the outcome free. So the schedule, the entry types and the set of layers at which mass can be lost are shared by a mortal family and an open one. Any argument for s_n > 0 whose only discriminator against index 5 is the schedule proves index 8 uniformly mortal, which is false at depth 18. Both known extinctions, index 5 at 23 and index 27 at 16, occur at point layers.
records.sc: Two families and the layers they share, 9 to 18 of an identical schedule; index 8 is not run past 18 and index 5's layers 19 to 23 have no index-8 counterpart. It identifies what does NOT decide, not what does: the seam word and the body2 transport are what remain, and nothing here shows which of the two, or that either is decisive. It is not an argument that index 8 or index 15 has unbounded lifetimes; index 8's counts are a growing finite prefix and the stop reason is a cap. The point-layer observation is two data points, the only two extinctions available. The schedules are compared as computed by first_star_schedule on each manifest's own config, which is the same function the lift's layer types are asserted against, so this is one program agreeing with itself about a quantity that depends on two strings.

records.t: Refuted: the registered [0.15, 0.55] band for s_n on an open capacity-18 seam, killed from above by index 23
records.st: experiments/rule30/PREREGISTRATION-cap18-safe-set-and-seam-23.md predicted, before either family's s_n was computed, that s_n lies in [0.15, 0.55] at every computed depth of indices 23 and 34, with a kill outside [0.10, 0.60]. The kill fired: index 23's s_14 is 0.6214. It fired on the high side, which is the opposite of what the kill was written to catch; the registration's stated worry was an s_n of 0, which it said would be the first ever seen on an open seam and would put a common-depth certificate for that seam back in play. 0.6214 is instead the largest s_n ever measured on an open seam. The band was set from the two families then available, indices 15 and 8, whose maxima are 0.4274 and 0.5000, and was simply too tight above. Across all four open seams s_n is now never 0 at any computed depth, n = 4..18 for index 15, 8..17 for index 8, 12..18 for index 23 and 8..16 for index 34, and the whole range is [0.1765, 0.6214]; both closed seams take only the values 0 and 1.
records.sc: What is refuted is this session's own registered band, a prediction about a measurement, not any statement about Rule 30 or about the family. It is recorded because the registration said a fired kill is reported as a fired kill rather than rescoped after the fact. It carries no implication for mortality in either direction, and in particular a high s_n is not evidence against mortality: the companion control record shows both closed seams hold s_n at its maximum within four and three layers of the layer that empties them. The clean split between the four open seams (s_n never 0) and the two closed ones (s_n only 0 or 1) is a description of six families, not a criterion, and the closed pair's values are quantised by having at most 8 columns.
records.nt: The two profiles are in cap18-self-sufficient-share-i23-i34.json, which is that program's own output for these two manifests, and in section 13 of the document. A future band for s_n on an open seam should be set from all four seams, not from the two that happened to exist first.

source_context.heading: 13. The last open seam lifted, and a guard-independent survival count

records.t: A guard-independent count of columns that cannot die, equal to the GOOD set on both closed capacity-18 seams and 2.0 to 2.6 times larger on all four open ones
records.st: A column of G_n dies at layer n+1 exactly when its reachable set R misses its accepted set A, and the balanced guard lemma makes A one of {0,1}, {2,3}, {0,3}, {1,2}. Those four are the lines of AG(2,2) in directions (0,1) and (1,1) under the pair labelling the programs already use, so the two lines in direction (1,0), {0,2} and {1,3}, are never accepted sets and a column whose R lies inside no guard line has a child whatever its own guard is. Define SAFE_n as the count of such columns, so SAFE_n > 0 forces G_(n+1) nonempty. A z-pair is exactly {0,2} or {1,3} and corollary 3 closes a z or four-cycle cycle's entries to a set containing one, so the GOOD set is inside SAFE; that containment is asserted at every layer of all six two-parameter capacity-18 families and never fails, and lift_lemma reports zero violations on all six. Pre-registered in PREREGISTRATION-cap18-safe-set-and-seam-23.md. Both forced control values hold: SAFE_22 = 0 for index 5 and SAFE_15 = 0 for index 27, the depths whose successor layer is empty. SAFE_n is positive at every computed depth of indices 15, 8, 23 and 34. The registered ratio prediction, mean SAFE/GOOD over index 15's depths at least 1.5 with a kill below 1.2, holds at 2.63. The new fact is the split: SAFE equals GOOD at every depth of index 5 and at every depth of index 27 but n = 6. SAFE_n equals |G_n| at every z-pair and fibre layer with no counterexample across all six families, so the count is forced except at guard-line and point layers and only those are informative. Restricted to them the mean SAFE/GOOD ratios are 2.58 for index 15 over 5 layers, 2.14 for index 8 over 5, 1.40 for index 23 over 3 and 2.07 for index 34 over 6, with minima 1.32, 1.63, 1.24 and 1.56; the unrestricted means, 2.63, 2.45, 2.01 and 2.59, average the forced layers in and are not the right number. Both closed families have no ratio at all at an informative layer, because there GOOD_n = SAFE_n = 0 and the quotient is 0/0. Sharper and exceptionless: call a layer destructive when it is a guard line or a point, the two types at which anything can die. On both closed seams SAFE_n = 0 at every one of their 18 destructive layers and equals |G_n| at every non-destructive one, so there it is a function of the layer type alone; on all four open seams SAFE_n lies strictly between 0 and |G_n| at every one of their 19 destructive layers and is never 0. SAFE_n = |G_n| at every z-pair and fibre layer holds with no counterexample across all six families.
records.sc: SAFE_n positive at finitely many layers bounds nothing and decides neither uniform nor individual mortality; what would close the route is a proof that SAFE_n > 0 at every n, and this is not one. SAFE is SUFFICIENT for a column to have a child and never necessary, and both controls show the difference: index 5 has SAFE_n = 0 at ten depths and G_(n+1) is nonempty at nine of them, so SAFE_n = 0 is not extinction. SAFE_n equals |G_n| at every z-pair and fibre layer by construction, since every entry is then a z-pair or the fibre, so like s_n it carries information only at guard-line and point layers. The two families whose answer is known CANNOT test what SAFE adds over GOOD, because on them the two sets coincide at every depth but one; the 2.0-to-2.6 gain exists only where the answer is unknown, which is exactly where it cannot be checked against an outcome. The derivation rests on the balanced guard lemma and on the pair labelling and GUARD_LINES of cap18_entry_supply.py, both taken as given rather than re-derived here, and the reachable sets are that program's own, asserted by it to equal the monodromy closure of the cycle's entries.

records.t: Dyadic-lag seed estimate at 2^23: null at every lag, below its own resolution floor, and not the first such measurement
records.st: D_N(h)/(N-h) was computed at all 254 lags of D = {2^a - 2^b} inside [1, 2^22] on the stored 2^23-bit singleton centre trace, over prefixes N = 2^20, 2^21, 2^22, 2^23. Every ratio at N = 2^23 lies in [0.499544, 0.500591]. This is NOT the first evaluation of the statistic and the pre-registration's assertion that it was is false: experiments/overnight-arms/frontier_attack/a18_cryptanalysis/test4_autocorrelation.py computes z(l) = A(l) sqrt(T-l) with A(l) = 1 - 2 D_T(l)/(T-l), the exact negative of this statistic, on a sequence byte-identical to the little-endian decode of this trace, at EVERY lag from 1 to 100,000, at T = 2^20 and 2^21, with Bonferroni control over 100,838 declared tests and a twenty-seed empirical null band; the two z values sum to zero at every lag checked. What this run adds is the 115 dyadic lags above 100,000, the prefixes 2^22 and 2^23, and the first evaluation of aggregate alternative (3), which that arm never forms. The band is not evidence for (2): D_N(h) is exactly Binomial(N-h, 1/2) under a fair-coin null, since partitioning [0,N) by residue mod h makes the mismatch indicators independent within a class, so the ratio's standard deviation is exactly 1/(2 sqrt(N-h)) = 2.44e-4 at the largest lag and the observed band spans -2.56 to +2.72 in those units. It is the resolution floor. The registered kill was uncalibrated, naming a direction and no magnitude, and fired at 29 of the 232 ELIGIBLE lags against a null expectation of 28.0, with 127 of 254 ratios below 1/2 against 127 expected. An exclusive range bound had dropped h = 2^22, the largest lag; its ratio is 0.499790, inside the band, so the headline did not move but the count 253 was wrong. Three controls all fail the hypothesis as required.
records.sc: A finite measurement, and it confirms nothing: no finite N establishes a liminf, so the test could only have killed the hypothesis and did not. Ratios at or above 1/2 are not evidence FOR (2). Any liminf below 1/2 by less than 1/(2 sqrt(N-h)) is invisible here. The novelty claim in the registration is withdrawn, not the measurement; the registration is left as written and the correction is disclosed in the source section, as is a registered control that was not met (control 1 required reproducing {6: 1/3, 12: 1} and the run reports {6: 1/3, 12: 0}; the two are consistent because the prior audit records C-densities and this reports D-ratios, but the h=6 agreement is a coincidence, 1/3 being the fixed point of x -> 1 - 2x, so that entry was never the cross-check intended). The a18 arm's calibration is stronger than this run's. One trace, one statistic; no second program reproduces the counts here, though the a18 arm independently reproduces them on the overlapping lags. Nothing here bears on whether (2) or (3) is true.
records.nt: Reproduce with `uv run python experiments/rule30/p2_dyadic_lag_seed_estimate.py`, about a minute. NO CATALOG RECORD CITED THE a18 ARM BEFORE THIS ONE, which is the mechanism behind the false novelty claim: a tracked cryptanalytic sweep was invisible to the record graph, so this document's status field could truthfully report that no seed estimate existed while one sat on disk. Indexing that arm is open work. Two control lessons are wired into the script: Rule 90's centre column is 1 at t=0 and 0 after, so D_n(h) = 1 at EVERY lag and it takes one distinct value over 154 lags, meaning it cannot detect a wrong lag set, which is how h = 2^22 went missing; the repair is a Fibonacci (Sturmian) control whose ratios run 0.004133 to 0.763932 over 191 lags and whose exact frequencies (density 1/phi^2, D(1)/(N-1) = 2/phi^2) are uniform to infinity. A control now asserts failure when SOME lag drops below 1/2, not when every lag does, since (2) quantifies over every h.

source_context.heading: 6. A seed estimate at the dyadic lags, and what it cannot decide

records.t: The aggregate alternative and the per-lag hypothesis are sensitive to opposite alternatives, so a clean aggregate does not strengthen the per-lag result
records.st: Write P for a set of k dyadic lags and consider the aggregate (1/N) sum_(h in P) C_N(h) beside the per-lag ratio. Under a Bernoulli(1/2) null the cross-covariances vanish identically: for h != h', E[z_t z_(t+h) z_s z_(s+h')] = 0 because pairing the index multisets forces h = h' or h + h' = 0. So Var of the sum is exactly sum_(h in P) (N-h) and the aggregate's null standard deviation is sqrt(sum_P (N-h))/N, exactly rather than by an independence approximation. Against a COMMON-MODE alternative, D_N(h)/(N-h) = 1/2 - eps at every lag of P at once, the aggregate accumulates signal linearly and noise in quadrature, giving |z| = 2 eps sqrt(sum_P (N-h)) against a single lag's 2 eps sqrt(N-h). The ratio is sqrt(sum_P (N-h)/(N-h0)), which depends on the reference lag h0 and is NOT sqrt(|P|); that would require every N-h equal, and at the measured pair set sum_P h is 8 percent of |P|N. Referenced against the best-sampled lag the factor is 15.30, the aggregate resolving eps to 3.39e-5 where that lag needs 5.18e-4. Against an alternative confined to a SINGLE lag the same pooling is a loss of exactly the same factor. Since (2) fails as soon as one h fails while (3) constrains only the sum, the per-lag test is the correct instrument for (2) and the aggregate for (3); the converse fails, one lag with C_N(h)/N -> delta > 0 not refuting (3) because other lags may cancel it. So a clean aggregate does not certify (2) UNIFORMLY over alternatives, although against the common-mode class specifically it IS the sharper of the two tests, and that qualification is the content of the claim. The aggregate's lag set is also not the per-lag table's: (3) requires only h < N where the per-lag test wants h <= N/2, a distinction worth 22 of the 276 pairs at m = 24 carrying 55 percent of the sum.
records.sc: About what each measurement can decide, not about whether (2) or (3) is true; both remain open and unproved for Rule 30, exactly as their source record states, and neither statistic constrains a liminf or limsup at any finite N. The common-mode and single-lag alternatives are two extreme shapes and real failures need be neither; the point is only that the ordering of the two tests' power reverses between them, so no unqualified statement that either test is the more sensitive is available. The gain figure is computed at this k and this N and is not a uniform constant. It does not show (3) is weaker than (2) as an implication, which is the source record's claim taken as given here. No sign-agnostic triangle bound is asserted: it is the wrong tool for a one-sided statement, discarding the signs (3) is about, and at fixed m it tends to zero anyway since k is constant in N. This record supersedes TWO earlier formulations, neither committed. The first claimed (3) could not be empirically falsified at fixed m at rate O(m/sqrt N); a refuter showed the rate was the cancelling one quoted inside a sign-agnostic claim and the power conclusion inverted. The second quoted the gain as sqrt(254) and asserted the triangle bound was not small at large m; a second refuter showed the gain is lag-dependent and that the bound is small under (3)'s own order of limits. Both rounds of error were hand-derived numbers in prose, so every figure here is now computed by the cited script and read out of its artifact.
records.nt: The artifact's aggregate_alternative_3 block reports, beside every partial sum, the exact null standard deviation the sum is read against and the common-mode detection thresholds for both tests, so the numbers cannot later be quoted as evidence for (3). Measured there: partial sums peak at +4.3e-3 at m = 14 and fall to +4.8e-4 at m = 24 over the full 276-pair set, every z within [-0.44, +1.40]. The gain is reported against both the smallest and the largest lag because it is not a single number; the largest-lag figure is degenerate at m = 24, that lag having N - h = 1.

source_context.heading: 6. A seed estimate at the dyadic lags, and what it cannot decide

records.t: A pre-registered cryptanalytic battery finds no distinguisher for the centre column at T <= 2^21, on a decision rule its own power controls did not meet
records.st: The a18 arm fixed a ledger of N = 100,838 hypotheses before any data (Berlekamp-Massey profile 18, correlation attack 780, NIST SP 800-22 40, autocorrelation 100,000) and applied Bonferroni at family-wise alpha = 0.05, per-hypothesis 4.9584e-07. For the lone-seed centre column the smallest raw p is 6.214e-06, adjusted 6.266e-01, with 0 Bonferroni and 0 Benjamini-Hochberg rejections: NO BIAS FOUND. Depth extension to T = 2^21 repeats tests 2 and 4 with the same result, max |z| 4.393 at lag 36578 against an i.i.d. seed band of [4.160, 4.907]. Controls that fire: lfsr32 (linear complexity plateaus at L = 32 where the centre column reaches 131,072 at n = 2^18, a factor of 4,096), bern51 (rejected at the registered p < 1e-3 by whole-sequence monobit at 1.0189e-89 and by both cumulative-sums streams at 0.0), copy1000 (autocorrelation z = 20.738 exactly at lag 1000). HOWEVER the registered decision rule reads NO BIAS FOUND only when 'all three non-degenerate power controls fire as registered' and INCONCLUSIVE otherwise, 'including a power control that fails to fire'. The three registered are lfsr32, bern51 and lag1000, and lag1000 failed BOTH of its requirements: its test-4 run rejects at NO lag at all, 0 of 100,000 exceeding the Bonferroni line, and the registered test-2 grid contains no Delta = 1000 at any k, its nearest cell being 1024, so that requirement was registered at a lag the same document's own ledger excludes. The control is mis-specified by construction and not merely by grid: for s_t = r_t XOR r_(t-1000) the shifted XOR is s_t XOR s_(t+1000) = r_(t-1000) XOR r_(t+1000), and at any other lag it is an XOR of four distinct fair bits, so the sequence is balanced at EVERY lag and has zero power anywhere, not only at its own. Recomputed here from the arm's own seq/lag1000.npy it gives z(1000) = +0.150462, in the same run in which copy1000 reproduces the committed 20.73840682678574 to sixteen digits. The arm found and disclosed this itself as deviation D1 and substituted copy1000, chosen after seeing the output. By the letter of the registered rule the outcome is INCONCLUSIVE, and PREREG is more explicit still: a test failing its registered power requirement 'is reported as having unknown power, not as a passing null'. The substitution is defensible because the control was provably null, but the headline rests on a post hoc control and a record must carry that. D3 is a second, independent ground for the same reading: test 1 was registered as {J, Hbar, D} x 6 prefixes and delivered as {G, J} x 9, so two of three registered statistics left the ledger while N = 100,838 still matched, which the arm records as happening by accident rather than by design. PREREG.md also requires deviations be appended to PREREG.md itself; they live in cryptanalysis.md section 7 instead.
records.sc: A negative result about DETECTABILITY by four techniques at T <= 2^21. It does not IMPLY P1 or P2 in either direction: no finite-prefix statistic can imply aperiodicity, and symmetrically a surviving hit would not have refuted P1 either, a biased sequence being free to be aperiodic. But it is NOT true that the arm bears on neither prize, and the arm's own 'does not bear on P1, P2 or P3' is too strong: its null autocorrelation sweep yields an explicit period exclusion, recorded separately as r30-a18-autocorrelation-excludes-period-band. Three further limits, none of which changes the verdict. Test 2's sensitivity to a lag correlation is demonstrated ONLY outside the ledger, by a supplementary check at one hand-picked lag chosen after the fact, because the two in-ledger firing controls are both degenerate for that purpose: rule90 gives eps = 0.5 at every cell and bern51 gives eps = |2p-1|/2 independent of Delta. The autocorrelation sweep tests 100,000 of 1,048,576 available lags, 90.5 percent untested, and that cap is also what fixes N. The generator gate compares 65,536 bits against two independent implementations, 6.25 percent of the 2^20 prefix and 3.1 percent of the 2^21 extension. The arm's own Obstruction H governs all of it: every result is a statement about a finite prefix and can never establish randomness, absence of structure or nonperiodicity as an infinite statement.
records.nt: This is the second record to cite this arm and the first to index it as a whole; before 2026-09-21 no record cited it at all and no record in the database sources from experiments/overnight-arms. The source index rglobs docs/rule30 and experiments/rule30 and otherwise indexes only what records cite, so an uncited tree is invisible by construction. The measured cost of that invisibility is r30-sdc-dyadic-lag-seed-estimate-extends-a18-sweep, a record that exists only to withdraw a false novelty claim this arm would have prevented. Two further defects found while indexing, neither affecting the verdict: single_column_gate.py raises NameError on a name never bound, after writing its JSON and before its txt, so the committed txt is from an older script and its headline contradicts the committed JSON; and null_calibration.py's committed outputs predate the current script, so that script's exculpatory DFT verdict appears in no committed output while both committed outputs say the DFT stream 'is MISCALIBRATED and must be discounted'. Any record citing the DFT stream must carry the committed verdict, not the write-up's.

source_context.heading: 7. Deviations from the pre-registration

records.t: The centre column's Berlekamp-Massey profile, not just its ceiling, matches a random sequence through n = 2^18 against a 500-seed null
records.st: Berlekamp-Massey gives L(n) = 513, 2049, 8192, 32771, 65537, 131072 at n = 2^10, 2^12, 2^14, 2^16, 2^17, 2^18, so L(n) - ceil(n/2) = +1, +1, 0, +3, +1, 0 and L/(n/2) = 1.0020, 1.0005, 1.0000, 1.0001, 1.0000, 1.0000. The column sits ON the n/2 line, which is the random-sequence expectation, not above or below it. This record is NOT the ceiling result: that is ea4c789fd2294772, already proved through n = 16384, and this reproduces it exactly at n = 16384 (L = 8192, ratio 1.0000). What is new is the PROFILE, which a maximal ceiling does not determine, together with its null. The jump count J(n) = 273, 1048, 4095, 16340, 32829, 65502 lies inside a 500-seed empirical null at all nine tested prefixes, empirical p from 0.128 to 0.984, and the mean jump height Hbar approaches 2.00, the geometric expectation, from n = 2^14 up. The exact integer G(n) = sum_(m<=n) (2L(m) - m) equals n/2 exactly at 2^10 through 2^15 and at 2^17, 2^18, 2^20, and departs from it twice: n/2 - 12 at n = 65536 and n/2 - 4 at n = 2^19. A first pass reported that anomaly as REJECT (profile anomalous) at z = -5.415; it is an ARTIFACT and the arm retired it, the null taking only four distinct values across 500 seeds at that prefix so that a normal z on a 20-seed standard deviation of 1.5e-5 is a normal approximation to a lattice statistic at near-degeneracy. Against the 500-seed empirical null the same deviation has p = 0.0639 and does not persist with depth.
records.sc: Capped in depth and in comparison, and the two caps differ. The profile-against-null comparison holds to n = 2^18 = 262,144; G alone was computed to 2^20 with NO null at 2^19 or 2^20, so that figure is a bare number with nothing to read it against; and the 20-seed band underlying the original z stops at 2^17, leaving the n = 262,144 row with no null comparison at all. Hbar is a deterministic function of the same jump list as J, so the two are not independent hypotheses despite being counted separately in the ledger. The delivered test-1 ledger is {G, J} x 9 prefixes against the registered {J, Hbar, D} x 6, which the arm discloses as deviation D3 and notes matches the registered count of 18 'by accident, not by design'. The measurement DOES carry one infinite-statement consequence, and it is already subsumed: an eventually periodic sequence with preperiod q and period p satisfies a linear recurrence of order q+p, so L(n) <= q+p for EVERY n, and L(2^18) = 131,072 therefore forces q+p >= 131,072 if the centre column is eventually periodic at all. That is the same logical shape as the recorded subword-complexity exclusion 7e73f8c439ee894e, which uses p(n) <= r+q to force r+q >= max_n p_hat(n) = N - L with L the longest repeated factor, empirically about 2 log2 N; that bound is LINEAR in the prefix length and its 200,000-bit run actually excludes r+q <= 199,966, against this route's 1.31e5; the Berlekamp-Massey profile therefore adds nothing to period exclusion and must not be reported as if it did. (The autocorrelation sweep in the same arm does much better, see r30-a18-autocorrelation-excludes-period-band.) What a profile on the n/2 line does NOT do is exclude eventual periodicity, since any period exceeding the measured depth reproduces it exactly. The empirical p floor of 1/501 = 0.00200 is 4025 times the global Bonferroni threshold, so by the arm's own statement this audit 'can refute a hit, not confirm one'.
records.nt: Two existing records are consistent with this and neither is contradicted: 7a656f9e4beb60b0 gives L(50..2000) = 26, 48, 101, 249, 500, 1000 and 6546acd5619c9050 gives L(50,000) = 24,999. The retired-statistic story is the transferable lesson: a z-score against a 20-sample standard deviation of a lattice-valued statistic produced a 5.4-sigma false alarm that a 500-seed empirical null dissolved to p = 0.064.

later_amendments.heading: Global correction

records.t: The null autocorrelation sweep excludes every eventual period up to 100,000 with preperiod below 995,021
records.st: If the centre column is eventually periodic with period p and preperiod q then c_t = c_(t+p) for every t >= q, so over t in [0, T-p) at most q positions mismatch and the autocorrelation obeys A(p) = (T-p-2D)/(T-p) >= (T-p-2q)/(T-p), giving z(p) = A(p) sqrt(T-p) >= (T-p-2q)/sqrt(T-p). The a18 depth extension reports 0 of 100,000 lags exceeding the Bonferroni threshold 5.032 at T = 2^21 = 2,097,152. Hence for every p <= 100,000 we need (T-p-2q)/sqrt(T-p) < 5.032, and since sqrt(T-p) <= 1413.2 in that range this forces q > (T - p - 7111)/2 >= 995,020. THEREFORE the lone-seed centre column has no eventual period p <= 100,000 with preperiod q <= 995,020, excluding p+q up to about 1,095,020 in that regime. The comparison that matters: the catalogued subword-complexity exclusion 7e73f8c439ee894e achieved r+q <= 199,966 on a 200,000-bit run, so this is roughly 5.5x further in the band it covers. The argument is elementary counting on top of a committed measurement; no new computation was needed to obtain it.
records.sc: A BAND, not a bound in one variable, and the two axes trade off: it excludes small period with large preperiod and says nothing about a period above 100,000 at any preperiod, that cap being the arm's registered lag ceiling rather than anything intrinsic. The subword exclusion it is compared against is not dominated, since that one bounds r+q with no cap on r; the two cover different regions and neither subsumes the other. It does not touch P2. It rests on the arm's committed autocorrelation output rather than a re-run, and that output inherits the arm's own caveat that its lag1000 power control is provably null, though nothing about this exclusion depends on a power control: it is a one-sided counting argument that uses only the ABSENCE of a large positive autocorrelation, so a weak test can only make the exclusion more conservative, never false. Widening the lag cap widens the excluded band directly and was not done here. CORRECTION, inherited and repeated once before being caught: this record's comparison against 7e73f8c439ee894e is against that method's 200,000-bit erratum, while 70faaffe0b04ef36 applies the same subword-complexity argument at N = 8,388,608 and forces r+q >= 8,388,565 with no cap on the period. This record's band, and the wider one in r30-full-lag-autocorrelation-null-2e23, are both STRICTLY DOMINATED by it; the 'roughly 5.5x further' claim above is false and the autocorrelation route buys nothing for period exclusion.
records.nt: This record exists because an independent refuter attacked the claim that the arm bears on neither prize. It does, and the arm's own section 8 ('This does not bear on P1, P2 or P3') is too strong about its own result. The exclusion was available from a committed output for weeks and no record carried it, which is the same invisibility this indexing pass exists to fix.

records.t: No autocorrelation distinguisher at any of 4.19M lags at T = 2^23, at a maximum indistinguishable from the sample-size expectation
records.st: Every lag 1 <= l <= 2^22 on the stored 2^23-bit centre trace, z(l) = A(l) sqrt(T-l) with A(l) the balance of c_t XOR c_(t+l), by FFT zero-padded to 2^24 >= 2T so the circular correlation is exactly linear. Result: max z = 5.5216 at lag 1,656,153, min z = -5.2703 at lag 661,856, and 0 of 4,194,304 lags reach the two-sided Bonferroni threshold 5.701. The maximum is not a finding but the sample size: the one-sided expected maximum for that many i.i.d. normals is sqrt(2 ln L) = 5.5225, and the observed 5.5216 sits 0.0009 below it. Twenty i.i.d. Bernoulli(1/2) seeds at the same T and lag range give empirical max z = 5.7157 and max |z| = 6.0485, both ABOVE Rule 30's maximum, so the column is less extreme than a typical random sweep of the same width. A registered gate requires the FFT to reproduce a direct mismatch count at 24 spread lags; observed maximum discrepancy 1.221e-15 in z. This extends the prior sweep of 100,000 lags at T = 2^21 by 42x in lags and 4x in length, and that extension is the contribution.
records.sc: A finite-prefix statistic. It cannot imply aperiodicity in either direction and does not touch P2. ITS PERIOD COROLLARY IS TRUE AND STRICTLY DOMINATED, and is recorded only so it is not rediscovered: z(p) < thr forces q > (T-p-thr sqrt(T-p))/2, excluding p <= 4,194,304 with q <= 2,091,314 and reaching p+q = 6,285,618 at most, whereas 70faaffe0b04ef36 forces r+q >= N-L from subword complexity with NO cap on the period and gives r+q >= 8,388,565 at this same N. Verified directly on this trace: at window length 44 all 8,388,565 windows are distinct, so L = 43. The margin is 2,102,947 and no region of the band survives. The domination is structural, not incidental: p(n) <= r+q uses every window while the autocorrelation uses one lag at a time, so extending the sweep cannot close the gap. Three registration defects are disclosed in the source section: the Rule 90 power bar was unreachable at the length first used and was repaired by raising the length rather than fixing the threshold, which is the wrong direction; both positive controls are constants independent of the Rule 30 data, sitting at 475x and 508x the decision boundary, so the registered kill clause is dead code; and the Sturmian word was cast as a negative control but exceeds the threshold at 260,436 of 524,288 lags, correctly. The first run reported INCONCLUSIVE under the registration's own control rule and the exclusion was withheld, but that run left no artifact, the JSON being overwritten in place while untracked.
records.nt: An independent refuter recomputed every number from the trace with its own FFT and its own generators and reproduced max z = 5.521645634593456 at lag 1,656,153 to the digit, along with the direct mismatch count D = 3,359,064 there, which is why independently_reproduced is true. The same refuter found the domination that retitled this record. Reproduce with `uv run python experiments/rule30/p1_full_lag_period_exclusion.py`, a few minutes and about 400 MB resident.

source_context.heading: 1. The measurement, which is what is new

records.t: The autocorrelation maximum cannot discriminate a sequence from its balanced-masked version, exactly invariant under the period-2 mask
records.st: XOR-ing a binary mask m into a sequence multiplies its sign sequence by (-1)^(m_t). For the period-2 mask m_t = t mod 2 this gives x'_t x'_(t+l) = x_t x_(t+l) (-1)^t (-1)^(t+l) = x_t x_(t+l) (-1)^l, so corr'(l) = (-1)^l corr(l) and |z(l)| = |corr(l)|/sqrt(n-l) is PRESERVED EXACTLY AT EVERY LAG. The autocorrelation maximum is therefore blind by construction, not merely underpowered, to that mask and to every mask whose complement-shift set contains the argmax lag. Measured on the Rule 30 centre column: max |z| and its argmax lag are identical under the period-2 mask to fifteen digits. Calibration of the whole family: the largest movement any balanced deterministic mask produces is about 0.50, while the Gumbel standard deviation of max |z| at N = 4.19e6 lags is 1/sqrt(2 ln 2N) = 0.18. The occasioning run measured the Thue-Morse residual R_t = c_t XOR theta(t) over t in [1, 2^23) and found residual density 0.5002161 (+1.25 null sd) against the column's 0.5002196 (+1.27 sd), and residual max |z| 5.2244 against the column's 5.5220, a gap of 0.2976 against a registered kill at 1.0. That kill is twice the largest achievable effect and 5.6 standard deviations of the statistic's own noise: IT COULD NOT FIRE. The observed -0.2976 sits inside the range seven i.i.d. random masks produce, -0.499 to +0.030. The null was forced by the design.
records.sc: A statement about the INSTRUMENT, not about Rule 30. It says max |z| cannot resolve a balanced deterministic mask at this N; it says nothing about whether the Thue-Morse decomposition simplifies the centre column, and the occasioning run's headline that the residual is 'statistically indistinguishable from the column' is WITHDRAWN as unsupported. The exact invariance is proved only for the period-2 mask; for other masks the blindness is empirical (the 0.50 ceiling over the masks tried) except where the argmax lag lies in the mask's complement-shift set, where it is again exact. The measurement's Rule 90 control was VACUOUS: that column is 0 for every t >= 1, so the asserted identity (0 XOR theta)[1:] == theta[1:] holds for any array and passes with a deliberately wrong theta, establishing only that the Rule 90 column is all-zero after t = 0 rather than that the residual is formed correctly, which is what the registration gated INCONCLUSIVE on. Nothing here bears on P1 or P2.
records.nt: WITHDRAWN AND RETITLED after an independent refuter. The original claim was that the residual is statistically indistinguishable from the column, so the decomposition buys no simplification. Three defects: the discriminator is blind by construction (above); the novelty claim was false against section 7 of this very document, which already measures the residual at 4147/8192 with 2007 pair-disagreements, and section 9, which already pre-registers the counter-argument with theta XOR (t mod 2) = theta(floor(t/2)) as the worked example, the same period-2 mask; and 4cdee047bcdb8c0d already proves the absolute Walsh multiset, its maximum and every absolute spectral moment are unchanged under theta-masking, so 'no simplification' was in the catalog in exact proved form. A catalog grep for mutual information, row weight and column entropy returned zero and was taken as novelty; the document the identity record points at held both the measurement and its refutation. Thin companion: zscores, direct_z, rule30_centre and rule90_centre are imported unchanged from p1_full_lag_period_exclusion.py, which r30-full-lag-autocorrelation-null-2e23 cites, so no second implementation of the sweep exists and that record's recorded source_sha256 does not move. The identity record 0081391386ad06b3 sits in prize node p2's `context` list, which next.targets does not read, so the identity this measurement is about is itself invisible on every ladder; not restructured here.

nodes.title: Formalize the reduction chain
nodes.statement: Program-carrying reductions must be checked as finite logical theorems, preferably in Lean, separately from the finite computations they connect.
nodes.scope: Mortality->period two, SEP->period two, RW/DLP->SEP, BWH->RW, capacity/budget->mortality, and analogous P2 energy bridge.
nodes.success: Each of the six bridges named in the scope checked as a finite logical theorem, preferably in Lean, whose hypotheses are exactly the finite computations it cites and whose conclusion is the target statement, with the proof term free of sorry and a control in which a weakened hypothesis makes the check fail. The attached ledger is a prioritization of that work, not any part of it, so extending the ledger is not success. Unbounded lifetimes proved for an open seam refute uniform mortality for that seam; for indices 8, 23 and 34 that closes the rung negatively, since they have no other target, but for index 15 it only closes the common-depth form, since a uniform bound on D would survive it and the rung would then be restated through D; for index 15 the instrument is whether every G_n carries a survivor on a z or order-4 cycle.
