nodes.scope: Local laws only. The local rank is not monotone under switches (unbounded refill families), so these do not by themselves bound cumulative repeats; that bound is the open task.
nodes.success: Closed as a set of local laws: history-preserving composition with every seam and survival guard retained, the exact inverse-fibre suffix count, phase-rank descent and the phase-switch height reset. It reopens if any law fails on an object in its stated domain: a guarded composition, a predecessor-suffix fibre, or an actual image under the zero-extension convention. They do not by themselves close budget: rank_control shows the local rank is not monotone under switches, so no bound follows from these laws alone. They are inputs to a cumulative argument, which must also bound the cumulative switch refill, for which the source says additional realizability information is essential; citing them as that bound is a scope error.

nodes.title: Repeat potential
nodes.statement: A nonnegative, independently computable or verifiable potential Phi(history), bounded initially by B(r), with Phi(hs) <= Phi(h) - 1[s = last(h)] on every accepted extension (the first emission carries no repeat charge).
nodes.scope: A proposed certificate format for the repeat budget, not a proved potential. It may retain the initial length, ordered history and seam information; defining Phi as the number of future repeats would assume the missing result.
nodes.success: A nonnegative Phi, bounded initially by B(r) with B depending only on the initial length, not the current length or the elapsed time, satisfying the stated drop inequality on every accepted extension, defined without reference to future repeats, and with a formula that is independently computable or verifiable. Defining Phi as the number of future repeats assumes the missing result.

nodes.title: Local rank not monotone
nodes.statement: Defect-population rank cannot be nonincreasing under switches; phase switches produce an unbounded refill family.
nodes.scope: Kills the local-rank mechanism for the repeat budget. Says nothing about a history-dependent potential.
nodes.success: Settled negatively: no rank C_q + SUM (X_d + Y_d) with fixed finite phase constants, nor any fixed nonnegative depth weighting whose sum over the refill depths diverges, can be nonincreasing under switches, because phase switches produce an unbounded refill family. The mechanism revives for a more elaborate function of the full ordered defect profile or for a quantity that retains additional history, and any candidate must be evaluated on the refill family first. This kills the local-rank route to budget and nothing more, so a budget argument is not excluded by it.

nodes.title: Ancestor count plateaus
nodes.statement: Counting compatible original ancestors cannot charge repeats: C_3(0)=C_3(00) has eight elements and C_6(101)=C_6(1011)=C_6(10111) has 36, and the extension C_6(10111)=C_6(101110)=C_6(1011100), three repeats at 36, disproves the absolute bound |C_r|*4^D <= 2^(2r-1).
nodes.scope: Kills bare ancestor counting per repeat; that approach would need a cumulative bound whose information is acquired within the first r updates, or additional information.
nodes.success: Settled negatively for per-repeat charging: C_3(0) = C_3(00) at eight elements and C_6(101) = C_6(1011) = C_6(10111) at 36 show that neither every repeat nor every consecutive pair of repeats shrinks the ancestor set, and the extension to C_6(1011100), three repeats at 36 with 36*4^3 = 2304 > 2048, disproves the two-bit bound |C_r|*4^D <= 2^(2r-1). The one-bit bound |C_r|*2^D <= 2^(2r-1) is not refuted. Once the history has length r, every later successful repeat carries zero information about the original ancestor, so no window, however long, crosses such a plateau: the mechanism revives only if the information is acquired within the first r updates, the class freezing after update r and not after r-1, or with a quantity beyond the ancestor count. A candidate must be checked against the three-repeat length-6 plateau first.

nodes.title: Infinite-support xhat(y)
nodes.statement: For every finite right seed y, the left row xhat(y) reconstructed from the wall trace rho(y) by left permutivity has infinite support; equivalently no finite right trace equals, symbol for symbol, the demand sequence 1-l_(2k) of a finite left seed.
nodes.scope: Exact pinned reformulation of period two, not a subgoal: by the prefix lemma the pin holds forever iff the left row equals xhat(y). The left supplies no separating property, since its survivors biject with free rho prefixes until the seed is exhausted. The prefix lemma (r30-rsm-prefix-lemma, attached here) and the eventually-periodic-traces lemma (r30-rsm-eventually-periodic-traces-safe, under settled_traces) passed an adversarial referee (crosscheck/verify-0916/margin/REFEREE.md); both are catalog records.
nodes.success: Infinite support for xhat(y) for every finite right seed y. The prefix lemma and the eventually-periodic lemma are already proved and refereed, so they are inputs to an argument, not success.

nodes.title: Zero-wall statement S3
nodes.statement: On the zero-wall half-line no finite seed has s(2k+1,-1)=1 for all k. Sufficient forms (S3-hc, S3-hc5) add s(2k,-4)=0 at all even times and never five consecutive even times with s(2k,-1)=1.
nodes.scope: One half-line automaton with no reference to the endpoint machinery; open. Proved: the wall trace conjugates the zero-wall step to the full one-sided 2-shift, and the section count is unbounded so the wall trace is not finite-state. Exponential section growth is not proved. The written attempts (backward tree, counterexample hunt, density rigidity, edge meets wall, knot theory) each received an adversarial refutation pass; none claims a proof of S3, S3-hc or S3-hc5.
nodes.success: A proof of S3, S3-hc or S3-hc5 on the half-line automaton. Exact section counts are not success: the count is already proved unbounded, exponential growth is still open, and the exact counts now run to depth 22.

nodes.title: Settled traces excluded
nodes.statement: A finite right seed whose trace rho(y) is eventually periodic has no finite left partner (uniform proof). At width 16, 1,905 of the 65,536 right seeds have provably eventually periodic traces at buffers J <= 32: 1,803 by a closed reachability certificate and the rest by entering one of eleven certified traps. r30-xhat-period5-shields-close-j44 certifies four more pure period-5 seeds at J = 44 and 48, 1,909 in all.
nodes.scope: Partial case only: period two is excluded for those seeds, not for any seed whose trace never settles. The census is finite (width 16, seeds screened by their trace to k=2048), though each certificate holds for all time; 215 of the 649 purely periodic width-16 seeds and 473 of the 1,846 strict settlers of periods 2 and 7 with a preperiod still fail the certificate at the buffers run, J<=32 for all but 99cb.
nodes.sources_note: Numbers follow docs/papers/Rule 30 with a Period-Two Center Column/main.tex (abstract) and P1/RESULTS-RIGHT-SEED-MARGIN.md section 7, not the earlier 377/1,895 figures in POSITION-PT2-2026-09-16.md.
nodes.success: Closed as a uniform partial case: a finite right seed whose trace is eventually periodic has no finite left partner. It reopens if a finite left partner is exhibited for such a seed. The width-16 census is not part of the closure and is not success for pt2: its certificates hold for all time on seeds screened to trace horizon 2048 and decide 1,905 of 65,536, and r30-xhat-period5-shields-close-j44 closes four more pure period-5 seeds at J = 44 and 48, 1,909 in all, a count derived here since every census certificate has period 2 or 7 and every trap comes from a period-2 certificate. 215 of the 649 purely periodic width-16 seeds and 473 of the 1,846 strict settlers of periods 2 and 7 with a preperiod still fail the certificate at the buffers run, J <= 32 for all but 99cb, which fails at all fourteen buffers run from 34 to 60. Raising the width, the horizon or the buffer moves that census and closes nothing.

nodes.title: PSI on (12)^k family
nodes.statement: For the alternating source family W=(12)^k the endpoint state is one period-28 sequence, proved for every k>=2 by an induction whose step is finitely many lockstep-transducer state returns; the leading constant stretch of the forced cut satisfies k_E(2)<=3 and k_E(3)<=6, against the n+2=2k+2 a failure needs.
nodes.scope: One source family only. The pre-registered bound k_E<=5 is false: at k=144, k_E(3)=6 exactly.
nodes.success: Closed on one source family: W = (12)^k has a single period-28 endpoint state, proved for every k >= 2 by an induction whose step is finitely many lockstep-transducer state returns. That makes the first seven cut cells a function of k mod 1792, and a finite check over one period gives k_E(2) <= 3 and k_E(3) <= 6 against the 2k+2 a failure needs. It reopens if the induction step or that periodicity is exhibited failing, or if a k is found with k_E(2) > 3 or k_E(3) > 6. One family is not bwh: the family has measure zero among sources, and its one-defect perturbation (12)^a 2 (12)^b is measured, not proved: for a = 2..40 and b <= 95 the anti-diagonal is a factor of the period-28 sequence at no cell and for fixed a the cut run b -> k_E has no period of length at most 40, while the column is again a period-14 pair stack once b > a (RESULTS-ALTERNATING-FAMILY.md section 3, scope finite). Separately, the pre-registered k_E <= 5 failed at k = 144 because a census to k = 60 saw 59 of the 224 residues of k_E(3); a finite census inside a periodic family is no bound until it covers a full period.

nodes.title: Shell maximum o(N)
nodes.statement: For N=2^k and the actual temporal word z_N,...,z_(2N-1), M_k = max over 0<=u<=N of |sum_(r<u) z_(N+r)| is o(N).
nodes.scope: Exactly equivalent to P2. The maximum retains excursions inside a shell, so checking only dyadic endpoint densities is insufficient. A reformulation, not a bound.
nodes.success: A bound M_k = o(N) on the actual temporal word. Exact M_k over a finite range is not success: the measured k <= 28 integers are the present frontier, and the screens refute the uniform sqrt form only for C < 2.4555.
nodes.next_action: Two open branches. (1) Extend the exact shell integers past k = 28 only with a law to reject; the rejection frontier record lists the forms already excluded on the recorded shells, so a new proposal has to clear it before it is measured. (2) Estimate the adjacent-block cross term I(uv) - I_u - I_v = n_v D_u^2 + 2 D_u A_v, which r30-p2-route1-reduces-to-adjacent-block-cross-term proves is the only place Rule 30 can enter the shell seam. Its two local forms fail at the parameters tested; beyond them nothing is closed except the one untwisted case named below. The lag-2^j digit-coupling residual after the Rule 150 linearization depends on every cell of its window except x_(-L), exactly for L = 1, 2, 4, 8 only, and is balanced on the orbit to 2.61 sqrt(N) over shells k = 14..20 and lags j = 3..10, a finite count with no asymptotic statement. Rule 30 has no spatially twisted local additive conservation law of window <= 11 for any periodic weight of period 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 or 8, so route 3's interior current cannot be removed by such a density; windows above 11 and other twists are not covered by that run, and only the untwisted period-1 case is excluded further, through window 12, by r30-bco-no-local-additive-conserved-density. What survives is those forms past the tested parameters, and a coupling written with growing windows, with history, or as an identity valid on the orbit rows alone. The orbit-only branch is bounded by three finite searches on the first 2^20 lone-seed rows, which are evidence and not a proof: r30-p2-history-window-horizon-refuted-shape-independent refutes, at the measured depths d = 1 to 7, 9, 11 and 13, a correction reading the last d windows of radius r whenever r + d - 1 <= 18, whatever its support shape inside that neighbourhood; r30-p2-clocked-window-horizon-refuted-or-vacuous refutes corrections clocked by t mod p at p = 1 to 8, 12 and 16 up to r_pair(p) between 15 and 18; and r30-p2-orbit-window-horizon-refuted-or-vacuous is the unclocked depth-one case both extend. Separately, and proved over Q by exact integer certificates on the seed orbit t < 2048, r30-qw-current-not-additive-difference-on-orbit refutes additive phase-periodic window functionals with m <= 8 and p in {1, 2, 4} on the right half-row and the full row. At radius 19 the rows hold one window return, which refutes only the centred case lambda = 1, rho = 1/2; at r >= 20 no window repeats in t < 2^20, so the identity is untested there rather than allowed. For an unclocked correction what remains is an h reading a cell outside [-18, 18]; a clocked one also keeps the radii above r_pair(p), and history depths above 13 are not covered.

nodes.title: Ordered energy o(N^2)
nodes.statement: H_k = sum_(j<=k) E_(k,j) is o(N^2), equivalently max_j E_(k,j) is o(N^2), with E_(k,j) the sum of squared aligned block sums of length 2^j.
nodes.scope: Equivalent to P2 through proved energy inequalities; any bound H_k=O(N^(2-eps)) would suffice. An exact reformulation with useful algebra, not a proof of decay.
nodes.success: A proof that H_k = o(N^2) on the actual singleton seed shells, a statement about every k. Any proved bound H_k = O(N^(2-eps)) with eps > 0 would suffice, but a power saving is not required. The finite table through k = 28 is not such a proof, and a further exact reformulation of H_k is not success.

nodes.title: Fixed-window recurrence
nodes.statement: For some l>=1 and constants 0<eta<1, C independent of k and j: V_(k,j+l) <= (1-eta) V_(k,j) + C 2^(-j) whenever j+l <= k/2 (P2-C).
nodes.scope: Stronger than necessary and neither observed nor proved as a seed law; worth pursuing only if the seed supplies a mechanism for these uniform constants. Must not replace the flexible-scale target P2-F as the primary one.
nodes.success: Uniform l>=2, eta>0 and C independent of k and j satisfying P2-C at every shell and every admissible j, by an argument in k; or a refutation covering every l>=2, which the l=1, C=0 kill explicitly does not. The pass over the stored shells is already done and is not success: r30-fwr-seed-min-loss-k28 exhibits C=0 with eta=5/8 for l=2 on all 169 admissible pairs of k<=28, 1611/1940 for l=3 on 144 and 3711/4040 for l=4 on 121, and the Rule 90 and balanced-run controls of the source document's section 3 already reject perturbed constants, so the earlier finite form of this criterion was satisfied on the day it was written. C is a trap rather than a free parameter, by r30-fwr-additive-remainder-vacuity: wherever eta V_(k,j) <= C 2^(-j) the inequality reduces to monotonicity and tests nothing. A refutation would also not reach P2, since ed8bae2f15256b6e proves P2-C strictly stronger than P2.
nodes.next_action: Do not search l >= 2 and C >= 1/4 on the stored shells. That instruction stood here until 2026-09-21 and both of its premises are false against records already attached to this node. l = 2, 3 and 4 are tested and hold with C = 0 on every admissible pair of k <= 28 (r30-fwr-seed-min-loss-k28). C does not rescue l = 1 either: at the killing pair (k,j) = (2,0), V_(2,0) = V_(2,1) = 1, so absorbing the witness needs C >= eta, which is exactly the condition under which the source document's Criterion A calls that same pair vacuous, and r30-fwr-additive-remainder-vacuity measures the regime empty of content at C = 1. What is open is uniformity in k, and the one measured threat to it is the small-block regime: on the extended domain j+l <= k the l = 2 minimum falls from 5/8 to 19/188 at (9,7), where N/2^j is four blocks (r30-fwr-extended-domain-minima). Recompute the per-shell l = 2 minimum over k <= 28 restricted to pairs with block count N/2^j >= B, for B = 4, 8, 16, 32, and report the smallest B at which the per-shell minima stop dipping. A B at which they stop localizes the obstruction to a bounded-block-count artifact and says where a uniform argument has to work; no such B, or per-shell minima still falling in k, is evidence against a k-uniform eta and is worth more than another pass at a fresh (l, C).

nodes.title: Seed matching deficit
nodes.statement: For a radius schedule R_k>=1 with R_k=o(N_k): D_+(R_k)+D_-(R_k)=o(R_k), the largest positive and negative single-interval deficits of the seed sign sequence.
nodes.scope: Sufficient for P2 if proved for the seed, by an explicit packing factor; explicitly unproved. Bounding only the largest deficit by o(N) is insufficient: many bounded deficits can sum to a linear matching loss. Freely optimized matching is equivalent to the discrepancy target.
nodes.success: A radius schedule R_k >= 1 with R_k = o(N_k), specified in advance or obtained from an independently proved seed property and not chosen from the unknown discrepancy, together with a proof on the seed that D_+(R_k) + D_-(R_k) = o(R_k). The packing bound U_R <= K_{N,R}(D_+(R) + D_-(R)), K_{N,R} = 1 + floor((N-1)/(2R+1)), is already proved for every sign word (record 3d05f972790014e7) and carries this estimate to P2; it is not part of what remains open. Bounding only the largest deficit by o(N) is insufficient by the node's own scope, since many bounded deficits can sum to a linear matching loss.

nodes.title: Cut data insufficient
nodes.statement: At a late seed age, alternative finite rows retain both moving edge strips, a growing recent centre history and the entire right half at the observation cut while prescribing an arbitrary macroscopic future centre block; they are not singleton evolutions. A seed certificate must impose an origin constraint. Maximal finite ancestry depth n characterizes the singleton row and n-d_fin(y) is invariant.
nodes.scope: The invariant's vanishing on the singleton orbit is proved; no cancellation consequence of that vanishing has been proved.
nodes.success: Closed as a control: alternative finite rows retain both moving edge strips, a growing recent centre history and the entire right half at the observation cut while prescribing an arbitrary macroscopic future centre block, so a seed certificate must impose an origin constraint. It reopens only if the construction fails inside its proved range, that is, if for some d >= 2, h >= 0, T >= 1 and a >= h+T+d some prescribed T-bit future centre word cannot be realised by a finite row sharing those cut data; a certificate using the cut data alone cannot exclude alternatives that share them. The ancestry-depth invariant vanishing on the singleton orbit is proved and no cancellation consequence of that vanishing is, so citing the invariant toward p2 is not support.

nodes.title: Potential-current identity
nodes.statement: A(T)-T/2 = P_T + sum_(t<T)(K_t-1/2), with P_t = sum_(m>=0)(x_(4m+1)^t - x_(4m+3)^t) and K the local integer charge current q_i=2x_i(x_(i+1) OR x_(i+2))+x_(i+1)x_(i+2).
nodes.scope: An exact identity. It splits the density target into a spatial and a current term and proves neither.
nodes.success: Closed as an exact identity: x_0 = P(Fx) - P(x) + K(x) is proved algebraically for every finite-support row, and telescoping from P_0 = 0 gives A(T) - T/2 = P_T + sum over t < T of (K_t - 1/2) on the seed; the checks on 6,138 finite-row cases and every seed step to T = 131,072 corroborate it and are not the proof. It reopens only if that algebra is wrong, which an arithmetic failure at some T would show. It bounds neither term, so a bound on one term alone is not a consequence of this node: spatial_potential and spatial_current are declared joint components of p2 precisely because neither suffices.

nodes.title: Quarter-wave P_t=o(t)
nodes.statement: P_t=o(t) on the actual seed; a first step is |P_t|<=kappa t+C with kappa<1/4, ultimately |P_t|<=eps_h t+C_h with eps_h->0 and C_h independent of t.
nodes.scope: The elementary bound |P_t|<=floor((t+3)/4) is proved and cannot be improved uniformly over arbitrary rows ((0100)^Z saturates it). The exact uniform quarter-loss constant delta>=1/4 is refuted on the seed (delta_(20,4)=17/84). Separate bounds are sufficient but not individually necessary; the two terms may cancel jointly.
nodes.success: |P_t| <= eps_h t + C_h on the actual seed with eps_h -> 0 and C_h independent of t. A bound with coefficient below 1/4 and a constant uniform over arbitrary rows is already known to fail: the elementary |P_t| <= floor((t+3)/4) is proved, (0100)^Z saturates it, and the finite-origin family a^(n) violates |P_t| <= ct + C for every c < 1/4 and every fixed C uniform over the family. A global initial-mass estimate P(F^t a)^2 <= C t m is not excluded by any of this and remains unproved.

nodes.title: Current sum o(T)
nodes.statement: sum_(t<T)(K_t-1/2) = o(T) on the actual seed.
nodes.scope: No established estimate closes this step and spatial cancellation alone does not prove it. The all-phase observation theorem shows a finite list of balanced local statistics cannot propagate the needed spatial property over all inputs.
nodes.success: An estimate for sum_(t<T)(K_t - 1/2) that is not a finite list of balanced local statistics. The all-phase observation theorem rules that class out over all inputs only: b24aed5480f1fc3b is scoped to periodic inputs and the dependencies document leaves the class open under seed restrictions, so an argument that uses the seed is what is asked for. On the first 2^20 lone-seed rows the window-horizon results refute every memoryless local boundary correction h reading inside radius 18 whatever its support shape; every correction reading the last d windows of radius r with r + d - 1 <= 18, which reaches 13 past windows only at r <= 6; and clocked corrections at the ten tested periods 1 to 8, 12 and 16, each up to its own radius between 15 and 18. Periods 9, 10, 11, 13, 14 and 15 were not run.
nodes.next_action: What survives the memoryless window-horizon kill is an h reading a cell outside [-18, 18]: untruncated half-row sums, about 2^20 cells wide at t = 2^20, and windows growing past radius 18. Two corrections to the wording that stood here until 2026-09-21. It said exactly, but clocked corrections also survive inside radius 18 above their own r_pair(p), for example p = 8 or 16 at r = 16 to 18 and p = 3 at r = 17 to 18, and at the six periods below 16 that were never run. It said test there, but that branch is already entered: r30-qw-current-not-additive-difference-on-orbit closes the additive phase-periodic window functionals with m <= 8 and p in {1, 2, 4} on the right half-row and the full row, at T = 2048 and so at every larger horizon. Its scope lists what is left: windows longer than 8, phase periods other than 1, 2 and 4, non-additive functionals, and functionals of history. Test one of those, or a clocked h in the surviving band, or abandon the coboundary form.

nodes.title: No finite-state predictor
nodes.statement: No finite-state machine reading the binary index of n computes c_n.
nodes.scope: Smallest restricted milestone; more general algorithms may still be fast. Nonexistence of a finite-state digit predictor would itself imply P1, so it is not automatically an easier prerequisite. All milestones are open for the required index function.
nodes.success: An explicit infinite family of 2-kernel residuals a(2^e k + r_e), one for every depth e, whose pairwise distinctness is proved for every pair by an explicit witness index w(e,e') rather than measured; or a proof that a 2-kernel of size m forces one of size m+1. Either proves the centre column is not 2-automatic. The measured lower bounds of 8191 residuals and rank 512 are not success, and neither is re-running the probe deeper: both exclude only a bounded family, the mechanism this node has already died to, and 29b767d4f735d666 records that its depth-12 bound kills the small fixed-state explanation, not finite automaticity. Falsified by a pair (e,e') whose residuals agree at w(e,e'), or by the same argument producing a spurious third residual on Thue-Morse.

nodes.title: No polylog-time query
nodes.statement: No exact query for c_n runs in polylog(n) time.
nodes.scope: Fractional-power algorithms remain. A nested restricted milestone, not a known method for proving the next one.
nodes.success: A proof, in the p3 model (canonical binary n, one fixed uniform multitape machine, all work charged, no advice growing with n), that no machine computes c_n in O((log n)^k) for any k. The proof's key lemma must fail on the control d_n = c_(floor(log n)), which plain simulation computes in O(log^2 n). Excluding a decimation law of fixed radius, or any other parameterized law family, is not success, and r30-p3-decimation-window-collision reaches only R <= 8; nor is any argument using only finitely many values of c. Falsified by a finite check showing the key lemma holds on a prefix of d_n, or on c patched to zero past some N.

nodes.title: No n^alpha-time query
nodes.statement: For every fixed 0<alpha<1 no exact query for c_n runs in O(n^alpha).
nodes.scope: Bounds such as n/log n remain sublinear. A nested restricted milestone, not a known method for proving the next one.
nodes.success: One argument covering every fixed 0 < alpha < 1 at once, in the p3 model with every cost charged, that no machine computes c_n in O(n^alpha). It must fail on the control d_n = c_(floor(n^(alpha/2))), which simulation computes in O(n^alpha), at each alpha. Excluding polylog queries is not success, nor is excluding alpha below some fixed alpha_0 one exponent at a time, and a lower bound for one chosen algorithm, exclusion of one fixed representation, or a bound on explicit local evaluation is not a partial result. r30-p3-dyadic-sections-machine is exact but makes n section advances, so it neither achieves nor excludes n^alpha. Falsified by a finite check of the key lemma that passes on a prefix of d_n at some alpha.

nodes.title: Exact binary sections
nodes.statement: The three binary Mealy recursions A=(A,C), B=(A,C)swap, C=(B,C)swap give exact ordered sections of the powers of the right-edge map G and an executable shared-expression evaluator for the singleton query, built from n without a supplied orbit table.
nodes.scope: Its evaluation still makes n section advances, so it fails the conservative P3 target. An isometric affine conjugacy is impossible, and successive full sections along the actual seed cannot repeat before the centre query.
nodes.success: Closed as an exact construction: the three binary Mealy recursions give exact ordered sections of the powers of the right-edge map and an executable evaluator built from n with no supplied orbit table. It reopens if the evaluator disagrees with direct simulation at some n. It is not a P3 bound: its evaluation makes n section advances, a binary-prefix-compatible conjugacy to an odd affine map is impossible while nonisometric codings and nonaffine maps are untreated, and successive full sections along the actual seed cannot repeat before the centre query, so cycle detection on full sections cannot skip. A jump0 operation computing only the root toggle, bulk manipulation of unequal sections, or a coarser equivalence keeping only the needed output is not excluded and is the stated missing step.

nodes.title: Sufficient summary S_n
nodes.statement: Define a state S_n from which c_n is exactly decoded and which preserves every boundary dependency needed for its future use.
nodes.scope: Step 1 of the constructive route. The existing prescribed-trace frontier states have not been shown to give index-doubling summaries of the actual seed.
nodes.success: A state S_n from which c_n is exactly decoded, together with a proof that it preserves every boundary dependency its future use needs. A summary that decodes c_n but cannot feed the step-2 extension maps fails here. The existing prescribed-trace frontier states are not success by the node's own scope: they have not been shown to give index-doubling summaries of the actual seed.

nodes.title: Binary-index extension
nodes.statement: Exact maps from S_m to S_(2m) and to S_(2m+1), starting from a fixed base state, with correctness proved by induction on the bits of the requested index.
nodes.scope: Step 2 of the constructive route.
nodes.success: Exact maps S_m -> S_(2m) and S_m -> S_(2m+1) from a fixed base state, with correctness proved by induction on the bits of the requested index. Agreement with direct simulation to any finite N is evidence, not the induction, and a deliberately wrong base state is a useful control: if agreement survives it at every checked index, the check did not exercise the base state.

nodes.title: Construction bound
nodes.statement: Bound the cost of the extension maps, the size of their operands and the final decoding, including all preprocessing.
nodes.scope: Step 3 of the constructive route. Two independent half-size recursive calls, an exponentially large summary or uncharged precomputation can destroy the desired bound.
nodes.success: Explicit bounds, as functions of l = ell(n), for the step-2 maps: the operand size |S_m|, the cost of each map and the cost of the final decoding, in a form the step-4 recurrence can use; a per-extension cost C n^alpha (log n)^b with 0 < alpha < 1 on a one-branch recursion is enough, and a polylogarithmic cost per extension is the stronger case, and all preprocessing is charged: fixed finite tables are free, and any query-dependent table or unproved value read from a saved center archive must be charged, not assumed free. Proving the total is o(n) is p3_total_cost, not this node. A summary as large as the whole row, plain O(N^2) simulation, two half-size calls, or an exponentially large summary is not success. Falsified by an instrumented run at some finite m whose decoded output disagrees with direct simulation, or whose measured operand size, call count or bit-operation count exceeds the stated bound. Not met by r30-p3-dyadic-sections-machine, which makes n section advances, nor by r30-p3-decimation-window-conditional, whose cost formula assumes a decimation law refuted for R <= 8.

nodes.title: R1 zero-set obligation
nodes.statement: If the center column c is eventually periodic, then the column r next to it is eventually periodic on the zero-set {c_t = 0} (the c_t = 1 half is discharged by the pin). By the reduction in PATH.md section 2 this yields column -1 eventually periodic, contradicting the two-adjacent-columns theorem, and closes P1.
nodes.scope: Open. PATH.md ranks it as route R1, the best route, though RESULTS-four-convergent-statements.md section 2.1 proves it equivalent to P1: R1 localizes the obligation to rho but does not reduce it, and 'close R1 first, then P1 follows' is circular. PATH.md gives it the kill condition: exhibit a Rule 30 space-time diagram, or a consistent formal model of one, with c eventually periodic and r provably aperiodic on the zero-set. Many documents under experiments/rule30/r1-* attack it; none proves it.
nodes.sources_note: Definition: docs/rule30/REFERENCE/PATH.md section 4 (R1) and docs/rule30/REFERENCE/START-HERE.md (P1 row).
nodes.success: A proof that c eventually periodic forces r eventually periodic on {c_t = 0}, the c_t = 1 half discharged by the pin, so PATH.md section 2 yields column -1 eventually periodic. 73a5bb062873a7de and 23894e5200c348d9 prove this obligation equivalent to P1, so success here is success on P1 itself and no easier subgoal exists. r30-gap-proposition-a-lone-seed-zero-set says why from the inside: on the lone seed an eventually periodic c forces r on the zero-set NOT eventually periodic, so the implication can hold only with a false antecedent, and a proof of this node is a proof that the antecedent never occurs. r30-gap-pin-biconditional-eventually-periodic is the proved step both use. Nine of the attached records are the MSB-automatic toolkit, not the obligation, and several say in their own scope that nothing there concerns Rule 30; the remaining four refute neighbouring premises, NEPC, transitivity, literal PIN-Pi and the i.o. implication, and close no case. PATH.md's registered kill stands: a Rule 30 space-time diagram, or a consistent formal model of one, with c eventually periodic and r provably aperiodic on the zero-set; by Proposition A that is the same event as P1 failing.

nodes.title: Dyadic-lag correlation hypothesis
nodes.statement: For D = {2^a - 2^b : a > b >= 0} and the singleton centre trace, liminf_N D_N(h)/(N-h) >= 1/2 for every h in D; equivalently limsup_N C_N(h)/N <= 0. The weaker aggregate alternative asks only that limsup_N (1/N) sum_(0<=i<j<m) C_N(2^j - 2^i) <= 0 for an unbounded set of m.
nodes.scope: Sufficient for P2 and, separately, for P1, by r30-sdc-dyadic-hypothesis-suffices; explicitly unproved in either form and not claimed necessary for either prize. These are ordinary time shifts, not XOR shifts of binary time indices, and no uniform rate in h or m is required. The P1 direction is the sharper one: an eventually p-periodic trace forces C_N(h)/N -> 1 at the lag h in D divisible by p, so the hypothesis excludes every eventual period. No finite measurement settles either form.
nodes.success: A proof on the singleton seed that limsup_N C_N(h)/N <= 0 for every h in D, or the aggregate alternative for an unbounded set of m. Neither is established. Measurement is NOT success and cannot become success: the seed estimate at 2^23 resolves the per-lag ratio only to 1/(2 sqrt(N-h)), extending the trace buys resolution at rate sqrt(N) and never a limit, and the per-lag and aggregate tests are sensitive to opposite alternatives (r30-sdc-aggregate-alternative-power-asymmetry), so neither clean result strengthens the other. DO FIRST, before any new measurement here: the statistic has already been swept at every lag to 100,000 at T = 2^21 by experiments/overnight-arms/frontier_attack/a18_cryptanalysis, with stronger calibration than the dyadic run, and no record cited that arm until r30-sdc-dyadic-lag-seed-estimate-extends-a18-sweep; read it before claiming any measurement is new. What would count is an origin-specific cancellation argument using the singleton seed's own structure, since the hypothesis is false for general sequences: r30-sdc-powers-of-two-insufficient exhibits a periodic word balanced at every pure power-of-two lag and unbalanced at a difference lag, so no argument treating the trace as an arbitrary balanced word can work. Falsified by exhibiting one h in D with limsup C_N(h)/N > 0 on the seed.

nodes.title: Statistical distinguishers for the centre column
nodes.statement: Two facts that are easy to conflate. No finite-prefix statistical test can IMPLY aperiodicity, in either direction: for every finite T there are eventually periodic sequences agreeing with the column on [0,T), and a detected bias would not refute aperiodicity either. But a null autocorrelation sweep DOES exclude an explicit period band by an elementary counting argument, because an eventually periodic column can mismatch its own p-shift at most q times. So a cryptanalytic battery is a cost measurement on the distinguisher route AND, at the same time, a period-exclusion instrument; only the first half is what a null buys you for free.
nodes.scope: Proved here means the obstruction and the counting exclusion, both elementary, NOT the battery's verdict, which rests on a power control substituted after the fact and is INCONCLUSIVE by the letter of its own registered decision rule. Nothing here says the column is random or structureless; it says a standard battery at T <= 2^21 did not separate it from i.i.d., which is the expected outcome of a test that could have failed and did not.
nodes.success: The distinguisher half cannot be closed and that is the point; the exclusion half CAN be pushed, and pushing it is cheap. Extending the sweep to all T-1 lags at T = 2^23 would widen the excluded band directly, the cap of 100,000 being a choice and not a limit. It is a control that tells a later session the distinguisher route is shut in principle rather than merely unproductive in practice, so a proposal to 'try cryptanalysis on Rule 30' is not a new idea. The technique class has been run, pre-registered, at T <= 2^21, over 100,838 hypotheses, and found nothing; and by a61b9c6df7819df3 and r30-aut-theorem-o-finite-prefix-obstruction no amount of further depth could have made it bear on P1. DO FIRST if extending anything here: repair the lag1000 power control, which is provably null at its own lag, before trusting any future correlation or autocorrelation result from this arm. What WOULD be new is an attack that is not a finite-prefix statistic at all -- state recovery in the Meier-Staffelbach sense, which is a different claim the arm explicitly does not make and for which the arm's own source was never obtained.

edges.statement: Completes only K≤17; does not discharge the quantifier over every K.
The new certificates close 15 of 19 new exact-capacity-18 patterns; closing the four remaining seams would complete only K=18. General K would still need a uniform capacity argument.

Each original has finite Q_2. A finite bound on its repeats and the survival inequality force a finite lifetime. Originals failing before two updates are immediate. The bridge itself is now kernel-checked in full generality as `mortality_of_capacity_budget` in Rule30SurvivalBridge.lean (commit 82ac91b6): a repeat bound at every capacity K, together with the proved survival inequality, yields mortality, for every capacity function at once and so for Q_2. What remains open is the hypothesis that such a finite B(K) exists for Q_2 at every K; that is the capacity node's own open claim, not a gap in this edge's formalization.

The repeat inequality proves sufficiency; conversely finite mortality for the finitely many words at each r gives a finite maximum repeat count. Both directions are now kernel-checked as `budgetAt_iff_mortalAt` (each length r) and `budget_iff_mortality` (all r, unconditionally) in Rule30SurvivalBridge.lean (commit 82ac91b6), using the same proved survival inequality; neither direction ever involved the Q_2 automaton.
Alternating-trace reconstruction turns a period-two counterexample into a surviving legal finite Z frontier.
RW is equivalent to DLP, and the all-length DLP exclusion is sufficient for the endpoint-derived separator.
For n≥7 a DLP witness would force at least n+2 binary continuation symbols; the finite smaller cases retain their own guards.
The established rank-descent and first-infinite-shift reductions leave exactly the two endpoint-derived separator obligations.
Period two is only one rung. The remaining nonconstant periods and all onsets must also be excluded.
The exact ordered-energy comparison is equivalent to singleton density one-half; the decay itself is unproved.
This refuted generic inference supplies no fixed-sequence lower bound. Even a valid representation obstruction would need a separate algorithm-class bridge.
Period-two consequences should not be treated as discharged by computations until the reduction chain is formalized.

The remaining capacity-18 seams should be attacked by finite guarded joint closure certificates. For index 15, the current frontier is the depth-16 set with 673 survivors, completed from the depth-12 base under an 8,000,000-state route cap, not the depth-15 set with 545 nor the older depth-12 set. The record lifetime 46 in the layer 22/23 mass census puts a common-depth certificate for index 15 at depth 47 or more, so exact layer-by-layer lifting alone does not reach it.

The ledger asks RW/DLP for a finite separator automaton or closed transducer section whose states retain reachability, the hard-core junction and terminal 12a. None is built. The defect-cocycle erasures and the leading-defect absorption lemma are anchored source-prefix rules, not moves of a closed object, and a state retaining the full ordered suffix action has exponentially many classes on the measured range (3773 at n=22 on the period-two source language, 0 of N covered at n=9..13 by the proved exclusion families). Interior defects, three or more independently spaced defects and the full hard-core language are the remaining gap.
The established observer fixes which B/C fields and origins the scan equations must evaluate.
The exact coupled scans imply the interior pause and ordered chain criterion; no cost decrease is implied.
Applying supplied chain certificates to c_n still requires their actual history constructor.
These exact shortcuts apply only after their required input objects are constructed in the stated representation.
The constructor must distinguish the saved actual collision; forgetting falls is insufficient.
Correct control construction must additionally satisfy a proved total-work bound; neither obligation is discharged.
A correct uniform o(n) singleton query would refute the operational no-sublinear target. This is a conditional route, not a proved shortcut.

Kopra's width-two theorem rules out the constant-one word (catalog record b73d29804e858707); the zero-tail note classifies both constant fibres independently and credits Jen 1986 Thm 7a for the one case.

sources: docs/papers/Finite Configurations Cannot Generate a Constant Trace in Rule 30/zero-tail-note.tex

P1.4: "Period-two mortality is a partial theorem, not P1."
P1.4: "The distinct period-three cases 001 and 011 provide the next finite targets."
The proved local laws are inputs to, not a proof of, the open task: "Bound cumulative repeats by a finite function of the initial length | Open | Turn the local laws into mortality."

"(PT2) therefore follows from: on the zero-wall half-line, no finite seed has s(2k+1,-1) = 1 for all k; and with the two proved right-side constraints it suffices that no finite seed has that together with s(2k,-4) = 0 at all even times and never five consecutive even times with s(2k,-1) = 1."

(PSI) is the endpoint form of a horizon statement stronger than (PT2); it is proved here only for the family W=(12)^k, k>=2.

P2.4: iterating the recurrence to j*=l floor(k/(2l)) gives V_(k,j*)->0 uniformly and "The prefix bound then gives M_k/N->0 and proves P2." The recurrence itself is unproved for the seed. The arrow is strictly one-way and must not be read as an equivalence: ed8bae2f15256b6e proves that a balanced-run sign sequence with runs of length 2^floor(sqrt(k)) has density one-half while every fixed (l, eta>0, C) eventually fails P2-C at the admissible scale j = floor(sqrt(k)) - l. So a refutation of P2-C on the seed would leave P2 untouched.

RESULTS-four-convergent-statements.md section 2.1: "Therefore S1 <=> P1." S1 => P1: an eventual period of c maps through the proved pin biconditional (l eventually periodic iff rho, r sampled on {c_t = 0}, eventually periodic) to an eventual period of l, and c, l are then two adjacent eventually periodic columns of a nonzero finite seed, excluded by Kopra TCS 946 (2023) 113668 Thm 3.5; p = 1 needs no citation (PATH.md register rows 25/26). P1 => S1 vacuously, since P1 falsifies S1's antecedent. So closing R1 is closing P1, not a reduction to something weaker; section 8's 2026-09-09 correction withdraws neighbouring separations but keeps this equivalence. For p >= 2 it rests on the cited theorem, checked against the journal text (RESULTS-kopra-eventual-verification.md); r30-prs-left-finite-adjacent-period-obstruction re-derives the obstruction with no external theorem but was not checked line by line, so it does not yet replace the citation.

RESULTS-eventual-period.md: "Jen's Proposition 3 and Kopra's width-two theorem give a second exact target: derive an eventually periodic adjacent column from the periodic centre. That would supply a forbidden second periodic column."

The proved identity A(T)-T/2=P_T+sum_(t<T)(K_t-1/2) splits the density target into two terms; this is the term P_T. The identity itself bounds neither term, and the source lists each as a separate open obligation.

The proved identity A(T)-T/2=P_T+sum_(t<T)(K_t-1/2) splits the density target into two terms; this is the term sum_(t<T)(K_t-1/2). The identity itself bounds neither term, and the source lists each as a separate open obligation.

Dividing the exact Cauchy-Schwarz inequality by m^2 N^2 at fixed m, the finitely many cross terms have nonpositive limsup, giving limsup (S_N/N)^2 <= 1/m, and only afterwards is m let tend to infinity; the order of limits is essential. The aggregate alternative gives the same 1/m bound along its unbounded set of m.

For any period p two powers of two share a residue mod p, their positive difference h lies in D and is divisible by p, and an eventually p-periodic trace has C_N(h)/N -> 1. The hypothesis therefore excludes every eventual period. This direction needs only the per-lag form at the single lag h, not the full family.
A clean statistical null at any finite depth is consistent with P1 being true and with P1 being false, so this node constrains the prize in neither direction and exists to close the route.

controls.title: Full degree can coexist with two states
controls.statement: Sequential AND has degree n and two memory states. Use a distinguishable-continuation argument for a true state lower bound.

controls.title: Frontiers keep growing after synchronization
controls.statement: A unique endpoint after r steps has length 2r, then 2r+1 on its next success. A fixed square temporal matrix needs a separately proved quotient.

controls.title: Spatial mixing uses the opposite limit order
controls.statement: For each fixed tape depth n, p_r(α)→4^(−n) as original length r→∞. Mortality asks about growing depth at fixed r.

controls.title: A fitted matrix gap need not describe the real process
controls.statement: The fitted de Bruijn transition satisfies T_k^k=2^(−k)11ᵀ while its underlying process is periodic. Seed-specific measure and operator identification are essential.

controls.title: Supplied information has a construction cost
controls.statement: Fixed-width large-time powers, supplied grammar scans and last-rise observers are exact. Their input construction remains charged on the actual center query.

controls.title: Actual rise-only summary collision
controls.statement: Actual B inputs at times 0 and 4 share the two-digit (Z,rho) prefix and phase, yet their high endpoint after four fine time steps differs: rise-only causal closure fails. The full alternating pruning guard occurs only in the two classified small actual cases. Keep saved period/transient witnesses, nonaffinity, Cartier defects and Rule 90 fast controls. Arbitrary-input sensitivity, faithful representation dimension and finite-state profile size do not lower-bound the singleton query.

controls.title: Retracted alternating-fibre and period-two claims
controls.statement: Nine claims from the alternating-trace fibre report and one from the eventual-period report are retracted: alternating-fibre normal form, depth certificate completion, support count saturation, suffix parity invariant, zero-cost normal forms, Omega bilinear form, reachable-state mortality, DFA image characterization, sector reconstruction theorem, and the period-two obstruction for an unrestricted centre. No ladder edge may cite them; the proved zero-set reduction and bounded depth and support certificates in the same report stand.

controls.title: Fixed finite quotients of the frontier are large
controls.statement: Nerode classes of the frontier grow about 1.77x per symbol (DFA of at least 2,255 states), and any DFA for the ones-run language L_1(c) has at least 2^18 = 262,144 states, from explicit anti-periodic suffixes at levels 4 to 17. Non-regularity itself is open, and no uniform mechanism carries the separating family past a fixed level.

controls.title: Endpoint machinery is Rule 30 in a chart
controls.statement: The endpoint triangle is the pinned left half-plane in one affine chart, the constant cut at depth n is a finite time-zero row of width 2n+3 or 2n+4, and the endpoint run is the survival count of one finite forward seed (up to one scale and two steps). The separator target O_c intersect I(HC_omega) = empty is therefore period two read in that chart, and the endpoint machinery adds no structure to plain Rule 30.

controls.title: Bounded-degree F_2 certificates fail
controls.statement: Polynomial-calculus and Nullstellensatz refutation degree equals the free seed-bit count (w-2) at every width 4 to 14, and the axiom floor is full through width 27, so the refutation degree grows with width and no width-independent bounded-degree certificate is available on that range; the hard-core condition linearizes the pinned half-plane only to column -7.

controls.title: Trace-language entropy is open
controls.statement: The right-trace language R (11 and 00000 forbidden, 4,189 minimal forbidden factors through length 60, |R_60|=103,220) has entropy at most 0.124 bits per symbol by a Collatz-Wielandt bound (proved, finite type through length 60); whether h(R)=0 is open, exact counts cannot separate 0.04 bits from zero below length about 100, and the written attempts at zero entropy, non-soficity and masking entropy were each refuted by an adversarial second pass, leaving those claims unestablished. No mechanism for the defects, forbidden factors or entropy is on record.

controls.title: The right trace is not a favourable partner
controls.statement: Over the 2^16 width-16 right seeds the reconstructed row's longest zero run follows fair-coin extremes (maximum 26 at M=4096 against nulls 27 to 29), the trace is the period-5 word 00001 for 96.9 percent of positions, and the deep zero runs are single displaced symbols in that regime. Counting cannot supply a separator: the joint run sits within 2.3 of the independence null.

controls.title: Temporal means alone do not close
controls.statement: Period-14 rows X (integer 1614) and Y (integer 2067) share the complete Phi_4 one-count field yet Phi_4(F^4 X)_0=+1/2 against -1/2 for Y, so no deterministic evolution on temporal means alone exists, and no fixed-radius mean-only closure holds on finite support. Explicit periodic counterexamples, not lone-seed P2.

controls.title: No sublinear cutoff fits every balanced sequence
controls.statement: No predetermined sublinear dyadic schedule L_k=o(N_k) captures cancellation for every sign sequence satisfying P2, so any chosen cutoff schedule needs an additional seed-specific proof; a cutoff chosen after measuring the discrepancy verifies a representation, not the all-scale estimate.

controls.title: P3 scope: uniform machine, all work charged
controls.statement: The input is the canonical binary representation of n. One finite algorithm must return c_n for every n, and all n-dependent preprocessing, summary construction, arithmetic and memory access are charged. T_M(n)=o(n) iff W_M(m)=o(2^m) for W_M(m)=max over 2^(m-1)<=n<2^m of T_M(n). A lower bound for one chosen algorithm is weaker than one covering every correct uniform machine; the official prose and displayed predicate differ, and a submission must say which it proves.

controls.title: ANF degree does not transfer to the index function
controls.statement: The time-t centre output as a function of 2t+1 arbitrary initial cells has degree 2t-1 for t>=3, but the actual index function n -> c_n has only m variable bits and degree at most m. Neither degree nor decision-tree complexity of the arbitrary-input function lower-bounds evaluation on the one fixed seed, and no circuit, proof-system or boundary bridge covering all uniform algorithms is supplied.

controls.title: Newton doubling and schedules fail
controls.statement: A Newton round count does not automatically double the exact temporal prefix (two adjacent wrong cells in row m give a first wrong row m+1<2m), and four specified logarithmic initialized schedules return the wrong centre at (A,n,k)=(1,6,3),(2,21,10),(3,40,18),(4,50,24). Only those specified schedules are refuted.

controls.title: P3 implies P1
controls.statement: P3 in the no-sublinear sense implies P1: an eventually periodic sequence has a fixed finite prefix and cycle, allowing exact queries in O(log n) time by reducing the binary index modulo its period. Nonexistence of a finite-state digit predictor would also imply P1. Cross-problem relation, so it is recorded here rather than drawn.

controls.title: P2 alone does not imply P1
controls.statement: P2 alone does not imply P1: the sequence 010101... has density one-half and is periodic. Cross-problem relation.

controls.title: P1 and P2 together do not imply P3
controls.statement: P1 and P2 together do not imply P3: Thue-Morse is a nonperiodic balanced sequence with a logarithmic-time population-parity query. Cross-problem relation.

routes.title: Close the four remaining capacity-18 joint seams
routes.target: Mortality for the four unresolved exact-capacity-18 two-parameter families: indices 8, 15, 23, and 34. For index 15 the certificate shape is individual mortality through a uniform bound on D, not uniform mortality at a common finite depth. The proved repeat bound r+N+1 <= 2^(D+1)(r+2) turns a uniform D bound into a lifetime bound for every member, which is what the capacity-to-mortality edge needs, and the route's own success criterion already admits unbounded lifetimes as a negative closure. Indices 8, 23 and 34 keep uniform mortality as the target. All three are now measured by the guarded lift, index 8 to depth 18, index 23 to depth 19 and index 34 to depth 17, with growing |G_d| and s_n never 0 on any of them; index 23's s_14 = 0.6214 is above index 15's whole measured range. Neither measurement re-scopes them, since none reaches its certificate depth of 34, 32 and 29. Reverse this field alone if a census finds a kept fraction materially below one half at a guard-line or point layer, or s_n falling toward 0: either puts a common depth back in play.
routes.unlocks: Completes the capacity-18 rung. It still remains a partial capacity ladder; a formal capacity-to-mortality-to-period-two reduction is tracked separately.
routes.known: The cap-18 language audit closes the labeled product at 126 states and 504 edges. Of 19 new exact-capacity-18 patterns, 12 simpler families and 3 two-parameter joint seams have uniform mortality certificates. Exact seam-intertwining explains the three completed joint families by reducing their full column action to a+b. The requested 1213 seam has exact guarded survivor layers through depth 15. A window-quotient test on the depth-13-to-15 index-15 lift found no fixed-width chronological key: k_min is n-1 at every layer, so the width-6 proposal fails. Cycle monodromy and the guard mask jointly leave 8-20 of 27-32 classes mixed at every layer, so the outcome does not factor through either. Direct evaluation of explicit members (RESULTS-cap18-open-seam-lifetimes.md) finds every open seam outliving every closed capacity-18 pattern: N=35, D=22 for index 8 at (753,12291); N=33 for index 15 at (1534,15247338); N=33 for index 23 at (533,2533308); N=30 for index 34 at (20,8964344), against N<=25, D<=14 on the closed patterns and N<=24 at capacity 17; every cited witness has two-step fiber exactly 18 by a direct count. A pre-registered census of all 2^27 index-15 pairs a<2^11, b<2^16 finds the count surviving n guards roughly halving per step through n=27. The exact guarded-lift offspring mean falls 1.73, 1.63, 1.55 at depths 13-15, so these data do not decide whether any survivor tree dies. A pre-registered test of the simplest inductive invariant, that a survivor with all four sheets reachable always has a child with all four, fails in both measurable generations (17 of 73 and 54 of 122 parents, above the independence floors 13.8 and 34.6), and a proved lift lemma shows that the children of an order-4 cycle always have identity or central monodromy, so order-4 reproduction never acts at two consecutive depths (RESULTS-guarded-two-block-lift.md section 7). routes.known: Right-permutivity forces the continuation. A DLP witness would require at least n+2 binary symbols. High-bit elimination leaves a one-bit defect condition. The algebraic normal form of the defect has degree exactly n at every checked n from 4 to 15, ruling out a bounded-arity polynomial seam law (a bounded-state sequential mechanism is not thereby ruled out; AND has full degree and two states). The two-time high observer is a last-rise/range-parity query with distinct B and C origin terms. A single interior middle rise pauses the high bit; complete predecessor histories certify chains through the reachable pair language {00,12,22}. Exact supplied-repeat grammar transduction and finite-width core powering are available with their construction costs charged. The additive two-time high-bit guard chain was measured directly on the real B- and C-orbits (site up to 2198, depth up to 2200): it plateaus around 17 for both generators, about 1.8x an i.i.d. random-column control (also measured), so it is genuine but bounded, not growing with depth over the tested range. The unconditional low-bit nonzero-count identity (rise-chain-transparency equation 4) was verified exactly (zero mismatches, 89,400 cases) but does not telescope across two sites (mixed at every tested site); algebraic inspection shows the coupling is inherently two-dimensional in site and time. B^N(0) is spatially eventually periodic (period 16, an information-front effect of constant-zero input), but the onset site scales linearly with N at ratio 1.5-1.65, always beyond the query site (ratio about 1), so this periodic tail structurally cannot reach the singleton query at any tested depth. Two further dangling implicit-boundary threads were closed this session: rho's rises are dense on the measured prefixes (density 0.15 to 0.25, maximum gaps 8, 10, 10, 13 through h=1000), so a sparse index over them is no shortcut, which is no lower bound on the last-rise/range-parity query: most of those prefixes are the periodic tail of B^N(0), where the same density coexists with an O(1) last-rise query, and constructing the query's inputs in o(h) stays the open obligation of p3_control_construction, and the Cartier accumulated-correction's natural homogeneous-propagation scheme is refuted by a real witness (two actual zero-orbit columns with identical annotations diverge one column later). A third thread was measured and gives no bound: the self-referential LZ77 factor count of the first n base-four digits of B^n(0) is 29, 52, 85, 145 and 253 at n = 64 to 1024, within 6% of one i.i.d. random draw at each length and inside the range of 20 draws, against 5 for a periodic control, with z/n falling from 0.453 to 0.247. LZ77 finds no more repetition in these words than in a random word, and a plain straight-line grammar producing the n = 1024 word needs at least 253 rules. No sublinearity statement follows: every length-n word over a fixed alphabet has a grammar of O(n/log n) rules, which is o(n), the five measured words are not prefixes of one another, and the quaternary evaluator's grammar is over the A/B/C generator word, not this digit word. The Phi/K-automaton route is not ruled out by this measurement.

previous.known: Both center parities have an exact B-power digit correspondence. A dyadic step retains two coupled fields. Direct and Gray bitplanes admit two conditionally affine scans. The two-time high observer is a last-rise/range-parity query with distinct B and C origin terms. A single interior middle rise pauses the high bit; complete predecessor histories certify chains through the reachable pair language {00,12,22}. Exact supplied-repeat grammar transduction and finite-width core powering are available with their construction costs charged. The additive two-time high-bit guard chain was measured directly on the real B- and C-orbits (site up to 2198, depth up to 2200): it plateaus around 17 for both generators, about 1.8x an i.i.d. random-column control (also measured), so it is genuine but bounded, not growing with depth over the tested range. The unconditional low-bit nonzero-count identity (rise-chain-transparency equation 4) was verified exactly (zero mismatches, 89,400 cases) but does not telescope across two sites (mixed at every tested site); algebraic inspection shows the coupling is inherently two-dimensional in site and time. B^N(0) is spatially eventually periodic (period 16, an information-front effect of constant-zero input), but the onset site scales linearly with N at ratio 1.5-1.65, always beyond the query site (ratio about 1), so this periodic tail structurally cannot reach the singleton query at any tested depth. Two further dangling implicit-boundary threads were closed this session: the two-time last-rise/range-parity query cannot be made sublinear because rho's rise density is Theta(h) with bounded gaps (measured 0.21-0.25 density, single-digit max gap through h=1000), and the Cartier accumulated-correction's natural homogeneous-propagation scheme is refuted by a real witness (two actual zero-orbit columns with identical annotations diverge one column later). Seven local mechanisms are now closed with no sublinear constructor found; remaining leads require either a structurally different representation of the itinerary map itself (Phi conjugacy / K-automaton, untested for sublinearity) or attacking the unrestricted lower bound directly. A third dangling thread was closed this session: the itinerary map A itself (not just its rise mask) cannot be represented by any SLP/grammar-based evaluator sublinearly, since its LZ77 factor count z(n)/n tracks an i.i.d. random control within 5% at every scale tested (n=64..1024), unlike the flat periodic control. This rules out the Phi/K-automaton quaternary evaluator and its repeat-transduction extension as a route to sublinearity, for any grammar construction, not just the ones already tried.

reference_review.method: Each unresolved depends_on reference was read against its source document by an agent and given a verdict. A resolution requires a text-level tie in the document and a target statement that is mathematically the one used; wording similarity alone is not accepted. assumptions.ref: c exactly p-periodic from time T
assumptions.st: The centre column c_t = s(t,0) is exactly p-periodic from time T onward, i.e. c_{t+p} = c_t for all t >= T (the 'periodicity hypothesis' under which the spark's gate is analysed).
assumptions.note: This is the antecedent hypothesis of a conditional (a hypothesis for the analysis, whose truth is the open R1 question), not a hidden gap in a proof.

assumptions.st: d_t(0) = d_{t+1}(0) = 0 for the defect d_t(x) = s(t+p,x) XOR s(t,x), i.e. the centre satisfies c_{t+p} = c_t and c_{t+1+p} = c_{t+1} (a direct consequence of exact p-periodicity of the centre).
assumptions.note: It is the local form of the same centre-periodicity hypothesis, assumed as the premise of the defect equation rather than derived from anything.

assumptions.st: The reconstruction sample (source) sequence of an immortal zero-cost continuation has period p after index n_0, i.e. it is ultimately periodic; the bound 4(n_0+p)(K+1)-1 is derived under this hypothesis.
assumptions.note: It is the hypothesis of the conditional bound (the aperiodic-tail case is stated as remaining open); the proof is sketched inline and attributed to experiments/rule30/panel/runs/p1.4.md.

assumptions.ref: eventual periodicity reductio hypothesis (for the proof's own conditional form)
assumptions.st: c_t = c_{t+p} for all t >= T0 (the centre column of the lone seed is eventually p-periodic), assumed for contradiction, with no claim that it holds.
assumptions.note: Explicit hypothesis-for-contradiction serving as the antecedent of the record's own conditional statement, so unproved by design (it is the open P1 target being refuted), not a hidden gap; a strict reading could also file it as not_a_dependency.

assumptions.st: Two Rule 30 orbits a and a' agree at the center column at times t and t+1, i.e. D_t(0)=D_{t+1}(0)=0 where D=a XOR a'. 'this is the regime any "forbids periodicity" argument needs to hold *forever*, not just at one instant.'
assumptions.note: The identities are proved exhaustively only under this case restriction, which is the antecedent (no disagreement yet at center); the document proves no way this can hold forever, but it is the hypothesis of the lemma, not a gap in it.

assumptions.st: There is a finite function B(r), depending only on the initial frontier length r, such that every successful scalar tape (and every successful prefix) from every legal initial Z-frontier of length r has D<=B(r), D being the number of equal adjacent scalars. Doc: "This is a conditional corollary, not a new repeat upper bound."
assumptions.note: The finite-B(r) bound is an explicitly hypothetical premise of a conditional corollary; the only stated instance, B(r)=r-1 (e5a09dbf8873a358), is itself an unproved conjecture.

assumptions.ref: unproved independence approximation for the Psi constraints
assumptions.st: The n+1 constancy constraints on Psi_n(W) (Psi has n+2 coordinates, Psi_0 free) behave as independent fair-coin events over the 2^n binary sources W, so the expected number of constant-Psi sources at length n is 2^n * 2^-(n+1) = 1/2, constant in n.
assumptions.note: It is a null model, never proved; the prereg file later reports it refuted by measured R_k up to 18 at n=15, while PSI-ANCESTRY-LAW section 9 still cites a ratio of 1.00+/-0.05 to the null as showing no suppression mechanism.

taxonomy.name: Argument survives Rule 90 substitution
taxonomy.definition: A proof step uses only properties shared by a class C of rules (left-permutivity, finite propagation speed, linearity of the influence matrix) that contains Rule 90, whose lone-seed centre column is provably periodic or density-degenerate. Then the argument proves the same conclusion for Rule 90, where it is false, so it cannot use Rule 30 specifically.
taxonomy.mechanism: Rule 90 is F_2-linear and left-permutive, so it satisfies every structural lemma Rule 30 does while having a closed-form periodic centre column; any invariant computed from those lemmas alone is blind to the OR nonlinearity that separates the rules.
taxonomy.test: Substitute Rule 90 (or another left-permutive rule) for Rule 30 in the document's key lemma. If the proof text still goes through, or the document itself reports the quantity is the same for Rule 90, the pattern holds.
taxonomy.evades_or_limits: Use an ingredient Rule 90 lacks: the OR term c=b+c+bc, the pin/pass identity, the non-autonomy of the defect D, or an identity with a seed-specific parameter. Note Rule 90 is a vacuous control for some objects (Topal), so the filter must be chosen per object.

uniform.title: Uniform to infinity
uniform.question: Which patterns, measures, averages and signals about Rule 30 hold for ALL n, and which only over the range someone measured?
uniform.why: finite-data-not-uniform is this repo's dominant failure mode and nothing rendered it. Of 2041 records, 23 carry uniform_computational_proof or machine_checked_certificate and are not refuted, against 700 exhaustive, 168 numerical and 115 SAT. A band that lists what is proved uniform is only safe beside a band that lists what merely looks it.
uniform.gate: A record enters band A only with a positive unbounded universal quantifier in its statement AND no integer cap on that variable in either statement or scope. Bands are NOT a partition: an exact identity keyed off Thue-Morse is legitimately in B and C at once. Membership is a claim about the quantifier in a record's statement, not about how much the result matters: A3 is a band of guardrails nothing builds on, and a band-E measurement can be the more useful result.
uniform.curated_by: Catalog sweep of all 2041 records, 2026-09-21; band membership hand-checked, per-entry prose pulled live from each record rather than paraphrased

bands.title: Proved uniform to infinity
bands.blurb: Holds for all n, all T, all rows, or all seeds, with a proof or a uniform computational proof. An exhaustive check over a finite range is NOT here no matter how large the range. These are the facts a prize argument may build on.
