entries.t: Odd weight of the wedge-restricted center function for every t
entries.st: Let v_k = y_(t+1-2k) be the t free wedge cells and h_t(v) = s(t,0) restricted to the wedge variety, so that M(t) = weight(h_t) = #{w on cells -t+1..t : s(t,0) = 1 and s(u,t-u) = 0 for u = 0..t-1}. Then M(t) is ODD for every t >= 1. Proof: pointwise self-similarity gives the recursion h_t(v) = (v_t OR h_(t-1)(v')) XOR h_(t-1)(w_1,...,w_(t-1)) with w_k = v_(k+1) XOR (h_k(v_1..v_k) OR v_k); summing over v in {0,1}^t, the first term contributes M(t-1) + 2^(t-1) = M(t-1) mod 2 and the second is even because the w-map is exactly 2-to-1, so M(t) = M(t-1) mod 2 with M(1) = M(2) = 1. This is claim C1, and since the ANF induction gives coeff(M_(t+1)) = N(t) mod 2 = M(t) mod 2, it closes deg f_t = 2t-1 with unique top monomial M_t for every t >= 3.
entries.sc: A parity statement only; no closed form for M(t) itself is obtained or claimed. The proof is an argument produced by one of three independent prover agents, which passed its adversarial verifier (re-derived with its own code and indexing, tested at t = 7, 8, 9, one cosmetic notation issue in S4) and was re-checked here by a third independent implementation pointwise for t = 2..11. It is not machine-checked or peer-reviewed. A second prover reported a different route (an involution on the one free cell appearing in no wedge condition) which is corroborating but not relied on.
entries.note: Wedge-restricted centre weight M(t) is odd. Parity only; no closed form for M(t).

entries.t: Period-1 (eventually constant) lone-seed center column is impossible
entries.st: The lone seed's center column c cannot be eventually constant 1: the all-one trace would force the left column L_k=1 for every positive even k, which is an infinite left support, contradicting that the diagram has a finite (nonzero) seed. This closes the p=1 case of the S1/P1 equivalence independently of the Kopra citation.
entries.sc: covers only the eventually-constant (p=1) case; independently corroborated by Jen 1986 Thm 7a
entries.note: Period 1 excluded: the lone-seed centre cannot be eventually constant.

entries.t: Elementary left-finite obstruction to two adjacent columns periodic from a common onset
entries.st: If two adjacent columns of a nonzero left-finite Rule 30 diagram are eventually P-periodic from a common onset, the inverse Rule 30 equation propagates that same period and onset to every column to their left; but the leftmost one advances one site left per step, so at a sufficiently late time T its position at time T+P holds a zero at T and a one at T+P, contradicting the propagated periodicity.
entries.sc: A self-contained re-derivation of the obstruction, invoking no external theorem. The common-onset hypothesis costs nothing against the published statement: two adjacent eventually periodic columns are both P-periodic from a common onset, for P the lcm of their periods and the later of their two onsets. The hypothesis needs a leftmost one, so spatially periodic tori are outside it, which is why the two torus witnesses of the same document are not a contradiction. It proves no case of P1. Read 2026-09-16.
entries.quantifier: uniform in seed width and period
entries.note: Two adjacent eventually-periodic columns propagate the period leftward forever, against the one-site-per-step left edge.

entries.t: At most one eventually periodic column of the driven half-plane (Theorem 2)
entries.st: For every finite y and any c with (ND) (LHP_y(c) not identically zero), there are no x_1 < x_2 <= 0 such that columns x_1 and x_2 are both eventually periodic. In particular, if c is eventually periodic, no column x<=-1 is eventually periodic.
entries.sc: driven half-plane; labelled as Jen 1986 Theorem 2b / Jen 1990 Proposition 3 transferred to the driven half-plane, not a new discovery

entries.t: A finite right seed with an eventually periodic trace has no finite left partner keeping the pin
entries.st: If rho(y) is eventually periodic then no finite left row keeps the period-two pin against y. Sketch as written: if (W,0,y) kept the pin forever, W is nonzero, column -1 is l_t with l_(2k) = 1 - rho_k and l_odd = 1, so l has the even period P = 2p from t_0 = 2k_0; by left permutivity every left column is P-periodic for t >= t_0; but Rule 30 moves the left edge of the finite W one cell per step, so a far column takes value 0 at time m - w_L - P and 1 at time m - w_L, congruent mod P, a contradiction.
entries.sc: Uniform in the width of y and in the seed; this is the Jen 1990 / Kopra argument for two adjacent eventually periodic columns applied to the pin and its forced neighbour. It excludes (PT2) only for seeds whose trace settles; a counterexample needs a right seed whose trace never settles, and the source reports no sign that every trace settles.

entries.t: Periodic-enclosure lemma
entries.st: In a binary radius-one cellular automaton, if columns a<b are both eventually periodic with common period L after time T, then every intervening column is eventually periodic with period L*d for some 1<=d<=2^m (m=b-a-1), after at most L*(2^m-1) further steps.
entries.sc: elementary finite-state result, rule-generic; requires the two boundary columns to be actual eventually periodic columns, not derived from a bounded window of centre history

entries.t: Strong connectivity and aperiodicity of T_n at every depth
entries.st: T_n is strongly connected for every n>=1 and is aperiodic because the all-zero vertex has a self-loop on input symbol zero; proved by showing every real-valued function constant on directed edges must be constant, via inductive elimination of coordinates A_0,...,A_(j-1),B_1,...,B_j using paired inverse moves, then converting weak connectivity plus degree balance into strong connectivity.
entries.sc: Holds for arbitrary n, without any finite-depth extrapolation.
entries.note: Scope is explicit: holds for arbitrary n with no finite-depth extrapolation.

entries.t: All-depth theorem: limiting density and explicit finite-r bound per tape
entries.st: For every fixed length-n tape alpha, lim_{r->infinity} p_r(alpha) = 4^-n, uniformly over tapes at that depth; explicitly, for every r>=R_n=1+L_n*4^L_n, 2/(2*4^n+1) <= p_r(alpha) <= 3/(2*4^n+1), proved via strong connectivity/mixing of T_n and an explicit spectral-gap-style cutoff.
entries.sc: R_n is a deliberately crude, enormous cutoff; no inference that the true cutoff grows linearly is made.
entries.quantifier: limit over r, uniform over tapes at that depth
entries.note: Quote the limit only; the companion finite-r bound uses a deliberately crude cutoff.

entries.t: Full-projection theorem: bounded-arity supports are unconstrained
entries.st: Fix n>=1 and k>=0. For every length-n tape alpha and every original length r>=1+(k+1)L_n, the projection of C_r(alpha) onto any set J of at most k free original bits is all of {0,1}^J, proved by finding an untouched run of L_n sites and applying the gap-completion theorem to fill it.
entries.sc: Proves full support of the projections, not uniform marginal probabilities or statistical independence; original length and tape are fixed throughout.
entries.quantifier: every tape of length n and every original length r >= 1+(k+1)L_n

entries.t: Spatial-limit theorem for the mean forced-bit statistic
entries.st: For every n and every pair state s, lim_{r->infinity} Q_(r-1)(s)/G_(r-1)(s) = mu_n, an exact dyadic rational independent of the full-support cutoff K used to define it
entries.sc: gives the limiting mean as original length grows at fixed n; does not establish the required lower bound in temporal depth
entries.quantifier: every n and every pair state; limit independent of the cutoff

entries.t: All-one trace fiber theorem
entries.st: The all-one trace forces the checkerboard left half L_k=1 iff k is a positive even integer, which is infinite, so no finite row has a constant-one trace; combined with the zero-tail theorem this excludes every eventually constant lone-seed centre.
entries.sc: reproved in one line from the OR-latch pin; Jen 1986 Theorem 7a already excludes the eventually-one case for every finite Rule 30 configuration -- the novel content here is the explicit fiber, sharp horizon, and extremizer count

entries.t: Aperiodicity of hard-core endpoints with finite Peel rank
entries.st: Every hard-core endpoint whose inverse cut has finite Peel rank is aperiodic, derived from the rotated Peel identity's linear drift together with the rank-zero last-support argument; the remaining open collision target is the aperiodic-endpoint case.
entries.sc: Leaves the aperiodic-endpoint case (endpoints whose inverse cut has infinite Peel rank) as the remaining open target for the period-two collision.

entries.t: Weaver preimage count P(t) = 2 closed form
entries.st: Under Reading B of the preimage-count construction (fix the true seed and entire right half at time 0, vary only the left-window bits b_{-1..-t}, forward-evolve, and count candidates reproducing the true center-column prefix a_0..a_{t-1}), the count P(t) is exactly 2 for every t>=1, for every left-permutive rule (Rule 30 and Rule 90 alike), independent of whether the target trace is periodic.
entries.sc: holds for every left-permutive rule and every t>=1; does not distinguish the periodic (Rule 90) from the conjecturally-aperiodic (Rule 30) case, so it does not bear on P1, P2, or P3
entries.note: Exactly 2 preimages. Uniform but non-separating: see band D.

entries.t: Phi_T injectivity on common-right-tail configurations
entries.st: For every T>=1, Phi_T is injective on any set of configurations having a common right tail: if two configurations have rightmost discrepancy at d, left permutivity puts their rightmost discrepancy at time t at d+t, so their T-term integer sums at coordinate d+T-1 differ by exactly one and their mean fields cannot agree everywhere.
entries.sc: left-permutive rules including Rules 30 and 90; not a density statement

entries.t: 11-state image-count transition matrix T
entries.st: Let T be the integer transition-count matrix of the exact 11-state one-step image DFA, e its start row and v its accepting column. The number of images of length-q seeds is a(q)=e*T^(q+1)*v.
entries.sc: image-count of the one-step image DFA only
entries.note: Image count from the exact 11-state DFA; with 498f90ae8a2f2305 it satisfies a linear recurrence.

groups.title: Uniform in one variable, capped in another
groups.blurb: The catalog's strongest uniform_computational_proof results. Each is genuinely all-length in one index and class-bounded in the other. Keeping that distinction visible is the point of this band.

entries.t: Uniform capacity-17 mortality theorem: N<=24 and D<=14, both sharp
entries.st: For every original length r and every legal auxiliary frontier w surviving its first two guards, Q_2(w)<=17 implies mortality with at most 24 successful updates and at most 14 adjacent equal-scalar repeats. Both bounds are attained already at Q_2=6.
entries.sc: Uniform over unbounded original length in the specified capacity class. No conclusion for capacity>=18 or unrestricted mortality.
entries.note: Scope: no conclusion for capacity >= 18.

entries.t: Complete all-length two-step capacity-17 endpoint language
entries.st: The complete guarded two-step original fibers with Q_2<=17 have exactly the 13 labeled second-bulk patterns in the capacity-17 report. Only capacities 1,2,6,12 occur. A closed 74-state, 296-edge product proves equality of the counted automaton and pattern NFA at every original length.
entries.sc: All legal auxiliary originals and all original lengths, retaining both initial scalars and guards; language theorem, not mortality by itself.

entries.t: Sharp uniform mortality of the six-ancestor periodic family
entries.st: For every k>=0, originals with initial scalars 00 and full second endpoint 21213(13)^k03 have N<=24 and D<=14. The complete spatial period at further depth 23 is 1048576 and no guarded residue survives; both bounds occur at k=816932.
entries.sc: All k in this one endpoint family. Auxiliary originals; no singleton reachability asserted.

entries.t: Seam-intertwining identities reduce three capacity-18 joint families to a+b
entries.st: For the three completed capacity-18 two-parameter seams, exact column-seam intertwining shows that the full guarded history agrees with the member whose parameters are (a+b,0). The proof closes a vertical Mealy product with ordered output on every input column in the required high-bit slice; the analogous global identity for the 1213 seam fails already at depth one.
entries.sc: Explains indices 5, 12, and 27 only. It is not a proof for the requested 1213 seam and is not inferred from finite orbit sizes.
entries.quantifier: every input column in the required high-bit slice

entries.t: All-length RW exclusion for homogeneous sources
entries.st: Both constant tails are excluded for every homogeneous source W=1^n and W=2^n, for every n>=1.
entries.sc: Homogeneous sources only. Strictly narrower than RW: it fixes no mixed source and supplies no descent.

entries.t: Exact guard-preserving prefix rewrite 122 to 222
entries.st: F^3(122v) = F^3(222v) for every suffix v. The rewrite preserves the entire cut and stays inside the source language.
entries.sc: Leftmost 1 at depth one. Proved for every suffix with the complete ordered action retained.

entries.t: Exact guard-preserving prefix rewrite 2122 to 2222
entries.st: F^3(2122v) = F^3(2222v) for every suffix v, preserving the entire cut and staying inside the source language.
entries.sc: Leftmost 1 at depth two. Same fixed step count F^3 as the depth-one rule.

entries.t: Two mixed source families excluded by reduction to 2^n
entries.st: Both constant tails are excluded for W=12^(n-1) with n>=3 and for W=212^(n-2) with n>=4, by the two exact rewrites reducing each to the homogeneous case.
entries.sc: Two one-parameter families. Four covered families in total against 2^n binary sources of length n, so coverage per length is linear against exponential.

entries.t: Exact RW source defect correction for 22122 versus 22222
entries.st: For every finite suffix v, F^3(22122v)=02R_2^3(v) and F^3(22222v)=22R_2^3(v); at F^4 the outputs are 1R_2^4(v) and 2R_2^4(v), and at F^5 they are R_1R_2^4(v) and R_2^5(v). The defect is exactly one leading endpoint symbol with the ordered suffix action retained.
entries.sc: All finite four-state suffixes v in the endpoint morphism coordinates. This is a correction formula, not an immediate erasure and not a proof of RW or period-two exclusion.

entries.t: Guard-preserving RW prefix erasure with sharp pure-2 padding
entries.st: For every k>=0 and finite suffix v, F^(4k+3)(2^k1 2^(3k+2)v)=F^(4k+3)(2^(4k+3)v). The sharper cutoff has minimum padding f(0)=f(1)=0, f(2)=f(3)=2, and f(k)=3k-8 for k>=4; in particular F^7(2212222v)=F^7(2222222v) and F^8(22212222v)=F^8(22222222v).
entries.sc: The displayed block must begin W and lie wholly inside W. The replacement preserves RW binary source, hard-core suffix junction and terminal guard, but can introduce 22222 and does not preserve a stronger source restriction or actual endpoint ancestry.
entries.quantifier: every k >= 0 and every finite suffix v

entries.t: Invariant three-prefix union for the 0001-driven right half-line
entries.st: For Rule 30 on sites i>=1 with prescribed boundary c=(0001)^infinity and no rule equation at site zero, the union of the four-cell prefix cylinders A=0010, B=0011 and C=0111 is mapped into itself by the four-step driven map for every infinite continuation, the zero-initial trajectory entering it at time eight. Writing r_t=s(t,1) and e_k=1 exactly when the prefix at time 4k is C, (r_(4k),r_(4k+1),r_(4k+2),r_(4k+3))=(0,e_k,1,1) for k>=2, and e_k*e_(k+1)=0 since C cannot follow C.
entries.sc: Two of the three centre-zero phases are fixed and only phase 4k+1 is unresolved. This is not an autonomous three-state evolution and e is not an autonomous binary evolution: the transitions still read cells five and six, and treating those as independently selectable would describe a larger system than the zero-initial orbit. No eventual lock, no periodicity of e and no mismatch upper bound follows. The drive has c_0=0, so it is not the actual singleton centre; the three-step phase rotation to boundary (1000)^infinity with zero initial right row fails the left pin at its first test, l_0=0 against the required 1. The source is dated 2026-09-15, was read 2026-09-16, and is uncommitted in the working tree along with its checker and artifact.
entries.quantifier: every infinite continuation, under the (0001)^inf drive

entries.t: A leading defect immediately before another defect is absorbable at gap>=2
entries.st: For every k>=2 and every finite four-state suffix v, F^(k+2)(1 2^k 1 v) = F^(k+2)(2^(k+1) 1 v): a leading defect followed by k twos then another defect is exactly interchangeable with a plain 2, with no trailing padding required. Proved for every k>=2, not just a tested range: the pure-2 background is a fixed point of the morph (BOUNDARY[2]=1, PHI[2][1]=2, PHI[1][2]=1 form a 2-cycle, giving morph(2^n)=2^(n-1) for every n), and inverse_terminal/peel/terminal are each local enough that morph(2^k 1) and morph(2^(k+1)) agree at position 0 for every k>=2. The boundary cases k=0 (adjacent defects) and k=1 need padding 5 and 1 respectively, both sharp, verified as finite exact certificates.
entries.sc: Resolves one narrow interrupted-run case with a genuine all-length proof for k>=2: two defects with gap>=2. Says nothing about three or more independently-spaced defects, the full RW/DLP hard-core source language, or a formal reduction to DLP/RW/SEP.
entries.quantifier: every k >= 2 and every finite four-state suffix
entries.note: The catalog's only proof_plus_finite_boundary_check, yet its evidence kind reads reported_finite_check. See overclaims.

entries.t: Density one-half, the shell maximum, the flexible energy and the ordered energy are kernel-checked equivalent for every Boolean sequence
entries.st: Rule30P2Bridge.lean proves in core Lean 4.33.1, for every c : Nat -> Bool and so for the Rule 30 singleton centre column: A(T) - T/2 = o(T) iff M_k = o(N) (densityHalf_iff_shellMaxLittleO); M_k = o(N) iff F_k -> 0 with F_k = min_j (V_(k,j) + 4^(j-k)) (shellMaxLittleO_iff_flexibleEnergyToZero); and H_k = o(N^2), max_j E_(k,j) = o(N^2) and M_k = o(N) are equivalent (shellMaxLittleO_iff_orderedEnergyLittleO, orderedEnergyLittleO_iff_maxBlockEnergyLittleO). Control, also kernel-checked: the sequence that is +1 on the first half of every dyadic shell and -1 on the second has S(2^k) = 2 and E_(k,k) = 0 and fails density one-half, so neither the dyadic endpoints alone nor the flexible energy without its 4^(j-k) penalty carries the bridge (dyadicEndpoints_bridge_fails, unpenalizedEnergy_bridge_fails). Replayed from the repository root at lean exit 0, no sorry, every result on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only.
entries.sc: An equivalence of targets, true of every Boolean sequence and using nothing about Rule 30. It bounds none of M_k, F_k, H_k on the centre column and P2 is exactly as open as before. The little-o statements are over Nat and Int with denominators cleared; their faithfulness to the documents' real-valued forms is a reading of lines 34 to 129 of the file, not something the kernel checks. fixed_window -> p2 and matching -> p2 are not covered, and the merge recurrence of Rule30ResearchReduction.lean is not connected to these definitions. This is one of the six bridges node formal_reductions names.
entries.quantifier: every c : Nat -> Bool, kernel-checked, sorry-free
entries.note: An implication whose hypothesis is an open node: proves no bound.

entries.t: The survival inequality, budget <-> mortality and capacity -> mortality are kernel-checked for every legal Z-frontier
entries.st: Rule30SurvivalBridge.lean proves in core Lean 4.33.1, with no finite computation assumed: the reconstruction thresholds (reconstruction); an alternating scalar run from a legal frontier of length a has length at most a+3, at most a+1 when the terminal high bit is one (runBound), the period-28 table being evaluated in the kernel by decide; r+N+1 <= 2^(D+1)(r+2) on every successful prefix (survival); a repeat budget at length r holds iff every legal frontier of length r dies, at each r and for all r (budgetAt_iff_mortalAt, budget_iff_mortality), with the explicit horizon N <= 2^(B+1)(r+2)-r-1 (horizon_of_budget); and a repeat bound at every capacity gives mortality for every capacity function Q at once (mortality_of_capacity_budget). Control, kernel-checked: the counting inequality is false for tapes in general (survival_counting_fails_without_runBound). Replayed from the repository root at lean exit 0, no sorry, standard axioms only.
entries.sc: Proves no budget, no capacity bound and no mortality: both bridges are implications whose hypotheses are the open nodes. The frontier, Z and the chronological guards are lines 40 to 146 of the file; Z and run were compared with aperiodic_mortality_audit.step on all 682 legal frontiers of length at most 5 before any proof, and that comparison is outside the kernel. The capacity bridge is stated for an arbitrary function Q, so it does not define Q_2 and says nothing about whether capped_edge computes it. Three data controls did not fail through length 6 to 8 (a_0 = 0 starts, an unguarded scan, an XOR variant), so the run bound is not sharp there.
entries.quantifier: at each r and for all r, no finite computation assumed

entries.t: Mortality of the Z-frontier implies period-two exclusion, kernel-checked through an explicit diagram-to-frontier dictionary
entries.st: Rule30AlternatingTraceBridge.lean proves in core Lean 4.33.1: a Rule 30 row with a leftmost one whose centre trace has c_(t+2) = c_t and c_1 != c_0 yields a legal finite frontier that passes every chronological guard (immortalFromAlternating), hence if every legal finite frontier eventually fails a guard then no nonzero finite row has a nonconstant period-two centre trace (periodTwoExcluded_of_mortality'). The frontier after n updates is a_k(n) = x(q+1+n+k, -(p+n-k)), b_k(n) = x(q+n+k, -(p+n-k)) for 0 <= k < p+n, with the leftmost one at -d, c_T0 = 0, p = floor((d+T0)/2), q = T0-p-1; each scan step is Rule 30 at one cell and the n-th guard is Rule 30 at the cell (T0+2n+1, -1) given the pin. Control, kernel-checked: the 7-periodic row with ones at j = 6 mod 7 has centre trace 0,1,0,1,..., so finiteness cannot be dropped (alternatingCenter_without_finiteSupport). Every result on propext and Quot.sound only.
entries.sc: An implication whose hypothesis is the open node mortality; it proves neither mortality nor period-two exclusion. Exact period two from time zero only: the reduction of an eventual period to this form is P1.1 and is not formalized. The written sources assert this bridge without assembling it, and the dictionary is not in them; it was brute-force checked on 38,973 random left-finite rows before the proof. Z ignores right-realizability of the scalar tape, so no converse is claimed.

groups.title: Proved-uniform NO-GOs
groups.blurb: Guardrails against argument shapes, not facts to build on. Listing them beside A1 without this label would invite exactly the misreading this tab exists to prevent.

entries.t: Finite-prefix certification limit for factor-complexity nonperiodicity (obstruction H)
entries.st: No finite computation, at any prefix length N, can certify p(n) > n for all n (the universal Morse-Hedlund nonperiodicity condition); it can only certify this for n up to a bound depending on N, since a finite computation reaches only finitely many n.
entries.sc: universal (applies to any finite-prefix computation of factor complexity, not specific to Rule 30)
entries.quantifier: any finite-prefix computation, at any prefix length N
entries.note: No finite computation can certify p(n) > n for all n.

entries.t: Theorem O: no finite prefix of the center column can imply non-automaticity
entries.st: Theorem O: for every N, the sequence agreeing with a on [0,N) and 0 thereafter is eventually periodic, hence 2-automatic, with 2-kernel size <= 2N+1. Therefore no property of any finite prefix computed from a alone can imply non-automaticity or non-periodicity, and a count of distinct residuals from a prefix is exactly a lower bound on a complexity function and can never be more. Quantitatively, with A^ker(N) := min{|K_2(b)| : b 2-automatic and b agrees with a on [0,N)}, non-automaticity is equivalent to sup_N A^ker(N) = infinity; A^ker was pinned within a factor 1.08 at N = 2^16, so N terms buy a kernel lower bound of about N/8 and nothing more, ever.
entries.sc: The theorem is an argument; the factor-1.08 pinning at N = 2^16 is a single measured adjunct, not part of the theorem. It bounds what finite prefix data can ever deliver and says nothing about Rule 30's true kernel. It is complementary to the ladder, whose rungs S(n,d) are finite computations settling bounded-complexity cases only.
entries.note: No finite prefix can ever imply non-automaticity.

entries.t: Uniform saturation theorem for terminal-window messages
entries.st: H_ell(q) = 1 for every q, whenever m=n-k>=3 and ell>=2*(4^k-1); every vertex of the projected 4^k-tuple graph reaches every target retained signature in every exact length ell>=2*(4^k-1) via the zero self-loop, and section-2 constant channels realize each such edge for all four original symbols simultaneously.
entries.sc: requires m>=3 hidden layers; the hidden hidden-channel choices reselected at each spatial step need not correspond to one actual original history
entries.quantifier: every q, once m >= 3 and ell >= 2(4^k-1)
entries.note: Uniform saturation floor; kills terminal-window message certificates. Taxonomy: sharp-constant-floor.

entries.t: Uniform limiting floor for horizon-dependent additive certificates
entries.st: liminf_(r->infinity) R_r >= 2^(-k-2b), where R_r = nu_n P_n^(r-1-b_r) F_r is any upper-count certificate with bounded arity k and exact-step bound b using a nonnegative additive majorant at each r.
entries.sc: certificates with fixed bounds k,b independent of n and alpha; universal over choice of F_r at each r
entries.quantifier: liminf over r, any bounded-arity additive upper-count certificate

entries.t: Gauge-holonomy plaquette defect kappa is identically zero for any left-permutive rule
entries.st: kappa(x,t) := PathA(x,t) XOR PathB(x,t), where Path A evolves a triple directly one step forward and Path B evolves forward then applies the left-permutive inverse identity one row later to solve back for the same target cell, is the zero function for every left-permutive rule (Rule 30 and Rule 90 both), because Path B is definitionally inverse(forward(...)) = identity, independent of periodicity or dynamics.
entries.sc: Holds for the entire left-permutive rule class by construction; a nonzero kappa only arises by injecting an assumed (possibly false) periodic continuation into one of the two paths.
entries.note: The gauge-holonomy plaquette defect is identically zero; a nonzero value only arises by injecting an assumed periodic continuation.

entries.t: Morse-Hedlund periodicity/complexity equivalence with linear bound
entries.st: For an infinite word w over a finite alphabet with factor complexity p(n) = #{distinct length-n factors}, w is eventually periodic (preperiod r>=0, period q>=1) iff p is bounded iff exists n with p(n)<=n; equivalently w is not eventually periodic iff p(n)>=n+1 for every n. Moreover if w has eventual period q and preperiod r, p(n) <= r+q for every n.
entries.note: Morse-Hedlund.

entries.t: Rationality-periodicity equivalence for the center generating function
entries.st: For A(z) a formal power series over F_2 with an honest denominator (Q(0)!=0), A(z) rational is exactly equivalent to the coefficient sequence a(t) being eventually periodic.
entries.sc: universal, for formal power series over a finite field with Q(0)!=0
entries.note: Rationality over F_2 iff eventual periodicity.

entries.t: At a rational frequency an eventually periodic trace has bounded or linear sums
entries.st: Let s_t be bounded and eventually periodic and let alpha = p/q be rational. Then s_t*exp(-2*pi*i*alpha*t) is eventually periodic with period dividing a common multiple of the tail period and q, so S(N) = sum_(t<N) s_t*exp(-2*pi*i*alpha*t) = N*ell + O(1). Either ell = 0 and |S(N)| is bounded, or ell != 0 and |S(N)| grows linearly; no intermediate growth rate occurs.
entries.sc: A general statement about eventually periodic bounded sequences at rational frequencies, with no Rule 30 content. It is the exclusion half of every target in this cluster: an upper bound alone does not use it, since ruling out eventual periodicity needs both o(N) and unboundedness of the same sums. The source is dated 2026-09-16, was read 2026-09-16, and is untracked in the working tree, as are its checkers and artifacts.
entries.note: No intermediate growth rate occurs.

entries.t: Bounded-index 1-Lipschitz encodings of the center column exist exactly when P1 is false
entries.st: If there exist a 1-Lipschitz map f : Z_2 -> Z_2, a point x_0, a FINITE bit-index set S and a map phi with s(t,0) = phi(bits_S(x_t)) for all t, then the Rule 30 single-seed center column is eventually periodic with eventual period a power of 2, at most 2^(max(S)+1). Proof: for 1-Lipschitz f the low k bits form an autonomous system on 2^k states, so every orbit is eventually periodic mod 2^k, and eventual periods double at most one level at a time, hence are powers of 2. Conversely, if the column were periodic with period 2^m, the odometer with S = {0..m-1} realizes such an encoding. Searching for ANY bounded-index 1-Lipschitz state object carrying the center column is therefore exactly as hard as refuting P1.
entries.sc: Frame-independent, and it closes in one step every reformulation of the route (other encodings, quotients, van der Put coefficients, right-aligned rows, skew products over a 1-Lipschitz base). It does not exclude unbounded-index encodings, and it proves nothing about P1 itself. The eventual periodicity with power-of-two period of each fixed cone-edge column is adjacent to Rowland 2006 Lemma 2 and is labelled validation rather than discovery.
entries.note: A bounded-index 1-Lipschitz encoding exists exactly when P1 is false: closes every reformulation of the 2-adic route in one step.

bands.title: The invariant algebra
bands.blurb: Where one quantity is an EXACT function of another, so a bound on one transfers to the other for free. The transfer DIRECTION is the load-bearing field: a two-sided identity moves a bound both ways, a one-sided inequality does not, and an equivalence moves the difficulty along with the bound.

groups.title: The P2 equivalence chain
groups.blurb: All two-sided. Bound any one and you have them all. This is the single most useful structure on the tab.

entries.t: Dyadic-shell lemma
entries.st: P2 is equivalent to M_k / 2^k -> 0, where M_k = max_{0<=u<=2^k} |sum_{2^k <= t < 2^k+u} x_t|.
entries.sc: single-seed center sequence x_t = 2c_t-1
entries.transfer: two-sided

entries.t: PP2 dyadic-shell discrepancy equivalence
entries.st: Define M_k = max_(0<=u<=2^k)|sum_(2^k<=t<2^k+u) x_t| for x_t=2c_t-1. Then PP2 <=> M_k/2^k -> 0.
entries.sc: exact reformulation, not a proof of PP2 itself
entries.transfer: two-sided

entries.t: Integrated-energy lemma
entries.st: P2 is equivalent to I_k / 2^(3k) -> 0, where I_k = sum_{u=1}^{2^k} S_k(u)^2 is the integrated square discrepancy inside shell k.
entries.sc: single-seed center sequence, uses dyadic-shell lemma
entries.transfer: two-sided

entries.t: PP2 integrated-energy equivalence
entries.st: With S_k(u) = sum_(0<=r<u) x_(2^k+r) and I_k = sum_(u=1)^(2^k) S_k(u)^2: because I_k <= 2^k M_k^2 and I_k >= M_k^3/8, PP2 <=> I_k = o(2^(3k)).
entries.sc: exact reformulation, currently the weakest exact scalar target for PP2; not itself a proof
entries.transfer: two-sided

entries.t: Energy criterion equivalence for P2
entries.st: H_k / 2^(2k) -> 0 is equivalent to P2.
entries.sc: seed-specific equivalence
entries.relation: P2 iff H_k/2^(2k) -> 0 iff max_j E_(k,j)/2^(2k) -> 0
entries.transfer: two-sided

entries.t: P2 equivalence chain via energy
entries.st: P2 iff M_k/2^k -> 0 iff H_k/2^(2k) -> 0 iff max_j E_{k,j}/2^(2k) -> 0.
entries.sc: seed-specific equivalences after substitution into universal inequalities
entries.transfer: two-sided

entries.t: F_k definition and universal comparison (restated)
entries.st: F_k=min_{0<=j<=k}(V_{k,j}+4^{j-k}); (1/2)(M_k/N_k)^2 <= F_k <= 5(M_k/N_k), so F_k->0 is equivalent to P2
entries.sc: universal over all sign words and scales
entries.transfer: two-sided, so F -> M and M -> F both

entries.t: Universal F-comparison bound
entries.st: Writing m=M/N: m^2/2 <= F <= 5m, where F = min_{0<=j<=k} (V_j + 4^j/N^2)
entries.sc: universal over all sign words and all dyadic scales
entries.transfer: two-sided

entries.t: P2 equivalent to F_k->0
entries.st: Together with the established shell-prefix equivalence, this proves P2 <=> F_k -> 0
entries.sc: acceptance test, not a predictive seed bound

entries.t: P2 iff sublinear-cutoff energy vanishes (eq 2)
entries.st: P2 iff there exist cutoffs j_k with 2^(j_k-k) -> 0 and V_(k,j_k) -> 0
entries.sc: singleton seed shell criterion (both sufficiency and necessity proved)
entries.relation: P2 iff there are cutoffs j_k with 2^(j_k-k) -> 0 and V_(k,j_k) -> 0
entries.transfer: necessity and sufficiency both proved

entries.t: Optimized matching equivalence for P2
entries.st: P2 iff there exists R_k = o(N_k) with U_{R_k} = o(N_k), giving another exact reformulation of P2 (radius allowed to vary freely), even up to a universal constant factor in the optimized finite cost.
entries.sc: reformulation only; does not supply a seed-specific asymptotic estimate
entries.relation: P2 iff there is R_k = o(N_k) with U_(R_k) = o(N_k)
entries.transfer: two-sided

entries.t: Density one-half, the shell maximum, the flexible energy and the ordered energy are kernel-checked equivalent for every Boolean sequence
entries.st: Rule30P2Bridge.lean proves in core Lean 4.33.1, for every c : Nat -> Bool and so for the Rule 30 singleton centre column: A(T) - T/2 = o(T) iff M_k = o(N) (densityHalf_iff_shellMaxLittleO); M_k = o(N) iff F_k -> 0 with F_k = min_j (V_(k,j) + 4^(j-k)) (shellMaxLittleO_iff_flexibleEnergyToZero); and H_k = o(N^2), max_j E_(k,j) = o(N^2) and M_k = o(N) are equivalent (shellMaxLittleO_iff_orderedEnergyLittleO, orderedEnergyLittleO_iff_maxBlockEnergyLittleO). Control, also kernel-checked: the sequence that is +1 on the first half of every dyadic shell and -1 on the second has S(2^k) = 2 and E_(k,k) = 0 and fails density one-half, so neither the dyadic endpoints alone nor the flexible energy without its 4^(j-k) penalty carries the bridge (dyadicEndpoints_bridge_fails, unpenalizedEnergy_bridge_fails). Replayed from the repository root at lean exit 0, no sorry, every result on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only.
entries.sc: An equivalence of targets, true of every Boolean sequence and using nothing about Rule 30. It bounds none of M_k, F_k, H_k on the centre column and P2 is exactly as open as before. The little-o statements are over Nat and Int with denominators cleared; their faithfulness to the documents' real-valued forms is a reading of lines 34 to 129 of the file, not something the kernel checks. fixed_window -> p2 and matching -> p2 are not covered, and the merge recurrence of Rule30ResearchReduction.lean is not connected to these definitions. This is one of the six bridges node formal_reductions names.
entries.transfer: the whole chain, kernel-checked for every Boolean sequence
entries.note: Its control is load-bearing: +-1 on dyadic half-shells has S(2^k)=2 and E_(k,k)=0 yet fails density 1/2, so the 4^(j-k) penalty cannot be dropped.

entries.t: Exact ordered block-merge energy identity
entries.st: E_{j+1} = 2E_j - D_j, 0 <= D_j <= 2E_j, V_{j+1} = V_j(1-delta_j), delta_j = D_j/(2E_j) when E_j>0 (delta_j=0 when E_j=0)
entries.sc: universal deterministic identity, no independence assumption or CA property used
entries.relation: E_(j+1) = 2E_j - D_j, 0 <= D_j <= 2E_j, V_(j+1) = V_j(1 - delta_j), delta_j = D_j/(2E_j)
entries.transfer: universal deterministic identity; no independence assumption or CA property used

entries.t: Accumulated loss product formula
entries.st: Since V_0=1, the exact accumulated loss is V_j = product_{i<j} (1-delta_i)
entries.transfer: ONE WAY: lower bounds on the delta_i give upper bounds on V_j; a bound on V_j constrains only the product, never an individual delta_i

entries.t: Projection-energy telescoping identity
entries.st: ||(I-P)u||^2 = E_{k,j} - 2^{-l}*E_{k,j+l} = sum_{s=0}^{l-1} 2^{-s-1}*D_{k,j+s}, where P is the orthogonal group-mean projection over groups of size m=2^l.
entries.sc: universal exact identity
entries.transfer: universal exact identity

entries.t: Exact spatial-window doubling identity
entries.st: E_(2L) = 4*E_L - 2*Q_L - D_L, giving strict normalized energy loss at every doubling on a nonzero finite positive row.
entries.sc: universal identity
entries.transfer: strict normalized energy loss at every doubling on a nonzero finite positive row

entries.t: Density-energy decomposition via A channel
entries.st: H(z) = N + 4*H(A), since every dyadic block of z of length at least two has sum twice the sum of its corresponding A-block.
entries.sc: universal exact identity
entries.transfer: ONE WAY: A -> z, the A-block being the coarse variable

entries.t: Exact tree-energy criterion without log factor
entries.st: For every nonempty dyadic sign word: M^3 <= 16*N*E*, E* <= 2*N*M, and E* <= H <= 8*N*M.
entries.transfer: two-sided M <-> E*, with cubes

entries.t: Variance decomposition with centering
entries.st: V = Var(block mean) + (shell signed mean)^2.
entries.sc: universal identity

entries.t: H_k closed form via correlations
entries.st: Since C_k(0)=N, H_k = (k+1)N + sum_{h=1}^{N-1} (k - floor(log2 h)) C_k(h).
entries.sc: seed-specific time-index sequence
entries.transfer: the bridge from correlations to tree energy

entries.t: Dyadic-lag correlation hypothesis sufficient for P2 and for P1
entries.st: Let c_t be the singleton Rule 30 centre trace, z_t = 1 - 2 c_t, and D = {2^a - 2^b : a > b >= 0}. If limsup_(N->infinity) C_N(h)/N <= 0 for every h in D, then centre density is 1/2 and P2 follows: dividing the exact inequality by m^2 N^2 with m held fixed, the finitely many cross terms have nonpositive limsup and H_m/N -> 0, giving limsup (S_N/N)^2 <= 1/m, and only afterwards is m let tend to infinity. Equivalently, with D_N(h) = #{0<=t<N-h : c_t != c_(t+h)} and C_N(h) = (N-h) - 2 D_N(h) for N > h, the hypothesis is liminf D_N(h)/(N-h) >= 1/2 for each h in D. The same hypothesis also excludes every eventual period, hence would prove P1: for any period p two powers of two share a residue mod p, their positive difference h lies in D and is divisible by p, and an eventually p-periodic trace has C_N(h)/N -> 1. A weaker aggregate alternative suffices too: it is enough that for an unbounded set of m, limsup_(N) (1/N) sum_(0<=i<j<m) C_N(2^j - 2^i) <= 0.
entries.sc: Conditional only. Neither the per-lag hypothesis nor the aggregate alternative is established for Rule 30, and neither is claimed necessary for P2. No uniform rate in h or m is required, but letting m grow with N without further bounds would not be justified. These are ordinary time shifts, not XOR shifts of binary time indices. The missing step remains an origin-specific cancellation argument.
entries.transfer: two-sided and EXACT; a bound on the disagreement count IS a bound on the correlation
entries.note: The identity is unconditional. The record's conditional status attaches to the hypothesis limsup C_N(h)/N <= 0, NOT to the identity.

entries.t: Same-orbit defect theorem
entries.st: If, for every fixed h>=1, C_N(h)/N -> 0, then P2 holds, where z_t=(-1)^c_t and C_N(h)=sum_{t=0}^{N-1-h} z_t z_{t+h}.
entries.sc: sufficient condition; requires the limit for every fixed shift h
entries.relation: if C_N(h)/N -> 0 for every fixed h >= 1, then P2 (van der Corput)
entries.transfer: ONE WAY: correlations -> density. Not claimed necessary.

entries.t: van der Corput sufficient condition for PP2
entries.st: With z_t=(-1)^(c_t) and C_N(h)=sum_(t=0)^(N-1-h) z_t*z_(t+h): if C_N(h)/N -> 0 for every fixed h>=1, then PP2 holds by van der Corput.
entries.sc: a sufficient, not equivalent, condition; the hypothesis itself (limiting density-1/2 center defect) is unproved for the lone seed
entries.transfer: one way

entries.t: Cauchy-Schwarz finite discrepancy-correlation inequality
entries.st: For integers N,H>=1: H^2 |sum_{t<N} z_t|^2 <= (N+H-1) [HN + 2 sum_{h=1}^{H-1} (H-h) C_N(h)].
entries.sc: universal, finite N,H
entries.transfer: ONE WAY: correlations -> discrepancy

entries.t: Exact Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for dyadic-difference correlations of a sign word
entries.st: For any signs z_0,...,z_(N-1) with N>=1, put S_N = sum_(t<N) z_t and C_N(h) = sum_(t<=N-1-h) z_t z_(t+h) for h>=1 (zero when h>=N). For m>=1 set a_j = 2^j - 1 for 0<=j<m and H_m = 2^(m-1) - 1. Then m^2 S_N^2 <= (N + H_m) [ m N + 2 sum_(0<=i<j<m) C_N(2^j - 2^i) ]. Proof: extend z by zero to all integers, set Y_t = sum_(j<m) z_(t+a_j), whose support lies in the N + H_m positions [-H_m, N-1] and whose total is m S_N; expanding squares gives sum_t Y_t^2 = m N + 2 sum_(i<j) C_N(a_j - a_i), and Cauchy-Schwarz finishes. The bracket is nonnegative even when individual correlations are negative, there is no independence assumption, and the inequality also holds when N <= H_m.
entries.sc: An exact finite inequality for arbitrary sign words, with no Rule 30 content. It is a specialization of the elementary Cauchy-Schwarz / van der Corput argument to dyadic translations, not a new general analytic method, and it proves no cancellation estimate for Rule 30.
entries.transfer: ONE WAY: the O((log X)^2) dyadic lags -> the full sum

entries.t: Unsigned bound |D_j| <= 2*V_j by four-adic parent/child residual mismatches
entries.st: Let V_j = #{(n,r): 0 <= n < 4^j, 0 <= r < 4, b_(4n+r) != b_n}. Subtracting b_n separately in the four terms of delta_n, whose coefficients have modulus one and sum three, gives |D_j| <= 2*V_j, so replacing |D_j| by 2*V_j in the absolute-tail certificate is sufficient.
entries.sc: Sufficient but strictly stronger than the certificate it replaces: it discards the signs, and signed cancellation in the defect sum can matter even when the mismatches are numerous. It is an inequality about the identity, not a measurement of the seed. The source is dated 2026-09-16, was read 2026-09-16, and is untracked in the working tree, as are its checkers and artifacts.
entries.transfer: ONE WAY ONLY: scope says it discards the signs, so V_j -> D_j and never the reverse

entries.t: Exact finite defect/run/one-count identity
entries.st: 5D+4H=2U-3(n'-n), where D counts adjacent 11 pairs, H counts 101 blocks, U counts length-three one-containing windows, n and n' are one-counts before/after one Rule 30 update
entries.sc: universal finite binary-row identity
entries.transfer: universal finite binary-row identity

entries.t: Local defect-current identity
entries.st: 3(y-q)+5D_i+4H_i = 2U_i+J(p,q)-J(q,r), where p=x_(i-1), q=x_i, r=x_(i+1), y=p XOR (q OR r), D_i=qr, H_i=p(1-q)r, U_i=p OR q OR r, J(p,q)=p-q-4pq.
entries.sc: pointwise local identity over the eight binary triples; not itself a global discrepancy bound
entries.transfer: the local form of the above

entries.t: Exact rank-pairing identity for signed words and matching-discrepancy equivalence
entries.st: For a finite sign word z with prefix sums S(u) and M=max|S(u)|, with p_i, m_i the i-th positive/negative positions: p_i = 2i - S(p_i), m_i = 2i + S(m_i), m_i - p_i = S(p_i) + S(m_i); every matched pair has separation at most 2M-1, and U_{2M-1} = |S(N)|, with M <= min_R(U_R + R) <= 2M-1+|S(N)| <= 3M-1.
entries.sc: universal combinatorial identity for any nonempty finite sign word, not specific to the Rule 30 seed
entries.relation: p_i = 2i - S(p_i), m_i = 2i + S(m_i), m_i - p_i = S(p_i) + S(m_i)

entries.t: Telescoped potential/current identity for the seed
entries.st: With P_t=P(x^t), K_t=K(x^t), A(T)=sum_{0<=t<T} x_0^t, and P_0=0: A(T)-T/2 = P_T + sum_{t<T}(K_t-1/2).
entries.sc: P_T=o(T) plus sublinear current bound would suffice for P2 but is not known necessary (cancellation between terms is permitted)
entries.transfer: P_T = o(T) PLUS a sublinear current bound suffices for P2; neither alone does, and cancellation between the two terms is permitted, so the converse fails
entries.note: Recorded twice with two different wrong methods. See overclaims.

entries.t: Quarter-wave potential identity
entries.sc: universal exact identity for the actual seed
entries.note: Duplicate of the above.

entries.t: Telescoped transfer of the centre Fourier average to the nonlinear current
entries.st: Fix a nonreal unit lambda, let x^t be any actual Rule 30 orbit, and write c_t = x^t_0, P_t = P_lambda(x^t), K_t = K_lambda(x^t). For every N >= 1 the identity telescopes exactly to sum_(0<=t<N) lambda^(-t)*(c_t - K_t) = lambda^(1-N)*P_N - lambda*P_0. After division by N the error is at most 2W/N, and at most (W+|C|)/N for the singleton initial row, where P_0 = C. Hence the centre and current Fourier averages have the same limit whenever either limit exists, and their finite averages differ by O_lambda(1/N).
entries.sc: An exact reformulation transferring the centre question to the nonlinear current at a fixed frequency. No existence and no vanishing of either limit is proved, and the current stays nonlinear and dependent on the actual orbit. It applies only off the two real unit frequencies, where the uniform potential bound fails. The source is dated 2026-09-16, was read 2026-09-16, and is untracked in the working tree, as are its audit, probe and both JSON artifacts.
entries.relation: sum_(t<N) lambda^(-t)(c_t - K_t) = lambda^(1-N) P_N - lambda P_0, for every N >= 1
entries.transfer: two-way at the level of limits, off the two real unit frequencies; the averages differ by O(1/N)

entries.t: Same-orbit defect recurrence
entries.st: For D_t(i)=F^(t+2)(y)(i) XOR F^t(y)(i) and s_t=F^t(y): D_(t+1)(i) = D_t(i-1) XOR D_t(i) XOR D_t(i+1) XOR s_t(i)*D_t(i+1) XOR s_t(i+1)*D_t(i) XOR D_t(i)*D_t(i+1). If the two center traces agree, D_t(-1) = (1 XOR s_t(0))*D_t(1).
entries.sc: identity underlying the same-orbit reduction of eventual periodicity
entries.relation: the same-orbit defect recurrence, exact and quadratic in D_t

entries.t: Exact phase-rank accounting identity
entries.st: rho_N = rho_1 - D - E + sum(J_switch), where rho=R-1-H (H the depth to which inward bits agree with the q-alternating birth pattern), D counts repeated neighboring scalars, E is additional height gain on repeats, and J is the per-switch refill.
entries.sc: an exact accounting identity that is insufficient by itself: the switch refill term J is unbounded (witnessed by the family 3 2^(4k-1)), so it does not prove mortality/termination
entries.transfer: exact phase-rank accounting

entries.t: Rule 30 / Rule 150 error decomposition
entries.st: f30(l,c,r) = l ^ (c | r) = l ^ c ^ r ^ (c & r) = f150(l,c,r) ^ E, where E(x,t) = s_t(x) AND s_t(x+1).
entries.sc: universal, definitional identity over GF(2)
entries.relation: f30 = f150 XOR E, E(x,t) = s_t(x) AND s_t(x+1)
entries.transfer: the definitional split every Duhamel route uses
entries.note: This is the affine decomposition: Rule 30 is linear in the left neighbour and nonlinear only through a two-input OR.

entries.t: Nonlinear-feedback two-step identity for accumulated Rule 150 response
entries.st: U^(t+2) = L^2 U^t XOR L Q^t XOR Q^(t+1), where U^t is the accumulated Rule 150 response and Q^t the nonlinear source with the mandatory left-edge source removed; equivalently for the full state F^2(x)=L^2 x XOR L N(x) XOR N(F(x)).
entries.sc: universal identity, exact evaluation of nonlinear feedback rather than treatment as independent noise
entries.relation: U^(t+2) = L^2 U^t XOR L Q^t XOR Q^(t+1)

entries.t: Exact two-step Rule 30 local update equation
entries.st: F30^2(x)_i = a+d+e+bd+cd+be+ce+de+bde+cde = a+(1+b+c)(d+e+de), equivalently x_(i-2) XOR [(1 XOR x_(i-1) XOR x_i) AND (x_(i+1) OR x_(i+2))], for input bits a,b,c,d,e at positions i-2..i+2.
entries.sc: universal (all 32 five-bit assignments)

entries.t: Corrected one-step interface identity at the centre
entries.st: a_{t+1} XOR a_t = u_{t,-1} XOR u_{t,1} XOR (a_t AND u_{t,1}), derived directly from f_30(x)_i=x_{i-1} XOR (x_i OR x_{i+1}) at i=0.
entries.sc: Verified for all 1999 checked steps at T=2000; a tautological restatement of the local update rule, offering no new constraint on the interface columns
entries.relation: a_(t+1) XOR a_t = u_(t,-1) XOR u_(t,1) XOR (a_t AND u_(t,1))
entries.transfer: NONE
entries.note: Scope calls it a tautological restatement of the local update rule, offering no new constraint. Listed so nobody rediscovers it.

entries.t: Exact backward-message aggregation identity
entries.st: M_k T_n = T_k M_k, where pi_k truncates a column after its kth temporal pair and M_k sums a function over all coordinates above k; the column transition maps the source's remaining temporal tail bijectively onto the target tail for each of the four input symbols.
entries.sc: universal identity on the exact spatial transfer matrix T_n=4P_n
entries.relation: M_k T_n = T_k M_k on the exact spatial transfer matrix T_n = 4P_n

entries.t: Rotated Peel identity
entries.st: With I(e) the inverse-terminal cut, sigma the one-sided shift, and zero-indexed Peel P, the identity P(I(sigma e)) = sigma^2 I(e) holds exactly, implying linear drift of positive finite Peel rank under endpoint shift.
entries.sc: Proof and checks are in the companion file RESULTS-ROTATED-PEEL-IDENTITY.md; a last-support argument using phi(s,0)=3 for s!=0 handles the rank-zero case separately.

entries.t: Iterated rotated Peel identity
entries.st: P^j(I(sigma^j e)) = sigma^(2j) I(e), for every j >= 0
entries.sc: arbitrary four-state endpoints
entries.relation: P^j(I(sigma^j e)) = sigma^(2j) I(e) for every j >= 0
entries.transfer: linear drift of positive finite Peel rank

entries.t: All-length continuation identity linking a source to its next-scale shift
entries.st: Write Q = Q_c(W) for a nonempty W in A^n and define the length-(n+1) word S_c(W) = W[1:] Q[:2] (delete the first source symbol, append the first two forced symbols). Then Q_c(S_c(W)) = Q_c(W)[2:] for every nonempty four-state source W and c in {2,3}. The proof applies the rotated inverse-cone identity P I(sigma f) = sigma^2 I(f) together with P sigma = sigma P to f = W Q, giving G_(n+1)(sigma f) = sigma^2 G_n(f) = c^infinity; the first n+1 symbols of sigma f are exactly S_c(W) and uniqueness of the forced continuation finishes. Iterating, the compatible source at scale n+k is the block f[k:n+2k] and its forced continuation is Q[2k:], so neighbouring scales cannot be chosen independently along one forced trajectory.
entries.sc: An exact identity between forced continuations at neighbouring scales, for every nonempty four-state source. This transformation DELETES a symbol before appending two, so it does not assert that a scale-(n+1) source extends the scale-n source, and therefore does not contradict the append-only obstruction of RESULTS-GAMMA-PROOF-ATTEMPT.md section 2. It supplies no mortality bound and no separator.
entries.relation: Q_c(S_c(W)) = Q_c(W)[2:] for every nonempty four-state source W

entries.t: Exact four-adic recurrence F_(k+1) = 3*F_k + D_k for the residual variation
entries.st: With tau_t = (-1)^theta(t), b_t = (-1)^R_t for t>=1 and b_0 = -1, so that s_t = tau_t*b_t for every t>=0, define delta_n = b_(4n) - omega*b_(4n+1) - omega^2*b_(4n+2) + b_(4n+3) - 3*b_n and D_k = sum_(n<4^k) tau_n*omega^n*delta_n. Then tau at the four children equals tau_n*(1,-1,-1,1), omega^(4n) = omega^n and 1-omega-omega^2+1 = 3, so F_(k+1) = 3*F_k + D_k and 3^(-k)*F_k = b_0 + sum_(j<k) D_j/3^(j+1).
entries.sc: An exact identity with no approximation, independence assumption, limiting measure or P1/P2 hypothesis. It holds for an arbitrary binary sequence once b_t = s_t*tau_t is defined, so it supplies no Rule-30-specific estimate by itself. The D_k are Fourier sums of residual variations and are not the local integer correction of the spatial extraction identity. The source is dated 2026-09-16, was read 2026-09-16, and is untracked in the working tree, as are its checkers and artifacts.
entries.relation: F_(k+1) = 3 F_k + D_k, hence 3^(-k) F_k = b_0 + sum_(j<k) D_j/3^(j+1)
entries.transfer: exact for an arbitrary binary sequence; supplies NO Rule 30 estimate

entries.t: Exact radial energy recurrence and its integer Eisenstein cross term
entries.st: With E_k = |F_k|^2, squaring the exact recurrence gives E_(k+1) = 9*E_k + 6*Re(F_k*conj(D_k)) + |D_k|^2, and for Eisenstein pairs F = a+b*omega, D = c+d*omega the cross term is the integer expression 2*Re(F*conj(D)) = 2*a*c - a*d - b*c + 2*b*d, so the whole recurrence is evaluated without numerical complex arithmetic.
entries.sc: An algebraic consequence of the four-adic recurrence, valid for any binary sign sequence. It supplies no growth mechanism: the sign and size of the cross term are exactly what remains unknown. The source is dated 2026-09-16, was read 2026-09-16, and is untracked in the working tree, as are its checkers and artifacts.
entries.transfer: cross term an exact integer in Eisenstein coordinates

entries.t: The frequency-one-third target is exactly an unbounded sublinear residue spread
entries.st: With s_t = 1-2*c_t, A_r(m) = sum_(0<=j<m) c_(3j+r), X_m = A_2-A_0, Y_m = A_2-A_1 and Delta_m = max_r A_r - min_r A_r, grouping by 1+omega+omega^2 = 0 gives S(3m) = 2*(X_m + Y_m*omega), |S(3m)|^2 = 2*sum_(r<s) (A_r-A_s)^2, Delta_m = max(|X_m|,|Y_m|,|X_m-Y_m|) and sqrt(3)*Delta_m <= |S(3m)| <= 2*Delta_m. Since the remainder to the next prefix has magnitude at most sqrt(3), the all-prefix target is exactly: Delta_m unbounded and Delta_m = o(m).
entries.sc: An exact translation of the analytic target into three integer counts. It asks for agreement between the three residue classes with unbounded absolute fluctuation, and does not require that their common asymptotic density exist or equal one half. Neither half of the target is established. The source is dated 2026-09-16, was read 2026-09-16, and is untracked in the working tree, as are its checkers and artifacts.
entries.transfer: two-sided: the analytic target is exactly Delta_m unbounded and Delta_m = o(m)

entries.t: Maximal finite ancestry criterion (Eq. 8)
entries.st: For a nonzero finite-support row y with support endpoints [-n,n] and d_fin(y) the greatest number of successive Rule 30 predecessors all having finite support: 0 <= d_fin(y) <= n, and d_fin(y)=n iff y=x^n.
entries.sc: nonzero finite-support rows with support endpoints [-n,n]
entries.relation: 0 <= d_fin(y) <= n, and d_fin(y) = n iff y = x^n
entries.transfer: exact characterization of the singleton origin

entries.st: On shell t=2^k+j (0<=j<2^k, m=2^k-1): b_k(j) = -a_k(j)*(-1)^popcount(j), and Walsh(b_k)(u) = -Walsh(a_k)(u XOR m), where a_k(j)=(-1)^c_{2^k+j}, b_k(j)=(-1)^R_{2^k+j}.
