entries.t: No monotone complexity-growth statement on the space-time pattern can imply centre-column aperiodicity
entries.st: For ANY complexity measure B(t) defined on the space-time pattern, the statement that B(t) tends to infinity monotonically cannot imply centre-column aperiodicity, because the implication is false for Rule 90: the Rule 90 lone-seed pattern has unbounded structural complexity (Sierpinski, nested at every scale, defect structures growing without bound) while its centre column IS eventually periodic, identically 0 for all t >= 1. This kills the braid-length arm and the maximal-scrambling half of the OTOC arm outright, independent of whether the measures are well defined.
entries.sc: A filter on argument shapes, not a result about Rule 30. It applies to any measure defined on the pattern as a whole; it does not exclude measures defined on the centre column itself.
entries.note: For ANY complexity measure B(t) on the space-time pattern, B(t) -> infinity cannot imply centre aperiodicity, Rule 90 being nested at every scale with an eventually-periodic centre.

entries.t: Rule 90 is a vacuous control for Frobenius/dilation-based transcendence arguments
entries.st: Rule 90's lone-seed centre column is the constant series C=1 (cell 0 at time 2m is C(2m,m) mod 2, which is 0 for every m>=1 by Kummer's theorem since m+m always carries), which is precisely the degenerate case an argument of this shape excuses itself on; the argument therefore never fires on Rule 90 and Rule 90 gives no discriminating check for this argument shape. A non-constant 2-automatic series (e.g. sum_j y^(2^j-1)) must be used instead.
entries.note: Rule 90 is a VACUOUS control for Frobenius/dilation transcendence: its centre is the constant series, the degenerate case such arguments excuse themselves on. The filter must be chosen per object.

entries.t: The comoving Anashin object does not separate Rule 30 from Rule 90
entries.st: Rule 90 has the identical comoving structure, y = x XOR (x<<2) in the right-edge frame, which is also 1-Lipschitz, also a 4-state Mealy automaton, and also measure-preserving; both maps are verified bijective mod 2^k for k = 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 12, 16. Since Rule 90's single-seed center column is eventually 0, the mere existence of the Anashin object, its measure-preservation, and its automaton finiteness are all non-separating and prove nothing about the Rule 30 center column.
entries.sc: A control result: it kills the inference from the existence of the object, not any finer 2-adic statement. Bijectivity was checked exhaustively only at the seven listed moduli.
entries.note: Rule 90 has the identical comoving structure y = x XOR (x<<2): also 1-Lipschitz, also 4-state, also measure-preserving.

entries.t: Rule 90's ideomotor residual rho_k is unbounded with exact closed form, refuting the universal periodicity-implies-bounded premise
entries.st: For Rule 90's lone seed (true period 1 from T0=1), rho_k reduces to the running signed sum over the x=1 column, whose ones occur exactly at t=2^j-1 (by Kummer's theorem on Pascal's-triangle-mod-2 carries), giving the exact closed form rho_k = 2*floor(log2(k+1)) - k, so rho_k -> -infinity as k -> infinity: a proved instance where periodicity holds but rho_k is unbounded, refuting the spark's universal claim that periodicity implies bounded rho_k.
entries.sc: Refutes only the universal (rule-unspecified) form of the claim; silent on the Rule-30-specific claim, which is separately closed by the free-bit argument in the same document's section 2.
entries.note: Rule 90's rho_k -> -infinity WHILE periodic, refuting 'periodicity implies bounded rho_k'.

entries.t: Weaver preimage count P(t) = 2 closed form
entries.st: Under Reading B of the preimage-count construction (fix the true seed and entire right half at time 0, vary only the left-window bits b_{-1..-t}, forward-evolve, and count candidates reproducing the true center-column prefix a_0..a_{t-1}), the count P(t) is exactly 2 for every t>=1, for every left-permutive rule (Rule 30 and Rule 90 alike), independent of whether the target trace is periodic.
entries.sc: holds for every left-permutive rule and every t>=1; does not distinguish the periodic (Rule 90) from the conjecturally-aperiodic (Rule 30) case, so it does not bear on P1, P2, or P3
entries.note: Exactly 2 preimages for every left-permutive rule: uniform, and therefore non-separating.

entries.t: Rule 90 control shell statistics
entries.st: For the Rule 90 seed, every shell k>=1 is all-zero in bits, hence M=N, W=N, and H=2N^2-N; none of the vanishing hypotheses holds.
entries.sc: Rule 90 control only, not Rule 30

entries.t: Fibonacci and zero-interleaved Thue-Morse rho prescriptions are right-unrealizable
entries.st: Prescribing rho directly by the Fibonacci substitution (0->01,1->0) or zero-interleaved Thue-Morse fails right realization: the Fibonacci prescription's shortest forbidden factor is 101001 (first source index 4, confirmed by zero matches among 2,048 width-11 initial rows and 8,192 width-13 rows for its shortest infeasible prefix 0100101), and the zero-interleaved Thue-Morse prescription's shortest forbidden factor is 00000 (first source index 9, zero matches among 512 width-9 rows).
entries.sc: A precise rejection of these two specific substitution constructions as full-diagram witnesses; no claim about all substitutions, all Sturmian words, or all possible witnesses follows.
entries.note: Fibonacci substitution and zero-interleaved Thue-Morse are both right-unrealizable as rho prescriptions.

entries.t: A pre-registered cryptanalytic battery finds no distinguisher for the centre column at T <= 2^21, on a decision rule its own power controls did not meet
entries.st: The a18 arm fixed a ledger of N = 100,838 hypotheses before any data (Berlekamp-Massey profile 18, correlation attack 780, NIST SP 800-22 40, autocorrelation 100,000) and applied Bonferroni at family-wise alpha = 0.05, per-hypothesis 4.9584e-07. For the lone-seed centre column the smallest raw p is 6.214e-06, adjusted 6.266e-01, with 0 Bonferroni and 0 Benjamini-Hochberg rejections: NO BIAS FOUND. Depth extension to T = 2^21 repeats tests 2 and 4 with the same result, max |z| 4.393 at lag 36578 against an i.i.d. seed band of [4.160, 4.907]. Controls that fire: lfsr32 (linear complexity plateaus at L = 32 where the centre column reaches 131,072 at n = 2^18, a factor of 4,096), bern51 (rejected at the registered p < 1e-3 by whole-sequence monobit at 1.0189e-89 and by both cumulative-sums streams at 0.0), copy1000 (autocorrelation z = 20.738 exactly at lag 1000). HOWEVER the registered decision rule reads NO BIAS FOUND only when 'all three non-degenerate power controls fire as registered' and INCONCLUSIVE otherwise, 'including a power control that fails to fire'. The three registered are lfsr32, bern51 and lag1000, and lag1000 failed BOTH of its requirements: its test-4 run rejects at NO lag at all, 0 of 100,000 exceeding the Bonferroni line, and the registered test-2 grid contains no Delta = 1000 at any k, its nearest cell being 1024, so that requirement was registered at a lag the same document's own ledger excludes. The control is mis-specified by construction and not merely by grid: for s_t = r_t XOR r_(t-1000) the shifted XOR is s_t XOR s_(t+1000) = r_(t-1000) XOR r_(t+1000), and at any other lag it is an XOR of four distinct fair bits, so the sequence is balanced at EVERY lag and has zero power anywhere, not only at its own. Recomputed here from the arm's own seq/lag1000.npy it gives z(1000) = +0.150462, in the same run in which copy1000 reproduces the committed 20.73840682678574 to sixteen digits. The arm found and disclosed this itself as deviation D1 and substituted copy1000, chosen after seeing the output. By the letter of the registered rule the outcome is INCONCLUSIVE, and PREREG is more explicit still: a test failing its registered power requirement 'is reported as having unknown power, not as a passing null'. The substitution is defensible because the control was provably null, but the headline rests on a post hoc control and a record must carry that. D3 is a second, independent ground for the same reading: test 1 was registered as {J, Hbar, D} x 6 prefixes and delivered as {G, J} x 9, so two of three registered statistics left the ledger while N = 100,838 still matched, which the arm records as happening by accident rather than by design. PREREG.md also requires deviations be appended to PREREG.md itself; they live in cryptanalysis.md section 7 instead.
entries.sc: A negative result about DETECTABILITY by four techniques at T <= 2^21. It does not IMPLY P1 or P2 in either direction: no finite-prefix statistic can imply aperiodicity, and symmetrically a surviving hit would not have refuted P1 either, a biased sequence being free to be aperiodic. But it is NOT true that the arm bears on neither prize, and the arm's own 'does not bear on P1, P2 or P3' is too strong: its null autocorrelation sweep yields an explicit period exclusion, recorded separately as r30-a18-autocorrelation-excludes-period-band. Three further limits, none of which changes the verdict. Test 2's sensitivity to a lag correlation is demonstrated ONLY outside the ledger, by a supplementary check at one hand-picked lag chosen after the fact, because the two in-ledger firing controls are both degenerate for that purpose: rule90 gives eps = 0.5 at every cell and bern51 gives eps = |2p-1|/2 independent of Delta. The autocorrelation sweep tests 100,000 of 1,048,576 available lags, 90.5 percent untested, and that cap is also what fixes N. The generator gate compares 65,536 bits against two independent implementations, 6.25 percent of the 2^20 prefix and 3.1 percent of the 2^21 extension. The arm's own Obstruction H governs all of it: every result is a statement about a finite prefix and can never establish randomness, absence of structure or nonperiodicity as an infinite statement.
entries.note: The control-design lesson, and it is the same defect twice from different directions. This arm registered lag1000 = r_t XOR r_(t-1000) as its non-degenerate autocorrelation control and it is provably null at its own lag, since s_t XOR s_(t+1000) = r_(t-1000) XOR r_(t+1000) is balanced, and at any other lag it is an XOR of four distinct fair bits; measured z(1000) = +0.150462 on the arm's own sequence. Its other two in-ledger controls are degenerate for the correlation test, rule90 giving eps = 0.5 at every cell and bern51 giving |2p-1|/2 independent of the lag. A control whose answer does not move with the parameter being swept cannot detect a wrong parameter set.

groups.title: Controls Rule 30 passes, and one that was lost

entries.t: The pin-augmented ladder has no Rule 90 soundness control
entries.st: The pin is rule-specific by design: Rule 90 violates the Rule 30 pin identity at all 7,227 of its ones, so the true Rule 90 lone-seed word is rejected by the filter (accepted = False, hits = 1 at every (R,k) tested) and the Rule 90 automaton collapses to 3 states and returns EMPTY. Consequently the pin-augmented ladder carries no rule-90 analogue of the constraint to run as a negative control, and any future EMPTY verdict from this encoding rests solely on the Rule 30 lone-seed regression and the p = 1 calibration, which the document says must be stated wherever such an EMPTY is reported.
entries.sc: A statement about the soundness apparatus of the pin-augmented R7 ladder, not about Rule 30. It does not claim the pin is unsound, only that the section-0 Rule 90 filter can no longer be run against it. The 7,227 figure is the count of ones in the Rule 90 lone-seed diagram over the range this run used, not a universal constant.
entries.note: The pin identity is violated at all 7,227 Rule 90 ones, so the pin is rule-specific and the ladder consequently has NO Rule 90 soundness control left to run.

entries.t: Rule 90 control showing the five-zero exclusion is OR-dependent
entries.st: Enumerating all 512 nine-cell right light cones for each rule and comparing a shrinking-cone implementation built on the unmodified ladder.FWD against the existing right_trace_forbidden.numeric_rho gives zero disagreements for both rules; under Rule 30 there are zero five-zero witnesses, while under Rule 90 there are 16, the first at mask 0x114. The prior exact ANF certificate agrees: the four-zero indicator is nonzero, the Rule 30 five-zero indicator is identically zero, and the Rule 90 five-zero indicator is nonzero. Hence the exclusion of five successive zero-phase right-neighbour zeros depends on the OR in Rule 30's local map and does not hold for the XOR control.
entries.sc: A finite exhaustive check over the nine-cell right cone determining five zero-phase observations, for the two rules only. It establishes that the five-zero exclusion is not rule-generic; it is not evidence about any other forbidden word, and it says nothing about eventual periodicity under either rule.
entries.note: Rule 30 has zero five-zero witnesses in the nine-cell right cone against Rule 90's 16: the exclusion is OR-dependent.

entries.t: Rule 90 five-state renormalization as a passing positive control for the gate-closure checker
entries.st: The exact five-state radius-one binary renormalization of the Rule 90 lone-seed diagram is admitted by the all-coordinate gate-closure checker direct_dfa_check.py: its gate product has 113 states, 16 terminal states and 380 transitions, its centre product has four states, and a separate scalar source calculation agrees at 16,384 coordinates. The same frozen five-state model satisfies the observation CNF with clock T=2, q=1, distinct from the Rule 30 search clock T=4, q=14; under the original reversed bound the solver found n=8589934591, r=1, i.e. actual times 17179869183=2^34-1 and 1240417074208453515280383, where the exact Rule 90 formula gives neighbour values one and zero. Exact reversal of the control's residue subsequences yields one state for the constant even subsequence and three for the aperiodic odd subsequence.
entries.sc: A positive control establishing that the framework does not vacuously reject every diagram; it is not a Rule 30 result. The Rule 30-specific obligation comes from the OR constraints in the local gate condition, and the nonzero-centre-clock pruning is deliberately not applied to this control.
entries.note: Rule 90's five-state renormalization IS admitted by the gate-closure checker, proving the framework does not vacuously reject everything.

entries.t: No Rule 90 carry kernel reproduces the Rule 30 growing-survival bounded-gamma census signature
entries.st: Replacing the p2 census carry action with any of the four genuine Rule 90 (additive) analogues K1..K4 destroys the Rule 30 growing-max-survival-row / bounded-gamma exclusion at the admissible tails c in {2,3}. Over a complete search of {1,2}^n for n = 8..16 no Rule 90 kernel reproduces the Rule 30 signature; the two anti-Rule-30 modes observed are vacuity (msr pinned at 0..2 and gamma about n+2 growing: K2 and K3 at both tails, K1 at c = 3) and intermittent full or high survival with gamma near 0, non-monotone in n (K1 at c = 2 with msr 8, 6, 4, 2, 18 and K4 at c = 3 with msr 10, 9, 5, 1, 14), which is a degeneracy of their linear cones rather than a Rule-30-like trend. The disconfirming Outcome B, Rule 90 also giving gamma >= 1 with a matching bounded margin, is therefore ruled out and the p2 needle route is not shown to be rule-blind.
entries.sc: Admissible tails c in {2,3} only, n = 8..16, brute force over {1,2}^n. Outcome A holds by inapplicability rather than by a clean non-vacuous distinguishing curve. A finite census is a lower bound on a complexity function, so this control does not prove period-2 exclusion for Rule 30; it shows only that the census does not survive the substitution non-vacuously.

entries.t: Sup-deviation decay slope sits inside the i.i.d. seed range at every tested block length
entries.st: At the registered T = 2,000,000, the least-squares slope of log2 S(L,W) against log2 W over W in {2^12, 2^14, 2^16, 2^18, 2^20} lies inside the range spanned by 20 i.i.d. null seeds at every tested L: L=1 gives -0.473 in [-0.658, -0.364], L=2 gives -0.518 in [-0.622, -0.383], L=4 gives -0.581 in [-0.629, -0.399], L=8 gives -0.518 in [-0.594, -0.490] and L=12 gives -0.563 in [-0.657, -0.551]. Seed-range containment is a descriptive comparison, not the pre-registered test: the pre-registration's consistency branch asks for a slope in [-0.65, -0.35] at each L <= 8, which -0.473, -0.518, -0.581 and -0.518 satisfy, and its disconfirming plateau criterion asks for a slope above -0.25, which no L reaches.
entries.sc: A measured single-run outcome, not a proof and not an inference to ergodicity. One column, one run, T = 2,000,000, 20 numpy null seeds. A block-frequency diagnostic has power only to disconfirm; the document's own status line calls it measured and diagnostic only and says it proves nothing about P2 in either direction. Each slope is a five-point regression. The pre-registered decision rule covers L <= 8 only, so L = 12 is reported outside it. The sup over depth uses 10 depths at W <= 2^18 and 9 at 2^20, so the pre-registered floor of 8 depths per window holds at every W and the largest-window end of each regression is no longer the weakest by depth count.
entries.note: 20 numpy null seeds.

entries.t: Exact survivor count for the 4/3 stopping map
entries.st: For the stopping map n_(j+1) = (4 n_j + e_j)/3 with e_j in {0,1} (e_j=0 on residue 0, e_j=1 on residue 2, residue 1 stops), each binary word (e_0,...,e_(D-1)) specifies exactly one starting residue class modulo 3^D; hence precisely 2^D of the 3^D classes survive D updates, and any set of positive integers that never stops has natural density zero with upper density at most (2/3)^D for every D.
entries.sc: the 4/3 arithmetic stopping problem, an outside control unrelated to Rule 30's cellular dynamics; does not prove the surviving set is empty
entries.note: The 4/3 stopping map as an outside arithmetic control.

entries.t: Reusable projector and superposition-identity verification
entries.st: The projector: projects_to_center is a verified 24 ns/call O(log n) primitive, and the superposition identity s_n(0) = rule150_center(n) XOR parity(projected errors) is exhaustively checked for all n <= 512 and on 37 banded targets to n = 10,000.
entries.sc: primitive and identity only; arm 5's broader route to o(n) remains closed (N_eff ~ n^1.68, row parity ~ n/2)

entries.t: Rule 30 vs Rule 90 exact adaptive decision-tree depth, n=1..4
entries.st: Brute-force minimum worst-case adaptive decision-tree depth D(f) over the full 2^(2n+1)-row truth table of the center cell c0(n): Rule 30 gives D(f)=2n+1 exactly at n=1,2,3,4 (i.e. 3,5,7,9 -- the full window is needed). Rule 90 gives D(f)=2,2,4,2 at the same n -- far below the 2n+1 window size, matching 2^popcount(n) (2,2,4,2 for n=1,2,3,4), since by Kummer's theorem only 2^popcount(n) of the 2n+1 positions carry a nonzero coefficient in Rule 90's center formula and the rest are exactly zero-influence, not merely low-influence.
entries.sc: n=1..4 only, brute force; Rule 30 result consistent with but not a proof of full-window necessity at larger n

entries.t: Rule 90 control: GMUS equals the exact odd-binomial dependency set
entries.st: By linearity the Rule 90 group-MUS (GMUS) sufficient constraint set is unique and equals the diamond cells with odd dependency-path count into (n,0) (binomial parity via Kummer's theorem); its size scales as n^(log2 3) ~ n^1.585, and the pipeline reproduces this set exactly at every completed n (8,16,32,64,128).
entries.sc: Rule 90 control only, additive rule; says nothing about Wolfram's Problem 3 in its Turing-machine formulation

entries.t: Rule 90 ROBDD width in right-to-left order
entries.st: In right-to-left order its reachable diagram has 3--15 nodes through horizon 16 and maximum width 2, as expected from its linear self-similarity.
entries.sc: Rule 90 positive control, right-to-left variable order, horizons up to 16

entries.t: Rule 90 lone-seed single periodic column
entries.st: The Rule 90 lone-seed centre is eventually zero, and every fixed nonzero spatial column is not eventually periodic: for a=|j|>0 and n with 2^(n-1)>=a, column j has value binomial(2^n-a,2^(n-1)) mod 2 = 1, and is zero throughout 2^n<=t<=2^(n+1)-a-1, giving infinitely many ones and arbitrarily long zero intervals.
entries.sc: Rule 90 control result only, not Rule 30; confirms the real Rule 90 lone-seed diagram satisfies the necessary condition from the isolated-column obstruction

entries.t: Rule 90 lone-seed centre column is eventually constant
entries.st: The Rule 90 lone-seed centre column is 1,0,0,0,...: at even t=2s the value is C(2s,s) mod 2, odd only at s=0 by Kummer's theorem, and zero at odd t by parity, so the column is eventually constant, hence eventually periodic, with density 0.

entries.t: Rule 90 lone-seed column vanishes after t=0
entries.st: The Rule 90 lone-seed center column is 1 at t=0 and provably 0 afterwards, because C(2k,k) is even for all k>=1.
entries.sc: Rule 90 lone-seed centre column only; used as a pipeline kill-condition control, not a Rule 30 claim

entries.t: Rule 90 lone-seed even-time centre parity
entries.st: At even time 2m>0 the Rule 90 centre is binomial(2m,m) mod 2, which is zero because binomial(2m,m)=2*binomial(2m-1,m-1)
entries.sc: Rule 90 only, not Rule 30/P2; used as a control showing the algebraic reductions do not by themselves prove decay

entries.t: Exact shift-mismatch count for the lone-seed Rule 90 neighbour
entries.st: For Rule 90 from the single one at the origin, l_t=r_t=1 exactly at t=2^a-1 with a>=1, and for fixed P>=1 the number of times in [0,N) with r_(t+P)!=r_t is exactly floor(log2 N) + floor(log2(N+P)) - floor(log2 P) minus twice the indicator that an overlap time t_P=2^a-1 exists below N, the overlap occurring precisely when P=2^a(2^d-1) for integers a,d>=1 and being unique. Restricting to the centre's zero phases subtracts the indicator that P+1 is a power of two, leaving 2 log2 N + O_P(1).
entries.sc: An exact control for an actual finite-seed orbit of a different rule, which settles the order of the R1 lower bound and refutes any universal omega(log N) lower bound. The control's coefficient is two and the recorded lower bound's is one; neither is shown optimal, and nothing here excludes a Rule-30-specific strengthening that uses the seed and the pin together. The orbit formulas themselves are known archive controls; what is new is the exact count for every fixed shift. The source is dated 2026-09-15, was read 2026-09-16, and is uncommitted in the working tree along with its checker and artifact.

entries.t: Lucas' theorem for binomial parity (Rule 90)
entries.st: Lucas' theorem gives C(n,k) mod 2 = [k AND ~n == 0] for the binomial (1+z)^n. That is Rule 90, not Rule 150.
entries.sc: binomial (1+z)^n only; does not apply to the trinomial (1+z+z^2)^n used for Rule 150

groups.title: Sturmian: the control this repo did not have
groups.blurb: Added 2026-09-21. No Sturmian control was recorded anywhere in the catalog. It is the only sequence that is APERIODIC while having exact uniform averages to infinity, which is precisely the regime P2 occupies; the periodic and Rule 90 controls are both degenerate in the lag.

entries.t: Dyadic-lag seed estimate at 2^23: null at every lag, below its own resolution floor, and not the first such measurement
entries.st: D_N(h)/(N-h) was computed at all 254 lags of D = {2^a - 2^b} inside [1, 2^22] on the stored 2^23-bit singleton centre trace, over prefixes N = 2^20, 2^21, 2^22, 2^23. Every ratio at N = 2^23 lies in [0.499544, 0.500591]. This is NOT the first evaluation of the statistic and the pre-registration's assertion that it was is false: experiments/overnight-arms/frontier_attack/a18_cryptanalysis/test4_autocorrelation.py computes z(l) = A(l) sqrt(T-l) with A(l) = 1 - 2 D_T(l)/(T-l), the exact negative of this statistic, on a sequence byte-identical to the little-endian decode of this trace, at EVERY lag from 1 to 100,000, at T = 2^20 and 2^21, with Bonferroni control over 100,838 declared tests and a twenty-seed empirical null band; the two z values sum to zero at every lag checked. What this run adds is the 115 dyadic lags above 100,000, the prefixes 2^22 and 2^23, and the first evaluation of aggregate alternative (3), which that arm never forms. The band is not evidence for (2): D_N(h) is exactly Binomial(N-h, 1/2) under a fair-coin null, since partitioning [0,N) by residue mod h makes the mismatch indicators independent within a class, so the ratio's standard deviation is exactly 1/(2 sqrt(N-h)) = 2.44e-4 at the largest lag and the observed band spans -2.56 to +2.72 in those units. It is the resolution floor. The registered kill was uncalibrated, naming a direction and no magnitude, and fired at 29 of the 232 ELIGIBLE lags against a null expectation of 28.0, with 127 of 254 ratios below 1/2 against 127 expected. An exclusive range bound had dropped h = 2^22, the largest lag; its ratio is 0.499790, inside the band, so the headline did not move but the count 253 was wrong. Three controls all fail the hypothesis as required.
entries.sc: A finite measurement, and it confirms nothing: no finite N establishes a liminf, so the test could only have killed the hypothesis and did not. Ratios at or above 1/2 are not evidence FOR (2). Any liminf below 1/2 by less than 1/(2 sqrt(N-h)) is invisible here. The novelty claim in the registration is withdrawn, not the measurement; the registration is left as written and the correction is disclosed in the source section, as is a registered control that was not met (control 1 required reproducing {6: 1/3, 12: 1} and the run reports {6: 1/3, 12: 0}; the two are consistent because the prior audit records C-densities and this reports D-ratios, but the h=6 agreement is a coincidence, 1/3 being the fixed point of x -> 1 - 2x, so that entry was never the cross-check intended). The a18 arm's calibration is stronger than this run's. One trace, one statistic; no second program reproduces the counts here, though the a18 arm independently reproduces them on the overlapping lags. Nothing here bears on whether (2) or (3) is true.
entries.relation: Fibonacci word: density of ones = 1/phi^2 = 0.381966 exactly; D(1)/(N-1) = 2/phi^2 = 0.763932 exactly, the word having no 11 factor
entries.note: Introduced as the repair for a real defect: Rule 90's centre column gives D_n(h) = 1 at EVERY lag, one distinct value over 154 lags, so it cannot detect a wrong lag set, which is how h = 2^22 went missing. The Sturmian ratios run 0.004133 to 0.763932 over 191 lags and collapse at Fibonacci lags.

bands.title: Looks uniform, is not
bands.blurb: Finite measurements and exhaustive checks over a bounded range that read like uniform statements. The range each is actually valid over is the field that matters. 122 records carry a scope warning of this kind; 752 have a finite verification method at all.

entries.t: Exact shell maxima M_k, energies I_k and endpoint sums D_k of the Rule 30 centre column for shells k = 10..28
entries.st: For the signed centre column of the lone-seed Rule 30 orbit, the shell maxima M_k = max_u |S_k(u)| over complete dyadic shells k = 10..28 are 36, 25, 65, 183, 249, 180, 367, 889, 330, 1006, 1198, 940, 3049, 6654, 5288, 6374, 14660, 14700, 8303, with the integrated energies I_k, endpoint sums D_k and first maximizing prefixes u* recorded exactly; the partial shell k = 29 (first 463,129,088 of 2^29 bits) gives M_29 >= 44301. Three independent sources (a new light-cone-trimmed simulator on 2^23 bits, the repository band cache on 2^25 bits, and the Wolfram Data Repository file on 10^9 bits) agree on every overlapping bit, and the deterministic inequalities M^3/8 <= I_k <= N M^2 hold on every complete shell. Rows 12..24 reproduce the cross-review's M_k and I_k tables exactly.
entries.sc: Finite exact computation on shells k <= 28 plus a lower bound at k = 29. Says nothing about M_k/2^k -> 0; the ladder statement 'Shell maximum o(N)' stays conjectured, and no finite list of M_k is evidence for or against it.
entries.note: Scope: no finite list of M_k is evidence for or against M_k/2^k -> 0.
entries.range: k = 10..28 plus a lower bound at k=29

entries.t: The seed's dyadic tree energy H_k stays within a factor of 1.73 of its random-sign value (k+1)N at every shell through k=28, re-derived from the payload by a second code path
entries.st: E_(k,j) is the sum of squared aligned block sums of length 2^j over shell k and H_k = sum_(j<=k) E_(k,j); H_k/N^2 -> 0 is equivalent to P2 and M_k^2 <= (k+1)H_k is proved, so H_k is the quantity the ordered-energy node's target is about. The per-level energies are NOT new: experiments/rule30/p2-cross-science-explore.json has stored every E_(k,j) for k <= 28 since at least 2026-09-17. What had not been written down is H_k itself past k=20 and three facts about it. Over k=8..28, H_k/((k+1)N) stays in [0.674, 1.727], minimum at k=11 and maximum at k=9, and (k+1)N is the expected value of H_k for independent fair signs, so the seed's dyadic energy sits at the random-sign scale, about N/log N below the o(N^2) threshold; at k=28, H_k/N^2 = 1.017e-7. H_k/N^2 strictly decreases at every step from k=9 to k=28. And argmax_j E_(k,j) = k, so that max E = D_k^2, at exactly k=9, 13, 17, 23 and 26, the shells with the largest signed sums relative to N. The computation is a second code path: a chunked fold over the payload that agrees with the sum of the stored E arrays at every k=8..28, where those arrays had been independently cross-checked only through k=12, and that reproduces the seven published H_k at k=8,10,...,20 as exact integers.
entries.sc: Exact over shells 8 <= k <= 28 and nothing past it; k=29 needs 2^30 centre bits and the only cache holds 1e9. The agreement with the stored arrays is independent of the code that wrote them but NOT of the payload: both read the same cache, verified against a regenerated centre column only on its first 8192 bits, which this run re-derives each time. The success criterion H_k = O(N^(2-eps)) is asymptotic and no finite table reaches it; sitting at the random-sign scale through k=28 is what a proof would have to explain, not evidence one exists. The band moves by a factor of 2.6 with no trend, so no constant is fitted. The node stays conjectured. Corrected 2026-09-20: the first version of this record claimed to extend a table the repository already held.
entries.note: k=29 needs 2^30 centre bits and the only cache holds 1e9.

entries.t: The aligned-block absolute-sum profile of the Rule 30 shells follows the exact simple-random-walk law to 2.25 percent through shell 28, so the triangle-inequality branch of route 1 survives the measured data
entries.st: Pre-registered in experiments/rule30/shell-maximum-o-n/PREREGISTRATION-aligned-block-seam.md, written before seam_profile.py existed and with the band calibrated against the iid control before any Rule 30 number was read. For the lone-seed centre column and shell K = [2^K, 2^(K+1)), let L(K, j) be the sum over the 2^(K-j) aligned blocks of length 2^j of the absolute block sum, and let m_j = n C(n, n/2) / 2^n with n = 2^j be the exact mean absolute displacement of a simple random walk of n steps. With r(K, j) = L(K, j) / (2^(K-j) m_j), over every K = 10..28 and every 1 <= j <= K - 12, that is every depth with at least 4096 blocks, 136 pairs in all, max |r - 1| = 0.0225. The iid control over the same construction gives 0.0196 over 78 pairs, the all-ones control 79.2170 and the biased control P(+1) = 1/2 + 1/k gives 5.6663; the last two are pre-registered kills of the screen and both fire. The deviation shrinks with block count as sampling predicts: at j = 4, r is 1.0741 at K = 10 and 1.0002 at K = 28. Hence on the measured shells L(K, j)/2^K equals sqrt(2/(pi 2^j)) to within 2.3 percent. Section 6.1 of the cross-review requires L(K, j) = o(2^K) for the triangle inequality over aligned blocks to bound the adjacent-block cross term from the halves' own bounds, and the measured profile satisfies that at every measured pair, so the data does not kill that branch.
entries.sc: Exact integer counts on the complete shells k = 10..28 of the centre column and on depths with at least 4096 blocks; no asymptotic statement and no bound on M_k. A finite profile satisfying o(2^K) at each measured K is not the uniform statement the branch needs, and nothing here produces the cross-term estimate that r30-p2-route1-reduces-to-adjacent-block-cross-term identifies as the only place Rule 30 enters route 1. What the screen measures is fixed by its controls: the biased control satisfies P2 and still fails the screen by 57 times the band, so S1 is a bias screen at the aligned-block level and passing it says the shells carry no block-level bias through K = 28, not anything about P2. r(K, 0) = 1 identically is structural, L(K, 0) = 2^K and m_0 = 1, and is excluded from the screen rather than counted; the first run counted those 19 structural entries and reported 155 pairs where 136 were measurements, which changed no maximum and no verdict.
entries.note: Follows the exact simple-random-walk law to 2.25 percent. Scope: a finite profile satisfying o(2^K) at each measured K is not the uniform statement the branch needs.

entries.t: Dyadic-lag correlations on the centre column show no drift through 2^29
entries.st: With R_N(h) = sqrt(N)*C_N(h)/(N-h) on the singleton centre column and D = {2^a - 2^b : a > b >= 0}, the quantity max_(h in D) |R_N(h)| over all 211 dyadic lags h <= 2^20 has log-log slope -0.0084 against N across eight nested prefixes N = 2^22 to 2^29, a factor 128 in N. No dyadic lag has |C_N(h)/(N-h)| above 1e-3 at any of the three largest prefixes; the three largest at N = 2^29 are 1.39e-04 at h = 24, 1.32e-04 at h = 32,760 and 1.07e-04 at h = 28, none holding its sign across the ladder. Against 211 seeded non-dyadic control lags of the same magnitude the dyadic-to-control ratio of max |R| at the top rung is 1.133. All three pre-registered kill conditions, set at slope 0.25, at 1e-3 and at ratio 2, were silent.
entries.sc: A finite measurement that can refute the hypothesis it tests and cannot confirm it: limsup_N C_N(h)/N <= 0 is asymptotic and eight prefixes of a half-billion-bit cache decide nothing about the limit. The eight rungs are nested and so are not independent trials, and the control is a calibration rather than a statistical rejection rule. It gives no bound on liminf D_N(h)/(N-h) at any lag, makes the remaining estimate no easier, and bears on no prize problem. The lag set is capped at h <= 2^20, so nothing is measured about larger dyadic lags. The source and its artifact are untracked in the working tree at the time of extraction.
entries.note: The scope line is exactly right and worth copying: a finite measurement that can refute the hypothesis it tests and cannot confirm it. The eight rungs are nested and so are not independent trials.

entries.t: Bounded support certificate on periodic-center rows (min_deepest_one)
entries.st: For rule 30, depth=256, periods 2-6, all 114 nonconstant words, widths W=1..16: no finite row with right endpoint at most W and left endpoint above -min_deepest_one has a center trace agreeing with any nonconstant p-periodic target through time 256; global minimum is 233 at p=6, word 001010, W=16
entries.sc: Bounded UNSAT only, not a nonperiodicity proof; conditional on agreement through depth=256; does not apply directly to the lone-seed orbit where B=T are not independent parameters
entries.note: Bounded UNSAT only, not a nonperiodicity proof.
entries.range: depth 256, periods 2-6, all 114 nonconstant words, widths W = 1..16

entries.t: The actual-right language acquires new minimal forbidden factors at every length measured
entries.st: New minimal forbidden factors appear at every length from 9 to 49, with 146 of them at m = 49 and 1,758 in all through length 49 (237 through length 30 and 1,612 through 48), so R is not of finite type on any range seen. The structural consequence is that no finite-state description of R is available for a transfer-matrix count, and the growth question needs either a different exact method, a description of R that is not a factor list, or an argument about Rule 30's right light cone under the driven boundary.
entries.sc: Finite and exact through m = 49 for the factor counts, with the enumeration continuing past 48 in a record rewritten after every length. 'Not of finite type on any range seen' is a statement about the measured range and not a proof that R is not sofic or not of finite type.
entries.note: Not of finite type on any range seen is a statement about the measured range.

entries.t: Certified anti-periodic suffixes to level seventeen and a DFA lower bound of two to the eighteen states
entries.st: For every level a = 4..17 there is an explicit suffix A[a] of length a, namely 2112, 21112, 212112, 2111112, 21111112, 211111112, 2211111112, 21111121112, 221111111112, 2111112111112, 21211111111112, 211121111111112, 2111211111111112 and 22111111211111112, which is anti-periodic at 2^a: f_c(m + 2^a) != f_c(m) for all m >= 0 and both tails c. Each is certified by a tower recurrence plus an exhaustive check over one period: the least even P with tower(P) = tower(0) over columns 0..q-1 gives U(j, e+P) = U(j, e) for all e >= 0; the product Phi of column q-1's letters over [0, P) satisfies Pi_(m + P/2) = Phi_m Pi_m with Phi_m a cyclic rotation of Phi, hence conjugate to it, so L = (P/2) ord(Phi) is a period of f_c; and the check covers all m < L. The column periods P run 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 8192, 16384, 65536, 131072, 262144, with L equal to P except at a = 13 and 14 where L = 2P. For a <= 3 every suffix has membership period dividing 16, and two covering sets of six suffixes each give 16 distinct signatures over m mod 16, one for each tail, with no set of five sufficing. Theorem: for c in {2,3} and all m != m' with m != m' mod 2^18, the prefixes 1^m and 1^(m') are Nerode-inequivalent for L_1(c), since a = v_2(m'-m) <= 17 and either the mod-16 table applies or A[a] flips membership an odd number of times. Hence every DFA for L_1(c) has at least 2^18 = 262144 states.
entries.sc: A finite theorem: it separates every pair of prefix lengths not congruent mod 2^18 and says nothing about a pair that is congruent, so it does not prove non-regularity. The certificates are exhaustive checks at fixed a over one membership period, not an induction on a, and the search for A[a] ranged only over the families 2 1^n 2, 2 1^i 2 1^j 2, 2 1^i 2 2 1^j 2 and, at level 17, 2 1^i 2 1^j 2 1^k 2; the listed suffixes are the first certified in that order, not the only ones. 1^m probes the wide language only, since it is not hard-core.
entries.note: A finite theorem: says nothing about a pair that is congruent, so it does not prove non-regularity.

entries.t: Bounded but residue-structureless cut run on the one-defect alternating family
entries.st: On the one-defect family W = (12)^a 2 (12)^b the maximum cut run k_E over both tails is 8 on the grid a <= 24, b <= 24 (575 words, attained at (3, 22), (8, 23) and (13, 20)) and 11 on both a <= 45, b <= 70 (3,124 words) and a <= 40, b <= 95, that is through n = 271, against the need n + 2, so the family retains slack at least n - 9; the histogram over the 3,124-word grid is 1: 1591, 2: 748, 3: 397, 4: 199, 5: 98, 6: 42, 7: 27, 8: 13, 9: 2, 10: 5, 11: 2, with the maximum attained only at (a, b) = (9, 41) and (18, 65), n = 101 and 167. The run has no residue description: for fixed a and b >= a the sequence b -> k_E has no period of length at most 40 for b <= 95, and k_E is not a function of (a mod m, b mod m) or of (a mod m, (b - a) mod m') for m, m' in {14, 28, 56}, with 598 of 784 residue classes disagreeing at m = 28. Including a = 0 over a = 0..45, b = 0..70 raises the maximum to 13, attained only at (a, b) = (1, 7), the word 1 22 (12)^7 that meets the charge bound of RESULTS-EVENTUAL-CONSTANT-TAIL.md (12) with zero slack at c = 2.
entries.sc: Finite grids only, a <= 45 and b <= 95 at most, one implementation, no pre-registration; boundedness of k_E on this family is measured, not proved, and nothing is claimed for two or more defects or for general sources. The absence of periodicity is the absence of a period of length at most 40 on b <= 95 and of a residue description at the three moduli tested. The a = 0 rerun's settled-regime section aborts at a = 0 and is not used.
entries.note: Boundedness of k_E on this family is measured, not proved.

entries.t: Pre-registered regularity kill and the resulting DFA state lower bounds
entries.st: The pre-registered kill (REG-m) fires for all six (m,c) pairs with m <= 3: S_m(11) > S_m(10), S_m(11) >= 2 S_m(8) and S_m(11) >= 0.25 E(11), with ratio S/E of 0.938 to 0.945. Consequently any DFA for L_1(c) needs at least 701 states at prefix length 11, and the extension to p = 12 and 13 at suffix horizon 7 gives E(12), E(13) = 1329, 2376 and E13(12), E13(13) = 1257, 2255, with S_1 = 1256, 2254 at c = 2 and 1257, 2255 at c = 3, so the lower bound is at least 2254 at p = 13 (2255 for c = 3, and for c = 2 at horizon 11), and at least 2192 for every m <= 3. The c = 2 shortfall of one is the horizon rather than the quotient: the unseparated pair 111112122222 against 112211222222 at p = 12 separates at suffix length 12 and the p = 13 pair at length 11.
entries.sc: This is finite evidence, not a proof of non-regularity. Finite, p <= 13, horizons 9 at p <= 11 and 7 at p = 12, 13; the p = 12, 13 extension is post hoc and not in the pre-registration. Non-regularity of L_1 would not transfer to L_m in any case, and even a proved non-regular L_m would not exclude a regular over-approximation of the survivors that is empty at the required depth.
entries.note: The p = 12,13 extension is post hoc and not in the pre-registration.
entries.range: p <= 13, horizons 9 at p <= 11 and 7 at p = 12,13

entries.t: Single-isolated-one family generalized five-zero bound
entries.st: For centre word 0^(p-1)1, the maximum forced run of consecutive centre-zero-time zero samples of column 1 equals p+2 exactly for p=2 and p=5,...,10 (width-stable across widths 12-24), matching the known p=2 bound of 4; at p=3,4 no such bound was found (the run grows unboundedly, checked to run-length 18 by two independent methods with no sign of stopping).
entries.sc: single-isolated-one family only, periods 2 and 5 through 10; p=3,4 results are empirical (checked to run-length 18) not a proof of unboundedness
entries.note: p = 3,4 are empirical, checked to run-length 18.

entries.t: Rule 30 vs Rule 90 exact adaptive decision-tree depth, n=1..4
entries.st: Brute-force minimum worst-case adaptive decision-tree depth D(f) over the full 2^(2n+1)-row truth table of the center cell c0(n): Rule 30 gives D(f)=2n+1 exactly at n=1,2,3,4 (i.e. 3,5,7,9 -- the full window is needed). Rule 90 gives D(f)=2,2,4,2 at the same n -- far below the 2n+1 window size, matching 2^popcount(n) (2,2,4,2 for n=1,2,3,4), since by Kummer's theorem only 2^popcount(n) of the 2n+1 positions carry a nonzero coefficient in Rule 90's center formula and the rest are exactly zero-influence, not merely low-influence.
entries.sc: n=1..4 only, brute force; Rule 30 result consistent with but not a proof of full-window necessity at larger n
entries.note: Consistent with but not a proof of full-window necessity at larger n.

entries.t: Almost every stored deepest-run source fails realizability inside the source word itself
entries.st: Of the 856 stored deepest-run sources, the 312 wide words at n = 10..22 from demand_transient.json and the 544 narrow words at n = 10..38 from seam_history_narrow_sub5.json (capped lists holding 856 of 980 maximisers), 811 are not factors of an actual right trace already inside W. The first proved or SAT-audited forbidden factor is 11 in 274 of them, 101001 in 204, 0100101 in 96, 010010001 in 41, 0101000101 in 31, 0101010000 in 29, 00000 in 21, 01010001001 in 15, 0001000010001 in 15, 010100010001 in 14, 010010000101 in 11, and one of 19 longer factors in 10 or fewer each. Every one of the 312 wide deepest words is unrealizable, containing 11 or a length-6 or length-7 factor.
entries.sc: Finite: 856 words only, each decided by one CaDiCaL query on the complete right light cone, and these are the stored maxima of two grammars rather than a census of realizable sources. Two of the forbidden factors used, 11 and 00000, are proved uniform members; the remaining minimal forbidden factors through length 30 are finite computation.
entries.range: 856 words, capped lists holding 856 of 980 maxima

entries.t: Reusable projector and superposition-identity verification
entries.st: The projector: projects_to_center is a verified 24 ns/call O(log n) primitive, and the superposition identity s_n(0) = rule150_center(n) XOR parity(projected errors) is exhaustively checked for all n <= 512 and on 37 banded targets to n = 10,000.
entries.sc: primitive and identity only; arm 5's broader route to o(n) remains closed (N_eff ~ n^1.68, row parity ~ n/2)
entries.note: The identity is algebraic; the record's evidence is a check.
entries.range: all n <= 512 and 37 banded targets to n = 10,000

entries.t: All-length finite-observation obstruction to quarter-wave atom absence
entries.st: Fix k>=1 and t>=3 with 2t-1>k. There is a binary periodic row w of period divisible by four such that every real observable depending on k consecutive cells has zero spectral mass at both quarter frequencies under mu_w, while Q(F^t w) != 0, i.e. the output coordinate has a nonzero quarter atom.
entries.sc: periodic input rows, not the lone seed; does not prove or disprove P1, P2, or P3; row depends on k,t
entries.note: A title that overstates a correctly-scoped result.
entries.range: all-length in k and t, but periodic input rows, not the lone seed

entries.t: Uniform shell-maximum bounds M_k <= C sqrt(2^k) with C < 2.4555, and the LIL envelope, are false on the Rule 30 orbit
entries.st: Pre-registered screens in RESULTS-shell-maximum-o-n.md section 0.2. The candidate uniform bounds M_k <= sqrt(N) (H1), M_k <= 2 sqrt(N) (H2) and M_k <= sqrt(2 N ln ln N) (H4), N = 2^k, are refuted on the centre column: H1 first at k = 10 (M = 36 > 32), H2 at k = 13, 17 and 23, H4 at k = 17 (889 > 804.1). The smallest C with M_k <= C sqrt(2^k) on every complete shell k = 10..28 is 889/sqrt(2^17) = 2.4555, so any such law with C < 2.4555 claimed from any k0 <= 17 on is false, with the k = 17 prefix as an exact re-addable witness. H3 (3 sqrt N), H5 (N^(3/4)) and H6 (I_k <= N^(5/2)) are not refuted on k <= 28, and the Brownian sup|W| null (H7, KS p = 0.71) is not rejected.
entries.sc: Refutes these uniform screens only. Each screen is sufficient, not necessary, for P2: the control iid P(+1) = 1/2 + 1/k has M_k = o(N) and still kills H1..H6, so a refuted screen says nothing against P2. Survival of H3, H5, H6 is not evidence past k = 28.
entries.note: The REVERSE warning: refuting a uniform screen says nothing against P2, because the iid control with P(+1) = 1/2 + 1/k has M_k = o(N) and kills the same screens.

entries.t: A pre-registered cryptanalytic battery finds no distinguisher for the centre column at T <= 2^21, on a decision rule its own power controls did not meet
entries.st: The a18 arm fixed a ledger of N = 100,838 hypotheses before any data (Berlekamp-Massey profile 18, correlation attack 780, NIST SP 800-22 40, autocorrelation 100,000) and applied Bonferroni at family-wise alpha = 0.05, per-hypothesis 4.9584e-07. For the lone-seed centre column the smallest raw p is 6.214e-06, adjusted 6.266e-01, with 0 Bonferroni and 0 Benjamini-Hochberg rejections: NO BIAS FOUND. Depth extension to T = 2^21 repeats tests 2 and 4 with the same result, max |z| 4.393 at lag 36578 against an i.i.d. seed band of [4.160, 4.907]. Controls that fire: lfsr32 (linear complexity plateaus at L = 32 where the centre column reaches 131,072 at n = 2^18, a factor of 4,096), bern51 (rejected at the registered p < 1e-3 by whole-sequence monobit at 1.0189e-89 and by both cumulative-sums streams at 0.0), copy1000 (autocorrelation z = 20.738 exactly at lag 1000). HOWEVER the registered decision rule reads NO BIAS FOUND only when 'all three non-degenerate power controls fire as registered' and INCONCLUSIVE otherwise, 'including a power control that fails to fire'. The three registered are lfsr32, bern51 and lag1000, and lag1000 failed BOTH of its requirements: its test-4 run rejects at NO lag at all, 0 of 100,000 exceeding the Bonferroni line, and the registered test-2 grid contains no Delta = 1000 at any k, its nearest cell being 1024, so that requirement was registered at a lag the same document's own ledger excludes. The control is mis-specified by construction and not merely by grid: for s_t = r_t XOR r_(t-1000) the shifted XOR is s_t XOR s_(t+1000) = r_(t-1000) XOR r_(t+1000), and at any other lag it is an XOR of four distinct fair bits, so the sequence is balanced at EVERY lag and has zero power anywhere, not only at its own. Recomputed here from the arm's own seq/lag1000.npy it gives z(1000) = +0.150462, in the same run in which copy1000 reproduces the committed 20.73840682678574 to sixteen digits. The arm found and disclosed this itself as deviation D1 and substituted copy1000, chosen after seeing the output. By the letter of the registered rule the outcome is INCONCLUSIVE, and PREREG is more explicit still: a test failing its registered power requirement 'is reported as having unknown power, not as a passing null'. The substitution is defensible because the control was provably null, but the headline rests on a post hoc control and a record must carry that. D3 is a second, independent ground for the same reading: test 1 was registered as {J, Hbar, D} x 6 prefixes and delivered as {G, J} x 9, so two of three registered statistics left the ledger while N = 100,838 still matched, which the arm records as happening by accident rather than by design. PREREG.md also requires deviations be appended to PREREG.md itself; they live in cryptanalysis.md section 7 instead.
entries.sc: A negative result about DETECTABILITY by four techniques at T <= 2^21. It does not IMPLY P1 or P2 in either direction: no finite-prefix statistic can imply aperiodicity, and symmetrically a surviving hit would not have refuted P1 either, a biased sequence being free to be aperiodic. But it is NOT true that the arm bears on neither prize, and the arm's own 'does not bear on P1, P2 or P3' is too strong: its null autocorrelation sweep yields an explicit period exclusion, recorded separately as r30-a18-autocorrelation-excludes-period-band. Three further limits, none of which changes the verdict. Test 2's sensitivity to a lag correlation is demonstrated ONLY outside the ledger, by a supplementary check at one hand-picked lag chosen after the fact, because the two in-ledger firing controls are both degenerate for that purpose: rule90 gives eps = 0.5 at every cell and bern51 gives eps = |2p-1|/2 independent of Delta. The autocorrelation sweep tests 100,000 of 1,048,576 available lags, 90.5 percent untested, and that cap is also what fixes N. The generator gate compares 65,536 bits against two independent implementations, 6.25 percent of the 2^20 prefix and 3.1 percent of the 2^21 extension. The arm's own Obstruction H governs all of it: every result is a statement about a finite prefix and can never establish randomness, absence of structure or nonperiodicity as an infinite statement.
entries.note: The archetype for this band: 100,838 pre-registered hypotheses, Bonferroni-corrected, NO BIAS FOUND, and it bounds nothing. The arm says so itself and repeats it next to every headline number by design.
entries.range: T <= 2^21; 100,000 of 1,048,576 lags; NIST block protocol over c[0:10^6]

entries.t: The centre column's Berlekamp-Massey profile, not just its ceiling, matches a random sequence through n = 2^18 against a 500-seed null
entries.st: Berlekamp-Massey gives L(n) = 513, 2049, 8192, 32771, 65537, 131072 at n = 2^10, 2^12, 2^14, 2^16, 2^17, 2^18, so L(n) - ceil(n/2) = +1, +1, 0, +3, +1, 0 and L/(n/2) = 1.0020, 1.0005, 1.0000, 1.0001, 1.0000, 1.0000. The column sits ON the n/2 line, which is the random-sequence expectation, not above or below it. This record is NOT the ceiling result: that is ea4c789fd2294772, already proved through n = 16384, and this reproduces it exactly at n = 16384 (L = 8192, ratio 1.0000). What is new is the PROFILE, which a maximal ceiling does not determine, together with its null. The jump count J(n) = 273, 1048, 4095, 16340, 32829, 65502 lies inside a 500-seed empirical null at all nine tested prefixes, empirical p from 0.128 to 0.984, and the mean jump height Hbar approaches 2.00, the geometric expectation, from n = 2^14 up. The exact integer G(n) = sum_(m<=n) (2L(m) - m) equals n/2 exactly at 2^10 through 2^15 and at 2^17, 2^18, 2^20, and departs from it twice: n/2 - 12 at n = 65536 and n/2 - 4 at n = 2^19. A first pass reported that anomaly as REJECT (profile anomalous) at z = -5.415; it is an ARTIFACT and the arm retired it, the null taking only four distinct values across 500 seeds at that prefix so that a normal z on a 20-seed standard deviation of 1.5e-5 is a normal approximation to a lattice statistic at near-degeneracy. Against the 500-seed empirical null the same deviation has p = 0.0639 and does not persist with depth.
entries.sc: Capped in depth and in comparison, and the two caps differ. The profile-against-null comparison holds to n = 2^18 = 262,144; G alone was computed to 2^20 with NO null at 2^19 or 2^20, so that figure is a bare number with nothing to read it against; and the 20-seed band underlying the original z stops at 2^17, leaving the n = 262,144 row with no null comparison at all. Hbar is a deterministic function of the same jump list as J, so the two are not independent hypotheses despite being counted separately in the ledger. The delivered test-1 ledger is {G, J} x 9 prefixes against the registered {J, Hbar, D} x 6, which the arm discloses as deviation D3 and notes matches the registered count of 18 'by accident, not by design'. The measurement DOES carry one infinite-statement consequence, and it is already subsumed: an eventually periodic sequence with preperiod q and period p satisfies a linear recurrence of order q+p, so L(n) <= q+p for EVERY n, and L(2^18) = 131,072 therefore forces q+p >= 131,072 if the centre column is eventually periodic at all. That is the same logical shape as the recorded subword-complexity exclusion 7e73f8c439ee894e, which uses p(n) <= r+q to force r+q >= max_n p_hat(n) = N - L with L the longest repeated factor, empirically about 2 log2 N; that bound is LINEAR in the prefix length and its 200,000-bit run actually excludes r+q <= 199,966, against this route's 1.31e5; the Berlekamp-Massey profile therefore adds nothing to period exclusion and must not be reported as if it did. (The autocorrelation sweep in the same arm does much better, see r30-a18-autocorrelation-excludes-period-band.) What a profile on the n/2 line does NOT do is exclude eventual periodicity, since any period exceeding the measured depth reproduces it exactly. The empirical p floor of 1/501 = 0.00200 is 4025 times the global Bonferroni threshold, so by the arm's own statement this audit 'can refute a hit, not confirm one'.
entries.note: Linear complexity on the n/2 line at every measured prefix forces p+q >= 131,072 if the column is eventually periodic at all, since L(n) <= p+q for every n. That is real but weaker than the catalogued subword exclusion r+q >= 199,966, and far weaker than the same arm's own autocorrelation band. A profile on the n/2 line does NOT exclude eventual periodicity.
entries.range: profile-vs-null to n = 2^18; G to 2^20 with no null at 2^19 or 2^20

entries.t: No autocorrelation distinguisher at any of 4.19M lags at T = 2^23, at a maximum indistinguishable from the sample-size expectation
entries.st: Every lag 1 <= l <= 2^22 on the stored 2^23-bit centre trace, z(l) = A(l) sqrt(T-l) with A(l) the balance of c_t XOR c_(t+l), by FFT zero-padded to 2^24 >= 2T so the circular correlation is exactly linear. Result: max z = 5.5216 at lag 1,656,153, min z = -5.2703 at lag 661,856, and 0 of 4,194,304 lags reach the two-sided Bonferroni threshold 5.701. The maximum is not a finding but the sample size: the one-sided expected maximum for that many i.i.d. normals is sqrt(2 ln L) = 5.5225, and the observed 5.5216 sits 0.0009 below it. Twenty i.i.d. Bernoulli(1/2) seeds at the same T and lag range give empirical max z = 5.7157 and max |z| = 6.0485, both ABOVE Rule 30's maximum, so the column is less extreme than a typical random sweep of the same width. A registered gate requires the FFT to reproduce a direct mismatch count at 24 spread lags; observed maximum discrepancy 1.221e-15 in z. This extends the prior sweep of 100,000 lags at T = 2^21 by 42x in lags and 4x in length, and that extension is the contribution.
entries.sc: A finite-prefix statistic. It cannot imply aperiodicity in either direction and does not touch P2. ITS PERIOD COROLLARY IS TRUE AND STRICTLY DOMINATED, and is recorded only so it is not rediscovered: z(p) < thr forces q > (T-p-thr sqrt(T-p))/2, excluding p <= 4,194,304 with q <= 2,091,314 and reaching p+q = 6,285,618 at most, whereas 70faaffe0b04ef36 forces r+q >= N-L from subword complexity with NO cap on the period and gives r+q >= 8,388,565 at this same N. Verified directly on this trace: at window length 44 all 8,388,565 windows are distinct, so L = 43. The margin is 2,102,947 and no region of the band survives. The domination is structural, not incidental: p(n) <= r+q uses every window while the autocorrelation uses one lag at a time, so extending the sweep cannot close the gap. Three registration defects are disclosed in the source section: the Rule 90 power bar was unreachable at the length first used and was repaired by raising the length rather than fixing the threshold, which is the wrong direction; both positive controls are constants independent of the Rule 30 data, sitting at 475x and 508x the decision boundary, so the registered kill clause is dead code; and the Sturmian word was cast as a negative control but exceeds the threshold at 260,436 of 524,288 lags, correctly. The first run reported INCONCLUSIVE under the registration's own control rule and the exclusion was withheld, but that run left no artifact, the JSON being overwritten in place while untracked.
entries.note: A null over 4.19M hypotheses whose maximum sits 0.0009 below the value the sample size predicts. Its period corollary looks like a uniform gain and is strictly dominated by an existing subword-complexity record at the same N, which is exactly the band-E failure: a finite result that reads as progress.
entries.range: every lag to T/2 at T = 2^23; 4,194,304 lags

entries.t: The autocorrelation maximum cannot discriminate a sequence from its balanced-masked version, exactly invariant under the period-2 mask
entries.st: XOR-ing a binary mask m into a sequence multiplies its sign sequence by (-1)^(m_t). For the period-2 mask m_t = t mod 2 this gives x'_t x'_(t+l) = x_t x_(t+l) (-1)^t (-1)^(t+l) = x_t x_(t+l) (-1)^l, so corr'(l) = (-1)^l corr(l) and |z(l)| = |corr(l)|/sqrt(n-l) is PRESERVED EXACTLY AT EVERY LAG. The autocorrelation maximum is therefore blind by construction, not merely underpowered, to that mask and to every mask whose complement-shift set contains the argmax lag. Measured on the Rule 30 centre column: max |z| and its argmax lag are identical under the period-2 mask to fifteen digits. Calibration of the whole family: the largest movement any balanced deterministic mask produces is about 0.50, while the Gumbel standard deviation of max |z| at N = 4.19e6 lags is 1/sqrt(2 ln 2N) = 0.18. The occasioning run measured the Thue-Morse residual R_t = c_t XOR theta(t) over t in [1, 2^23) and found residual density 0.5002161 (+1.25 null sd) against the column's 0.5002196 (+1.27 sd), and residual max |z| 5.2244 against the column's 5.5220, a gap of 0.2976 against a registered kill at 1.0. That kill is twice the largest achievable effect and 5.6 standard deviations of the statistic's own noise: IT COULD NOT FIRE. The observed -0.2976 sits inside the range seven i.i.d. random masks produce, -0.499 to +0.030. The null was forced by the design.
entries.sc: A statement about the INSTRUMENT, not about Rule 30. It says max |z| cannot resolve a balanced deterministic mask at this N; it says nothing about whether the Thue-Morse decomposition simplifies the centre column, and the occasioning run's headline that the residual is 'statistically indistinguishable from the column' is WITHDRAWN as unsupported. The exact invariance is proved only for the period-2 mask; for other masks the blindness is empirical (the 0.50 ceiling over the masks tried) except where the argmax lag lies in the mask's complement-shift set, where it is again exact. The measurement's Rule 90 control was VACUOUS: that column is 0 for every t >= 1, so the asserted identity (0 XOR theta)[1:] == theta[1:] holds for any array and passes with a deliberately wrong theta, establishing only that the Rule 90 column is all-zero after t = 0 rather than that the residual is formed correctly, which is what the registration gated INCONCLUSIVE on. Nothing here bears on P1 or P2.
entries.note: The archetype of a forced null. A registered kill at 1.0 against a statistic whose largest achievable movement is 0.50 and whose own noise is 0.18 could not fire. Band E is where a result that reads as a finding but was determined by its own design belongs.
entries.range: exact for the period-2 mask at every lag; empirical 0.50 ceiling for others

targets.title: Fixed-window recurrence
targets.prompt:
TASK: Fixed-window recurrence (P2, ladder statement 'Fixed-window recurrence', currently conjectured)

TARGET: For some l>=1 and constants 0<eta<1, C independent of k and j: V_(k,j+l) <= (1-eta) V_(k,j) + C 2^(-j) whenever j+l <= k/2 (P2-C).
IF IT HOLDS: it establishes P2: density one-half by declared sufficiency or equivalence.

STATEMENT: For some l>=1 and constants 0<eta<1, C independent of k and j: V_(k,j+l) <= (1-eta) V_(k,j) + C 2^(-j) whenever j+l <= k/2 (P2-C).
SCOPE: Stronger than necessary and neither observed nor proved as a seed law; worth pursuing only if the seed supplies a mechanism for these uniform constants. Must not replace the flexible-scale target P2-F as the primary one.
DO FIRST: Do not search l >= 2 and C >= 1/4 on the stored shells. That instruction stood here until 2026-09-21 and both of its premises are false against records already attached to this node. l = 2, 3 and 4 are tested and hold with C = 0 on every admissible pair of k <= 28 (r30-fwr-seed-min-loss-k28). C does not rescue l = 1 either: at the killing pair (k,j) = (2,0), V_(2,0) = V_(2,1) = 1, so absorbing the witness needs C >= eta, which is exactly the condition under which the source document's Criterion A calls that same pair vacuous, and r30-fwr-additive-remainder-vacuity measures the regime empty of content at C = 1. What is open is uniformity in k, and the one measured threat to it is the small-block regime: on the extended domain j+l <= k the l = 2 minimum falls from 5/8 to 19/188 at (9,7), where N/2^j is four blocks (r30-fwr-extended-domain-minima). Recompute the per-shell l = 2 minimum over k <= 28 restricted to pairs with block count N/2^j >= B, for B = 4, 8, 16, 32, and report the smallest B at which the per-shell minima stop dipping. A B at which they stop localizes the obstruction to a bounded-block-count artifact and says where a uniform argument has to work; no such B, or per-shell minima still falling in k, is evidence against a k-uniform eta and is worth more than another pass at a fresh (l, C).
SUCCESS MEANS: Uniform l>=2, eta>0 and C independent of k and j satisfying P2-C at every shell and every admissible j, by an argument in k; or a refutation covering every l>=2, which the l=1, C=0 kill explicitly does not. The pass over the stored shells is already done and is not success: r30-fwr-seed-min-loss-k28 exhibits C=0 with eta=5/8 for l=2 on all 169 admissible pairs of k<=28, 1611/1940 for l=3 on 144 and 3711/4040 for l=4 on 121, and the Rule 90 and balanced-run controls of the source document's section 3 already reject perturbed constants, so the earlier finite form of this criterion was satisfied on the day it was written. C is a trap rather than a free parameter, by r30-fwr-additive-remainder-vacuity: wherever eta V_(k,j) <= C 2^(-j) the inequality reduces to monotonicity and tests nothing. A refutation would also not reach P2, since ed8bae2f15256b6e proves P2-C strictly stronger than P2.

HISTORY: pattern-classified documents on this statement: 4, of them negative results by document role: 0; attached records killing a lever whatever their document's role: 2.

LEVERS ALREADY KILLED ON THIS STATEMENT. If your approach reduces to one of these it is already dead; read the kill's own scope before deciding it does not:
- The one-step pure contraction form of P2-C (l=1, C=0) fails on the singleton seed (2026-09-19). Refuted: V_(k,j+1) <= (1-eta) V_(k,j) with eta>0 for all admissible (k,j). At shell k=2, j=0 the centre-column cells c_4..c_7 = 1100 give z = (-1,-1,1,1), E_0=4, D_0=0, E_1=8 and V_(2,1)=V_(2,0)=1, so eta<=0 for l=1, C=0.
  SCOPE OF THE KILL: Kills only l=1 with C=0; any C>=1/4 absorbs this pair (for eta=1/4), and l>=2 is untouched. Does not refute P2-C (ladder node fixed_window).
- An additive remainder C=1 makes the fixed-window test vacuous on the stored seed shells (2026-09-19). For l=2 and eta in {1/4, 1/2}, taking C=1 leaves 0 of the 169 admissible pairs (k<=28) with eta E_(k,j) > C N, so the P2-C inequality there reduces to V_(k,j+2) <= V_(k,j), which every sign sequence satisfies; with C=0 all 169 pairs are non-trivial and satisfied at eta=1/2.
  WHAT IS DEAD: A finite pass of the fixed-window test carrying an additive remainder C >= eta min(E/N) is evidence for the P2-C recurrence.
  SCOPE OF THE KILL: A methodological finding about finite verification of P2-C on k<=28: a finite pass with C>=eta min(E/N) is not evidence for the recurrence. Not a statement about the uniform constants.

TARGET: For D = {2^a - 2^b : a > b >= 0} and the singleton centre trace, liminf_N D_N(h)/(N-h) >= 1/2 for every h in D; equivalently limsup_N C_N(h)/N <= 0. The weaker aggregate alternative asks only that limsup_N (1/N) sum_(0<=i<j<m) C_N(2^j - 2^i) <= 0 for an unbounded set of m.

STATEMENT: For D = {2^a - 2^b : a > b >= 0} and the singleton centre trace, liminf_N D_N(h)/(N-h) >= 1/2 for every h in D; equivalently limsup_N C_N(h)/N <= 0. The weaker aggregate alternative asks only that limsup_N (1/N) sum_(0<=i<j<m) C_N(2^j - 2^i) <= 0 for an unbounded set of m.
SCOPE: Sufficient for P2 and, separately, for P1, by r30-sdc-dyadic-hypothesis-suffices; explicitly unproved in either form and not claimed necessary for either prize. The P1 direction is the sharper one: an eventually p-periodic trace forces C_N(h)/N -> 1 at the lag h in D divisible by p, so… [+90 characters not shown, read the source]
SUCCESS MEANS: A proof on the singleton seed that limsup_N C_N(h)/N <= 0 for every h in D, or the aggregate alternative for an unbounded set of m. Neither is established. Measurement is NOT success and cannot become success: the seed estimate at 2^23 resolves the per-lag ratio only to 1/(2 sqrt(N-h)), extending the trace buys resolution at rate sqrt(N) and never a limit, and the per-lag and aggregate tests are sensitive to opposite alternatives (r30-sdc-aggregate-alternative-power-asymmetry), so neither clean result strengthens the other. DO FIRST, before any new measurement here: the statistic has already been swept at every lag to 100,000 at T = 2^21 by experiments/overnight-arms/frontier_attack/a18_cryptanalysis, with stronger calibration than the dyadic run, and no record cited that arm until r30-sdc-dyadic-lag-seed-estimate-extends-a18-sweep; read it before claiming any measurement is new. What would count is an origin-specific cancellation argument using the singleton seed's own structure, since the hypothesis is false for general sequences: r30-sdc-powers-of-two-insufficient exhibits a periodic word balanced at every pure power-of-two lag and unbalanced at a difference lag, so no argument treating the trace as an arbitrary balanced word can work. Falsified by exhibiting one h in D with limsup C_N(h)/N > 0 on the seed.

candidates.definition: A minimal-counterexample descent needs a map W to W' with |W'|<|W| that preserves membership in the survivor set. When a length-dependent parameter (padding 0^n) is coupled to |W|, deleting a boundary symbol also changes the padding and the initial condition of the causal recursion, so no shift identity holds beyond a vanishing fraction of words (7 matching words of 377 at n=12).

candidates.name: Derivation size mistaken for algorithmic lower bound
candidates.definition: A bound on the number of terms, sections or constraints used by one particular derivation or unfolding of a_n is presented as a lower bound on the work of every algorithm computing a_n. A fixed derivation existing with size s is compatible with another representation of much smaller cost, so the derivation size is only an upper bound on this formula.

next.constraints:
CONSTRAINTS
- Reproduce every number and identity you rely on from the code before using it; the atlas records what was true when it was written.
- Write results only under experiments/rule30/{slug}/ (RESULTS-{slug}.md plus scripts and logs). Do not edit the catalog, the atlas or another session's files.
- A claim is 'proved' only with an exhaustive or machine-checked certificate and a control that fails when the claim is false. Otherwise say conjectured or computed.
- Finite data is not a uniform proof: state the range checked and never extrapolate past it.
- Report exactly: STATUS, what is proved, what is refuted, what is still open, and which ladder statement changed.
